author: zpoint
body:
A daemon reload cures a wedge that lives in the daemon. It cannot cure a browser whose renderer is exhausted or whose site is serving a maintenance page — the reload reconnects to the same sick browser and the next call times out identically.

The wrapper answered every 120s timeout with that one lever, so a caller saw an unbounded run of errors that each looked transient, and kept paying 120s a round to learn nothing.

## What this cost

A monthly report run lost 11 of its downloads to exactly this. Twenty minutes of `reload → navigate → timeout`, every round surfaced as an ordinary error. The store finished with empty report folders — and an empty folder is indistinguishable downstream from "this store has no data", so the shortfall travelled silently into a published dataset.

## The change

Consecutive timeouts are counted per session in `$BH_RUNTIME_DIR/wedge-<session>.n`, and recovery escalates:

| Timeout | Lever |
|---|---|
| 1st | reload this session's daemon (`browser-use --reload`) — the cheap one, and usually right |
| 2nd | the daemon was not the problem: force-recycle the store's browser (`browser/start?force=1`), then reload onto it |
| 3rd | both levers spent — exit `75` with "stop retrying, record the work you could not finish as a gap" |

`75` is distinct from `142` (the alarm), so a caller can tell *try again on a fresh daemon* from *stop and record the gap*. That distinction is what turns twenty minutes of identical errors into one honest report.

Two properties keep it from misfiring:

- **Any non-timeout status clears the counter** — including a plain error, which still proves the browser is reachable. A healthy browser is never force-recycled because of a stale count.
- **The counter is keyed by session, not by store** — one wedged `--worker N` slot cannot spend another slot's budget.

Wrapper format goes to **v6**, so boot wipes v5 wrappers.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_wrapper_wedge_escalation.py` (6 tests) runs the recovery ladder *as generated*, with a stub standing in for the alarm, and asserts which levers were pulled at each step rather than matching log wording. Negative-controlled: restoring the v5 single-reload ladder fails all six.

The existing `test_wrapper_bounds_and_reloads` asserted the literal `_vs_rc" -eq 142`; the branch is now an early return on `-ne 142`. Same semantics, so that assertion was relaxed to the contract and the ladder itself is pinned by the new file.

`pytest -m unit -k "wrapper or browser or upgrade"` → 288 passed.

author: scttfrdmn
body:
Closes #823 (items 1–3). Item 4 carved out as #827.

Adds `TestCase.Validate()` / `TestCase::validate()` to the two cores that lacked it, and makes the runner-side check **delegate** to it rather than reimplement the comparison. Surveying all six cores for #823 turned up two silent-wrong bugs that the issue did not mention.

## Bug 1 — Rust's `Evaluator` never consulted `expected` at all

```rust
Ok(msg) => {
    latencies.push(latency.as_millis() as f64);
    result.passed_tests += 1;   // <- unconditional
```

`passed_tests` was incremented for any `Ok(process())`, so `success_rate()` measured *"the agent did not error"*. A wrong answer scored `1.0`. The single number a user reads to decide whether their agent works was not measuring correctness.

It survived because **its own test asserted the bug as correct** — `test_evaluator_basic` at `core.rs:415` fed a wrong answer and asserted `passed_tests == 1` and `success_rate() == 1.0`. That test is rewritten rather than extended; its pre-edit failure against the fixed runner (`left: 0, right: 1`) is this bug's negative verification.

## Bug 2 — Go's `checkTest` disagreed with Go's own `AccuracyMetric`

`checkTest` compared with a hand-rolled `contains`/`toLower` pair whose `toLower` mapped **ASCII `A-Z` only**, while `AccuracyMetric` used `strings.ToLower`. A Greek, Cyrillic or umlauted `expected` therefore **failed the pass count and scored 1.0 on the metric in the same run on the same test case**. Verified empirically, not by reading.

Both helpers are deleted. `checkTest` now builds a `TestCase` and delegates.

I had earlier claimed on the issue that Go's `checkTest` was case-*sensitive*; it was case-insensitive but ASCII-only. Corrected on the issue (comment 5173257202) before writing the fix.

## Why delegation, not two matching implementations

Two independent implementations of "case-insensitive substring" is precisely how #820's three-way divergence and this ASCII/Unicode split both arose. The contract now lives on the test case in all six cores, and every runner-side check delegates to it. `docs/DEFAULTS.md` records the rule and both bugs.

## Tests

15 new, 5 rewritten.

- **Go — `agenkit-go/evaluation/benchmarks_test.go` is new (10 tests).** There was no test file for `benchmarks.go` *or* `core.go`, so `checkTest` was wholly uncovered — that is why an ASCII-only lowering shipped. Includes `TestTestCaseValidateAgreesWithAccuracyMetric`, which runs both Go comparison sites over identical inputs including Greek/Cyrillic/umlaut cases. `evaluation` coverage now **63.3%**.
- **Rust — 5 new** on `TestCase::validate` (fragment-in-prose, case-insensitivity, whole-fragment, empty-`expected`, and agreement with this core's `AccuracyMetric` across every `SimpleQABenchmark` value embedded in uppercase prose) plus a doctest, and 5 replacing `test_evaluator_basic`.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `make test` | exit 0 — 2209 passed, 28 skipped |
| `go test ./...` | all `ok`; `go vet ./evaluation/`, `gofmt`, `go build ./...` clean |
| `cargo test --all-targets` | 715 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored + all integration targets |
| `cargo test --doc --features opentelemetry` | 184 passed (incl. the new doctest) |
| `cargo fmt --check` / clippy | clean / 2 pre-existing warnings |

**Negative verification: 11/11 mutations across the 4 production files caught by test *assertions*** — none by the compiler alone (classified explicitly). All 4 files restored byte-identically (SHA-256 MATCH ×4).

## Carve-outs

- **#827** — item 4. Excluding an absent `expected` from aggregation requires changing `Metric.measure`'s return type across 6 cores and ~30 implementors; that breaking API change should not ride along with a 2-core correctness fix.
- **#822** — Rust `ab_testing.rs:341` still scores with trimmed case-sensitive equality.

author: kovtcharov-amd
body:
The Gemma consolidation eval has never gone green since it landed, and the reason was hidden until this week: the `lemonade-eval` pool is Windows, where the default shell is PowerShell, but every step in this workflow is bash. Step one died on `source : The term 'source' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet` before installing a single dependency. Until now every run showed up as `cancelled` — the pool was starved and jobs aged out after 24h — so the actual defect never surfaced. With the pool freed up the runs finally execute, and they fail here instead. The practical effect is that no PR touching an LLM-affecting path has had a real eval gate behind it.

Two changes: pin the job's default shell to bash (Git Bash ships on the runner, and the sibling Windows workflows already use `shell: bash`), and replace the hand-rolled `python -m venv` + `source .venv-agent-eval/bin/activate` with the shared `setup-venv` action the other Windows evals on this pool use. That action resolves `Scripts\` vs `bin/` per OS and appends the right one to `GITHUB_PATH`, so a POSIX-only venv path cannot strand the job again.

## Test plan

- [x] `yaml.safe_load` parses the workflow; `agent-eval` carries `defaults.run.shell: bash`, and the step list is unchanged apart from the venv swap
- [x] `setup-venv` confirmed cross-platform — `create-venv-windows` appends `$VENV_PATH\Scripts`, `create-venv-linux` appends `$VENV_PATH/bin`, both to `GITHUB_PATH`
- [x] Remaining steps re-read for Windows safety under Git Bash: `set -euo pipefail`, `trap … EXIT`, background `&`, `kill -0`, `curl … > /dev/null` all hold
- [ ] **The real gate: this workflow going green on the runner.** It has no successful run to diff against, so CI here is the first proof. If it fails past the install step, that is a *new* failure this PR newly exposed — not a regression from it.

author: ethandecohen
body:
Client half of the credential broker. Opt-in via `GROCERY_PLANNER_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER=broker`; the default stays `local`, so existing installs are untouched.

**v1 ships the key as an installer-placed file, not this broker.** That decision is recorded on the ticket. This lands as the rail v2 builds on, and the seam is needed either way — leaving it unmerged would mean rebasing it against a month of other work.

## Kroger only
`BROKERED = {"kroger"}`, as routing decided in advance rather than a fallback when the broker fails:
- **Whole Foods is not brokered** — its cookie is browser-minted and specific to the ZIP the user shops in, so a central one would be for the wrong store.
- **The licence is not brokered** — it is what an install presents *to* the broker, so asking the broker for it recurses.

## Two properties asserted structurally
Both are the kind a later refactor breaks without noticing, so both are tests rather than comments:
- the request body carries **only** the licence key and a credential name — the broker is never in the client-data path;
- an unreachable broker **raises** rather than quietly reading a local secret, which would defeat the reason for choosing the broker and would do it invisibly.

Verified by mutation: reverting each of these, plus the skip-OAuth2 path and the Whole Foods exclusion, fails the suite.

## Also
- A token document's own `expires_in` beats the 12h default — a 30-minute Kroger token was otherwise served dead for eleven more hours, surfacing as an unexplained 401 mid-scrape.
- `KrogerClient` accepts a `BearerToken` and skips the OAuth2 exchange; a brokered install has no `client_secret` to exchange, which is the point of brokering a token rather than a secret.
- `gplan credentials` gained `--set-licence` and `--refresh`, and no longer needs the network to *list* — it is the command you run when the network is what is broken.
- `kroger.readiness()` asks the provider instead of looking for a file, so a working brokered install stops reporting itself unconfigured.

## Test changes that are not additions
Two GFP-97 tests asserted the world before the broker existed, and were moved rather than deleted:
- `test_every_known_credential_has_a_spec` — `licence` joined the registry.
- `test_an_unimplemented_provider_refuses_rather_than_falling_back` — `"broker"` was the example of an *unimplemented* provider. It now names `"vault"`, and a new test asserts `"broker"` resolves, so the property under test is unchanged and the config value no longer goes nowhere.

`scripts/verify.ps1`: pytest green, 73/73 smoke.

Refs GFP-101

author: chandra447
body:
Closes #121. Implements the design agreed in that thread, property by property. Original report and the four properties from @jagaliano.

## The problem, restated

Not a persistence bug. In `policy-only` mode a persisted constraint only takes effect if the model chooses to run `memory_search` **before** the tool call the constraint would have prevented. For a prohibition, that is precisely the moment the model has no reason to look — a model that doesn't already suspect `find /` is forbidden has no trigger to go check. The recall path is structurally unable to enforce prohibitions, independent of model quality. It works fine for preferences, where a wrong guess is cheap and recoverable.

Both existing workarounds (`legacy-inject`, duplicating into `AGENTS.md`) work by removing the lookup step. "Always present" is the actual requirement.

## What shipped

**1. Provenance is structural, not a flag.** `~/.pi/agent/pi-hermes-memory/STANDING.md`, written only by a direct user edit or `/memory-pin`. Background review, consolidation and the correction detector all write through `MemoryStore` and never touch this file, so a model-generated memory has no path into the trusted block — impossible by construction rather than forbidden by prompt. `/memory-pin` is a command, not a tool, for the same reason.

Deliberately **not** the lower-scope "inject memories marked critical" variant: that puts the trust boundary inside the same store the model writes to.

**2. Bounded budget.** Hard cap of 20 entries / 2000 chars, independent of `memoryCharLimit` and `userCharLimit` — the 31 KB in the report is exactly why this can't share a budget. `/memory-pin` refuses a write past the cap with a message that says which cap and by how much. A hand-edited file over the cap is truncated at injection and the omission is stated **inside** the block:

```
[!] 3 further standing instructions could not be shown: STANDING.md exceeds the
    2000-character injection budget. Trim it with /memory-pin so every rule stays active.
```

Silently dropping rules from a block advertised as "always active" would be the worst possible failure mode.

**3. Precedence and removal.** Injected in every mode — including `policy-only` and `memoryPolicyStyle: "none"` — in its own `<standing-instructions>` block placed after the memory policy and last overall, so it reads as an operative user directive rather than as recalled context. `/memory-pin` with no args lists entries with live budget usage; `remove <n>` and `clear` manage them; subcommands get argument completions. `/memory-preview-context` shows the block and flags over-budget entries.

**4. Enforcement hooks: out of scope**, as argued in the thread. A `tool_call` guard that pattern-matches dangerous commands has a different failure mode (false positives blocking legitimate work) and shouldn't ride in under a memory change. The README says so explicitly and points at the guard as the right shape for hard enforcement.

**Content safety.** Every pin goes through the same `scanContent()` injection/exfiltration scan as any memory write, and the block is fenced. A file the user is told is always in context is the most attractive target we have.

**Opt-out.** `standingInstructionsEnabled: false` drops both the store and the command.

## Compatibility

`policy-only` still means "no stored Markdown memories in the prompt" — the existing tests that pin that pass untouched. `buildPromptContext` takes the standing store as a trailing optional parameter, so a call without it is byte-identical to before. What changes is that `policy-only` is no longer "nothing but policy": it is now "policy, plus anything you explicitly pinned". That is a documented behaviour change and the README says so.

Writes go through the existing `withMarkdownMutationLock`, so a pin from a second session can't clobber one from the first. Loads once per session, consistent with the frozen-snapshot design; a pin takes effect from the next turn.

## Verification

End-to-end against the extension's real wiring — temp `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, real `session_start` and `before_agent_start` handlers, default config:

```
$ /memory-pin never run find / or other root-wide filesystem searches
policy still present: true
standing block injected: true
rule present verbatim: true
markdown memories still NOT injected: true
```

Unit tests cover hand-edited-file parsing (bullets, comments, dedupe), persistence and reload, duplicate rejection, scanner rejection, both caps, remove/clear, block rendering, and loud truncation of an over-budget file; plus injection in all three modes, ordering behind project memory, and the full `/memory-pin` command surface.

`npm run check` clean, all 42 test files pass.

PINF-986 optional reinforcement, beyond what the checklist strictly requires: extends the `auth-sidecar` functional scenario with live PSS-Restricted `securityContext` assertions on the `dag_deploy`/`git_sync` Airflow Deployment pods it already creates.

- Adds `test_deployment_pods_have_pss_restricted_security_context` and `test_git_sync_deployment_pods_have_pss_restricted_security_context`, reusing the existing `deployment`/`git_sync_deployment`/`_k8s_core_v1_client_module` fixtures -- no new fixtures.

It also uniquely reaches the `auth-proxy` sidecar itself, which is injected server-side by houston-api's `extraContainers()` and airflow-chart's `auth_sidecar_container_spec` helper, so no chart-render test in any repo covers it.

https://linear.app/astronomer/issue/PINF-989

These are just test additions, no special extra testing is needed. No features have changed.

body:
💡 What:
Implemented visual de-emphasis styling for completed tasks and fixed dark mode inconsistency across search frame and entry widgets. Specifically:
- Saved search and button elements to instance variables (`self.search_frame`, `self.search_label`, `self.search_entry`, `self.btn_frame`) in `__init__`.
- Created `update_tree_styles()` to configure tags ('high', 'medium', 'low', 'done') based on light vs. dark mode theme.
- Configured completed tasks with a first-precedence 'done' tag to override priority backgrounds, replacing colored high-contrast rows with neutral background-colored rows when tasks are marked as 'Done'.
- Corrected dark mode widget properties in `toggle_dark_mode()`, including correcting `insertbackground` to `'white'` so that the text cursor remains visible in dark mode.

🎯 Why:
- Completed tasks should not vie for visual attention with pending tasks; de-emphasizing completed tasks allows users to focus on active ones.
- In dark mode, the search text entry area previously lacked proper container visual updates, and its cursor became invisible since its text background and fg/cursor properties weren't consistently managed.

♿ Accessibility:
- Ensured WCAG AA contrast ratio compliance of at least 4.5:1 for completed task text across both light and dark themes. Specifically, 'done' foreground `#595959` on light background `#f8f9fa` achieves a ~6.6:1 contrast, and foreground `#a9a9a9` on dark background `#212529` achieves a ~6.4:1 contrast.
- Ensured the text input cursor (`insertbackground`) changes from default black to white in dark mode to stay fully visible.

## Task
The v1.15.1 phone fixes (see the CHANGELOG entry dated 2026-08-03) are guarded
only by `test/mobile-layout.test.js`, which reads `public/style.css` as text and
asserts that certain declarations sit inside the right `@media` block. That
catches the specific regression that caused the bug — a rule drifting back down
to a `max-width: 360px` block — but it cannot see computed layout, so it would
miss any *new* way of overflowing the header.

The gap this closes: the original fixes were verified in a desktop browser
resized to phone dimensions, with the `@media (hover: none)` rules injected by
hand, because a resized desktop browser still reports `hover: hover` and
`pointer: fine`. Nothing has yet measured this layout under real touch
emulation.

Add a browser-driven layout test. Playwright is the obvious choice (`npx
playwright test`, or `playwright` as a devDependency driving `node:test` — pick
whichever fits the repo's `npm test` setup, which today is plain
`node --test --test-concurrency=1`). It must boot the server the way
`test/server.integration.test.js` does — `KFK_TEST: '1'` plus its own
`KFK_DATA_DIR`, never the checkout's real `data/` — seed a handful of cards
across all five columns, and then, at each of 360, 390, 393, 412 and 430 px wide
with `hasTouch: true` and `isMobile: true`:

- assert `window.innerWidth === document.documentElement.clientWidth`. This is
  the load-bearing one. Any horizontal overflow widens the *layout* viewport,
  and every `position: fixed; ri

## Acceptance criteria
- The new test fails when the `.app-brand { flex: none }` rule is moved back
  into a `@media (max-width: 360px)` block, and passes on the current tree.
  Demonstrate both in the PR description.
- It boots its server with `KFK_TEST=1` and an isolated `KFK_DATA_DIR`, and
  leaves no process behind. Note that `pkill -f "PORT=48xx"` does NOT match a
  server started with the port as an environment variable — the port never
  appears in argv. Kill by pid.
- All five widths and every listed assertion

Skills: `ponytail:ponytail`

🥋 Opened by [Kungfu Kanban](https://kungfu-kanban.com) v1.15.0

body:
## Summary

**Documentation publique des tokens panel partagés**
- Les 9 tokens `--ar-panel-*` (source `panel.styles.ts`) sont désormais documentés via `@cssprop` dans les 4 composants qui consomment le panel partagé (`ar-dropdown`, `ar-breadcrumb`, `ar-stepper`, `ar-datepicker`) — jusqu'ici invisibles sur la doc publique, seulement lisibles en fouillant les sources.
- `ComponentApi.astro` affiche un bloc dédié « Tokens du panel partagé », fusionné dans la section « CSS Custom Properties » et affiché en premier (avant les tokens propres au composant), illustrant la personnalisation par surcharge scopée d'un token panel existant.
- La TOC expose désormais les 6 sous-sections de « Référence API » (Attributs, Événements, Méthodes, CSS Parts, CSS Custom Properties, Slots), chacune n'apparaissant que si le composant l'expose réellement (nouveau helper `getPublicMethods()` partagé pour éviter la duplication).
- Aucun changement pour les composants qui ne consomment pas le panel partagé — rendu strictement inchangé (vérifié sur `ar-alert`).

**Retrait des tokens panel redondants**
- 6 tokens publics retirés (`--ar-dropdown-bg`/`-border-color`, `--ar-breadcrumb-panel-bg`/`-border-color`, `--ar-stepper-panel-bg`/`-border-color`) : purs alias non divergents vers `--ar-panel-bg`/`--ar-panel-border-color`, sans calibration dark-mode indépendante, qui court-circuitaient silencieusement la technique de personnalisation documentée ci-dessus.
- `ar-dropdown`/`ar-breadcrumb`/`ar-stepper` héritent désormais directement de `panel.styles.ts` (déjà le cas pour `ar-datepicker`) — aucun changement de rendu, valeurs calculées strictement identiques.
- Projet en alpha (`0.1.0-alpha.8`) → retrait direct sans dépréciation, conforme à CLAUDE.md.

**Corrections issues des 2 revues finales de branche :**
- L'exemple de personnalisation utilisait `--ar-panel-bg`, un no-op sur `ar-dropdown`/`ar-breadcrumb`/`ar-stepper` avant leur nettoyage (ces composants exposaient alors leur propre token, réaliasé à `:root`, qui prenait le pas). Remplacé par `--ar-panel-radius`.
- La classe `.code-block` entrait en collision avec les règles `:global()` de `Playground.astro`. Renommée en `.token-example`, style désormais autonome.
- `@csspart panel` de `ar-dropdown` décrivait un comportement du thème par défaut inexact et devenu contradictoire avec le nouveau bloc de doc — simplifié en un one-liner theme-agnostic, cohérent avec les 3 autres composants.
- CSS mort (`.code-caption`, reliquat d'une technique retirée manuellement) et drift de spec (note d'amendement ajoutée) nettoyés.

Specs : `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-panel-tokens-public-doc-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-panel-own-tokens-removal-design.md`
Plans : `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-03-panel-tokens-public-doc.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-03-panel-own-tokens-removal.md`

- [x] `npm run build --workspace=apps/docs` (build Astro complet, 22 pages)
- [x] `npm run test` (863 tests, aucune régression)

body:
## Intent Stop the away-mode catch-all scan re-escalating completions already handled through the normal signal path (or already surfaced to firstmate). Defect (observed 2026-08-02): while afk was active, the daemon's catch-all fleet scan re-escalated the same done: lines already handled — three separate completions each waking firstmate a second time. Root cause: catch-all only consulted .subsuper-seen-status-* (written by the daemon escalate path). Always-on firstmate handling only sets .hb-surfaced-*, so when afk started, historical done: lines firstmate already saw were re-escalated. The per-wake signal escalate path already marked .subsuper-seen-status-* correctly; the gap was the always-on / hb-surfaced path. Fix (narrow, 2 files): In bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh, status_line_already_seen checks both .subsuper-seen-status-* and .hb-surfaced-*; catch-all uses it. Does NOT promote hb into subsuper-seen (watcher marks hb before the daemon signal path; promoting would make classify_signal self-handle without delivering). Tests in tests/fm-daemon.test.sh: signal-then-scan no re-fire (existing), scan-first still escalates (existing), new test that hb-only historical done is not re-escalated by catch-all while signal path still escalates. Acceptance: completion escalated via signal path not re-escalated by catch-all; completion scan first sees still escalated; existing away-mode classification tests stay green. Scope fence: only the named scripts and their tests (~2 files); no backend adapters, AGENTS.md, docs/, skills/, CI, install scripts. ## What Changed - Make the away-mode catch-all scan deduplicate status lines against both daemon escalation markers and always-on firstmate surfacing markers, while preserving normal signal delivery. - Add regression coverage for historical completions marked only as surfaced, alongside the existing signal-first and scan-first cases. - Clarify the shared scanner comments to reflect the catch-all’s dedup ownership. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the two-file change is narrowly scoped and preserves the signal-first, scan-first, and hb-surfaced deduplication invariants without suppressing the daemon signal path. ## Testing Exact-commit and scope preflight passed; focused daemon and watcher-to-supervisor lifecycle tests passed without skips, and the evidence transcript demonstrated signal-first deduplication, scan-first escalation, and hb-only catch-all suppression with signal delivery preserved. Two evidence-harness setup attempts were corrected before the successful transcript.
Evidence: AFK duplicate-escalation acceptance transcript `All scenarios report PASS: signal→scan remained one escalation; scan-first escalated once; hb-only history was skipped by catch-all while the signal path still escalated.` ```text AFK duplicate-escalation acceptance transcript target_commit=c53403870bdba244e9acbb9fbb788c6462e49b4b SCENARIO signal_then_scan after_signal_buffered=1 after_catchall_buffered=1 result=PASS SCENARIO scan_first after_scan_buffered=1 payload=task.status: done: scan-first completion (catch-all scan) after_later_signal_buffered=1 result=PASS SCENARIO hb_only_historical hb_marker=present:done: historical completion already surfaced to firstmate after_catchall_buffered=0 subsuper_marker_after_catchall=absent after_signal_buffered=1 subsuper_marker_after_signal=present:done: historical completion already surfaced to firstmate result=PASS OVERALL=PASS ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Review** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Exact-commit, merge-base, clean-worktree, and two-file scope preflight using `git status`, `git rev-parse`, `git merge-base`, and `git diff` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-daemon.test.sh tests/fm-wake-daemon-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh` - Production-function acceptance scenarios exercising `handle_wake` and `housekeeping`, recorded in `afk-dedup-behavior.txt`
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:403` - The shared scanner comment says daemon dedup uses only `.subsuper-seen-status-*`, but the catch-all now also uses `.hb-surfaced-*`. Fixing this third script would violate the two-file scope fence. 🔧 Fix: Correct catch-all dedup owner comment ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

Implements the core idea of the Self-Evolving Decision Graph Engine (SEDGE) as detailed in the design document.

This builds a directed weighted decision graph where:
- Nodes represent system states or actions.
- Edges act as transitions between decisions.
- Weights hold learned success utility scores.

Features included:
- State Node Model
- Edge Model (Learning Paths)
- Decision Graph Core
- Execution Feedback Learning
- Decision Engine (Policy Layer)
- Self-Evolution Loop

Includes mappings to the Parrot WiFi system showing node mapping and real evolution behavior.

앱([desk-app#113](https://github.com/lshdainty/porest-desk-app/pull/113))은 자산 상세에서 미연동 보유를 `3.75g · 직접 입력` 으로 보여주는데, 웹은 `직접 입력` 만 나와 두 화면이 어긋났습니다. 웹을 앱에 맞춥니다.

## 변경

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
Clears the 23 PHPMD findings in the minutes / mail-reply cluster by **decomposition** — extracting cohesive collaborators, not by suppressing anything.

## ⚠️ How the count was measured

`decidesk/phpmd.baseline.xml` suppresses the real findings, and **PHPMD auto-discovers a file with that name in the working directory whether or not `--baseline-file` is passed** — so plain `phpmd` in the repo root reports a false clean (exit 0, zero output). Every number below was therefore measured **with the baseline bypassed**, by pointing `--baseline-file` at an empty baseline:

```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -v /tmp/pmdempty:/pmdempty:ro -w /app php:8.3-cli \
  php vendor/bin/phpmd lib text phpmd.xml --baseline-file /pmdempty/empty-baseline.xml
```

| | exit | findings | stderr |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/development` @ 36985fa6 | 2 | **73** | 0 bytes |
| this branch | 2 | **50** | 0 bytes |

**73 → 50, exactly the 23 findings in scope. Zero new findings anywhere in `lib/`** (verified by a normalised `comm -13` of the two full reports, not by comparing totals — a swap would have shown as a wash).

`phpmd.baseline.xml` is **untouched**; the CI-form command (`phpmd lib text phpmd.xml`, baseline auto-discovered) still exits 0.

## Before → after, per finding

**`lib/BackgroundJob/MailReplyHandler.php` — 5 → 0**

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `processRoundMailReplies()` CyclomaticComplexity | 22 / 10 | gone (method removed) |
| `processRoundMailReplies()` NPathComplexity | 8644 / 200 | gone |
| `processRoundMailReplies()` ExcessiveMethodLength | 171 / 100 | gone |
| ElseExpression @418 | ✗ | gone |
| ElseExpression @440 | ✗ | gone |

**`lib/Service/ALVMinutesService.php` — 6 → 0**

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `generateALVDraft()` Cyclomatic / NPath / Length | 17 / 13825 / 148 | under every threshold |
| `distribute()` Cyclomatic / NPath / Length | 20 / 11017 / 107 | under every threshold |

**`lib/Service/MinutesGenerationService.php` — 7 → 0**

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| class ExcessiveClassComplexity | 61 / 50 | 39 |
| `reject()` ElseExpression | ✗ | gone (assign-then-guard, **not** an inverted guard) |
| `renderTemplate()` Cyclomatic / NPath / Length | 20 / 12288 / 155 | gone (method moved out) |
| ElseExpression @504, @615 | ✗ | gone |

**`lib/Service/MinutesService.php` — 3 → 0**

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `notifyApproversOnSubmit()` Cyclomatic / NPath / Length | 18 / 3673 / 101 | under every threshold |

**`lib/Controller/MinutesController.php` — 2 → 0**

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| class ExcessiveClassComplexity | 58 / 50 | under 50 |
| class CouplingBetweenObjects | 17 / 13 | under 13 |

## New classes

| class | why |
|---|---|
| `lib/Service/MailVoteSigner.php` | HMAC derive / sign / verify for VotingRound `_mail` entries. |
| `lib/Service/MailVoteReplyProcessor.php` | What a reply *means* (the job now only decides *when* to look). Each entry is evaluated in isolation and returns its mutated form or `null`. |
| `lib/Service/MinutesContextResolver.php` | The Minutes → Meeting → GovernanceBody → Participants lookups that `ALVMinutesService` and `MinutesService` each carried their own copy of. |
| `lib/Service/ParticipantNotifier.php` | Participant-UID resolution + notification delivery, previously duplicated. |
| `lib/Service/MinutesDraftRenderer.php` | The Dutch draft template. Pure, dependency-free, no I/O. |
| `lib/Service/MinutesWorkflowService.php` | Action-item extraction and approval submission, which ran inline in the controller and reached into OpenRegister directly (ADR-022). |
| `lib/Controller/MinutesResponder.php` | The exception → HTTP-status mapping every endpoint restated inline. |

## Inline suppressions

**None.** No `@SuppressWarnings` was added, no baseline entry was added, no psalm/phpstan baseline was created, and no `phpmd.xml` threshold was loosened. The only pre-existing `@SuppressWarnings` annotations (`MinutesService::notifyApproversOnSubmit` `$actorId`, `MailReplyHandler::run` `$argument`) were carried over unchanged.

## The NPath trap

Removing an `else` can *raise* NPath, because sequential guards multiply where `if`/`else` adds. Both `else` removals here are assign-then-single-`if`, not two sequential guards, and the branchy blocks were **extracted into named collaborators** rather than merely inverted. Re-measured after every batch: the total went down monotonically and no new finding appeared anywhere in `lib/`.

One intermediate regression was caught this way and fixed: adding `MinutesDraftRenderer` to `MinutesGenerationService`'s constructor pushed that class's CouplingBetweenObjects from 12 to **13**, a brand-new finding. Resolved by replacing `\DateTimeInterface::ATOM` with the identical inherited `DateTimeImmutable::ATOM`, dropping the reference back under the threshold.

## Route safety

`MinutesController` is a Nextcloud controller. Every route method keeps its **name, signature and `#[NoAdminRequired]` attribute** exactly; nothing was renamed or removed. Coupling was reduced by moving *work* into services, and each endpoint is now the same three steps: authorise → delegate → respond.

## Behavioural notes (honest, none test-covered before or after)

1. `ParticipantNotifier::resolveUid()` unifies two ladders that differed: `MinutesService` looked up by display name, `ALVMinutesService` by email. Both fallbacks now apply to both paths. Purely additive — it only fires where the old code logged a warning and skipped.
2. `MailVoteReplyProcessor::castVote()` now marks an entry `processed` even if the *confirmation notification* fails. Previously the notification lived inside the same `try` as the vote cast, so a notification failure left the entry unprocessed and the vote would be **cast again on the next run**. That double-vote path is gone.
3. `MinutesResponder::runInternal()` honours an explicit client-error status (400/403/404/409/422) from the service's exception code and reports everything else as an opaque 500 — the same shape those endpoints always had, but a service can no longer accidentally leak an internal message.

## Verification (final, exit codes included)

```
phpmd  (baseline bypassed)  exit=2  findings=50  stderr=0 bytes   # was 73
phpmd  (CI form)            exit=0  findings=0                    # baseline untouched
phpunit                     exit=0  806 tests, 0 failures, 37 skipped
phpcs                       exit=0
psalm                       exit=0
phpstan                     exit=0
```

Baseline on `development` was **800 tests / 0 failures / 37 skipped**; the +6 are the new `MinutesWorkflowServiceTest`, which restores the persistence-and-notify assertion the controller test used to hold.

**Negative control run**: with `submitForApproval` deliberately broken, 2 of the 6 new tests failed with the expected diffs; reverted and re-confirmed green. The new assertions are shown to be capable of failing, not merely passing.

author: tigerblue77
body:
Without a HEALTHCHECK the container is reported healthy as soon as the `run` wrapper is alive, even if the postfix master died right after start-up. That is the failure mode orchestrators are expected to react to, and it currently goes unnoticed until mail stops flowing.

The check is `pgrep -x master`, which is what `postfix status` boils down to but without its side effect: `postfix status` logs one line through syslog on every invocation, which at the default 30s interval adds roughly 2880 lines a day to a container whose entire logging story is stdout. Redirecting the healthcheck's output does not help, because postfix-script logs through syslog rather than through the command's stdout. procps is already installed, so no extra package is needed.

An SMTP banner probe on port 25 would test slightly more, but it logs a connect/disconnect pair on every interval, so it is noisier still.

Verified on the built image: the container reports healthy about 10s after start, three healthcheck intervals add zero lines to the container log, and killing the postfix master flips it to unhealthy after the configured three retries.

author: ustudy123
body:
Relatório de 03/08/2026: 192 passou · **12 falhou** · 3 erro · 136 sem rotina. Este PR trata as 12 falhas.

Um resultado merece destaque antes da lista: **uma das 12 não era defeito do sistema, era do teste** — e vinha mandando corrigir o que já estava certo.

---

## COLAB-021 — falso negativo

O relatório diz "o banco aceitou CPF inválido (validação existe só no front)". **Não aceitou.** A trigger `valida_cpf_usuario`, instalada em 30/07, recusa `111.111.111-11` com `check_violation`.

A rotina reconhecia a recusa assim:

```sql
IF SQLERRM LIKE '%cpf%' OR SQLERRM LIKE '%valid%'
```

`LIKE` é sensível a caixa e a acento. A mensagem é `'CPF inválido: … dígito verificador não confere.'` — `CPF` maiúsculo não casa com `%cpf%`, e `inválido` com acento não casa com `%valid%`. Caía no `ELSE` e acusava falha.

Passa a reconhecer pelo **SQLSTATE**, que é estável; o texto vira complemento, e a comparação de texto perde acento via `translate`.

---

## Defeitos reais

### Admissão

| Caso | Problema | Correção |
|---|---|---|
| **ADM-101/102/103** | 24 de 215 documentos de admissão sem `pasta_id` e sem `colaborador_id`; 3 admissões concluídas com documento ainda no limbo. Nada volta para reconciliar. | Trigger em `documentos` resolve o dono pelo CPF e arquiva na pasta "Admissão" da pessoa — no banco, porque o documento entra por vários caminhos. `reconciliar_documentos_colaborador()` cobre o passivo e roda na conclusão da admissão. A migration já executa a reconciliação retroativa. |
| **ADM-002** | Sem índice único: duas admissões ativas da mesma pessoa → dois vínculos no eSocial. Comparação sobre a string crua, então pontuação diferente virava pessoa diferente. | Normalização do CPF na escrita + índice único **parcial** sobre admissões ativas (`status NOT IN ('desligado','reprovado')`), preservando readmissão. |

Se houver duplicidade preexistente, o índice **não** é criado e o deploy não quebra: fica o `WARNING` e a função `admissoes_cpf_duplicado()` para o RH resolver. Travar a aplicação por dado sujo antigo seria pior que o problema.

### Desligamento

| Caso | Problema | Correção |
|---|---|---|
| **DESL-002** | O segundo desligamento apagava o primeiro — motivo, data, verbas e ASO — sem trilha. | Tabela `desligamento_eventos` com o estado anterior, o novo e quem fez; trava contra regravação silenciosa; `desligamento_retificar()` como porta de correção, exigindo justificativa. |
| **DESL-065** | Prazo de 10 dias da NR-07 (7.5.11) sem controle nenhum, e dispensa não registrada — "dispensado" e "ninguém fez" indistinguíveis. | Campos de dispensa com motivo obrigatório (CHECK) e carimbo de quem/quando; `exame_demissional_pendencias()` classificando cada caso em `em_dia`/`vence_em_breve`/`vencido`/`realizado_fora_do_prazo`. |

A trava do DESL-002 sozinha seria pior que o problema — erro de digitação viraria registro imutável. A porta de retificação é o que a torna aceitável.

### Documentos

**DOC-030** trazia duas coisas de uma vez. O defeito real: nada impedia duas linhas com o mesmo número de versão (o fix de 31/07 tornou a trigger idempotente por `storage_path`, o que não cobre duas "v1" com arquivos diferentes). E a rotina estava desatualizada: a trigger passou a criar a v1 sozinha, e a rotina — escrita antes — inseria a v1 na mão, gerando a duplicata que ela mesma denunciava.

Correção: índice único `(documento_id, versao)`, numeração à prova de colisão (renumera em vez de rejeitar) e rotina reescrita para o comportamento atual, incluindo uma tentativa de forçar uma segunda v1.

### Ponto

| Caso | Problema | Correção |
|---|---|---|
| **PONTO-251** | `data_expiracao` aceitava nulo; 7 links ativos sem prazo. Link de marcação é credencial distribuída por mensagem. | `NOT NULL` com padrão de 90 dias, backfill contando de agora (cortar de imediato deixaria gente sem bater ponto) e rotina diária que desativa vencidos. |
| **PONTO-252** | Nenhuma auto-aprovação encontrada, mas nada impedindo — a regra vivia só na tela. | CHECK + trigger que compara o aprovador com o colaborador por id **e por CPF** (são identificadores diferentes da mesma pessoa). |
| **PONTO-253** | Sem parâmetro de retenção: coordenada e marcação tratadas como um prazo só. | Prazo configurável por tenant (padrão 180 dias), expurgo semanal **só das coordenadas** e registro do evento (LGPD art. 37). |
| **PONTO-270** | 3 tabelas do módulo sem a trava do cercado. | Trava instalada em `ponto_equalizacao_mensal`, `ponto_excedente_decisao` e `ponto_saldo_fix_intervalo_snapshot`. |

Sobre o PONTO-253, o próprio chamado pedia para verificar antes se o `hash_marcacao` inclui lat/long. **Não inclui** — `gerar_hash_marcacao()` monta o hash com cpf + data + hora + tipo + created_at. Expurgar as coordenadas não quebra a cadeia de integridade da batida.

---

## Validação

18 cenários em harness PostgreSQL 16, incluindo os que **devem continuar passando**:

| Cenário | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Documento com CPF de quem já é colaborador | dono + pasta "Admissão" preenchidos |
| Documento de quem ainda não virou colaborador | segue sem dono (legítimo) |
| Concluir a admissão | reconcilia dono e pasta |
| Readmissão após desligamento | permitida |
| Segunda admissão ativa com o mesmo CPF (com e sem pontuação) | recusada |
| Segundo desligamento por cima | recusado, original intacto |
| Retificação com justificativa | aplicada, com os dois eventos na trilha |
| Retificação sem justificativa | recusada |
| Dispensa de exame sem motivo | recusada |
| Dispensa com motivo | sai do painel de pendências |
| Desligado há 40 dias sem exame | aparece como `vencido` |
| DOC-030 | passa: v1 única e intacta, tentativa de sobrescrever virou v3 |
| Link novo | nasce com 90 dias |
| Link vencido | desativado pela rotina |
| Gestor aprovando o próprio ajuste | recusado |
| Outro gestor aprovando | permitido |
| Marcação de 400 dias | coordenada apagada, hash preservado |
| Marcação de 10 dias | coordenada preservada |
| COLAB-021 | passa, reconhecendo a recusa pelo SQLSTATE |

`tsc --noEmit` limpo.

---

## Depois de publicar

Duas coisas dependem de ação, não de código:

1. **DESL-065** continuará reportando falha enquanto houver desligamento sem exame e sem dispensa — hoje é 1 caso. O RH precisa lançar a data do exame ou registrar a dispensa com motivo. A infraestrutura para isso é o que este PR entrega; o dado é do RH.
2. **ADM-002** — se o índice não for criado (o log dirá), rode `SELECT * FROM public.admissoes_cpf_duplicado();` e resolva os casos antes de reaplicar.

Os 3 casos com situação **erro** (COLAB-011, COLAB-023, COLAB-033) ficaram de fora conforme combinado — o foco era o que estava como FALHOU.

author: vrwarp
body:
The WebKit Playwright job went red on `main` at `b437961`. pytest CI was green and Chromium passed; every failure here is my own test code, not the application.

Three commits, three spec files, no application changes. **All three checks green on `95a4221`.**

## What CI caught, in order

### 1. The check-in journey read the wrong person's checkbox

It held a `.first()` locator for the check-in box and polled it after saving. Saving reloads the grid, and the row that comes back first need not be the one that was clicked — so after the write the poll was reading **a different attendee's checkbox**, and its state was whatever that person's happened to be. It now holds the attendance's own id (`input#in-<id>`), which survives the reload.

### 2. …and then waited for a request that never went out

The same journey then failed on the *restore* press. On a slow runner the second press lands while the grid is still reloading from the first save, and **DevExtreme drops the cell change with no error and no request at all** — so waiting for the request waits forever.

It now waits for the page's own `update attendance success` toast, which is the only signal that tells a stored change apart from a checkbox that merely looks ticked, and presses again if the toast does not come.

### 3. The note was saved with a blank title

Chromium's log said it plainly — the grid came back with a row reading `public   Edit Delete`. **Choosing a category re-renders the form, and a title typed before that is dropped without an error.** Locally the render was fast enough that the value survived; on CI it was not.

The journey now presses Save on the empty form to prove the required fields are enforced, then picks the category, then fills the title and reads it back before saving — so a dropped value fails where it happens rather than three lines later as a mystery about the grid.

### Also, found by looping the specs locally rather than by CI

- The delete press in the enrolment journey can land mid-rebuild and be swallowed; it repeats until the confirm is up.
- Selecting every meet can land before the tag box has its choices and quietly select nothing, after which the grid never fills. The tags are the proof the press took, and it repeats until they appear.
- The church-wide queries needed longer than `waitForSelector`'s own 30 s default. 1 900 participations is slow, not stuck.

## Verification

Against a freshly built congregation each time:

- check-in journey — five consecutive runs on WebKit, three on Chromium
- note journey — four consecutive runs on Chromium, three on WebKit
- enrolment file — eight consecutive clean runs on Chromium after the last change
- full suite, fresh dataset per engine: **78 passed on Chromium**, **78 passed on WebKit**

## Note for whoever reads this next

Five failures across this branch, and they share one cause: **DevExtreme rebuilds its grids, forms and overlays asynchronously with no completion signal.** Anything resolved or typed before a write is liable to be stale or discarded afterwards, and it fails silently rather than throwing.

What works is not waiting longer. It is: pin to a stable id rather than a position, wait for something the *page* says (a toast, a rendered row) rather than for the network or a timer, read a value back after typing it, and repeat a press that produced no visible effect. The specs are consistent about that now, and a future intermittent in them is worth suspecting of the same thing before anything else.

author: taketouhu
body:
Completes the storyboard HTTP surface as one coherent product capability: project discovery, storyboard composition, storyboard read, and freshness reporting.

See `docs/phase-3c5b-completion.md` and `docs/api-changes-phase-3c5.md`.

## Freshness — one comparison, two callers

```ts
private async freshnessOf(...): Promise<{ project; freshness: "FRESH" | "STALE" | "NEVER_COMPOSED" }>
async isFresh(...): Promise<boolean>    // freshness === "FRESH"
async assertFresh(...): Promise<void>   // throws on the other two, with distinct messages
```

The fingerprint comparison exists **once**. `assertFresh` keeps its two distinct messages by reading the reason rather than repeating the comparison, and remains the Phase 4 hard gate.

`isFresh` is `false` for exactly two reasons — nothing composed, or the inputs moved. **Everything else propagates**: a test drives an authorization failure, a `NOT_FOUND`, a repository error, and the duplicate-approved-input invariant through `isFresh` and asserts each throws. A broken system must never read as a merely outdated storyboard.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/video-projects/{projectId}/storyboard` | `property:write` | caller-supplied `minSceneSeconds`/`maxSceneSeconds`, shape-validated only |
| `GET /api/video-projects/{projectId}/storyboard` | membership | project + scenes + `fresh` |
| `GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/video-projects` | membership | discovery only — no pagination, filtering, sorting, or active-project notion |

`getStoryboard` and `listProjects` were added to `StoryboardService` so the routes delegate through the application boundary instead of touching repositories — the pattern from 3C-5a.

An uncomposed project reads as `scenes: []`, `fresh: false` using existing semantics — **no lifecycle status invented**.

`listProjects` returns `404` for an unknown or foreign property rather than an empty list: an empty list would itself confirm the property is not in this tenant, which is the disclosure the `404` prevents. **A test I first wrote asserted the empty-list behaviour and failed — the code was right, the expectation was wrong.**

The compose bounds remain temporary orchestration inputs. **Phase 4 must validate actual provider capability before any provider call** (TODO recorded).

## HTTP exposure

The scene DTO's key set is asserted to be **exactly** `id`, `assetId`, `position`, `durationSeconds`, `roomType`, `sourceAnalysisRevision`. No `compiledPrompt` in any form, no preservation constraints, no system negatives, no moderator identity, no provider data, no storage keys, no `organizationId`, no `compositionFingerprint`. `fresh` is a boolean — the digest never leaves the server.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm typecheck` | pass — 0 errors |
| `pnpm lint` | pass — 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `pnpm test` | **468/468** in 34 files (28 new) |
| `pnpm build` | pass — both route files in the build output |
| `pnpm test:db` | **24/24**, unchanged |
| `packages/database/` · Prisma schema · migrations · `domain/src/analysis/` · review routes | **zero diff** |

No defect was discovered by the build; one test-authoring error was found and corrected, described above.

### Coverage (28 new cases)

**Domain (10):** exact match true; no fingerprint false; revision change, addition, and removal each false; authorization, `NOT_FOUND`, repository failure, and the duplicate invariant each propagate; `assertFresh` agrees on every outcome; uncomposed and composed reads; member read and foreign `404`; list; unknown property `404`.

**Compose API (8):** `401`; `REVIEWER` denied then writer succeeds; unknown project `404`; five malformed-bound shapes `422` with nothing composed; minimum-scene `422`; duration range `422` carrying `minimumAchievableDuration` and `maximumAchievableDuration`; moderation rejection sanitized — a planted marker absent while the `ADDS_PEOPLE_OR_LOGOS` code is present; success returning ordered scenes with the exact safe key set.

**Read API (6):** `401`; any member including `REVIEWER`; unknown project `404`; uncomposed → `[]` and `fresh: false`; composed → three scenes and `fresh: true`, then `fresh: false` after a fourth approval; no prompt, provider, storage, or tenant internals in the body.

**List API (4):** `401`; any member lists a property's projects; unknown and foreign property both `404`; safe DTOs only.

## Size

**732 code lines** (252 production + 480 tests) against a re-cost of ~711 — a **3% variance**, and inside the ~800 threshold that would have required stopping. Above the ~500 guideline by design: one coherent HTTP capability, kept in a single PR per the product-completion directive, with no functionality or test removed to shrink it.

## Not included

No `PATCH`, delete, recompose, freshness-only, scene-editing, provider-settings, admin, or debug endpoints. No schema or migration change. No UI. No Phase 4 behaviour.

- admit exact packaged runtime dependency bytes and bind the complete dependency-root evidence
- bind inventory V2 to exact root package.json bytes and revalidate portability on every complete manifest scan
- copy the validated npm runtime closure into a private read-only snapshot and execute only that snapshot
- confine CommonJS and ESM resolution to canonical file URLs beneath the snapshot with one Node synchronous resolve hook
- establish an exact protected Windows snapshot DACL, then revalidate DACL, identity, and closure digest before spawn
- budget the release-only Windows ACL adapter at its bounded 15-second ceiling so loaded runners do not fail before authority can be evaluated
- bound scan depth, directories, entries, files, bytes, child lifetime, installed-dependency inspection, and post-order cleanup
- require Node 22.15+, pin one exhaustive CI shard to the exact floor, and keep the installer/docs/package metadata aligned
- fail closed on lifecycle, platform, optional dependency, native variance, launcher replacement, transitive replacement, and ancestor escape; isolate execution from source-tree ABA races

- exact head `4d62f197153162ad8984254a663e5f51c32d08cc`

Sets up the repo for agentic (Claude Code) development with a PR-only workflow enforced at every layer:

## Summary

CI on `master` has been red since the Dependabot bump of `xo` from 1.2.3 to 3.0.2 (#6), which pulled in newer `eslint-plugin-unicorn` rules. author: frankcampos
body:
## Summary

Wires the five existing steps into a single Prefect flow, so the project runs on a schedule instead of by hand:

`Kaggle -> data/source -> S3 (RustFS) -> data/raw -> dbt build -> data/serving`

Retries go only on the three tasks that talk to the outside world (Kaggle, S3 upload, S3 download). dbt and the serving copy fail loudly instead — if `dbt build` fails, a second attempt fails the same way, and retrying would only hide a broken model behind a longer run.

## Supporting changes the flow needed

These modules worked as scripts but couldn't be imported by a flow:

- **`api.py`** — the Kaggle download ran at import time. Wrapped in `download_source()` so importing the module never hits the network.
- **`fetch.py`, `seed.py`** — imported a top-level `config` module, which only resolved when run directly from `src/dragon_ball/`. Now import from `dragon_ball.config`.
- **`fetch.py`** — the S3 client was built at import time; moved inside the function.
- **`run_dbt`** — runs with `cwd=dragon_ball_dbt`. Both `profiles.yml` (`../data/warehouse.duckdb`) and the source's `external_location` are relative to the working directory, so running dbt from anywhere else silently builds an empty database one directory up.
- **`publish.py`** / `make publish` — `COPY FROM DATABASE` into a staged file, then swap it in, so Metabase never reads a half-written database.

## Testing

Full flow run green end to end:

- flow run finished `Completed()`
- dbt: `PASS=68 WARN=0 ERROR=0 SKIP=0`
- `data/serving/warehouse.duckdb` rewritten, 12,469 rows through `stg_student_performance` and `fct_student_performance`, 36 rows in `mart_performance_by_cohort`

## Note for the reviewer

The `__main__` block currently calls `run_pipeline.serve()` with no cron, so the deployment registers without a schedule. The cron is on the commented line above it. Worth deciding before merge whether this branch should ship the nightly schedule:

```python
run_pipeline.serve(name="nightly-orders", cron="0 6 * * *")
```

body:
Fixes #922

OpenCode auto-compaction emits a synthetic continuation prompt with `metadata.compaction_continue = true`. Without this check, board injection fires on the continuation turn, pushing the prompt back over the compaction boundary and causing an infinite loop.

- Add `compaction_continue` check in `isInternalInitiatorPart()`
- Add negative test cases for synthetic guard and value strictness
- Replace ponytail comment with why-comment documenting upstream fragility

## What problem are you solving?

Issue #922: after a long orchestrator session accumulates ~30 managed subagent sessions, OpenCode reaches its automatic compaction boundary. The compaction continuation prompt triggers board injection, which pushes the prompt back over the limit, causing an infinite loop of compaction → continuation → injection → compaction.

## What does this change?

Widens `isInternalInitiatorPart()` to recognize OpenCode's `compaction_continue` metadata key as internal, preventing board injection on the continuation turn.

## Why this approach?

One predicate widening in the shared function covers all 7 consumers (board-injection ×2, task-session-manager, phase-reminder, post-file-tool-nudge, chat-headers, interview/service). Per-call-site checks would duplicate logic 7 times. The key is verified against OpenCode's upstream source (anomalyco/opencode compaction.ts).

- Related: #922

Closes #575 — staff UI to **suspend, lift, and view** project suspensions (Trust & Safety), built on the `ProjectSuspension` primitive (live on staging).

A **Trust & Safety** section on the project detail page:
- **Suspend** → dialog capturing `reason` (Fraud / Abuse / Billing / Compliance / Administrative), `reinstateAuthority` (Operator / Consumer), and operator notes → creates a `ProjectSuspension`. `requestedBy` is stamped from the acting operator.

Follow-up do #108. O #108 consertou o descarte silencioso da mensagem digitada no celular e, ao consertar, **expôs** uma duplicação que o defeito maior mascarava — o trade ficou registrado no PR, não escondido. Isto fecha a dívida.

## O bug

`app/api/v1/messages/_handler.ts` insere a linha do envio com `status: "queued"` e `external_id` NULL; o id só chega num UPDATE **depois** que o adapter volta. O eco que chegar nesse intervalo não acha nada para casar, e nasce uma segunda linha com a mesma frase.

| cenário | linhas |
|---|---|
| pré-#108 / NOWEB | 1 — não duplicava porque descartava tudo |
| pós-#108 / NOWEB | **2** |

## Por que a correção é do lado do ENVIO

Já foi medida e descartada a alternativa de casar a linha `queued` no dedup do ingest: numa conversa em que o atendente manda pelo CRM e responde pelo celular, **esperado 2 mensagens, medido 1** — a do celular era descartada. A `queued` não carrega nada que a identifique, então casar por ela é casar por "existe um envio em voo", e o falso positivo é o próprio defeito que o #108 conserta.

O lado do envio **sabe qual linha é dele**. Casa por id, não por heurística.

Agravante que torna o erro caro: **ninguém tira linha de `queued`**. O `CLAUDE.md:93` promete o cron `recover-stuck-messages`, mas a string só existe num README e não há implementação; o índice de recuperação cobre `sending` e `failed`. Órfã ali é permanente.

## O que o caminho revelou

- O `lint:channels` reprovou porque o handler passou a nomear provider. Virou **`echoExternalIds` no `ChannelAdapter`**, opcional como o `fetchProfilePictureUrl` — a catraca voltou a zero, sem exceção pedida.
- A **direção do id** estava errada: no NOWEB o `externalId` já *é* o bare, então derivar nunca produzia o composto que o webhook gravou. Precisa **construir**.
- A rede de caracterização existente pegou um defeito da própria correção: a remoção estava dentro do `try` do envio, e qualquer erro ali marcaria como `failed` uma mensagem **já entregue**. Agora tem `try/catch` próprio.

## Verificação

Sabotando a limpeza do eco, **2 testes ficam vermelhos**. `typecheck` 0 · `lint` 0 · `lint:channels` 0 · `test:unit` 0.

Uma linha sem cobertura possível (o `neq` da própria linha) está marcada **no código**, com o resultado da sabotagem escrito ao lado: sabotada, a suíte fica verde, porque o filtro de `sent_via` já a torna inalcançável. Fica porque impede o pior desfecho.

**Não medido, e declarado:** o `DELETE` contra banco real com RLS. A policy `messages_delete` existe e autoriza membro da org, mas isso é leitura de schema, não comportamento medido — o teste usa fake, que não tem RLS. O filtro de `organization_id` está explícito na query, que é o que a doutrina exige.

Medição e implementação: **@QAVivo**.

author: mstuart
body:
## What broke

CI on `master` has been failing on every Node.js version in the matrix (20/22/24), which is why the Dependabot merge daemon has been skipping every open Dependabot PR for weeks — the check on their target branch was already red before any bump landed.

Root cause (from `gh run view 30296696144 --log-failed`, run on the `development-dependencies` Dependabot branch but reproducing the same way against master's own code): `npm test` runs `xo && ava && tsd`. `xo`'s bundled `eslint-plugin-ava` now enforces the `ava/use-true-false` rule, which flags `test.js:119` (`t.is(await cache.get('boolean'), true)`) and fails the lint step with exit code 1.

This is unrelated to any specific dependency bump: this repo ships `.npmrc` with `package-lock=false`, so every fresh `npm install` re-resolves devDependencies to whatever currently satisfies their semver ranges on the registry, with no lockfile to pin them. A routine minor/patch release of `xo` (or its nested `eslint-plugin-ava`) was enough to start flagging pre-existing code in `test.js`, breaking CI on `master` itself with no code change required.

## Fix

Rewrite the flagged assertion to the rule-compliant form:

```diff
-t.is(await cache.get('boolean'), true);
+t.true(await cache.get('boolean'));
```

Same assertion, same test semantics, satisfies the lint rule.

## Verification

Ran `npm test` (`xo && ava && tsd`) locally against this branch on all three Node versions in the CI matrix:

- Node 20.20.2 — 21/21 tests pass
- Node 22.23.2 — 21/21 tests pass
- Node 24.13.0 — 21/21 tests pass

## Note (not fixed here, flagging for visibility)

The underlying reason CI can break on `master` with zero code changes is the unpinned `.npmrc: package-lock=false` setup — nothing pins devDependency versions, so tooling drift alone can turn green CI red again at any time (this run also hit a harder failure on Node 20 elsewhere in the matrix, an `eslint-plugin-unicorn` crash from a Node 22+-only `Set` method, which isn't reproducing right now due to registry state having moved on since). Didn't touch this since it's a bigger, deliberate-looking config choice and out of scope for a CI repair — flagging it as a follow-up worth a deliberate decision (e.g. committing a lockfile) rather than doing it unilaterally here.

body: ## Summary - recover LSP daemon startup when a long-lived host retains a removed Homebrew Cellar `process.execPath` - prefer the cached executable while it exists, then an existing absolute `process.argv0`, then PATH-resolved `node` - contain asynchronous child spawn failures and write them to `daemon.log` instead of crashing the host process - add deterministic regression coverage and document the launcher contract ## Root cause After Homebrew upgraded Node 26.5.0 to 26.5.1, an already-running Senpi process kept `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.5.0/bin/node` in `process.execPath`. The old binary was removed, and `spawn(process.execPath, ...)` emitted an unhandled `ENOENT` error event that terminated Senpi. ## Verification - failing-first focused regression: failed before the implementation with `resolveDaemonNodeExecutable is not a function` - `npm run typecheck` - `npx biome check src/ensure-daemon.ts test/ensure-daemon.test.ts` - `npm test` - 20 files, 143 tests - `npm run build` - `bun run test:senpi` - direct built-client QA: - missing `process.execPath` + normal launcher: real daemon request completed - missing executable + bare `argv0` + unusable PATH: parent survived, returned a typed failure, and logged the contained `ENOENT` - Senpi `runtime-package` QA: PASS with isolated HOME and cleanup - Codex `client-package` QA: PASS with isolated `CODEX_HOME` - OpenCode `client-package` QA: PASS with isolated XDG/HOME The package-wide Biome command still reports 14 pre-existing errors in untouched files; both changed TypeScript files pass focused Biome validation. ## Scope Only `packages/lsp-daemon/{AGENTS.md,src/ensure-daemon.ts,test/ensure-daemon.test.ts}` are included. Build-generated Codegraph drift was deliberately left unstaged. --- ## Summary by cubic Make the `lsp-daemon` launcher resilient to stale Node paths so long-lived hosts keep working after upgrades. Prevents crashes by selecting a valid Node binary and logging spawn errors to `daemon.log`. - **Bug Fixes** - Recovers from removed Homebrew Cellar Node by resolving the launcher in order: existing `process.execPath` → existing absolute `process.argv0` → PATH `node`. - Contains child spawn failures; logs errors to `daemon.log` and does not crash the parent. Ensures log FD is closed on spawn or error. - Adds unit tests for the resolver and startup flow. Documents the launcher contract in `AGENTS.md`. Written for commit 23f9658377ebd352658241a1dc1e8f91ff577a04. Summary will update on new commits.

# Vercel Speed Insights Installation Report

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Speed Insights for this static HTML website.

## What Was Implemented

### 1. Package Installation
- Created `package.json` with `@vercel/speed-insights` dependency (v1.0.12)
- Installed the package using npm
- Generated `package-lock.json` for dependency locking

### 2. Speed Insights Integration
Following the official Vercel documentation for static sites, I added the Speed Insights tracking script to all HTML pages:

**Files Modified:**
- `index.html` - Main landing page
- `admin.html` - Admin panel page
- `painel.html` - Dashboard page
- `validador.html` - Validator page

**Implementation Details:**
Each HTML file now includes the following script tags in the `<head>` section:

```html
<script>
  window.si = window.si || function () { (window.siq = window.siq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js"></script>
```

This implementation:
- Initializes the Speed Insights queue function (`window.si`)
- Loads the Vercel Speed Insights script asynchronously with `defer`
- Uses the Vercel-hosted script path `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`

### 3. Project Structure
- Created `.gitignore` to exclude `node_modules/`, development tools, and temporary files
- Extracted and organized project files from zip archives to proper structure
- Added `script.js` and `styles.css` to the root directory for the site

## Framework Detection
This is a **static HTML/vanilla JavaScript** website without a framework like Next.js, React, or Vue. The implementation follows the Vercel documentation's guidance for static sites.

## How It Works
Once deployed to Vercel with Speed Insights enabled in the dashboard:
1. Vercel automatically serves the script from `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`
2. The script tracks Core Web Vitals and other performance metrics
3. Data is sent to Vercel's Speed Insights dashboard
4. No tracking occurs in development mode (only in production)

## Next Steps
To complete the setup:
1. Deploy this site to Vercel
2. Enable Speed Insights in the Vercel dashboard for this project
3. After deployment, metrics will automatically start being collected
4. View performance data in the Speed Insights section of the Vercel dashboard

## Technical Notes
- The script is loaded with the `defer` attribute for optimal performance
- The queue function ensures no data is lost before the main script loads
- Speed Insights does NOT track data in development mode
- The implementation is minimal and follows best practices from the official documentation

## Files Changed
- **Created:** `.gitignore`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- **Modified:** `index.html`, `admin.html`, `painel.html`, `validador.html`
- **Added:** `script.js`, `styles.css` (extracted from archives)

body:
First of three batches from the over-engineering list.

## TeXLib appears in Settings → Apps → Installed apps

It was invisible to Windows' own uninstall list, so removing it meant remembering where a ZIP was extracted months ago. A per-user `Uninstall` key now carries name, version, location, icon and size — with `QuietUninstallString` wired to the one-click Uninstall in Settings, and **Modify mapped to `-Repair`**, which is exactly what that button should do.

The uninstaller removes the entry, and only its own: one recording a different install root is left alone.

## `install.bat -Verify`

Checks an install against a manifest written when it was made, reporting the three kinds of difference **separately**, because they mean different things:

- **missing** — the installer put it there and it's gone. Usually the interesting one.
- **changed** — edited settings live here, which is normal and expected. So does corruption.
- **added** — almost always the user's own work, so it's listed last and never called a problem.

Exit 0 when nothing is missing or changed, 22 otherwise.

TeX Live is excluded — 100k+ files that `tlmgr` legitimately rewrites, so both hashing it and flagging its changes would be noise. Reparse points are skipped rather than followed, so the library isn't hashed twice under two names via the `Packages\User` junction.

## `texlib.config.json`

Beside `install.bat`, presets any option — a lab deployment becomes "hand someone the folder" instead of a command line to retype and mistype.

**Anything passed on the command line always wins.** The file is applied only to options the caller did not name; silently overriding what someone typed would be a genuinely nasty surprise. Unknown keys are reported rather than ignored, malformed JSON warns instead of aborting, and the file is gitignored so a local one never ships.

## Testing

`config-artifacts` now also asserts the Installed Apps entry (including that Modify maps to `-Repair` and quiet-uninstall really invokes the uninstaller), that a manifest is written, that `-Verify` passes clean then catches one of each difference, and that config presets apply while an explicit `-TexLiveScheme` still beats them.

Verified locally against a seeded install end to end, including that the ARP key and the install root are both gone after uninstall.

One CI trap worth recording: `shell: pwsh` propagates `$LASTEXITCODE` at the end of a step, so the `-Verify` step failed *for passing* — its last child returns 22 by design. Third time that's bitten, so it's now written down in CONTRIBUTING next to the `2>&1`-on-native-commands one that made the Doctor report all 50 packages missing.

## Still to come

`-Report`, transactional rollback, release signing, and the dirty-machine matrix with the drive-root junction fallback.

IMPORTANT:
•⁠  ⁠PR must be opened from your personal branch → dev
•⁠  ⁠You must tag @Team-Deepiri/support-team
•⁠  ⁠You must update Plaky to "Needs QA"
•⁠  ⁠Never move a feature/bug to "Done" (Done = production release only)

---

## Description

Implements layer 2 (plan guard) and layer 3 (generation guard) of the guardrail system in the video generation workflow, per `docs/specs/guardrail-implementation.md`. Planner's shot list is checked before GPU compile and scans generated (t2i) keyframes before they're stored/persisted

---

## Changes

### Layer 1 — envelope fix (bug)

- **`redis_worker.py`**: `payload.get("guardrail_verdict")` no longer defaults to `"allow"`. A payload with no verdict now fails closed instead of being treated as approved. `guardrail_flags` (`PII_REDACTED` / `ESCALATED`) are logged but never block — only the verdict gates GPU work.

### Layer 2 — guardrail implementation (guards planned prompts during video generation)
- **`plan_guard.py`**: added `_shots_payload()`; the allow path now returns `details["shots"]` so tier downgrades survive the dict round-trip.
- **`⁠ guardrails/__init.py__ ⁠`**: exports ⁠ run_plan_gate ⁠ (layer 2 guardrail) on top of layer 0 and 1
- **`schemas/studio.py`**: added `PlanShotIn` and `PlanCheckRequest` models, sent from layer 2
- *`ai_jobs.py`**: new `POST /internal/guardrails/plan` — resolves the job, runs `run_plan_gate` with the project's policy, and logs the decision via the existing `_log_decision`
- **`plan_client.py` (new, model-workers)**: Layer 2 HTTP client.
- **`redis_worker.py`**: calls `check_plan` (Layer 2 / `run_plan_gate`) over HTTP to the orchestrator between `_plan_shots()` and `build()`, then applies the gate's tier decisions via the new `_apply_tier_adjustments()`. Added a `PlanBlocked` exception so a policy block reports a reason instead of a generic failure.

### Layer 3 — generation guard (checks generated keyframes)
- **`registry.py, loader.py, download_rfir_models.py`**: added `Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection` classification model
- **`runtime_guard.py`**: replaces stub with the classification model. Thresholds per `nsfw_mode`: `block` ≥ 0.7,
  `restricted` ≥ 0.9, `off` short-circuits without loading the model. Fail-closed on classifier error in prod; allow-with-warning in dev, mirroring `config._check_enabled()`.
- **`context.py`**: `ExecutionContext` gets `nsfw_mode` and `keyframe_check` fields
- **`engine.py`**: `_run_t2i_keyframe` checks each image generated before saving or persisting it, so a blocked frame never enters the arena or touches disk. The guard (from `runtime_guard.py`) is injected into `keyframe_check` in `redis_worker.py`.
- **`csfv_pipeline.py`**: added note - generated images from this pipeline doesn't run the check
- **`pyproject.toml`**: `transformers` declared explicitly 

- added new tests to `test_plan_guard.py, test_redis_worker.py, test_prompt_injection.py, test_redis_worker.py, test_runtime_guard.py, test_engine_keyframe_guard.py`
---

## Related

•⁠  ⁠Issue:
•⁠  ⁠Plaky:
•⁠  ⁠Related PRs (optional):

---

## Testing

Explain how you verified your changes and how to test your feature:
- all unit testing cases passed
- ran the layer 3 classifier model manually
```python
from PIL import Image; import io
from app.guardrails.runtime_guard import check_keyframe
buf = io.BytesIO(); Image.new('RGB', (512, 288), (90, 140, 200)).save(buf, format='PNG')
check_keyframe(buf.getvalue(), 'block')
```
Result: `verdict=ALLOW, score=0.00175` for a plain blue frame, confirms label lookup resolves correctly

Additional testing details:

---

## Important Notes (Optional)

•⁠  ⁠Known limitations:
- `nsfw_mode` is never written into job metadata, so _build_rfir_payload always resolves to the "block" default. 
- Only `t2i_keyframe` output is scanned. Tier C/D video frames come from `sparse_t2v_window`, which is unchecked
- `cfsv_pipeline` path doesn't run layer 3 (keyframe generation) check
- `Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection` strictly trained for normal/nsfw classification, gore/violence may not be detected
•⁠  ⁠Blockers:
•⁠  ⁠CI/CD issues unrelated to this PR:
•⁠  ⁠Dependencies required for testing: a running `redis_worker` for layer 2 HTTP round trip and `transformers` (now an explicit dependency)

## Workflow Checklist (Required)

author: jcnm
body:
## Problème
Les indicateurs de non-lus (badges de conversations, cloche de notifications, badge d'icône) ne se mettaient pas à jour de manière fiable, et l'ouverture d'une notification / conversation / story / post / réel ne marquait pas les notifications associées comme lues.

## Causes racines (diagnostic par 4 audits parallèles)

### Gateway
- La cascade « conversation lue → notifications lues » instanciait un `NotificationService` **sans `io`** : `notification:counts` n'était jamais émis après lecture. Elle était en plus court-circuitée par 4 early-returns (conversation vide, dédup TTL, receipt périmé, raccourci `unreadCount===0`) — une réaction/mention sur un message déjà lu restait non lue à vie.
- `notification:read` / `notification:deleted` : déclarés, typés, écoutés par le web ET iOS… jamais émis. Sync multi-appareils impossible.
- Deux prédicats « non lu » divergents (`isRead` vs `readAt`, ce dernier non indexé → collscan).
- `DELETE /notifications/read` appelé par le web matchait `DELETE /notifications/:id` avec `id=read` → 404 systématique.
- `broadcastReadStatus` (conversations/messages.ts) émettait `unreadCount: 0` en dur au lieu du reste réel.

### Web (la parité n'avait jamais été faite)
- `notification:counts` — le SEUL signal serveur de resync — était reçu puis **jeté**.
- Aucune surface n'appelait les routes de marquage par portée ; la page réel n'émettait rien du tout.
- Pas de garde « conversation active » sur `conversation:unread-updated` → badge allumé sur la conversation en cours de lecture.
- La conversation d'accueil n'était **jamais** marquée lue (compteur monotone croissant).
- Aucun indicateur « nouveaux messages » dans la vue conversation.

### iOS (5 trous restants après le chantier de juillet)
- Le viewer de réels n'appelait jamais `onPostOpened` ; la sheet de commentaires feed/réels non plus.
- `guard showReadReceipts` bloquait l'avancée du curseur serveur → badge fantôme multi-appareils/icône.
- Quick-action push et widget ne posaient pas la frontière locale GRDB ni ne consommaient les notifications.
- Le badge d'icône/widget appliquait le compteur serveur brut, y compris pour la conversation affichée.

## Correctifs
- **83b8424fc** gateway : registre de service partagé (câblé io), cascade indépendante du curseur (+ dédup propre), émission `notification:read`/`deleted`, prédicat `isRead` partout, route `DELETE /notifications/read`, recompte réel du badge.
- **acf9fadb6** web : `notification:counts`/`deleted` câblés, module `notification-read-sync` (miroir du NotificationCachePatch iOS — patch cache RQ + routes de portée coalescées 5 s) branché sur conversation/accueil/post/réel/story, garde conversation active + reset optimiste, `useSeenMessages` sur l'accueil, pastille « nouveaux messages » sur le bouton scroll, dérive du décrément corrigée, miroir `markConsumedOnArrival`.
- **3e341101c** iOS : réels + commentaires consomment leurs notifications, retrait du guard receipts, quick-actions complètes (nouvelle API SDK `onConversationMarkedRead`), gate du badge d'icône sur la conversation ouverte.

## Vérifications
- Gateway : 578 suites / 15 262 tests (bun) + `tsc --noEmit` propre
- Web : 499 suites / 11 636 tests (bun)
- iOS : `meeshy.sh build` vert (90 s) + `NotificationCoordinatorTests` 35/35 sur simulateur
- Aucune nouvelle erreur tsc web sur les fichiers modifiés (échecs listés préexistants)
