author: joacominatel
body:
Closes #1198. Implements the **server side of [ADR-0093](../blob/dev/docs/03-decisions/0093-chassis-routing-and-asset-adoption.md)** — the ADR is the spec; nothing here re-litigates it. The frontend wave consumes this contract.

## What shipped, by ADR section

**§2 — `InfraNode.chassis`, agent-owned.** Additive nullable `String?` (deliberately *not* a Prisma enum: the wire vocabulary `.catch()`es an unrecognised value so a report is never rejected for one, and a DB enum would turn that same value into a write error on the hot report path). Written from `host.chassis` on **every** report — the ordinary create, the ordinary refresh, and the #1141 colliding-clone create. No `chassisSource`, no `MANUAL` counterpart: chassis is never on a DTO, so there is no human write to protect. Two rules the ADR implies and the tests pin:

- an **absent** chassis never clears a stored one — a downgraded or pre-v2 agent must not un-heal the estate;
- an explicit **`unknown` does** write, because "the probe did not run" is a different fact from any form factor, and refusing it would leave a re-imaged box hidden on the strength of a stale `laptop`.

A CONTAINER child never gets one — its blob carries no `host` key at all (#1139). The column rides on the **list row** (`InfraNodeListItemSchema` only omits `specs`, #1135), which is what lets the canvas filter endpoints client-side with no second request.

**§3 / §3a — adoption at the confirm gate.** On the `trackAsAsset && !node.assetId` branch: sanitized serial → corroboration gate → **one indexed `assets_serial_active_key` probe** → adopt or mint. `findIdentityMatches` is **not** called on this path and there is a test asserting so — it asks a different question (which *nodes* look alike) over an un-indexed jsonb containment scan, on the wrong side of the join. Corroboration is a pure shared function, `corroboratesAdoption(specs, serial)`: the sanitized serial must appear in the host's own `hostIdentityEvidence` (compared canonically, so vendor padding cannot split one machine into two answers), **at least one MAC** must survive `sanitizeIdentifierValue`, and the node must not carry `specs.identityConflict`. It **fails closed** — every miss mints, which is recoverable by hand where a mis-link is not.

**§4 — the marker and the audit trail.** `INFRA_AUTO_ASSET_MARKER` is stamped on the **mint branch only, never on adopt**. This is the load-bearing safety rule: `detachAsset` soft-deletes an asset carrying the marker, so stamping it on an adopted row would mean a later detach silently deleted the operator's curated inventory. Two tests guard it — one that the adopt branch writes nothing to the asset at all, and one end-to-end that **detaching an adopted asset leaves it intact**, which is exactly what the #1117 error message already promises. `AssetHistoryEventType.AGENT_LINKED` is emitted **once**, at the link, payload `{ nodeId, reportingSource, externalId }`; best-effort, so a failed audit write never fails a confirm (on the auto-confirm path it would fail a *report*). No per-report event: `syncAssetSpecs` stays `specs`-only, change-gated, silent.

**§5 / §7 / §8.5 — the read contract wave 2 needs.** Two display-only, per-read, `.nullish()` fields on `InfraNodeDetailSchema`, on the ADR-0090 `ipConflict` mold — never gates:

- `assetCandidate: { id, name, serial } | null` — the asset a confirm **would adopt**, so the tray says *"will link Dell-XPS-7490 (existing)"* rather than *"will create"*. Answered only for a node that is **PENDING and unlinked** (the one state where a confirm can still adopt), and only when §3a passes — so a populated field is a promise the confirm keeps. It runs the *same* helper the confirm runs, so hint and action cannot drift.
- `duplicateAssetSuspicion: { id, name, serial } | null` — §8.5, for installs that already duplicated: the linked asset is `_infraAutoCreated`, carries a **null** serial, and this node's reported serial belongs to a **different** live asset. Surfaced, **never** auto-merged, never retroactively re-linked; the remedy stays the deliberate §7 two-step.

The two are **mutually exclusive by construction**, so a drill-in costs at most **one** extra indexed lookup, never two. Plus `isEndpointChassis` / `ENDPOINT_CHASSIS` in `@lazyit/shared` — the pure mapper §1 asks for; **no signal is never an endpoint**, so routing can only ever remove noise a positive fact identified.

**§6 — chassis as an auto-confirm rule condition.** `chassis` joins `RULE_CONDITION_KEYS`, `InfraAutoConfirmRule`, the writable shape (strict on write: a typo is a clean 400) and `InfraAutoConfirmCandidate`. The existing contract is untouched: conditions still **AND**, first match still wins, and a rule stating only `chassis` satisfies `statesAutoConfirmCondition` on the same footing `reportedKind` does. A report with **no chassis or `unknown` never matches** a rule that states one — the same conservatism the subnet condition already applies.

## Explicitly unchanged, each with a guarding test

The #1117 re-point `400` · `modelId` null on mint and untouched on adopt · **no `Asset.serial` write-back** on adopt · `trackAsAsset` still a boolean on a `strictObject` · `syncAssetSpecs` still `specs`-only, change-gated, no per-report `SPECS_CHANGED` · the #1081 collision retry, which survives **as a race backstop** rather than the designed path (under §3 a serial that would collide is a serial that corroborates, and a corroborating serial adopts).

## Upgrade behavior (workflow rule #8)

Migration `20260803000000_chassis_routing_and_asset_adoption` — **additive only**, `prisma migrate deploy`-safe on a populated production database:

```sql
ALTER TYPE "AssetHistoryEventType" ADD VALUE 'AGENT_LINKED';
ALTER TABLE "infra_nodes"              ADD COLUMN "chassis" TEXT;
ALTER TABLE "infra_auto_confirm_rules" ADD COLUMN "chassis" TEXT;
```

No drop, no `NOT NULL`, no default, no backfill, no data touched. `ADD VALUE` **appends** — it never rewrites the type or the table, so it is O(1) on a populated `asset_history`, and it is transaction-safe on PG 12+ (compose pins 18) because the value is not *used* in the same migration. The [`ACKNOWLEDGED` precedent](../blob/dev/apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260718130000_asset_assignment_acknowledgement/migration.sql). What an operator sees, in order:

1. **Nothing moves at migration time.** Every existing node reads `chassis = NULL` = no signal = today's behaviour. Every existing rule reads "tests no chassis", so no rule changes behaviour.
2. **The estate self-heals within one report cadence** — each agent writes its own chassis on its next check-in. No backfill script, no maintenance window (the #1153 lazy-fill posture). Manual nodes and container children stay null forever, correctly.
3. **Then the map gets smaller**, as endpoints acquire a chassis and drop off the canvas — one click to undo, nothing left the CMDB. *(Wave 2 lands the toggle; this PR only supplies the fact.)*
4. **Adoption is enforce-only-on-write.** It changes what a *future* confirm does; already-confirmed nodes are **never** re-linked retroactively, and existing duplicates are surfaced, never merged.

Read-tolerance is end-to-end: `AgentChassisSchema.nullish().catch(null)` on the node read and on the stored rule condition, so a row predating the column, and a value a future collector invents, both degrade to "no signal" instead of failing a payload. `corroboratesAdoption` reads its `unknown` blob defensively for the same reason — a hand-edited `specs` must never throw on a confirm.

## What wave 2 (frontend) gets from this

- `InfraNode.chassis` on **both** the list row and the drill-in, plus `isEndpointChassis(chassis)` / `ENDPOINT_CHASSIS` from `@lazyit/shared` — everything the canvas needs to hide `{ laptop, desktop }` by default and show a hidden count, client-side, with no second request. (§5's *Show endpoints* toggle, the tray-row and drill-in chassis display.)
- `InfraNodeDetail.assetCandidate` — `{ id, name, s

author: an9xyz
body:
## Summary

`GET /v1/robot/space_bots?space_id=` was mounted with `AuthMiddleware` only. The handler reads `space_id` straight from the query string and runs its SQL with no membership check anywhere in the path, so **any authenticated user could pass an arbitrary `space_id` and receive that Space's complete bot roster** — `uid`, `name`, `description`, `creator_uid`, `creator_name`, `bot_commands`, `auto_approve`.

That is a cross-tenant read, the P0 class named in this repo's `space-isolation` rule. The tell was that the sibling roster endpoint `GET /v1/space/:space_id/members` has always checked membership via `queryMember` — two readers of the same `space_member` table enforcing different isolation strength.

Deliberately kept as its own PR rather than riding along with the directory endpoint that replaces this API: a gate on a shipped endpoint with five octo-web call sites plus the mobile app should not be timeline-coupled to an additive feature, and should stay independently revertable.

## Related Issue

None — found during an octo-web contacts API usage audit.

## Linked Spec

`.octospec/tasks/robot-space-bots-space-isolation/brief.md`

## Changes

- `space_bots` moves out of the shared `auth` group into its own group carrying `AuthMiddleware` → `SharedUIDRateLimiter` → `SpaceMiddleware`. The middleware already resolves `space_id` from the query string, which is exactly how this endpoint receives it, so neither the handler nor the response shape changes.
- Rate limiter added because this is an enumerable list endpoint that until now had only the global per-IP floor.
- New `modules/robot/api_space_bots_isolation_test.go` — the only pre-existing test naming this endpoint is `t.Skip`ped.

**No change** to the handler body, its SQL, ordering, field set, `status` derivation, or `botfather` exclusion.

## Testing

`go test ./modules/robot/` — passes on a clean database (MySQL 8.0.46 + Redis + WuKongIM v2.2.4). `golangci-lint run ./modules/robot/...` clean. `make i18n-extract-check` and `make i18n-lint` pass.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manually verified

Coverage:

1. **Non-member refused** — asserts the status **and** that neither the bot's uid nor its description appears in the body. A 403 that still ships the roster is equally a leak.
2. **Member unaffected** — every field the clients read is still present, `status` still derives `not_added`.
3. **Removed member loses access.**
4. **Missing `space_id`** still gets the handler's own parameter error rather than a middleware 403, pinning the middleware's opt-in passthrough — plus a variant carrying `X-Space-Id`, since octo-web's `APIClient` injects that header on every request and the bare-request shape is one real clients never send.

Tests use `testutil.NewTestServer` rather than the robot package's local `newTestServer`, which does not run migrations — that is why the pre-existing `TestSpaceBots_ExcludesDeletedSpaceMembers` is skipped. It stays skipped; these stand on their own.

## COMPREHENSION

**1. What does this change actually do to the load-bearing path?**

It inserts a membership precondition in front of a handler that previously had none, on a route that returns an entire Space's bot roster. `SpaceMiddleware` resolves `space_id` from the same `c.Query("space_id")` the handler reads — same `queryCache` on the same embedded `*gin.Context` — so there is no split-brain where the middleware validates Space A while the handler queries Space B. Duplicate query params, percent-encoded keys, and semicolon separators all resolve identically on both sides for that reason.

**2. What could break because of it (dependents + failure mode)?**

Five octo-web call sites (contacts AI tab ×2, BotStore, PersonaSettings, docs bot-name backfill) and the mobile app. All of them already pass the caller's *current* Space, so all remain members and are unaffected.

Two real behaviour deltas, both recorded in the brief rather than left to surface in production:

- **Disbanded Space.** `CheckMembership` additionally requires `space.status = 1`, which the handler never checked. A member of a disbanded Space goes from 200 + bot list to 403. Correct tightening, but it *is* a change for a legitimate caller.
- **429.** The endpoint now draws on the shared per-UID bucket (2 rps / burst 60, process-wide across routes). A cold web start that fans out to several bot-reading endpoints at once could touch it.

Fail-open analysis: on Redis error the cache reports a miss and falls through to the DB; on DB error the middleware aborts 500. Neither path admits the request. The rate limiter *is* fail-open on Redis errors, but it sits before `SpaceMiddleware`, so failing open there means "not throttled", not "not authorized".

**3. How do you know it works (specific test/repro/trace)?**

The three security assertions genuinely fail if the fix is reverted: without `SpaceMiddleware` a non-member gets 200 plus `sb_iso_bot`, and the removed-member case still returns 200 with one row because the handler's `sm.status=1` filters bots, not the caller. Membership cache is cleared before each request so no case passes on a stale verdict, and the UID bucket is reset so a parallel package draining it cannot turn a security assertion into a false 429.

**Known gap, scoped out and tracked:** `SpaceMiddleware` caches a positive verdict for 60s and `InvalidateMembershipCache` has **no production caller anywhere in the repo** — member removal fires `event.SpaceMemberCacheInvalidator`, which targets an unrelated in-process cache in `modules/notify`. So a removed user retains access for up to 60s if they touched any gated route just before removal. `TestSpaceBots_RemovedMemberLosesAccess` clears the cache by hand, so it proves the verdict flips once cleared, **not** that production clears it. Pre-existing gap in shared middleware; tracked in `.octospec/tasks/space-membership-cache-revocation/brief.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] PR description is in English
- [x] Added tests for my changes
- [x] Updated documentation — brief records the swagger acceptance item as deliberately not done: `modules/robot/swagger/api.yaml` has no `space_bots` entry at all, and authoring fresh docs for an endpoint being deprecated cuts against freezing it
- [x] Followed commit message conventions (Conventional Commits)

Reverts #37's Wed/Thu swap back to the #36 arrangement, then removes strides from Thursday.

| Day | After #37 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Tue Aug 4 | 3.5 mi · Easy aerobic | 3.5 mi · Easy aerobic *(unchanged)* |
| Wed Aug 5 | 4.5 mi · Easy + strides (5) | **4 mi · Easy + strides (4)** |
| Thu Aug 6 | 4 mi · Easy + strides (4) | **4.5 mi · Easy aerobic** |

Midweek reads 3.5 → 4 → 4.5 again. Volume untouched: midweek 12, week 21, all 17 weekly totals recomputed and asserted identical.

Thursday is stripped of strides in all three places they lived, not just the pace field: `type` goes `Easy + strides` → `Easy aerobic`, `pace` drops its ` + 5 strides` suffix, and the focus opens `"Easy aerobic."` instead of prescribing 5 × 20s. Asserted afterwards that the word "stride" appears nowhere in that day's type, pace or focus. The half-mile rationale on that day is preserved.

## One text repair

Wednesday inherits the 4-mile stride workout, whose focus read *"This is the added second stride day that brings strides to 2x/week."* With Thursday's strides gone that's false — it's now the only one — so it reads **"This is the week's stride day."** Nothing else in that string changed.

## On the twice-weekly strides rule

`meta.tibRules[3]` says *"Strides run twice weekly throughout."* This drops week 5 from two stride days to one, so it's worth being explicit that the rule is already aspirational rather than descriptive:

| Stride days | Weeks |
|---|---|
| 2 | 5, 7, 8, 11, 13 |
| 1 | 1, 4, 6, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17 |
| 0 | 2, 3, 9 |

Only 5 of 17 weeks currently run twice-weekly strides. After this change week 5 joins the nine weeks at one, which is the plan's actual majority behaviour — so this isn't introducing a new inconsistency so much as joining an existing one. The same *"added second stride day that brings strides to 2x/week"* boilerplate also sits in weeks 4, 6, 12 and 14, where it's already inaccurate for the same reason. I've only corrected week 5, since that's the week this change touches; happy to reconcile the rule text and the other four weeks plan-wide as a separate change if you want them consistent.

## Verified

- `meta` asserted unchanged; every week other than 5 asserted byte-identical; week 5's label and its Mon/Tue/Fri/Sat/Sun asserted byte-identical.
- `kind`, `hr`, `dow`, `date` asserted unchanged on both edited days.

body:
Two badge fixes on the Inbox Resolved tab:

**Root cause 1 — 'Demo Payment Agent' instead of 'Collections Agent'**

brain-core's `proposing_agent` in `proposal.decided` audit snapshots is the *execution* agent ULID (e.g. `agent_01KZ...`), whose registry `display_name` is the generic `"Demo Payment Agent"` — not the functional analysis agent type (`"collections"`). The only reliable source of the type key is the live proposal's `p.type` **before** the decision is made.

Fix: module-level session cache in `brainAudit.ts`. The `needsReviewProposals` loop calls `registerProposalAgentKey(p.id, agentKey)` for each visible proposal. When `mapAuditEventToRecord` processes the resulting audit event, `cachedProposalAgentKey(proposalId)` retrieves `"collections"` and stores it as `proposingAgent`. `proposingAgentDisplay` is only populated on a cache miss (historical records from a previous session). Badge priority: type-key `proposingAgent` → resolved display name → raw ULID.

**Root cause 2 — 'Cash Forecasting' without 'Agent' suffix**

`acknowledgedRecords` loop used `r.agentLabel` directly as the tag; the `agentLabel` from LiveInsight is the bare badge string (`"Cash Forecasting"`) with no `" Agent"` suffix.

Fix: tag now calls `agentBadgeLabel(r.agentLabel)` which appends `" Agent"` via the display-name lookup or best-effort capitalisation fallback.

author: acgeners
body:
## Por que

Entre 31/07 e 03/08 a satoria ficou no ar respondendo **HTTP 200** enquanto **toda** leitura do banco falhava com `Invalid API key` (o `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` da Fly não valia para o projeto vivo). Passou três dias despercebido porque o smoke da época testava `/sobre` e `/` — as duas únicas rotas que **não tocam o banco**.

## O que muda

**`GET /api/health`** faz uma query real e responde de acordo com ela:

- `count: "exact", head: true` → devolve o número no header e **zero bytes de corpo**, então monitorar de 6 em 6h não pesa na quota de egress (5 GB/ciclo no free).
- **Catálogo vazio = 503.** Query que "funciona" e volta 0 é o sintoma de credencial trocada ou banco errado. Um health que aceita 0 como saudável repete o bug que ele existe para pegar.
- A mensagem crua do PostgREST fica no log do servidor, não na resposta — o endpoint e o repo são públicos.

⚠️ **Por que a página normal não serve de monitor:** com Suspense, o Next escreve o `200` no shell e só falha depois, durante o streaming. A página quebrada responde 200 exatamente como a saudável. Aqui a resposta só é montada depois da query.

**Workflow agendado** a cada 6h + `workflow_dispatch`. Roda no GitHub em vez de launchd para vigiar mesmo com o Mac desligado; repo público ⇒ sem cota de Actions, e **sem nenhum segredo** (só chama URL pública). A cada 6h de propósito: cada chamada acorda a máquina da Fly, que dorme por padrão — de minuto em minuto ela nunca dormiria e passaria a custar.

## Verificação

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 erros
- `npm run test`: 1888 passando (4 novos)
- Rota testada no app rodando: `{"ok":true,"works":971,"ms":42}` em 31 bytes
- Testes cobrem os **dois ramos de falha** (erro do PostgREST e catálogo vazio) e o não-vazamento da mensagem crua — o caminho feliz sozinho não provaria nada, já que o monitor antigo também passava

## Summary

#68(optn5 미기재 → 크롤 전면 동결)과 동일한 클래스의 잠재 결함을 예방한다. `toAnnouncementType`은 `optn2`(공공/민간 코드)가 `'1'`/`'2'` 외 값이면 **null 포함** throw하므로, 같은 오입력이 이 필드에서 발생하면 목록 전체 파싱 중단 → 파이프라인 동결이 재발한다. PR #69와 대칭인 제목 폴백을 추가한다.

Closes #71

## 주요 변경 사항

### 1. `parseListJson.toAnnouncementType` 제목 폴백

- `optn2`가 `null`/빈 문자열이면 `parseDetailPage`와 동일한 제목 휴리스틱으로 폴백: `'공공임대'` 포함 → `public`, 아니면 `private`
- `'1'`/`'2'`는 기존대로 코드 우선. 미기재가 아닌 미지의 코드(`'9'` 등)는 기존대로 throw 유지 — 분류 체계 변경을 카나리가 계속 감지하도록 경계 보존
- PR #69(optn5 폴백)와 완전히 대칭인 구조

### 2. 테스트 3건 추가

- `optn2: null` + `'[공공임대]'` 제목 → `public`
- `optn2: null` + 공공임대 미포함 제목 → `private`
- 빈 문자열(`'  '`)도 폴백 경로를 태움

## 참고 사항

- 잠재 결함 예방(미발현) — 관측된 사고는 #68 참고
- 이 사이트 공고 제목은 `[공공임대]`/`[민간임대]` 접두가 관행이라 폴백 신뢰도 높음

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Audited error handling across the three JS files and fixed spots where errors were silently swallowed or hidden behind opaque failures.

**app.js**
- `fetchJSONP`: now throws on non-2xx responses (`if(!res.ok) throw ...`) instead of trying to parse an error page body, and error messages include the URL. Previously an HTTP 500/404 would surface as a confusing "返回格式异常".
- Terrain-fallback empty catch → logs. The nested fallback `try{ viewer.terrainProvider = new EllipsoidTerrainProvider() }catch(e){}` swallowed everything; now `console.error`s so a failed fallback is diagnosable.
- Per-typhoon detail fetch: `.catch(()=>null)` → `.catch(err=>{ console.warn(...id...); return null; })`. Still skips the failed typhoon (intended), but the failure is now logged with the typhoon id/name instead of vanishing.
- URL-param IIFE empty catch (`catch(e){}`) → `console.warn`. Bad `?lon=/lat=/base=` params were silently ignored with no trace.
- HDR try/catch: keeps the `highDynamicRange=false` fallback but adds a `console.warn`.

**wind-layer.js**
- `loadSample()` now checks `r.ok` before `r.json()`, so a missing/404 `wind-sample.json` throws a clear error (propagated to the existing `loadWind` catch that sets the "风场数据加载失败" status) instead of an opaque JSON parse error.

**scripts/generate-typhoon-svg.js** (runs in the every-3h GitHub Action)
- `fetchJSONP`: added `res.ok` check (same as app.js).
- Per-typhoon loop `catch(e){ /* 跳过 */ }` → `console.warn` with id/reason, and empty/no-path cases now log why they were skipped.
- New hard-fail guard: if there were selected typhoons but **all** of them failed, `throw` so `main().catch` exits non-zero. Previously the Action would silently generate an empty/stale SVG and commit it, masking an upstream outage. The genuine "no active typhoons" case (empty `chosen`) still renders normally.

No behavioral change to the happy path; these only affect what happens on failures (logging + propagation).

author: shamish
body:
## Problem

With `ExtraAttack_Warmagic;WarMagic`, the cantrip-for-attack swap works once per **turn** instead of once per **Attack action**. A Bladesinger who spends Action Surge (or is hasted) gets a second Attack action, but the free cantrip variant is no longer offered.

`WAR_MAGIC_BLOCK` had no `RemoveConditions`/`RemoveEvents`, so after `WarMagic` applied it the flag simply ran out its one-turn duration. Inside a single Attack action that is exactly the intent — one cantrip replaces one attack — but on the second Attack action the block is still up and the

```
IF(not HasStatus('WAR_MAGIC_BLOCK', context.Source) and HasPassive('WarMagic', context.Source)):
  UnlockSpellVariant(IsCantrip(), ...)
```

branch of `EXTRA_ATTACK` never fires. The 2024 rules bind the swap to the Attack action, not to the turn.

## Fix

Clear the block on the first weapon attack that actually spends an Action, which is what starts a new Attack action:

```
data "RemoveConditions" "ExtraAttackSpellCheck() and HasUseCosts('ActionPoint',false,context.Target) and not IsOffHandAttack()"
data "RemoveEvents" "OnSpellCast"
```

That predicate is not new — it is verbatim how vanilla `EXTRA_ATTACK` removes itself (`Shared.pak` → `Public/Shared/Stats/Generated/Data/Status_BOOST.txt`), on the same `OnSpellCast` event.

`WAR_MAGIC_BLOCK` is declared from scratch with no `using`, so nothing inherited by `ExtraAttack_Warmagic` / `ExtraAttack_Warmagic_2` is touched — the `StatsFunctors` chain that drives `EXTRA_ATTACK_Q` → `EXTRA_ATTACK` for all seven subclasses stays as it is.

## Why not `INITIAL_ATTACK_TECHNICAL`

It looks like the natural "new Attack action" marker, but vanilla `CombatStartAttack` gates it behind `not TurnBased(context.Source)` — it only exists for an attack begun outside turn-based mode. In combat it is never applied, and the `OnStatusRemoved` branch of `ExtraAttack.Conditions` never runs.

## Testing

Built and played with Bladesinger 6 + Action Surge: the free cantrip variant is offered again in the second Attack action, and remains limited to one cantrip per Attack action. Behaviour across turns is unchanged.

Scope is one status entry, two added lines; no other subclass or passive is affected.

# Implementação de testes E2E com pytest-playwright

## Descrição

Este Pull Request adiciona uma suíte de testes End-to-End (E2E) utilizando **pytest-playwright** para validar o comportamento do formulário de cadastro de lotes em um navegador real (Chromium).

Além dos testes unitários existentes com `MagicMock`, esta implementação garante que o **Page Object** funciona corretamente quando integrado à interface HTML, aumentando a confiabilidade da automação e cobrindo cenários reais de uso.

- Configurado o pipeline de CI para executar os testes E2E em um job separado após os testes unitários.
- Adicionado upload automático de screenshots como artefatos do GitHub Actions.

- [x] Carregamento da página com título correto.
- [x] Preenchimento do número do lote.

## Como testar

Instalar as dependências:

```bash
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

```

Executar apenas os testes E2E:

```bash
pytest tests/e2e/ -v
```

Ou visualizar a execução no navegador:

```bash
pytest tests/e2e/ -v --headed
```

- Todos os **8 testes E2E** executando com sucesso.

author: uphy
body:
## 症状

設計文書だけの PR を作り、実装を「別 PR」と称して先送りできてしまう。実際 #37 がそうなった。
このルールはどこにも書かれておらず、hook も止めなかった。

## 原因

`docs/development-process.md` 2.11（PR 戦略）にも CLAUDE.md にも、設計と実装の関係が書かれていない。
2.5 のサイクル（設計 → レビュー → 実装 → テスト）が 1 PR に収まる前提は暗黙だった。
`pr:status` は CI が緑なら `GREEN` を返すので、文書だけの PR も「フロー完了」に見える。

## 修正

**ルールの明文化**

- CLAUDE.md の worktree + PR フローに「設計と実装は同じ PR」を追加
- `docs/development-process.md` 2.11 に「1 PR = 1 サイクル」と、分けたときに何が壊れるかを記述。
  設計段階で Go/No-Go を仰ぐなら **commit する前に会話で聞く**（commit がフローの起点）

**hook による強制**

- `mise run pr:status` に `DESIGN_ONLY` を追加。`GREEN` を返す直前に判定する
- `.claude/hooks/pr-flow-guard.sh` が `DESIGN_ONLY` でターンを止め、同じ PR に実装するよう案内する

**判定（`.mise/tasks/pr/_design_only.sh`）**

誤検知を避けるため狭く取った。

| 条件 | 判定 |
|---|---|
| `docs/design/NN-*.md` が**新規追加**（git status `A`）で、実装パスの変更が 0 | DESIGN_ONLY |
| 既存の設計文書を編集しただけ（追補・撤回） | 対象外 |
| 実装パス（`Kikimi/` `KikimiTests/` `web/` `tools/` `.mise/` `.claude/` `.github/` `.githooks/` `Package.swift` `project.yml`）を触っている | 対象外 |

脱出口は `KIKIMI_ALLOW_DESIGN_ONLY_PR=1`（単独の設計文書が成果物のとき。理由を PR 本文に書く）。

## 変更ファイル

| ファイル | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `.mise/tasks/pr/_design_only.sh` | 新規。判定本体 |
| `.mise/tasks/pr/status` | `DESIGN_ONLY` を追加 |
| `.claude/hooks/pr-flow-guard.sh` | `DESIGN_ONLY` の案内文 |
| `.mise/tasks/test/hooks` | 新状態 + 判定 6 ケースを検証（38 checks passed） |
| `CLAUDE.md` | フローと hook 表に追記 |
| `docs/development-process.md` | 2.5 / 2.11 / 2.12 |

## 確認

- `mise run test:hooks` — 38 checks passed
- #37 の worktree で `_design_only.sh` を実行 → `docs/design/49-dictation-hud-slim.md` を検出（exit 0）。
  この PR がマージされれば #37 は緑でも止まる（狙いどおり）

UI に触れる変更はないので動作確認は不要。#37 には設計に対応する実装をこれから積む。

author: manderso90
body:
## What this adds

A clean, product-real **entry screen for Docside** at `/intro` that a first-time real estate agent can read in a few seconds and infer the whole shape of the product:

- Docside can help with a **single offer**
- Docside can help with a **multiple-offer comparison**
- The workflow **begins by uploading purchase agreement documents**

It doubles as the static capture source for **First Look Screen 2** (the first-impression test), replacing the build-time "capture pending" stand-in.

## Changes

- **`src/app/intro/page.tsx`** — a standalone product surface, deliberately *outside* the First Look flow guard (no `requireStage`), so it renders freely as both a prototype entry point and a screenshot source. Chrome mirrors the founder's reference (`design-reference/comparison-view-mockup-v3.html`): a 56px Deep Ocean rail + slim wordmark top bar, so it reads as genuine software rather than a marketing page. No functional navigation is implied.
- **`src/app/intro/entry.tsx`** *(client)* — headline "What would you like to review?" + subheadline; two large selectable cards (**Single Offer** / **Multiple Offer Comparison**) side-by-side on desktop, stacked on mobile; tasteful selected treatment (Deep Ocean ring + check). Selecting a card reveals a restrained drag-and-drop upload area whose copy swaps to reflect one document set vs. two or more, ending in `Accepted file types: PDF, DOCX`. Nothing posts to a backend — this is a prototype/capture surface.
- **`scripts/capture-intro.mjs`** — regenerates the Screen 2 asset from the live route in the most informative state (Multiple Offer Comparison selected, upload area visible), at a 16:10 canvas so nothing is cropped by Screen 2's `object-cover object-top` frame.
- **`public/docside-intro-capture.png`** — the generated 3200×2000 (16:10) capture, consumed by `src/app/first-impression/page.tsx`.

## Design & language

- Reuses the existing `@theme` tokens (`deep-ocean`, `paper`, `surface`, `ink`, radii, `shadow-card`) and IBM Plex type — **no new dependencies**.
- Copy stays in the inherited register — *review / verify / compare / source document* — and deliberately avoids promotional language ("best offer", "instant insights", etc.).

## Regenerating the capture

The main Docside app repo isn't part of this shell repo, so the asset is produced here from the `/intro` route:

```
pnpm build && PORT=3111 pnpm start        # serve the app
node scripts/capture-intro.mjs            # writes public/docside-intro-capture.png
```

(In this cloud env, Playwright's browser is pre-provisioned; the global `playwright` package resolves via a `node_modules` symlink. Locally, `pnpm add -D playwright` works.)

## Verification

- `pnpm tsc` — clean
- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm build` — succeeds; `/intro` prerenders as static (1.82 kB)
- Capture visually verified in the target state; lands at the exact path Screen 2 reads.

author: wanderlast
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-100930

cc @smottal

## What Is Being Fixed

`anonymize.spec.ts` › `Can delete and anonymize all entries` was flaky, failing 6 of 10 local runs. It timed out waiting for "You have successfully anonymized all remaining data." with the browser already back on the home page.

`completed_data_erasure.jsp` renders that message and, in the same response, opens a confirm whose `onConfirm` calls `Liferay.Util.navigate` on the delete-user URL. Because the test registered a blanket `page.on('dialog', ...)` auto-accept, the confirm was accepted with no delay, so the navigation destroyed the message while the assertion was still polling for it. The assertion was racing the test's own dialog handler.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The dialog handler now dismisses the erasure-complete confirm the first time it appears instead of accepting it. Dismissing runs `onConfirm(false)`, so no navigation happens and the page stays on `completed_data_erasure` with the message rendered — measured stable for 12 seconds, versus a race previously lost 60% of the time. The message is asserted there, then `page.reload()` re-renders the JSP and re-fires the confirm, which the handler accepts so the user deletion and the remaining assertions proceed unchanged.

## Why Are There No Tests?

The change is confined to an existing Playwright test and is itself test code, so it adds no separate coverage. It was verified by 10 consecutive passing runs of the fixed test (previously 4 of 10), and the restored assertion was mutation-checked: pointing it at deliberately wrong text makes the test fail, confirming it is not vacuously satisfied. The full `anonymize.spec.ts` was also run 3x; its one other failure, `@LPD-32063`, fails identically on a clean baseline and is unrelated.

## PR Check

**pr-check: PASS** — tested on `ed53b1de202230e64d7bcdb263ba98291bbe4fcd`

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Source Format | PASS |

author: connor5190
body:
Publishes the daily scan as a page with a checkbox per role. Ticking one moves it into an **Applied** section at the bottom; unticking puts it back.

**Live at** https://connor5190.github.io/internshipTracker/ once this merges and the workflow runs.

## What's here

- `site/index.html` — the board. Search box, the same today / this-week / still-open buckets and age chips as the email, light + dark, mobile-first.
- `scripts/build_site.py` — turns the enriched scan into `site/roles.json`. Reuses `format_recap._buckets`, so the email and the board can't drift on what counts as an active role.
- `daily-recap.yml` — builds and deploys `site/` via `actions/deploy-pages` after the email goes out.

## Applied state

No sign-in — ticking a box from a phone shouldn't need a login. State lives in a Firebase Realtime Database over its plain REST API: no SDK to version-pin, one URL of config, live sync via RTDB's `EventSource` stream so a tick on a phone lands on an open laptop tab.

Roles are keyed by a hash of the posting URL (the ledger's key), so ticks survive a re-scan. Each tick stores its own title/company/URL, so a posting that later comes down still reads as *no longer listed* in your history instead of vanishing.

## Before it syncs

`site/config.js` ships blank — the board falls back to `localStorage` and shows a banner. Fill in a Firebase Realtime DB URL (steps in the README) to turn on sharing.

## Verified

Rendering, checkbox → Applied, count updates, persistence, search, light + dark, and the delisted-role path all driven in headless Chrome against 228 roles built from the real ledger.

author: soochol
body:
## 발견

리포 루트에 `.env.bak-pre-prune-optin-20260803-111236` 이 **untracked** 로 있었고, **키움 앱키·시크릿 · KIS 앱키·시크릿 · hogaplay 쿠키가 전부 채워져** 있었습니다(2,590 bytes). `git add -A` 한 번이면 커밋되는 상태였습니다.

**히스토리 유출은 없습니다.** `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '.env*'` 로 확인했고, 지금까지 커밋된 `.env*` 는 `.env.example` 뿐입니다. 파일은 리포 밖(`~/hoga-ops-env-backups`, `700`/`600`)으로 옮겼습니다.

## 원인

`.gitignore` 의 `.env` 한 줄은 **정확히 그 이름만** 거릅니다. 변종은 전부 통과합니다:

```
.env.bak       ★ 추적 대상
.env.prod      ★ 추적 대상
.env.bak-...   ★ 추적 대상
```

## 왜 안 보였나 — 두 가지가 겹쳤습니다

**① 전역 gitignore 가 착시를 만듭니다.** 이 개발기에서 `.env.local` 이 무시되고 있어 "env 는 다 막힌다" 로 읽히기 쉬운데, 그건 리포 규칙이 아니라 **사용자 전역** `~/.config/git/ignore` 였습니다(`git check-ignore -v` 로 확인). 전역 설정은 클론·CI 로 따라가지 않으므로 **보호는 리포 안에 있어야** 이식됩니다.

**② 이런 백업은 사람이 아니라 도구가 만듭니다.** 어제 prune opt-in 작업이 자동 생성했습니다 — 의식하고 만든 게 아니라 만든 것도 잊습니다. "조심하면 된다" 로는 안 막히는 종류입니다.

## 수정

```
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
```

`.env.example` 이 계속 추적되는지 `git ls-files --error-unmatch` 로 확인했습니다.

| 파일 | 판정 |
|---|---|
| `.env` · `.env.bak` · `.env.prod` · `.env.bak-...` · `.env.local` | 무시됨 ✅ |
| `.env.example` | 추적 유지 ✅ |

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The codebase repeated the same handful of patterns across `shared`, `gateway`, and `channels`: lazy singleton accessors, `mkdirSync`-if-missing, JSON fallback read/write, recursive directory walks, `fetch` + status-check + `.json()`, and ad-hoc `Math.random()+Date.now()` IDs. This PR centralizes them in `packages/shared/src/utils/*` (plus two gateway-local helpers) and rewires the existing call sites. Behavior is unchanged; all 21 gateway tests pass.

New shared utilities (exported from `@nova/shared`):

```ts
createSingleton<T>(factory)           // replaces 10 copies of `let x|null; if (!x) x = new X(); return x`
ensureDir(dir) / removeFile(path)
readJsonFile<T>(path, fallback, label) / writeJsonFile(path, data, label)
walkFiles(dir, { extensions, skipDirectories })  // generator; skips node_modules/.git/dist
requestJson<T>(url, { label, method, headers, body|rawBody })  // throws `${label} returned HTTP ${status}: ${text}`
bearerJsonHeaders(token)
generateId(prefix?, randomLength?)
```

Notable consumer-side collapses:

- `lancedb.ts`: the near-identical episodic/catalog insert+search pairs became `addRecord(table, idPrefix, text, metadata)` / `searchRecords(table, query, limit)`, with the public methods delegating.
- `sqlite.ts`: every method's `try { stmt } catch { console.error(...); return fallback }` became `this.run(op, action, fallback)`, and the two tenant row→object mappings became `mapTenantRow`.
- `tools.ts`: the four copies of write-temp-script / exec / unlink (js|py × sandboxed|owner) became one `runTempScript` driven by a `SCRIPT_RUNTIMES` table.
- `server.ts`: added `authenticateOwner` (previously duplicated between the preHandler guard and `/api/analytics/overview`), `servePublicFile`, `resolveWebhookTenant` (tenant lookup + 404 + subscription check for the telegram/whatsapp webhooks), and `handleHubVerification` for the Meta `hub.*` handshake.
- New `services/meta.ts` (`sendWhatsAppCloudMessage`, `sendInstagramMessage`) and `services/redis.ts` (`createRedisClient`) absorb the Graph API and `REDIS_URL`+ioredis-import blocks duplicated across `queue.ts`, `limiter.ts`, and `server.ts`.
- `auth.ts`: `toBase64Url` + `signSegments` replace the three inline `.replace(/=/g,'')...` chains, and `deriveKey` replaces the two scrypt promise wrappers.
- `channels`: `registerOwnerHeartbeat(heartbeatService, channel, factKey, send)` replaces the identical telegram/whatsapp heartbeat listeners.

Verification: `pnpm run build` (clean) and `pnpm test` (21/21 pass).

author: nzou2017
body:
## What

Resolve client HTTP call sites to the OpenAPI endpoints that declare them, **across repository boundaries** — the same import-style join, keyed on a canonical API identity.

## How

- **`api_paths.py`** — canonical `apiendpoint:VERB /path` key that ignores path-parameter names and verb casing, so `client.get("/users/{id}")` and OpenAPI `GET /users/{userId}` collapse to one identity.
- **`docs.py`** — OpenAPI endpoint symbols carry that key as their `import_path` (+ method/path/normalized_path metadata).
- **`relationships.py`** — detect client call sites (`<obj>.<verb>("/path")` and `<obj>.request("VERB","/path")`) as `ApiCallRef`; `extract_relationships_and_imports` now returns a 3-tuple `(rels, imports, api_calls)`.
- **migration `0015` + persistence** — `api_call_references` staging table (RLS, indexed on `(org, api_key)`) with full/incremental replace helpers.
- **`pipeline.py`** — stage api-call references during full and incremental indexing.
- **`linking.py`** — second resolution pass emits `cross_repo_edges kind='calls_api'` with operationId/method/path evidence. Query traversal already unions all cross-repo edges, so linked API calls surface in blast radius with no query change.

Detection currently covers Python call sites (the `attribute` node type); TS `member_expression` is a natural follow-up.

## Tests

- Unit coverage for path normalization + call-site detection (31 relevant tests green).
- Live integration test resolves a cross-repo client call to its endpoint (`api_edges >= 1`, operationId evidence).
- Full suite: 629 passed, 1 skipped; ruff clean; mypy clean on new modules.
- Migration `0015` applied and validated against a live DB.

author: sdubois777
body:
Found while starting issue [#36](https://github.com/sdubois777/Cataclysm/issues/36), which needs to look skills up by weapon type. That lookup would have found nothing for **five of the fourteen weapon bases**, because two sheets in the design workbook held different names for the same three weapons.

| Weapon Skills sheet said | Everything else says |
|---|---|
| `2H Axe` | `Greataxe` |
| `2h Sword` | `Greatsword` |
| `2H Warhammer` | `Warhammer` |

"Everything else" is the Item Bases sheet, the weapon base table in section V of the design document, and the Weapon Types list in section V. Three places against one, so the skills sheet is the outlier and is what changed.

**The design document also contradicted itself.** Its Damage Type to Available Weapon Types table used the older spellings, while its own Weapon Types list two sections earlier used the newer ones. That table is the likeliest origin of the drift. It now matches.

## What changed

| File | What it is | What the change does |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/All_Things_Cataclysm.xlsx` | The design workbook, which is authoritative | 80 rows on the Weapon Skills sheet renamed across three weapon types. No skill, description or tag changed |
| `docs/Cataclysm_GDD_v2.md` | The game design document | The Damage Type to Available Weapon Types table now uses the same names as the rest of the document |
| `game/Data/WeaponSkills.csv` | The generated table Unreal loads | Regenerated. Row names derive from the weapon type, so 80 change |
| `tools/generate_datatables.py` | Turns the workbook into the CSV files | Adds a check refusing a weapon type that is not a weapon base, and a weapon base with no rows at all |

Row names are DataTable keys and the generator's own notes say they must be stable. Nothing references these yet, which is why this is the cheapest moment to change them.

The new check compares the two sheets against each other rather than against a list written in the file, so adding a weapon to the design needs no change there.

## What is not a problem

The Wand and the Staff have **no designed War skills, and that is the design rather than a gap.** I initially read it as a hole and the project owner corrected me: the design document's availability table gives War twelve weapon types and neither magic weapon is among them. Not every damage type has skills for every weapon type.

The new check therefore asks only whether a weapon type is real and whether it appears at all. It never asks whether a particular damage type covers a particular weapon, because that would fail on the design working correctly.

## Evidence

The design document's War row and the generated data now agree exactly, both listing the same twelve weapon types:

```
2H Crossbow, Axe, Crossbow, Dagger, Fist, Greataxe, Greatsword,
Shield, Spear, Sword, Warhammer, Whip
```

The new check was broken on purpose. Putting the twenty Greataxe rows back to `2H Axe` makes it report both halves and exit 1:

```
WeaponSkills: weapon type '2H Axe' is not a weapon base. The bases are [...]
WeaponSkills: the Greataxe has no rows at all
```

```
$ python -m pytest
718 passed in 8.71s

$ python -m ruff check .
All checks passed!

$ python tools/generate_datatables.py --check
All 13 DataTable CSVs are up to date.

$ python tools/generate_gameplay_tags.py --check --strict
CataclysmTags.ini is up to date (115 tags).
```

## What this does not do

It does not implement [#36](https://github.com/sdubois777/Cataclysm/issues/36). This is the data correction that issue needs before a weapon-type lookup can work at all. The slot machinery itself — an equipment component, the lookup, and granting one ability per slot on equip — is still to build.

author: kurtbruns
body:
Closes #52.

Builds on PR #46's v1.0 context doc, which documented the version stamp as a *readout* but never the **release discipline** itself. This fills that gap, splitting facts from procedure per Anthropic's Claude Code guidance:

- **Facts** Claude needs every session → `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- **The repeatable, side-effectful procedure** → an on-demand skill (zero context cost until invoked)

## Changes

### `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — new `## Releasing` section
States the facts only, cross-linking the existing Persistence section rather than duplicating it:
- **Deploy vs. release are separate** — deploy auto-fires on every merge to `main`; cutting a release is a deliberate, occasional act via `/release` (`npm version` + `git push --follow-tags`).
- **Two independent version axes** — app version (`__APP_VERSION__`, SemVer) vs. schema version (`SCHEMA_VERSION` + migrations).
- **The git SHA is the true deploy identifier** — the footer version may lag between bumps.

Doc stays at exactly 200 lines (within the ≤200-line best-practices target).

### `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md` — new `/release` skill
`disable-model-invocation: true` so it only runs on an explicit `/release`, with a scoped `allowed-tools` allowlist. Step-driven checklist grounded in the actual repo:
1. **Pre-flight** — on `main`, clean tree, `git pull`, CI green.
2. **Decide the bump** — patch/minor/major from `git log <last-tag>..HEAD`, with app-specific SemVer intent (major = schema break or redesign).
3. **`npm version <bump>`** — atomic bump + tag.
4. **`git push origin main --follow-tags`**.
5. **Watch the deploy** and verify the live footer at eddy.kurtbruns.workers.dev shows the new `v<version> · <sha>`.
6. **(Optional)** draft GitHub release notes, gated behind confirmation.

## Design decisions (from the issue)
- Eddy is a **hosted SPA, not a package** — a release is a human-legible milestone marker, not a distribution step. The `npm version` + tag mechanic is borrowed from the sibling `vector` library, but nothing publishes to npm.
- The two version axes (#16 document-schema vs. #17 app version) stay deliberately independent.

## Verification
- `npm run ci` — clean (Biome, 25 files, no fixes).

author: pedroapfilho
body:
## What an unauthenticated caller could learn before this

`getTeamMembershipRole(teamId, userId)` was exported from `apps/web/src/lib/actions/team-read.ts`, a `"use server"` module. Next compiles every export of such a module into a POST endpoint with a stable action id, reachable by anyone who can read the client bundle. Both arguments came from the request body, so with no session at all a caller could ask:

> for team `T` and user `U`, is `U` an `ADMIN`, a `MEMBER`, or not a member?

That is a membership-and-role oracle over the whole database. Given a team id (visible in any shared `/[teamId]` URL) and a user id, it confirmed whether that person belongs to that team and, when they do, whether they are an admin. Iterated the other way, it enumerated a user's team memberships. No rate limit, no session, no team gate. It leaked no names or emails, but it disclosed the membership graph and the admin set, which is exactly the reconnaissance step before targeting an admin.

## The fix

Stop accepting an identity from the caller:

- `getTeamMembershipRole(teamId)` now takes only the team id and delegates to `getTeamRole` in `apps/web/src/lib/team-auth.ts`, which derives the user from `getSession()`. A caller can only ever ask about itself.
- That also deletes a duplicate membership lookup: `getTeamRole` already did the same `prisma.membership.findUnique` plus `isTeamRole` narrowing.
- `team-auth.ts` is deliberately not a `"use server"` module (its own test asserts that), so delegating there does not re-expose anything.

The in-module caller, `getPublicTeam`, had already resolved the session two lines above the call, so the parameter was redundant even for the legitimate path. The client call site in `apps/web/src/app/[teamId]/client.tsx` drops the argument; its `enabled` guard still skips the request for anonymous visitors, and `userId` stays in the query key so the cache entry remains per-user.

## Caller-supplied-identity sweep

Every `"use server"` module in the repo, and every export of each:

| Module | Export | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/team-read.ts` | `getTeamMembershipRole` | **Was the bug.** Fixed here. |
| `actions/team-read.ts` | `getPublicTeam`, `getTeamName`, `validateTeam` | Team id only; identity from `getSession()`. |
| `actions/invitation-actions.ts` | `inviteMember(teamId, memberId, email)` | Legitimate. `email` is the invitee, not the caller: it names who to send to, and `requireTeamAdmin(teamId)` runs before it is used. It does reveal something about the address it is handed, but the only new fact returned is whether that address already has a membership, and only to an admin of that team. |
| `actions/invitation-actions.ts` | `acceptInvitation`, `declineInvitation` | Legitimate. Identity from the session and checked against the row: `invitation.email !== session.user.email` rejects. |
| `actions/join-requests.ts` | `requestToJoin`, `approveJoinRequest`, `denyJoinRequest` | Ids only; actor is `session.user.id`; admin actions behind `requireTeamAdmin`. |
| `actions/join-requests.ts` | `getPendingJoinRequests(teamId)` | Legitimate. Returns other users' emails and ids, but `requireTeamAdmin(teamId)` gates it and the rows are requests addressed to that admin's team. |
| `actions/member-actions.ts` | `addMember`, `updateMember`, `importMembers` | Legitimate, though the types read alarmingly: the payload is `Omit<TeamMember, …>`, and `TeamMember` carries an optional `userId`. `TeamMemberInputSchema` / `TeamMemberUpdateSchema` do not declare `userId`, and zod strips unknown keys, so a caller cannot plant a slot claimed by someone else. Admin-gated regardless. |
| `actions/member-actions.ts` | `updateOwnMember` | Legitimate. Skips the admin check on purpose, then requires a membership for `session.user.id`, refuses a slot already claimed by another user, and overwrites `userId` with the session's. |
| `actions/member-actions.ts` | `removeMember(teamId, memberId)` | No identity argument: two ids, admin-gated through `mutateTeam`. |
| `actions/member-actions.ts` | `reorderMembers`, `updateTeamName` | No identity argument. |
| `actions/group-actions.ts` | `createGroup`, `updateGroup`, `removeGroup`, `reorderGroups` | No identity argument; all admin-gated through `mutateTeam`. |
| `actions/team-create.ts` | `createTeam(timezone)` | Owner and member come from `requireAuth()`. |

One real instance, and it is the one fixed here.

## Tests

`team-read.test.ts` drops the second argument and adds two cases that would have passed against the old signature only by accident: the membership lookup uses the session user's id, and an anonymous caller gets `null` without a database query.

## Overlap

body:
## The problem, from the owner's screen

A GRN line for `NTYR MEMORY CONTOUR PILLOW` had grown **eight SO rows and nine DO chips of its own** — one accessory line taller than the rest of the document put together.

> 因为我的枕头进 500 粒，然后分配的话，它整个的 listing 会太长了 … 关于整个 accessories 它不需要显示出来，没关系的。不过，你的 Stock Movement Control 那边一定要有这个

A pillow arrives 500 at a time and spreads across dozens of orders. Listing each one on the receiving document is unreadable and tells you nothing you would act on there.

## The list goes, the counts stay

The cell now reads:

```
8 orders · 9 deliveries
see Stock Movement
```

**Not a blank cell**, deliberately. An empty assignment column reads as *"this stock is unassigned"*, and a document that quietly under-states its own linkage is the exact ambiguity behind `docs/unlinked-line-duplicate-coe.md` — the reason `2990-DO-2607-005` went unnoticed for weeks is that nothing on screen said those goods were already spoken for. Collapsing a list is fine; implying there is nothing in it is not.

## What is NOT touched

**The links.** `so_item_id` and `purchase_order_item_id` are what the remaining-qty ceilings count. Hiding a column must never become dropping a link — that distinction *is* the incident this month. This is presentation only.

The document-by-document trail stays on **Stock Movement**, which already records a clickable `source_doc_no` for every IN and OUT (`Inventory.tsx`), which is what the owner asked to be sure of.

## Scope

- `item_group = 'accessory'`, case-insensitive. A mattress line on the same GRN still names its orders — asserted.
- PO, GRN and Purchase Invoice all render through `DocumentLinesExpansion`, so one change covers the three screens named.
- Sales documents (DO / SI) are untouched: there the assignment *is* the document.

## Verification

20 component tests pass, covering the paired and assignment-only views, singular/plural, case-insensitivity, the untouched non-accessory line, and the no-assignment case still reading as stock rather than a blank.

**Not browser-verified** — this repo has no `launch.json` and reaching a real GRN needs backend auth. Flagging that rather than implying otherwise.

## Resumen

**PR 3** del encargo "biblioteca de temas + editor único". Un tema se elige mirándolo, no leyéndolo: la galería deja de ser una rejilla de botones con el nombre y una frase *dentro* del editor, y pasa a ser su propia pantalla donde cada tema se ve **pintado** antes de instalarlo.

- **`ThemeThumb`** (nuevo): el Inicio del portal a 392px reescalado, con los mismos tokens de `portal-design.ts` y las mismas CSS vars que `themeToCssVars()`, y la barra inferior **real** (`PortalNav`) — así `barraOscura` de Noir se ve en la miniatura tal cual se verá en el móvil. No es un iframe a propósito: la biblioteca enseña 6+ temas a la vez y cada `/portal-preview` pediría su propio token firmado. La vista previa **fiel** sigue siendo el iframe del editor (regla 2 del encargo).
- **`ThemeLibrary`** (nuevo): "Tu tema" (miniatura, versión, estado `Publicado` / `N cambios sin publicar`, paleta, tipografías, y Personalizar / Publicar / Volver a lo publicado) y la biblioteca, una fila por tema con `Personalizar` y `Usar`.
- **Rutas**: la biblioteca es ahora `/configuracion/apariencia`; el editor que había ahí se mueve a `/configuracion/apariencia/editor`. Ese es exactamente el hueco donde **PR 4** construirá el editor a pantalla completa, sin volver a mover nada.
- La categoría **"Tema" desaparece de `AJUSTES_CATEGORIAS`**: tener dos galerías para lo mismo confundía más que ayudaba.

## Tres cosas que el encargo no cubría y sí hacía falta resolver

1. **"Usar" ahora persiste.** `elegirTema` solo tocaba estado local; encadenarlo con `handleGuardar` habría guardado el borrador de *antes* del `setState` (React no lo actualiza en el acto) — la pantalla mostraría el tema nuevo y el servidor conservaría el viejo, **en silencio**. Se guarda el objeto fusionado a mano.
2. **Tras publicar se relee lo publicado**, o el contador seguiría diciendo "N cambios sin publicar" sobre algo que ya se publicó.
3. **Miniatura: foto de 108 → 78px.** Medido, no tanteado: el contenido sumaba ~591px sobre un marco de 565 y se colaba por debajo de la barra inferior — justo donde se ve `barraOscura`.

- [ ] Prueba con la sesión real de la propietaria tras el deploy

## Fuera de este PR

**PR 4** — editor a pantalla completa (3 columnas sin sidebar, un solo Publicar para tema + bloques + menú, panel "Antes de publicar"). Este PR le deja la ruta `/editor` preparada.

author: turdjali
body:
### Motivation
- Constrained mobile runtimes (especially Android WebView) were triggering large transient WebGL / glTF decoding memory spikes that lead to crashes during Murlan Royale scene setup. 
- The goal is to detect these environments and apply a memory-safe rendering and asset-loading profile to avoid out-of-memory conditions on low-memory or embedded browser runtimes.

### Description
- Add runtime detection helpers `isAndroidWebViewRuntime()` and `isConstrainedMobileRuntime()` and use them from `resolveDefaultPixelRatioCap()` to detect mobile / WebView contexts. 
- Enforce a mobile-safe graphics profile in the frame quality path by capping FPS, forcing `renderScale = 1`, and lowering the `pixelRatioCap` when `isConstrainedMobileRuntime()` is true. 
- Limit texture/HDR resolution for constrained devices by returning a 1k HDRI and a `MOBILE_PREFERRED_TEXTURE_SIZES` order, and ensure `activeTextureResolutionOrder` respects the mobile fallback. 
- Reduce renderer memory usage on constrained devices by disabling antialiasing, turning off dynamic shadows, and capping anisotropy, and set `powerPreference` to a safe default. 
- Avoid concurrent glTF decoding spikes by loading character models sequentially and, on constrained devices, loading only the selected/safe template instead of all roster themes concurrently.

### Testing
- Ran lint with `npm --prefix webapp run lint -- src/pages/Games/MurlanRoyaleArena.jsx` and it completed successfully. 
- Performed a production build with `npm --prefix webapp run build`, which completed successfully (the build reported existing chunk-size warnings but no errors). 
- Verified no outstanding whitespace or syntax issues with `git diff --check` which reported no problems.

author: rogersquare
body:
Task: bug-webshell-autoupdate-001

## Problem
Every containerized web-shell session shows Claude Code's **"Auto-update failed"** banner, and the container CLI drifts stale (2.1.220 vs 2.1.221 on the host).

## Diagnosis
The image installs the CLI with `npm install -g` **as root**, but the container runs as `node` (uid 1000). The self-updater can never write root-owned `/usr/local/lib/node_modules` → EACCES → banner on every launch.

## Fix
`ENV DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` baked into the image — the correct posture for an immutable container: updates arrive via image rebuild, which already installs the latest release. Web-shell PTYs inherit the env via `...process.env` (backend/sockets/web-shell.js), as do loop executor/summary spawns.

## Test plan
- Rebuild container → `docker exec atrium env | grep DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` shows the var
- CLI version current after rebuild (install line fetches latest)
- Open the global web-shell → no auto-update banner

author: verygoodsoftwarenotvirus
body:
Closes #74.

## What was wrong

`validation.Field(&cfg.X, validation.When(selected, validation.Required))` does not stop ozzo's nested validation. ozzo validates any non-nil pointer to a `Validatable` once a field's rules have run, whatever those rules were — so the `When` guard suppresses the `Required` rule and nothing else. Before `,init` was corrected these pointers were nil for unselected providers and nested validation never ran, which is what made the guard look sufficient.

Every provider's credentials were therefore demanded at once. Ten seams were affected:

| Package | Sub-configs |
|---|---|
| `observability/logging/config` | `OtelSlog` |
| `cache/config` | `Redis` |
| `email/config` | `Sendgrid`, `Mailgun`, `Mailjet`, `Resend`, `Postmark`, `SES` |
| `llm/config` | `OpenAI`, `Anthropic` |
| `embeddings/config` | `OpenAI`, `Ollama`, `Cohere` |
| `search/vector/config` | `Pgvector`, `Qdrant` |
| `analytics/config` | `Segment`, `Posthog` |
| `notifications/async/config` | `Pusher`, `Ably`, `WebSocket` |
| `capitalism/config` | `Stripe` |
| `distributedlock/config` | `Redis`, `Postgres` |

Three of the issue's candidates needed no change, and I'd rather say so than change them quietly:

- **`routing`** lists no rule for its backend sub-configs, so ozzo never validates them.
- **`server/http`**'s `AppleAppSiteAssociationConfig` is documented to accept an entirely empty one — the feature is simply off.
- **`eventstream`**'s websocket config has no required field, so an empty one is a fully defaulted one.

## The fix, and why it isn't `cfgnorm.ZeroToNil`

The issue suggests the one-liner #70 applied elsewhere. I went with `validation.Skip.When(not selected)` instead, for three reasons:

1. **It wouldn't have worked.** `search/vector`'s and `distributedlock`'s sub-configs carry `envDefault` fields (`Metric`, `Timeout`, `KeyPrefix`), so they are never zero once the environment has been parsed — `ZeroToNil` has nothing to release and the bug survives in 2 of the 10.
2. **Nothing here reads nil-ness.** #70's seams have `validation.Nil` rules, where the normalization is load-bearing *for the rule itself*. These seams don't, so `Skip` states the actual intent in ozzo's own terms rather than erasing data to route around it. `internal/cfgnorm`'s package doc now spells out which shape takes which remedy.
3. **It keeps the better error.** A selected provider configured with nothing still reports which credential is missing, because its own sub-config is still validated: `sendgrid: (apiToken: cannot be blank)` rather than `sendgrid: cannot be blank`.

The trade is that a sub-config filled in for a provider you did *not* select goes unchecked. None of these seams make that an error today, so nothing that used to be rejected on those grounds is now accepted — but it's the deliberate cost, and worth a second opinion.

While here, `email` and `distributedlock` read the selection **normalized**, matching what their dispatch does with it. Both accept a `"SENDGRID"` or `"REDIS"` that a raw comparison would not, and would otherwise have skipped the very block they were about to hand to a constructor.

## Tests

`TestUnselectedProvidersAreNotEnforced` pins the property across **every** config seam — including the ones with no pointer sub-config to get wrong — so it's a statement about the whole surface rather than about the packages that happened to be broken. It sits next to `TestSelectedProviderMustBeConfigured`, which asserts the opposite direction; the two fail in opposite ways and a fix for either one alone looks correct.

**That sweep lost two rows, and this is the part worth reviewing.** `embeddings/ollama` and `distributedlock/postgres` have no required field of their own — ollama defaults to the local daemon, the postgres locker to the database it is handed — so "naming this provider and configuring nothing" is a valid configuration, not something to refuse. They were green only because the *sibling* sub-configs were being enforced: they asserted on openai's and redis' credentials from a config that had named neither. They now join the two exclusions the sweep already documented (`eventstream`'s websocket, `notifications/mobile`'s FCM).

Both sweeps now parse the environment under a prefix nothing sets, so a stray `ADDRESSES` or `REGION` in a developer's shell can't decide the result.

No exported API changes, so no major bump — this only accepts configurations that were already meant to be valid.

## Verification

- `make format lint` — 0 issues
- `.scripts/test.sh false` — full suite green
- `RUN_CONTAINER_TESTS=true go test -race ./cache/... ./distributedlock/... ./search/... ./email/...` — green

author: ashita-planning
body:
Phase 1 of #9 — the core contract only. No tracker implementation, no HTTP, no GitHub vocabulary.

- `DTO\ErrorReportData` — plain text, **no Markdown, labels or links**
- `DTO\IssuePublicationResultData` — string `externalId`, `state`, and `action` of `created` / `commented` / `reopened` / `skipped` / `failed`
- `Contracts\IssuePublisher` — `enabled()`, `provider()`, `target()`, `publish()`
- `Contracts\IssueLinkRepository` — provider-agnostic throughout, plus `recordPublication()`
- Migration adding `provider`, `external_id`, `external_state`, `metadata` — **additive only**

### Decisions

**Identifiers are strings.** GitHub hands out `1234`, Jira `OPS-42`. A numeric contract would have to be broken for the second.

**`skipped` is an outcome, not a severity.** "Already reported today" is the most common thing a daily run says.

**Idempotency is shared.** The core records what it published and will not offer the same report twice — a report stops being "the same" once the occurrence count or last occurrence moves. That is a first line of defence, not the whole of it: only the adapter can see what the tracker holds, so the contract still requires adapters to be idempotent.

**Failure records nothing.** So the next run retries rather than believing the report was delivered.

### Backward compatibility

`repository`, `issue_number`, `issue_state` and `pull_request_number` keep their meaning and are still written when the identifier is numeric. Nothing is dropped or retyped.

The `IssuePublisher` signature change is breaking on paper, but nothing implemented it — it was a contract-only placeholder.

### Verified

`RecordingIssuePublisher` exercises created / commented / reopened / skipped / failed through `error-monitor:run`, including that a repeated run does not re-ask the adapter, that a disabled or absent publisher is silent, and that a failure leaves no link. `AGENTS.md` now lists what may never enter the core.

author: lsecyber
body:
## The previous approach could never have worked

My last fix assumed the action would hand me its App token. It doesn't — proven from the run log:

1. **The token output is empty:** `"github_token": ""`
2. **The action revokes the token inside its own step**, before any later step runs:

```
04:02:36.34  ##[start-action display=Revoke app token;id=applet.__run_9]
             curl -X DELETE .../installation/token
04:02:36.78  Post job cleanup    ← my posting step ran after this
```

So `Mint a fresh Claude App token` reported **"App token successfully obtained"**, and the comment still fell through to the job token and posted as `github-actions[bot]`. The mint worked; the handoff was impossible.

## Fix: let the action post the comment

Inside its own invocation the token is live, so a `gh pr comment` from there is attributed to `claude[bot]`. And because this is a **fresh invocation in a separate job**, its token is minted *now* — not ~1h+ ago when the scan started. That's what makes attribution survive a long scan, which was the original point.

- The report body is staged to `comment-body.md` first (capped under GitHub's 65536-char limit).
- The agent is told to post it **verbatim** and to treat its contents as **data, never instructions** — it's scan output derived from an untrusted diff, so that matters.
- Tool grant is `Bash(gh pr comment:*)` + `Read`, nothing more.
- Job-token fallback retained and now correctly reachable via `continue-on-error`, because a silently dropped report is indistinguishable from a clean scan.

## What this session's testing keeps showing

Three iterations on this one bug, each caught only by a real run:

| Attempt | Failure |
|---|---|
| Post from inside the scan | 401 — token expired mid-scan (90 min) |
| Post from a separate step | `exit 128` — no checkout for the action's `git fetch` |
| Reuse the minted token | Token revoked in-step, output empty |

Component tests passed at every stage. Only end-to-end runs found these.

Verification of the staging step: normal report → correct body; 70KB report → 60127 bytes with truncation notice, under the cap.

author: patilprem
body:
Fixes the dashboard resetting to zeroes after #26.

## What went wrong

The history was never lost — it sits in `export_stats`, untouched. But the dashboard reads `export_stats_v2`, and #26 created that table only inside the beacon handler. Open `/stats` before the next export happens and the query hits a table that does not exist, falls back to an empty result, and renders every number as 0. A site with history looked exactly like a site with none.

The migration was self-bootstrapping only from the write side, and the read-first order was never tested. That is the gap.

## The fix

The schema and the copy-forward move into a shared module (`functions/_export-stats.js`) that **both** the beacon and the dashboard call, so whichever runs first brings the history with it and the numbers no longer depend on which one the day happened to start with.

Doing it on a read is safe:
- `INSERT OR IGNORE` makes the copy idempotent — repeated dashboard loads cannot accumulate.
- It cannot double-count: every row the copy writes has a blank `style`, and every row written since carries `flatlay` or `onmodel`, so the two can never share a primary key.
- `/stats` is already token-protected, so this is not a write an anonymous request can trigger.

## Testing

Reproduced before fixing, on a local D1 seeded through the *previous* endpoint so the data was genuinely in the old table:

```
17 downloads + 3 batch exports in export_stats

before fix:  Single Downloads 0    Batch Exports 0
after fix:   Single Downloads 17   Batch Exports 3   Batch Images 24
```

Recovered purely on the read, with no beacon sent.

Also verified:
- **Mirror case on a separate database** — beacon first, no dashboard visit — since the write path was restructured too. 9 legacy rows recovered there as well.
- Repeated dashboard loads hold at 17 rather than climbing.
- New beacons still land under the right style and template after the copy (`park-m` / `miami-f` appeared correctly).
- Recovered rows show as "before this was recorded", not folded into flat lay, which would be a guess.
- `/_export-stats` returns 404 rather than being served as a route.
- `npm run build` clean.

## After deploy

Just load `/stats` — the recovery happens on that first page load, nothing to run by hand. Expect the restored history to appear under "Before this was recorded" in the Flat Lay vs On Model card; the Single Downloads and Batch Exports totals will be complete.

author: a-essawy
body:
## Why

The [Software Directory Policy](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13145358-anthropic-software-directory-policy) requires **a minimum of three working prompt/use-case examples**. The README had **one**. A directory submission would have been rejected on that alone.

This is the requirement I got wrong earlier: I flagged it, then withdrew it after not finding it on the review-criteria page. It is not there, it is in the **policy**. The requirement was real.

## What was added

| Example | Type | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| Mute the first 3 seconds (existing) | `ffmpeg` | Raw command execution |
| Get `demo.mov` under 25 MB | `compress.target` | Size budget, upload flow |
| Make a 1920x1080 title card | `image.generate` | Generation, and `inputs: {}` |

Chosen so the three cover **both halves of the product**. Generation had no example anywhere in the repo, despite being three of the nine live job types.

## Parameters are real, not invented

The policy says *working* examples, so the shapes come from the job definitions:

- `compress.target` takes `inputs.source` (a URL) plus a `target` union. `{ maxSize: "25MB" }` is one of four accepted forms.
- `image.generate` uses `inputs.render()`, which is an **empty object** because no media is being transformed. Params are the tier (`economy`/`standard`/`premium`) plus prompt and optional dimensions.

I also noted honestly that requested dimensions get snapped to what the chosen model can render, rather than implying 1920x1080 is guaranteed.

## Verification

All **8** tool-call payloads across the three examples parse as valid JSON (brace-matched extraction, whole-line comments stripped). Zero em-dashes.

author: turfaa
body:
## Summary

Adds `GET /api/v2/sales/drugs/{drug_code}/last`, which returns a drug's most recent sales as a display-ready `cui.Table`. This is the sales counterpart to the existing last-drug-procurements endpoint, so the price list page in `apotek-dashboard` can show the last selling prices of a drug next to the last purchase prices.

## AI attribution

Claude Opus 5

## Changes

- **`sale`**: new `GetLastDrugSales` on `Database`, `Service`, and a new `handler_v2.go` with the Gin handler and the `cui.Table` transform (columns: Tanggal Penjualan, Nomor Faktur, Jumlah, Harga Satuan, Total, Kategori Harga). New `LastDrugSalesRequest` and `DrugSale` in `models.go`. New `handler_v2_test.go` covering filtering/ordering/limit, exclusion of soft-deleted sales, and the empty case.
- **`proxy`**: registers the route under a new `/api/v2/sales` group, gated to `admin` / `staff`, cached by request URI for one minute — same middleware stack as the procurement equivalent.
- **`docs`**: `openapi.yaml` documents the new endpoint under the `Sales` tag.

## Verification

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] `gofmt -l .` and `go vet ./...` clean
- [ ] Exercised the affected endpoint or command against a real Vmedis / DB — not run; no Vmedis credentials or populated DB in this environment. The new tests cover the handler against an in-memory SQLite DB.

## Notes

- **API**: endpoint added — `docs/openapi.yaml` updated to match. The response uses `cui.Table`.
- **Database**: no schema change. The query filters on `sale_units.drug_code` (already indexed) and joins `sales` on the unique `invoice_number`, excluding soft-deleted rows on both sides. The limit is capped at 20 server-side.
  - Worth a reviewer's eye: unlike the procurement query, which sorts by `procurement_units.created_at` (same table as the filter), this one sorts by `sales.sold_at` across the join, so no single-table index can remove the sort. The planner can either fetch all of the drug's units and sort, or walk the `sales.sold_at` index backwards and probe by invoice number. Existing indexes make both plans available. If this turns out to be slow against real volumes — sales per drug are far higher than procurements per drug — the fix is denormalizing `sold_at` onto `sale_units` so `(drug_code, sold_at DESC)` serves filter and sort together, not another index on the current schema. Not done here, since it needs a backfill and a change to the bulk upsert path, and there's no evidence yet that it's needed.
- **Frontend**: paired `apotek-dashboard` change — turfaa/apotek-dashboard#14. This PR should deploy first; the dashboard dialog errors until the endpoint exists.

author: tristan578
body:
## Summary

`scripts/check-lockfile-sync.sh` reported drift on a **clean `main`**, blamed the contributor ("A package.json was changed without regenerating the root lockfile"), and printed a remediation that reproduces the identical diff forever — the printed fix *is* the command that produced it.

Root cause is **npm-version skew**, not the OS and not the Node version. Measured against this repo:

| npm | bundled with | `npm install --package-lock-only` on clean main |
|-----|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| 11.10.0 | Node 25.6.1 | **34 nodes lose their `libc` field** (102-line diff) |
| 11.16.0 | Node 24.18.0 (what CI resolves from `.node-version`) | zero drift |
| 11.16.0 | run under Node **25.6.1** | zero drift |

The third row is the control that isolates the variable: same OS, same Node, only npm swapped, drift gone. All 34 affected nodes are Linux-only optional native bindings (`@img/sharp-*`, `@next/swc-linux-*`, `@rolldown/binding-linux-*`, `@tailwindcss/oxide-linux-*`, `lightningcss-linux-*`). **0 nodes added, 0 removed, 0 version/resolved/integrity changes.**

## What changed

A "Stage 3" classifier runs only after regeneration has already produced a difference. It compares `git show :package-lock.json` (the index — the correct baseline, since `git diff` above compares worktree against index) with the regenerated file after stripping `os`/`cpu`/`libc` from every `.packages` node:

- identical → **exit 2** (fail-closed tooling error, the house convention from `check-npm-audit.sh` and stage 1 of this same gate), naming the running npm and the `.node-version` pin, with a remediation that actually works
- otherwise → the pre-existing **exit 1** drift path, unchanged, plus a note when real drift and the metadata rewrite land in the same regeneration so the reader does not chase noise lines

### Why this cannot mask real drift

A manifest change makes npm re-resolve, which adds/removes package nodes or changes `version`/`resolved`/`integrity` — all of which survive stripping `os`/`cpu`/`libc`. And `integrity` pins the exact tarball, so a given version can never legitimately change its own platform metadata. A difference that vanishes under the strip therefore carries no information about whether the lockfile matches the manifests. The classifier is strictly additive: anything it does not positively prove benign — including input it cannot parse — takes the existing exit-1 path.

## Test plan

Tests written first, hermetic via the existing `$LOCKFILE_REGEN_CMD` stub seam:

- [x] **10** metadata-only removal (`libc` stripped) → exit 2, message names the artifact, the running npm and `.node-version`; does *not* say "drift detected"; working tree restored
- [x] **10b** six real-drift mutations each → exit 1: version bump, resolved-URL change, integrity change, node added, node removed, top-level `lockfileVersion` change
- [x] **10c** metadata churn **plus** a real version change → exit 1 with the noise warning (artifact must not mask real drift)
- [x] **10d** semantics-preserving reformat → not reported as contributor drift, with an explicit vacuity guard that fails the case if the stub produces no textual diff
- [x] **10e** unparseable regeneration output → exit 1 (conservative fallback)
- [x] Full suite: 87 assertions, 0 failures
- [x] Real gate on clean `main` under Node 25.6.1 / npm 11.10.0 → exit 2 with the correct diagnosis, tree restored
- [x] Real gate under Node 24.18.0 / npm 11.16.0 (what CI resolves) → `package-lock.json is in sync` — **CI behavior unchanged**
- [x] `shellcheck` clean on both files
- [x] All 18 `scripts/__tests__/*.test.sh` self-defense suites pass

No `ci.yml` change — the gate rides the existing `lockfile-sync` job wiring unchanged.

## Docs

`.claude/rules/gotchas.md` gains an entry recording the measured root cause, an explicit warning not to conflate it with the separate full-relock footgun (which drops nodes entirely; this drops none), the detection mechanism, why it cannot mask real drift, and the local remediation. It also corrects prior guidance that framed this as a macOS artifact.

Closes #9081 (PF-1051)
