author: haggyroth
body:
Phase 1 of the PyQt6 port (#27), on top of the smoke tests from #52.

**Every spelling changed here works identically on PyQt5 5.15 and PyQt6.** So this is a no-op for the binding we ship, while removing almost all of the eventual port's diff — leaving Phase 3 a small, reviewable change instead of a 350-site one tangled up with a binding switch.

## What changed

| | count |
|---|---|
| enum references → scoped form (`Qt.AlignLeft` → `Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignLeft`) | 346 |
| `exec_()` → `exec()` | 2 |
| `Qt.MidButton` → `Qt.MouseButton.MiddleButton` | 3 |
| `QFileDialog.DirectoryOnly` → `FileMode.Directory` + `ShowDirsOnly` | 1 |
| `QDesktopWidget` → `QGuiApplication.screenAt` | 4 |

The `QDesktopWidget` rewrite adopts the idiom [`qt.util.move_to_screen_center`](qt/util.py:29) already used — `result_window.py` was the outlier, and `screenAt` returning `None` is exactly what `screenNumber() == -1` meant.

## How the enum rewrite was done

Not by hand, and not by a hand-written table of 119 mappings.

PyQt5 exposes its enums as sip types rather than Python enums, so it can't be introspected for this. **PyQt6 uses real Python enums**, so I derived the member→scope mapping by introspecting PyQt6 (362 classes, 1148 `Qt` members), then applied it mechanically. Ambiguous members — the same name in two enum types of one class — were audited first: 6 exist, all in `QColorSpace`/`QPointingDevice`, neither used here.

## Evidence

Three independent checks, not just "tests pass":

1. **Value equality under PyQt5** — all 119 distinct rewrites resolve and compare equal to the old spelling: `PyQt5: 119 rewrites checked, 0 problem(s)`
2. **Resolvable under PyQt6** — `PyQt6: 119 rewrites checked, 0 problem(s)`
3. **Whole-tree audit after rewriting** — every enum expression in `qt/`, not just the ones I changed:
   ```
   PyQt6: 380 enum spellings resolved, 0 unresolved
   PyQt5: 380 enum spellings resolved, 0 unresolved
   ```

Plus a sweep for removed *methods* the enum audit can't see (`setResizeMode`, `QTextCodec`, `QRegExp`, `AA_EnableHighDpiScaling`, `QApplication.desktop`, …) — all clean.

**830 passed, 6 skipped**, unchanged from master. `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.

## Two things the issue didn't have

- `QFileDialog.DirectoryOnly` is **removed** in Qt6, not merely rescoped. It was always defined as `Directory` + `ShowDirsOnly`, which is what it's spelled as now.
- There were **two** `exec_()` calls, not one — the issue's survey missed [result_window.py:508](qt/result_window.py:508).

## Deliberately left

`qt/recent.py:12` still does `from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QAction`. It's the only Qt5-only spelling remaining, and it genuinely cannot be fixed here: `QAction` moved to `QtGui` in Qt6 and **no single import works on both**. It needs the shim, so it belongs to Phase 3.

## Also in here

`HANDOFF.md`'s "The Qt layer is untested" section went stale the moment #52 merged. Rewritten as "smoke coverage only", with the things that actually bite: Linux legs skip the Qt tests entirely, and the resource tests need `dg_rc.py` which `build.py --modules` doesn't generate. Its #27 entry now records the phasing and the qtpy decision.

## Project Item

Unblocks traverse-framework/traverse#883 (blocked on issue #890, "Specify provider-neutral DataStore synchronization protocol").

## Governing Spec

- `089-datastore-synchronization`
- `004-spec-alignment-gate`
- `088-runtime-usage-telemetry`
- `070-runtime-event-sink-boundary`

(`088-runtime-usage-telemetry` and `070-runtime-event-sink-boundary` cover files pulled in by merging `main` into this branch to resolve the ID collision described below — not otherwise touched by this PR's own change.)

## Summary

Spec `533-datastore-synchronization` was merged in #893 already marked `Status: Approved`, self-assigning canonical governing ID `086-datastore-synchronization`, and its `## Decisions` section mirrors issue #890's recorded `## Approved decisions` verbatim. That PR only added `specs/533-datastore-synchronization/spec.md` and `docs/adr/0027-datastore-synchronization.md` — it never added a corresponding entry to `specs/governance/approved-specs.json`, the actual machine-readable approval registry. So the spec document said "Approved" but was never really registered, and `bash scripts/ci/spec_alignment_check.sh` has never recognized it.

Its self-assigned canonical ID `086` had independently been taken by a different, later spec (`086-mode-a-registry-mcp`, #925) by the time this was noticed. While preparing this fix, `088` (the next free ID at the time) was *also* independently claimed by another spec (`088-runtime-usage-telemetry`) that merged into `main` before this PR did — resolved as a merge conflict, landing this one on `089`. Two independent collisions on the same "pick the next free number" convention in short succession.

## Changes

- Reassigns spec 533 to `089-datastore-synchronization` (the next free canonical ID after this branch's merge conflict with `088-runtime-usage-telemetry`).
- Updates the spec's own `Canonical governing ID` self-reference and ADR-0027's `Governing spec` reference to match.
- Adds the registry entry (`path`, `governs: crates/traverse-runtime/, docs/adr/0027-datastore-synchronization.md, specs/533-datastore-synchronization/`), following the same shape used for the neighboring registry entries.

This is the mechanical registration step, not a new decision — no spec content changed, only the self-referenced ID (to resolve the collision) and the registry entry that should already have existed. Per the decision-log alignment exception for governance PRs: the spec's `## Decisions` and `## Definition of Done` sections match issue #890's recorded decision log exactly, so I'm merging this once CI is green rather than leaving it for review.

## Validation

- `jq empty specs/governance/approved-specs.json` — valid JSON, no duplicate IDs
- `bash scripts/ci/spec_alignment_check.sh` run locally against this PR body — passes
- No code changes; docs/governance only

body:
> ℹ️ **Note**
> 
> This PR body was truncated due to platform limits.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly) | minor | `v1.39.0` → `v1.40.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>dragonflydb/dragonfly (ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly)</summary>

### [`v1.40.0`](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/releases/tag/v1.40.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.39.0...v1.40.0)

##### Dragonfly v1.40.0

This is one of our biggest releases yet—both in terms of feature quality, total contributions, and the highest number of external contributors in the last two years.

This release delivers major new functionality alongside a large body of correctness and stability fixes for tiered storage, replication, pub/sub, and the experimental V2 I/O loop.

We added a new data type: Cuckoo Filters (CF.RESERVE, CF.ADD/ADDNX, CF.EXISTS/MEXISTS, CF.INSERT/INSERTNX, CF.INFO/COUNT/DEL/COMPACT, and RDB persistence). This brings Dragonfly to parity with RedisBloom's probabilistic structures alongside expanded Bloom filter (BF.INFO) and HyperLogLog support.

Vector search gains native-width storage across all vector dtypes, EPSILON-tuned HNSW range queries, and EF\_RUNTIME control. Meanwhile, a long list of fixes hardens tiered-storage interactions with strings, hashes, lists, bitops, and HLL commands, in addition to several replication-consistency fixes around lazy TTL expiry. Performance work includes lazy lock-table registration, zero-copy GET, and replica-side command batching.

- New Cuckoo Filter data type with full command set and RDB support.
- Vector search now stores/computes at native declared width, plus EPSILON and EF\_RUNTIME tuning for HNSW.
- Numerous tiered-storage and replication consistency fixes (HLL, hashes, lists, bitops, hash-field TTL expiry).

##### Highlights

- Added a full Cuckoo Filter data type with RDB persistence, bringing RedisBloom parity for probabilistic structures ([#​7646](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7646), [#​7700](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7700)).
- Vector search now stores/computes vectors at native declared width instead of always widening to FLOAT32, reducing memory usage ([#​7849](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7849)).
- Re-synced hyperloglog.c with upstream Valkey, fixing CVE-2025-32023 and adding AVX2/NEON kernels \[up to \~29x speedup on dense HLL merges] ([#​7961](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7961)).

##### Commands

- INFO now includes TLS certificate metadata (subject, issuer, validity dates) when TLS is enabled ([#​7844](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7844)).
- SAVE and BGSAVE now support a HELP subcommand ([#​7865](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7865)).
- JSON.STRAPPEND now supports an optional path argument, defaulting to root ([#​7868](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7868)).
- Implemented the RESET command, resetting a connection to a fresh-connection baseline ([#​7760](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7760)).
- Added Redis-compatible WAIT command, blocking until replicas acknowledge writes ([#​7454](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7454)).
- Added HGETEX and HPEXPIRETIME hash commands ([#​7717](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7717)).
- Added BF.INFO for Bloom filter metadata ([#​7761](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7761)).
- Added BM25STD.NORM and BM25STD.TANH scorers for FT.SEARCH/AGGREGATE/HYBRID ([#​7692](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7692)).

##### Vector Search

- Vector search (FLAT and HNSW) now stores and computes distances at native declared width (INT8, UINT8, FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, FLOAT32, FLOAT64) ([#​7849](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7849)).
- Added EPSILON parameter for HNSW-backed VECTOR\_RANGE queries to control overscan/recall near the radius boundary ([#​7718](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7718)).
- Added support for KNN query attribute block syntax (`=>{$EF_RUNTIME: ...; $YIELD_DISTANCE_AS: ...}`) ([#​7708](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7708)).
- Fixed filtered KNN vector search to serialize only actual winners instead of every pre-filter match, cutting CPU/memory overhead ([#​7670](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7670)).

##### Cuckoo Filter

- Added CF.INSERT and CF.INSERTNX for bulk insertion, with optional CAPACITY and NOCREATE ([#​7719](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7719)).
- Added compaction: CF.DEL auto-compacts past 10% deletions, plus a manual CF.COMPACT command ([#​7702](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7702)).
- Added CF.EXISTS and CF.MEXISTS for single/multi-item membership checks ([#​7682](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7682)).
- Added CF.ADD and CF.ADDNX, auto-creating filters with a default capacity of 1024 ([#​7681](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7681)).

##### Probabilistic Data Structures

- Added RDB serialization support for Cuckoo filters, enabling DUMP/RESTORE and persistence ([#​7700](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7700)).
- Added CF.INFO, CF.COUNT, and CF.DEL for filter metadata, occurrence counts, and item removal ([#​7691](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7691)).
- Added the base Cuckoo Filter data type via CF.RESERVE, with a new CUCKOO\_FILTER ACL category ([#​7646](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7646)).

##### Performance

- Extended parse-in-proactor pipelining optimization to more fiber park spots (shard hops, suspended replies on tiered I/O) ([#​7916](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7916)).
- Added `snapshot_egress_limit_bytes` to throttle per-shard socket egress during RDB/snapshot saves ([#​7774](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7774)).
- Reworked open-addressing hash container (OAHPair/OAHEntry) with compact variable-width size encoding, reducing fragmentation ([#​7853](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7853)).

author: aalzriqat
body:
## What changed

- Resolve Messenger DM senders from the Page conversation's participants before falling back to the legacy direct PSID profile endpoint.
- Keep Page access tokens in the Bearer header and bound each Meta lookup to five seconds.
- Make the Social Inbox resync button run contact-name repair only. It no longer runs post/DM vehicle matching or creates vehicle suggestions.
- Add production-regression coverage for conversation-participant names and for name-only resync leaving vehicle fields untouched.

## Why

Messenger webhooks contain a Page-scoped sender ID (PSID), not the Facebook account name. In production, Meta's direct PSID lookup still returns error code 100 / subcode 33 for real DM senders, while the Page conversations endpoint returns the real participant name. The old enrichment therefore left customers as **Facebook Contact**.

## Impact

- New Facebook DMs can resolve to the registered account name through the existing webhook enrichment path.
- Existing unresolved Facebook contacts can be repaired with the name-only resync.
- Staff-edited names remain protected by the existing overwrite guard.
- Normal live-message vehicle matching is unchanged; only the manual resync button is name-only.

author: slawa19
body:
Owner decision, 2026-08-04: audiobook mode gets **its own session** — code review, one run on a real book, eyes-on — rather than being folded into the current context.

The mode has never been systematically reviewed and has never been run end to end. Everything known about it so far surfaced as collateral while fixing other things, which is a poor basis for judging it.

## The requirement

**Drop the table of contents, the footnotes and the sources sections outright — but only where the region is clearly identifiable.** Nobody listens to a bibliography.

That is the opposite of every other operation, where those regions are passed through untouched — and it makes audiobook the *easy* case of the reference-material question that is otherwise still open, because here there is no argument about whether to keep the region, only about whether it can be recognised.

## The gap it points at

Already visible in the prompt: rule 1 tells the model to strip footnote markers, citations, DOI, ISBN and URLs, but **the model sees one block at a time**. Handed a whole bibliography entry, the honest answer is nothing — and a block that comes back empty is exactly the shape that produced the literal `(Пусто)` placeholders in the literary-edit run.

So the likely answer is **region exclusion before the model is called**, not a better prompt.

## What the spec carries

The context the next session would otherwise rediscover: the two entry points and how a defect can surface on a *translate* run; the narration validator change of 2026-08-03 and why the glyph gate must not be reinstated; that marker-mode paragraph restore applies here, and why that matters when the prompt legitimately empties a paragraph; that footnote markers now arrive as Unicode superscripts; and that cost is now measured, so this verdict can be made on the same terms the reader-cleanup verdict was.

Measure of success is stated plainly: **the manual post-editing removed**, not the defects enumerated.

Static tier 84 passed, 1 skipped.

author: dvrboxzone-bit
body:
## Signal Style Repair — quantitative constraints + 5 real few-shot examples

**Stacked on `fix/signal-jargon-guard` (PR #34, still open)** — base is that branch, not `main`, so this diff shows only what's new here.

## Baseline read (step 1)

Task's assumed path (`apps/web/lib/ai/prompts/enrichment-prompt.ts`) doesn't exist in this project — adjusted to the real path, `src/modules/signals/enrichment-prompt.ts` (same file PR #34 touches). Checked `strategic-score.ts` (the other AI-prompt file in this module) — confirmed its output schema is purely numeric (no text field), so it doesn't influence visible signal text and is correctly out of scope.

## What changed

- New **STYLE CONSTRAINTS** section (quantitative hard rules): 15-18 word average sentence length (25 max), 1-2 sentence paragraphs, target Flesch-Kincaid Grade 10-12 / Reading Ease 50-60, alternating short/medium sentence rhythm, ≥90% active voice, key claim at paragraph end, concrete-verb-with-object requirement.
- **5 new worked before/after examples** (jargon soup, abstract method, missing subject, buzzword removal, already-good-preserve) — appended after PR #34's existing 3, not replacing them.

## Owner-approved amendment: no fabricated numbers

Task's own Example 2 asked for `REQUIRED: "reduces CI failures by 15%"`-style numbers. Flagged before implementing: forcing the model to always produce a number, even when the source never stated one, risks fabricated statistics — contradicting this project's evidence-honesty stance. **Confirmed with owner**, then implemented an explicit guardrail: numbers only when the source itself states them; otherwise a concrete-but-non-numeric scale. Example 2's own AFTER text was adjusted accordingly (no invented percentage), modeling the guardrail directly in the few-shot the model learns from.

## Explicitly NOT done (task's own scope)

No FACT/INTERPRETATION/FORECAST/GAP structure, no `maxTokens`/model/temperature changes, no SEO metadata, no backfill of existing signals, no schema/API/auth/RLS changes.

## Validation (all live against this exact tree)

```
type-check -- 0 | lint -- 0 | test -- 0 (183/183, unaffected) | build -- 0
diff --check -- 0 | format check -- 0 (exactly 1 file: src/modules/signals/enrichment-prompt.ts)
```

## Known limitations

Same as PR #34: no real `GROQ_API_KEY` in this sandbox for live before/after generation — validated by prompt review + tests + build, not empirical output. Old signals not backfilled. No merge/production performed.

Card no orçamento (depois do escopo) + bloco na **carta do cliente** e no **link compartilhado**. Catálogo padrão: locução, trilha licenciada, legenda PT, janela de Libras, audiodescrição, legenda em outros idiomas, registro ANCINE, direitos de imagem do elenco — mais **período e praça de veiculação** e campo livre.

- **Status explícito por item** (incluso / não incluso / sob consulta / não se aplica) em vez de presença numa lista: não dizer nada sobre Libras ≠ dizer "não incluso" ≠ "sob consulta".
- **Nasce preenchido com o padrão da casa.** A tela é pra corrigir, não pra preencher do zero — campo em branco é campo que ninguém preenche, e a carta sai omissa de novo.
- **ANCINE** pergunta o regime só quando há registro a fazer. Internet está na lista de propósito: marcar "só internet" registra que a decisão foi tomada, não esquecida.
- No compartilhado anda junto da camada `escopo` — em flags separadas alguém mandaria metade.

Catálogo em `src/lib/condicoes.ts`, fonte única pro editor e pra carta. Migration `20260804010000` aplicada em produção.

## Что сделано

Компонент `KeyDownListener` доведён до AI-Ready (Phase 1, [TRI-48](https://linear.app/triplex-next/issue/TRI-48/keydownlistener-ai-ready-phase-1)) — закрыты все три колонки ROADMAP.

**AI refactoring**
- JSDoc на все props `IKeyDownListenerProps` и `IComposedKeyDownListenerProps`, на интерфейсы, класс и `handleKeyDown`.
- `handleKeyDown`: ветвление число/массив сведено к нормализации в массив + одна проверка `includes` — за счёт этого снят `eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-unused-expressions`. Поведение эквивалентно.
- `ComposedKeyDownListener`: убрано приведение `children as JSX.Element`, `let` + `for` заменены на `reduce` с сохранением порядка вложенности, убран избыточный guard, добавлен `displayName`.
- Внутренние (неэкспортируемые) `keyCode` → `TKeyCode` и `IKeyDownListenerManagerProps` → `IComposedKeyDownListenerProps` — по naming-конвенциям репозитория.

**Исправлено**
- `ComposedKeyDownListener` с пустым `keyDownListeners` и без `children` больше не возвращает `undefined` из рендера — на React 17 (ветка `release-0`) это приводило к ошибке «Nothing was returned from render».

**Stories** — `stories/KeyDownListener/` по modern pattern: `Playground`, `Default`, `WithMultipleKeys`, `Example: ComposedKeyDownListener`, `VisualTests`.

**Тесты** — 15 кейсов в двух новых файлах `__tests__/`, включая клавиатурные ветки, подписку/отписку на `window` и порядок вложенности слушателей в композиторе.

**Документация** — создан `KeyDownListener-ai.md`, отмечены колонки в `docs/ai/ROADMAP.md`, запись в release notes `v1/1.41.0.mdx`.

## Что НЕ менялось и почему

- **Публичный API не тронут**: props, их типы, `IKeyDownListenerProps`, имя класса, barrel-экспорты — как были. Переименованные тип-алиас и интерфейс не экспортировались (проверено по `origin/main` и barrel).
- **`KeyDownListener` остаётся class-компонентом** — переписывание на функциональный ломает публичный контракт (ref на инстанс, публичный метод `handleKeyDown`). Отдельная задача мажорного релиза.
- **`forwardRef` не добавлялся** — компоненты не рендерят собственный host-элемент, форвардить ref некуда (тот же осознанный отказ, что и у `Portal`). Зафиксировано в инвариантах AI.md.
- **`event.keyCode` не мигрировался на `event.key`** — устаревшее API, но миграция изменила бы наблюдаемое поведение и затронула бы `EVENT_KEYS.SPACE` и всех потребителей. Кандидат в отдельную задачу.

## Как проверить

- `npx vitest run src/components/KeyDownListener` — 15/15 зелёные; потребители (`SelectExtendedField`, `SliderExtended`, `Triggers`) — 45/45.
- `npx eslint src/components/KeyDownListener stories/KeyDownListener` — 0 errors / 0 warnings.

author: yury-knml
body:
Makes the Python samples on the Python via .NET pages correct.

## The problem

Every fenced `py`/`python` block in `en/python-net/` was parsed, its names resolved, and every
attribute reached through a module alias checked with `getattr` against the **installed
`aspose-slides` package**. Before this branch, **481 of 757 blocks were clean — 63.5%**.

Python starts from a better place than the other families here, so the interesting findings are not
missing imports. They are samples that are *silently wrong*.

## What changed

**Missing module imports (56 files).** Following the convention the corpus already uses — measured
from its own blocks: `import aspose.slides as slides` (540), `import aspose.pydrawing as draw`
(109), `import aspose.slides.charts as charts` (73). An alias was only added once every member the
block reaches through it was confirmed to exist in that module, so a missing import is never
swapped for a misleading `AttributeError`.

**Members that do not exist in the shipped package:**

- `slides.SlideSizeType.ON_SCREEN16X9` — the real member is `ON_SCREEN_16X9`
- `Html5Options.notes_comments_layouting` — gone; the current API is `slides_layout_options` with
  `NotesCommentsLayoutingOptions`

**Three bugs that would bite a reader at runtime, not at import time:**

- a sample binding `slides = presentation.slides`, which **shadows the module alias**, so every
  later `slides.*` reference in the block resolves against a slide collection
- a local named `type`, shadowing the builtin that the *next* loop iteration calls — the sample
  raises `TypeError` on any presentation with two video frames
- a removal loop calling `remove()` on a name that never existed in that section

**Blocks that were never valid Python.** Twenty carried `unexpected indent`: they had been cut out
of an enclosing `with` block and published as if they were top level, so pasting one is an
immediate `IndentationError`.

**Method-signature listings fenced as `py`** turned into runnable snippets, and undefined
`path +` prefixes replaced with the bare filenames the same pages already use in their `save()`
calls.

## Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Python blocks | 757 | 757 |
| clean | **481 (63.5%)** | **742 (98.0%)** |

## What is deliberately left

The `extracting-images-from-presentation-shapes` page opens with a prose-introduced **"Shared
Helper Methods"** section, and its later examples call those helpers on purpose. Making each block
standalone would mean duplicating ~60 lines into nine of them and contradicting the surrounding
prose. That is a page-structure decision, not a code fix, so nothing was changed there.

## Verification

Every edit was re-checked by re-running the analysis; nothing was kept unless it strictly reduced
that block's problem count. Samples were **not executed** — they write files and several need a
licence, and a missing attribute is already caught statically. Translations are untouched.

One note for whoever owns the API index tooling: introspection via `dir()` hides zero-valued enum
members, so `SlideSizeScaleType.DO_NOT_SCALE` and several `FillType` / `ShapeType` members are
absent from a generated index while existing perfectly well at runtime. "Not in the index" is not
safe to read as "does not exist" for enum members.

author: zjean
body:
Phase 2 of nine, following #432 and #433. The file browser's header, table and empty state rebuilt to the design's **D1/D2**. Other view modes untouched.

## The change with the most behavioural weight

**Selection no longer replaces the toolbar.** It used to swap the row's contents, moving `New` out from under the pointer at the moment the user was most likely to reach for it. The bulk-action bar now floats 16px above the content edge on `shadow-3`, and the toolbar stays put — verified in the browser with two rows selected.

Destructive is isolated past a spacer at the far right and stays text-on-tint until the confirm dialog.

## Table

- **Banding replaces dividers.** This is the design's answer to having a badge column: a hairline per row *plus* a badge column gives the eye two competing horizontal signals. Rows alternate surface-1/1.5, hover is a third value, no row borders at all.
- **Badges get their own 152px column** so the name column has one clean left edge. Favourite, lock and comments leave the name cell; the lock badge stays an *action* and keeps its mobile path. The now-empty Info column is gone.
- **Selection** is accent-tint plus a 2px cobalt marker drawn as `::before` on the inner content — never a border, which would shift the row's contents by 2px on select.
- **Density** is new: 36 / 44 / 56px, stored per view in `localStorage`, mirroring `viewModeStorageKey()` down to *why* it's a method rather than a repository field.

⚠️ **The density default is a real change.** v2 shipped 56px rows — the *relaxed* step — so everyone moves up one notch in information density.

## Toolbar, list end, empty state

Toolbar is the design's option **3b**: one filled cobalt primary, Upload earns a real secondary (it's the second-most-used action), Download from URL demotes to ghost, all at 36px.

The list ends in **totals plus the active sort, then a dashed drop affordance** — *"the folder ends in facts and a target, not in empty canvas"*. The totals count the **filtered** set, so the number under the list agrees with the rows above it.

The empty state is one bounded 560px panel, **left-aligned to the content gutter and never vertically centred**, so the page still reads top-down. Measured in place: left **260px** (hard against the gutter), width exactly **560**.

Loading is a skeleton at the current row height rather than the word "Loading…". The design forbids a spinner for a list, and a bare string is worse — it says nothing about the shape that's coming.

## Two things beyond this phase's plan

Both because the design calls them out, both small:

- **The filter is the `<app-v2-input>` primitive now**, which deleted ~55 lines of hand-rolled fill/border/focus/hint styling that had drifted out of the palette. ⌘F focuses *through* the component; `select()` went with the `ElementRef`, since the primitive owns its `<input>` and exposing the node just to select text would hand every caller write access to it.
- **The placeholder names the folder you're in.** `repository.filterPlaceholder` was a per-screen constant that said "Filter in Personal…" three folders deep — the opposite of *"placeholders describe scope"*. The screenshot below is what caught it.

## Tests

Four density cases in the shared browser contract — default, stored value, unknown value, and persistence-with-row-height — pinned for the same reason view mode is, plus the default matters on its own.

The harness gains an `L10nTranslationService` stub that returns the **key and its params** rather than prose, so a copy edit isn't a test failure.

`npm run test` from the root: lint clean, **2433** backend, **449** frontend.

### D1 — banded rows, badge column, list footer, one primary
![list](https://github.com/zjean/server/raw/c91a7243c593096a495b46f630a0ff99e0eb2935/docs/screenshots/2026-08-04-browser-list.png)

### The bulk bar floats; the toolbar keeps its primary
![bulk bar](https://github.com/zjean/server/raw/c91a7243c593096a495b46f630a0ff99e0eb2935/docs/screenshots/2026-08-04-browser-bulk-bar.png)

### D2 — bounded panel, left-aligned to the gutter, shortcut hints
![empty](https://github.com/zjean/server/raw/c91a7243c593096a495b46f630a0ff99e0eb2935/docs/screenshots/2026-08-04-browser-empty.png)

## Still owed

The design's `⌘K`-adjacent shortcut hints (`N`, `U`) are *printed* in the empty state but not yet **bound** — that's phase 8's ambient-keyboard work. Grid and gallery still use the old geometry; gallery is phase 6.

Refs #432 #433

author: amaurymagalhaes
body:
## Overview

AEO-12 experiment **E4** ([DEV-595](https://linear.app/showkarma/issue/DEV-595)) — contract pre-registered in `artifacts/aeo-measurement/experiments.md`. Draft on purpose: copy AND an auth-surface change need human review before the ready-PR AI stack spends.

**Revised per reviewer feedback**: the "Nonprofit research for donor advisors" answer block originally sat at the footer of `/nonprofit-research` and read as bolted onto the product page. It now lives as a knowledge-base article at **`/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence`**, following the established `app/knowledge/*` pattern (Article JSON-LD, truthful per-article date from `articleDates.ts`, knowledge index entry, static sitemap entry, llms.txt category map). `/nonprofit-research` stays public and indexable with the experiment title/meta, and keeps a footnote-level one-liner linking to the article (per a second review pass, the descriptive intro sentence was removed and the pointer shrunk to text-xs muted with tight padding).

## Contract (binding, from experiments.md)

Changed cohort **C13** (/nonprofit-research), control **C12** (/donor-advisors — interference caveat documented). Target prompts: P003, P004, P009, P017, P024, P034, P041, P042. Pass = citations earned on target prompts and citation-share movement beats C12 across two consecutive 7-day windows from ship date. releases.csv row at ship time.

## Contract note (E4 measurement after the reviewer's change)

The E4 contract targeted `/nonprofit-research` (C13) as the single changed surface carrying the diligence Q&A in its server HTML. Per review, the experiment now ships as a **two-surface change**, and the ship-time rows should be written accordingly (artifacts/ is deliberately NOT edited in this PR):

- **Informational prompts (P003, P004, P009, P017, P024, P034, P041, P042)** now target `/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence`: that page carries the full Q&A, the FAQPage JSON-LD, and the Article JSON-LD with `datePublished: 2026-08-04`. Any citation earned on these prompts is expected to land on the knowledge article URL, not on `/nonprofit-research`.
- **C13 (`/nonprofit-research`) keeps the buyer-intent framing**: the measurable change to that URL is now noindex removal + public index + experiment title/meta + a footnote-level one-liner linking to the article. Citation movement on C13 itself would come from indexability and title/meta, not from answer content.
- The knowledge article is a **new URL** with no baseline of its own (baseline citation share is zero by construction), so the E4 pass criterion "citation-share movement beats C12" should be evaluated on the combined pair (C13 + the article) or the article alone, and the releases.csv row at ship time should record both URLs so the windows can be attributed correctly.
- The article also feeds the existing knowledge-base distribution channels (`/knowledge` index, static sitemap, llms.txt generation via `scripts/generate-llms-txt.ts` CATEGORY_MAP), which C13 alone never had. That is an intentional confound in favor of the informational prompts and worth noting in the measurement row.

## Contract ambiguity found (flagging explicitly)

The contract's hypothesis says the page "does not state in server HTML what the product verifies." Reality is stronger: **the route had no public content at all** — the entire section is a signed-in client workspace, the index rendered only a client-side sign-in card, and the page carried `robots: { index: false }`. Earning citations or GSC presence required (a) public server-rendered content and (b) dropping the noindex. Both are in this PR; **the noindex removal and the layout gating change are deliberate scope calls for the reviewer to confirm.**

## What changed

- **New knowledge article `/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence`** ("Nonprofit Due Diligence for Donor Advisors", published 2026-08-04):
  - Carries the full 8-question diligence Q&A (single source `app/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence/content.ts`), rendered visibly and mirrored 1:1 in FAQPage JSON-LD.
  - Follows the knowledge-page pattern exactly: Breadcrumbs + BreadcrumbJsonLd, ArticleJsonLd with `datePublished` from `articleDates.ts` (no `dateModified`), visible `ArticlePublishedDate`, "In one sentence" / "Short answer" intro sections, related-article links, and a "Karma's role" section linking back to `/nonprofit-research`.
  - Registered in the `/knowledge` index (new "Nonprofit research" section), the static sitemap, and the llms.txt CATEGORY_MAP.
  - Every claim still traces to gap-indexer donor-research code: the four compliance checks exactly as implemented in `compliance-checks.ts` (IRS Pub 78 with the 990-freshness proxy, Form 990 within the last 3 years, **California AG charity registry for CA orgs — deliberately NOT broadened to "state registration" generally**, a test enforces this, and 990 governance signals), the five advisor-weighted composite dimensions (`composite-weights.ts`), the DEV-428 diligence-questionnaire surface, and the approved `FILINGS_STATS` copy (2M+ filings, $1.2T tracked). Comparison copy is positioned on Karma's workflow only; a test asserts no claims about what Candid/Charity Navigator do or lack.
- **Index becomes a public page, auth posture unchanged**: the section layout stops auth-gating/shell-wrapping this one route; a new `ResearchIndexExperience` client component reproduces the exact prior per-state UI (gate skeleton → sign-in gate → advisor shell + workspace). All other donor-research routes stay layout-gated; advisor queries still run only when signed in. Layout tests updated to encode the new contract; new experience tests cover all three states.
- **`/nonprofit-research` server content**: a footnote-level one-liner below the experience linking to the knowledge article (text-xs, muted, tight padding, no section framing). The footer FAQ block and page-level FAQPage JSON-LD are gone. Note: the page's non-chrome server-rendered text is now only this one-liner and the served HTML has no h1, so it would likely flag as thin under the DEV-586 crawler bar; see the verification comment for the numbers and options.
- **Title/meta**: "Nonprofit Research & Due Diligence for Donor Advisors" through the site-wide `| Karma` template; noindex dropped; route added to the static sitemap.

## Facts wanted but NOT verifiable (left out)

- Any state charity registry beyond the California AG (the product checks exactly one state registry today).
- Counts of nonprofits/organizations covered beyond the approved 2M-filings copy — no live public endpoint feeds this page, so no number is rendered dynamically.
- Any claim about competitors' product capabilities.

## Server-HTML verification (pnpm build && pnpm start, curl)

See the latest verification comment on this PR for the post-move curl proof of both `/nonprofit-research` and `/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence`.

## Tests

- `__tests__/app/knowledge/nonprofit-due-diligence.test.tsx` (12): all prior content guards (four real compliance checks, CA-AG scoping, five ranking dimensions, no competitor-capability claims, no ChatGPT) plus server-rendered assertions on the article page: every Q&A present in static markup, FAQPage JSON-LD 1:1 with visible content, Article JSON-LD carries the recorded 2026-08-04 date, link back to `/nonprofit-research`. A new guard asserts no em dashes in reader-visible copy.
- `ResearchIndexExperience.test.tsx` (3): loading / signed-out / signed-in states.
- `DonorResearchLayout.account-switch.test.tsx` updated: account isolation now exercised on a still-gated route; new case documents that the index page owns its gate.
- `knowledge-article-dates.test.tsx` provenance map auto-covers the new slug. Full donor-research + sitemap + scripts suites green.

author: lenhador88
body:
Every read function in `lib/data` wrote `const { data } = await query` and returned `data ?? []`.

That is not a default — it's a lie. **"No postcards exist" and "the query failed" are different answers**, and collapsing them renders the feed's empty state to every rider with nothing in the logs.

Seven call sites did it. Only `lib/data/media.ts` captured the error.

## This was not hypothetical

`011` added a `comments_count:postcard_comments(count)` embed. Deploying that code before the table existed would have failed the **whole** feed query in PostgREST — and produced `/postcards` showing *"No postcards yet"* rather than an error. CI was green either way.

It was caught by reading the code before merging #22, which is the wrong thing to have to rely on — twice in one day, after `/postcards/new` shipped dead through a fully green pipeline.

## What changed

`unwrap()` / `unwrapList()` throw a `DataReadError` that names which read failed and carries the PostgREST code. Every read in `lib/data` goes through them.

A structural type keeps the module free of `@supabase/supabase-js` imports — the same reason `columns.ts` stays import-free.

**`getPostcard` moves from `.single()` to `.maybeSingle()`** as a direct consequence: `single()` reports "no row" *as an error*, which would now throw for a postcard the viewer simply may not see. Not-found and could-not-ask have to stay distinct, and that distinction is asserted.

## Throwing needs somewhere to land

`app/(app)/error.tsx` catches it and offers a retry. It deliberately shows **no** detail beyond Next's `digest` — the PostgREST code and failing relation belong in the server log, not on a rider's screen, and the digest is what makes a bug report findable.

## What this deliberately does not do

It does not distinguish transient failures from structural ones. A timeout and a missing table both throw. Classifying them means mapping PostgREST codes, and a wrong classification would restore exactly the silent-degradation this PR removes. **Complexity 5/10, recommendation 3/10** — worth revisiting only if transient failures turn out to be common enough to be annoying.

## Verification

- **222 unit tests** (was 214) — the new ones pin that an empty result stays empty, that a failed query throws *even when the driver also hands back rows*, and that "not found" and "could not ask" stay distinguishable
- 264 RLS assertions, typecheck, lint and build clean

author: nolanjaycee2qve0a8-boop
body:
## Summary

- Add immutable `ObjectiveCapabilityActivationComposition`.
- Add abstract, stateless
  `ObjectiveCapabilityActivationCompositionBoundary`.
- Relate one exact objective to one complete active capability collection.
- Preserve exact objective, collection, tuple, order, and descriptor identities.

## Architecture

```text
ObjectiveDescriptor             ActiveCapabilityCollection
        |                                  |
        +----------------------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
          ObjectiveCapabilityActivationCompositionBoundary
                                           |
                                           v
             ObjectiveCapabilityActivationComposition
```

## Contract

- Composition stores the exact objective input.
- Composition stores the exact complete `ActiveCapabilityCollection` input.
- No second capability subset is accepted, preventing implicit omission or
  selection.
- Duplicate active descriptor identities are rejected.
- Reconstructed capability descriptors cannot enter through a valid active
  collection.
- No concrete production composition implementation is introduced.

## Non-goals

- No selection, ranking, priority, scoring, or weighting.
- No optimization, conflict resolution, or fallback.
- No Capability activation logic, instance creation, or execution.
- No `DecisionIntent` generation or resolution.
- No Constraint, Evaluation, Runtime, Execution, Device, CAN, or Modbus
  dependency.
- No persistence, telemetry, cache, or history.

## Validation

- pytest: 1027 passed
- ruff check .: passed
- ruff format --check .: passed
- mypy .: passed
- pre-commit run --all-files: passed

body:
## Resumo

Correções encontradas em um pentest completo (LP + admin + extensão) solicitado antes da publicação na Chrome Web Store.

author: suavecito585
body: Closes THE-723. Two compounding bugs took `audit_reports` from 2 writes/day to **243**. Neither alone produces that number. ## 1. The backoff cap had become a global 5-minute ceiling `effInterval` computed: ```ts Math.min(intervalMs * 2 ** consecutiveFailures, this.maxBackoffMs) // 5 * 60_000 ``` That is a backoff cap only while `intervalMs <= maxBackoffMs`. Above it, and with `failures = 0`, it reduces to `min(intervalMs, 5min)` — and `effInterval` computes **every** next-run, including the success path. A backoff cap shorter than the base interval does not slow a failing job down; it speeds every slow job up. Measured on the live store via the scheduler's own `job_schedule` table (`next_run_at - last_run_at`): | job | designed | actual | factor | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `plane-enqueue` | 240 min | 300.1s | 48× | | `maintenance-sweep` | 60 min | 300.3s | 12× | | `activation-recompute` | 60 min | 300.3s | 12× | | `note-quality-enqueue` | 60 min | 300.3s | 12× | | `goal-expiry` | 60 min | 300.8s | 12× | | `episode-evaluation` | 60 min | 300.3s | 12× | | `job-queue-runner` | 15s | 15.6s | 1× (below cap) | Now `Math.max(backoff, intervalMs)`. Backoff still grows exponentially and is still bounded by `maxBackoffMs`; it simply cannot schedule a job sooner than that job's own interval. **It survived since THE-462 because every test in `scheduler.test.ts` registers `intervalMs: 1000`** — entirely below the cap, the region where `Math.min` always picks the interval and the clamp cannot fire. ## 2. `replaceIfTerminal` defeated the plane's period keys THE-700 set it on the two PERIOD-keyed plane jobs so one failure would not cost the whole period. But `enqueue()` treats `complete` as terminal too, so every tick deleted and re-ran the plane's own **successful** work. This regressed a contract the option's own docblock states: *"Off by default so the plane's once-per-period dedup (a completed weekly synthesis must block re-runs) is unaffected."* New `EnqueueOptions.replaceIfFailed` is the narrow form: replaces a `failed` row, still dedups against `complete`. `synthesis` and `audit` switch to it, preserving THE-700's guarantee. `contradiction` keeps `replaceIfTerminal` — that key is content-hashed and replace-on-complete is deliberate there. ## Gates, each watched failing on the old code first | gate | on old code | | --- | --- | | job slower than the cap runs on its interval | `expected 6 to be +0` | | backoff on a fast job is still capped | guards the inverse bug | | `replaceIfFailed` skips a COMPLETE row | id mismatch | | completed synthesis not replaced on next tick | `expected 'queued' to be 'complete'` | | completed audit not replaced on next tick | `expected 'queued' to be 'complete'` | The new scheduler test deliberately registers a 60-minute interval and says why in a comment, so the fixture that hid this cannot hide it again. ## Blast radius, assessed deliberately `job-queue-runner` (15s) is the job that actually **drains** queued work, and it was below the cap and is untouched. This PR changes *enqueue and sweep* cadence, not work-draining responsiveness — nothing user-facing gets slower. Every restored interval is the designed one. The fast cadence is the anomaly and is only 14 days old (THE-462, 2026-07-21). One interaction was checked: the 12× accelerated `maintenance-sweep` was partly compensating for the 48× `plane-enqueue`, but the `jobs` table holds only 178 rows today, so pruning is comfortably ahead of creation even now, and creation drops ~48× after this. `next_run_at` is persisted, so each job's first post-deploy run still fires on the old schedule then settles. Self-correcting within one cycle. ## Verification - `bun run typecheck` — exit 0, all four packages - **105 tests passed** across the 12 test files naming the changed symbols, enumerated by grep rather than by picking the obvious file - `bun run lint` — exit 0 - `check:boundaries`, `check:duplicate-exports`, `check:export-surface`, `check:duplication`, `check:config-paths` — all exit 0 - `bun run map` re-run last 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? ### Summary

This PR adds explicit quantum and classical register support across the circuit model, backend API, circuit editor, simulator, and results view.

- Added register management for quantum and classical registers, including creating/deleting registers and adding/removing qubits or classical bits.

- Added UI flows for managing registers and selecting a classical bit when placing measurement gates.
- Reworked circuit rendering to display quantum and classical register sections, including collapsible classical registers and separate classical wire styling.
- Improved drag/drop and scheduling logic so operations are placed only on valid quantum rows and collisions are handled consistently.
- Reworked simulation execution to support single-qubit and mid-circuit measurements, classical memory/readout, measurement mappings, shot-based outcomes, and optional final readout of unmeasured qubits.
- Updated the results view to show measurement/readout histograms, outcome tables, measurement mappings, endianness/order controls, filters, and large-circuit warnings.
- Added and updated backend/frontend tests around registers, measurements, simulation translation, chart data, and results rendering.

author: vmuliadi-astro
body:
## Problem

The gateway logs only `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` / `total_tokens` on its "LLM response" debug line. Providers like DeepSeek (via Cloudflare AI Gateway) report cache metadata in the same `usage` object:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 85,
  "completion_tokens": 10,
  "total_tokens": 95,
  "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0},
  "prompt_cache_hit_tokens": 0,
  "prompt_cache_miss_tokens": 85
}
```

This metadata is parsed but then discarded: `UsageInfo` has no fields for it, and the debug log line never emits it. Any token-usage collector consuming the log therefore cannot report the real cache hit/miss split — it can only estimate (or treat cache as unknown).

## Fix

1. **`pkg/providers/protocoltypes/types.go`** — extend `UsageInfo` with:
   - `PromptCacheHitTokens *int` (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, DeepSeek-style)
   - `PromptCacheMissTokens *int` (`prompt_cache_miss_tokens`)
   - `PromptTokensDetails *PromptTokensDetails` (`prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, OpenAI-compatible style)

   Pointers distinguish "provider did not report" (nil) from a real zero (cold cache).

2. **`pkg/agent/pipeline_llm.go`** — surface those fields on the `LLM response` debug log line when present.

No provider behavior changes; purely additive logging. Verified against a live DeepSeek-via-AIG call and a full rebuild on linux/arm64.

author: arnazxx
body:
The first working version of the SDK: `init({ baseUrl, project })` + `getToken()` / `deleteToken()` / `onMessage()` / `isSupported()`, plus the self-contained service-worker bundle.

**Design highlights**
- **Stable tokens**: a per-browser installation id (minted once, stored in IndexedDB) keys the server registration, so browser endpoint rotation, VAPID key rotation, and `pushsubscriptionchange` all refresh the same token. Re-binding is only ever needed after a user clears site data.
- **Service worker** (`dist/sw.js`): always shows the notification, fires the best-effort delivered beacon, opens the tracking URL on click, forwards payloads to open pages (`onMessage`), and re-registers on `pushsubscriptionchange` without any page open.
- **Zero runtime deps**; page bundle ~9 KB ESM / ~10 KB IIFE before gzip.
- Typed error codes to branch on: `not-initialized | unsupported | permission-blocked | subscribe-failed | request-failed`.

**Toolchain**: plain npm + TypeScript (strict) + tsup + vitest (happy-dom, fake-indexeddb). 41 tests; CI runs typecheck → test → build.

**Try it**: `npm install && npm run build`, then `npx serve .` and open `/playground/` — point it at any Moonsender server.

author: delpicorp
body:
Adds [dev-report](https://github.com/delpicorp/dev-report) as an external link, matching the other entries in that section. The skill lives in its own repository.

### What it does

You finish a long Claude Code session. A dozen files changed and several implementation decisions were made along the way, but the end-of-session summary is file names and function names — accurate, and written for someone reading the diff alongside it. Asking for it "simply" removes the reasoning too.

`/dev-report` explains the session in plain language instead: what was built or changed, why that approach was chosen, what is still unfinished or unverified, and what to do next.

Technical terms aren't stripped out — they're explained the moment they first appear, so the reasoning survives. Two rules do most of the work: every finding leads with the raw artifact (the actual log line, the actual count) before it gets explained, and the section on how a problem was solved has to name the option that was rejected and what would have gone wrong.

### Details

```
/plugin marketplace add delpicorp/dev-report
/plugin install dev-report@delpicorp
```

- Single skill — no agents, hooks, or MCP servers. About 380 always-on tokens.
- Explicit-only, so it does not fire on a casual "what did you just do?"
- Reports come out in whatever language the command was typed in. Aliases ship for Korean (`/개발보고`), Japanese (`/開発報告`), and Spanish (`/informe-desarrollo`). File paths, function names, and log lines always stay in their original form.
- Two worked example reports ship in the repo (illustrative, not real customer sessions).
- MIT licensed. Disclosure: I'm the author.

Happy to reword or move the entry if it fits better elsewhere.

## Summary

- `VmwareRestConnector.fingerprint()` probed only `GET /api/about`, which is the **ESXi host REST surface** — vCenter answers 404, so every vCenter target permanently read `reachable=false`. The probe now runs the fallback chain from #2765: `/api/about` (kept first — richest for ESXi, regression-pinned) → on **404 specifically** the unauthenticated `GET /sdk/vimServiceVersions.xml` version-discovery document (`reachable=true` + the vim25 API version) → best-effort authenticated `GET /api/appliance/system/version` (VCSA-only; supplies authoritative `version`/`build` and observed `product="vcenter"`; any failure is swallowed so absence never turns a reachable fingerprint red).
- The unreachable arm no longer hardcodes `product="vcenter"` — it reports the target's registered product (else `"unknown"`), since a failed probe observed nothing. `probe_method` truthfully names every endpoint the chain used/attempted.
- Optional item from the issue implemented as a non-breaking internal improvement: `_about_version` reuses the same discovery read on an `/api/about` 404, so the VI-JSON `{release}` derivation (`/sdk/vim25/{release}`, #2466) now works on vCenter too — the discovery document's four-part vim25 version is exactly the VI-JSON release segment; the existing single `/api` fallback is unchanged.
- XML is parsed with `defusedxml` (in-repo idiom, pfsense connector precedent); the parser handles both the modern un-namespaced document and the older `http://www.vmware.com/vi/versions`-namespaced variant (both shapes verified against pyVim's `__VersionIsSupported` parser and govmomi's simulator template), and never lets `priorVersions` shadow the current version.

author: iamacoffeepot
body:
Second implementation slice of ADR-0172. The ribbon draw pass renders every curve unclipped; its vertex stage reads the stroke-parameter field at each vertex's own texel and folds the point's verdict, reach, run arc and curve coverage into one width scale. Hidden points scale to zero and their segments rasterize nothing, so the runs the CPU used to cut are not cut anywhere — they are what is left once the hidden widths vanish.

Measured on `main` at **992421fde** (before #4431's executor-pass caching, which may move the pacing numbers).

## Retirement

`visibility::runs` and the per-run `ribbon` leave the per-frame loop, as does the streamed `DrawTriangle` ink send. The CPU split survives as `Puppet::split` — the parity oracle, and the wash's flow source, which now runs behind the easel's settle gate instead of on every frame. `Subject.drawn` became a closure so that deferral is expressed in the type rather than by discipline.

## Fixed-framing A/B, 900x1200, kitsune-fine + `cache/144_material_labels_256.npy`

Luminance histogram over the whole frame; `px<120` is "clearly inked".

| | mean luminance | px<90 | px<120 | px<150 | px<180 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, az 0 | 230.47 | 14 | 31,982 | 48,495 | 89,030 |
| **this, az 0** | **230.22** | 10 | 35,862 | 50,652 | 90,073 |
| main, az 55 | 225.56 | 20 | 29,746 | 77,378 | 145,467 |
| **this, az 55** | **225.15** | 18 | 35,907 | 81,708 | 146,526 |

Mean luminance lands within 0.25 and 0.41 — the total ink is the same drawing. The distribution shifts slightly toward the darker bands (`px<120` up 12% and 21%), which is the supersampled composite resolving a stroke into fewer, denser pixels where 4x MSAA spread it into more, lighter ones. `px<90` stays in single/low double digits on both sides, so nothing is going hard-edged.

**Boundary drift is real and expected.** Taper anchors move from CPU run ends to the field's reach, so a stroke running into an occluder now thins into it over about one point of arc instead of cutting hard — the ADR's stated intent. At a curve's own end the barrier texel carries zero arc so the anchor is exact; only a run ended by a hidden point carries the two boundary arcs into its total.

**Whole-or-nothing holds at grazing azimuths.** At az 55 her visible eye arrives complete — lash, iris and brow as whole marks — and the occluded one is absent entirely rather than shattered into crumbs. The consumer applies the run-of-at-least-two rule itself (three `SEEN` reads) so an isolated survivor between two hidden points draws nothing, which is the crumb `visibility::runs` drops when it discards a run of one.

## Crispness: the honest verdict

**2x supersample is not worse than 4x MSAA here, and I did not need to measure 3x.** The evidence is the histogram above rather than an impression: at both azimuths the ink lands at the same total weight with a slightly *tighter* distribution, which is what a real raster resolved by a bilinear tap does against coverage-reconstructed samples. Lid, lash and hatch edges read as clean at 1:1. What changed in kind is that ink is no longer anti-aliased by the world pass at all — it is resolved on the way down from a 2x sheet — so the failure mode to watch in future is a canvas whose long edge makes the sheet exceed texture limits, not edge quality.

## Pacing — release wasm, no captures in the timed loop (#4422)

`cargo xtask dist --no-bins --profile release`, whole-frame, 900x1200.

| | main (992421fde) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| static frame | 1.03 ms | **0.45 ms** |
| orbit frame (ceiling, incl. harness settlement) | 41.17 ms | **51.17 ms** |
| develop (one-shot) | 604 ms | 562 ms |

**The static frame more than halves** — the drawing is retained pixels now, so a still view resends nothing.

**The orbit frame regresses by ~10 ms, and that is the headline finding.** It is not where the ADR expected to land (~10–11 ms extraction plus ~5 ms of GPU). The occlusion rays did leave the CPU, but they were replaced by shipping the whole drawing through mail every re-split: roughly 8.5 MB of field points plus 14 MB of ribbon vertices per frame at this drawing's scale. ADR-0171's own guidance names this shape — "a few kilobytes per frame is mail like any other, a character mesh per frame is not" — and 192k points is the second case. Moving the bytes instead of cloning them changed nothing measurable (51.01 → 51.17 ms), which is what says the cost is the mail path rather than the copy.

So the GPU work is cheap and the transport is not. The next lever is resident, incrementally-updated stroke geometry rather than a full re-upload per eye — worth its own issue, and it is the same lever the animation arc will need.

## Judgement calls

**No depth prepass, deviating from ADR-0172.** The record has the ink depth-tested against a prepass of the subject. Measured, that prepass removed nearly half the ink — `px<120` of 18,706 against 31,982, where dropping the depth test alone gave 35,862. The drawing's points are level-set crossings *on* the surface, so every stroke is coplanar with what it would be tested against, and a `Depth32Float` spanning 0.05–40 has little precision left at 5.4; biasing moved the fight around without settling it. It was also asking a question the field already answers per point, against the oracle's own semantics and under a parity test. The CPU path never depth-tested against the subject either — the mesh is never drawn — so leaving it out is parity with the drawing this has to match. What is given up is stroke-versus-stroke ordering; on this drawing it is not visible, and the histogram is the evidence.

**Its own program, because the supersample has to *be* the reference extent.** `SlotExtent` only divides, so the 2x sheet is the reference — which lands the canvas-resolution field planes exactly on `Divided { divisor: 2 }`. A depth attachment must match its colour attachment's size, so the field's canvas-resolution prepass could never have shared a slot with a pass writing at twice that; the two programs meet through registry textures instead, which is what the field's planes already are.

**Group-1 inputs widened to `VERTEX_FRAGMENT`** in `aether-substrate/src/render/program.rs` — shared surface, called out deliberately. The vertex stage could not read the field at all otherwise, which is ADR-0172's core mechanism. Precedented by the group-0 uniform, already `VERTEX_FRAGMENT` with the comment "visibility a stage does not use costs nothing"; WGSL still confines derivative sampling to the fragment stage, so this grants `textureLoad` and nothing more.

**The field gained a `TOTAL` plane and two directional scans.** `style::pressure` ramps over `min(RAMP, total * 0.45)`, so the taper needs the run's *arc*, not only the distance to its nearest end — and a symmetric `min` collapses head and tail before they can be added. The reach scan splits in two over a shared arc chain (+5 passes). `REACH` is unchanged and the merged parity gate still passes; without this every stroke under ~20 page pixels thins systematically, which is a look change rather than boundary drift.

**A camera-facing billboard rather than a screen rect**, which is also what removes the `WindowSize` dependency: the rect spans the frustum's cross-section at its own depth, so only its *aspect* has to agree with the view and its resolution is a free quality choice.

**`draws_scenario` primes twelve frames rather than one.** Program-rendered ink reaches the frame only once the register and the creates have answered; streamed triangles needed no warm-up. The wash layer has always behaved this way.

## Shared-file touches

`easel/mod.rs` — `Subject.drawn` becomes a closure and `develop` calls it past the gate. Minimal and additive, but flagged per the sibling coordination on `feat/realtime-easel-loop`: merge order is theirs, and I will rebase.

Closes #4419

author: delpicorp
body:
Adds **dev-report** to the **Documentation** section, vendored under `plugins/dev-report/` to match how every other plugin in this repo is listed. Also added to `README-zh.md`.

### What it does

You finish a long Claude Code session. A dozen files changed and several implementation decisions were made along the way, but the end-of-session summary is file names and function names — accurate, and written for someone reading the diff alongside it. Asking for it "simply" removes the reasoning too.

`/dev-report` explains the session in plain language instead:

- what was built or changed, in terms of the product rather than the file tree
- why that approach was chosen, including the option that was rejected and what would have gone wrong
- what is still unfinished or unverified — verified, assumed, and untested kept apart
- what to do next, and which calls are the user's to make

Technical terms aren't stripped out — they're explained the moment they first appear, so the reasoning survives.

### What's in the folder

```
plugins/dev-report/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
├── README.md            # description + attribution
├── SKILL.md             # the skill itself
├── commands/            # /dev-report + ko · ja · es aliases
├── references/          # craft.md, examples.md (two worked example reports)
└── LICENSE              # MIT
```

Markdown only — no agents, hooks, scripts, or MCP servers. About 380 always-on tokens. Explicit-only, so it does not fire on a casual "what did you just do?". Reports come out in whatever language the command was typed in.

### Attribution

Original: [delpicorp/dev-report](https://github.com/delpicorp/dev-report), MIT. Vendored unmodified at v1.0.1 except for the folder README and a `plugin.json` trimmed to the fields this repo uses. Attribution and the upstream marketplace install are both in `plugins/dev-report/README.md`, so anyone wanting updates can install from source. Disclosure: I'm the author.

Happy to move it to a different category if Documentation isn't the right fit.

Both proven by in-process-built workbooks. PDF stays formally descoped pending the HAD-120 consent design, as the stage-1 amendment records.
- **#68 (HAD-129)** — the signed-out landing at `/` with the reference dashboard moved behind `/example`; its e2e assertion fixed to accept the `trailingSlash`-rewritten href it actually renders.

## Phase 2 workstreams
- **D1 (HAD-118)** — `lib/ai/wording.ts` + a server-only Anthropic call: a model words the deterministic working, never computes it. A validator rejects the whole generation if it contains one number the engine did not compute. No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → the report renders exactly as before.
- **D2 (HAD-119)** — "Ask about your figures" on `/entitlement`: every fact on the model's sheet carries the route of the screen that proves it, every accepted answer must cite one (rendered as a real link), and a question the sheet cannot answer gets a fixed refusal. Same key gate.
- **HAD-83/HAD-110 (option A)** — the projection stops counting the settlement from day zero (`projectCashWithSettlementArrival`, arrival at last day + `SETTLEMENT_DUE_DAYS`), and `atRisk` becomes derived, never stored: a payment is at risk when the projected balance immediately before its due date cannot cover it. The seed's two hand-flagged rows derive clean; the flags land where the projection genuinely cannot cover. A test pins that mark-paid/un-mark cannot destroy the flag.

## Review fixes and gaps
- **HAD-13/HAD-113 (code half)** — the reminder sender delivers web push beside email: same copy, same send-once log under `channel: 'push'`, dead subscriptions pruned; dry-runs honestly without the VAPID pair.

- **HAD-127 (code half)** — Show/Hide toggle on every password field, inert before hydration, invisible to password managers.
- **HAD-77 §4** — the `signIn` comment stops claiming enumeration protection it never bought; the posture is now a decision on record.

## Documentation

Figma work landed directly in the **Fintec — Phase 2** file (`EoBOWZhkP9ZrY9gpEdeC78`): six new frames, `accent/*` interactive tokens from the code's `--s1` palette, spacing/radius fully bound. The design record in this PR describes it.

author: gordon1210
body:
## Summary

- run file analysis and duplication tokenization in one scan-wide Rayon pool governed by `--jobs`
- preserve deterministic detector output and the frozen public detector interfaces
- move source contents into the duplication corpus instead of cloning them, and persist the incremental cache before expensive cross-file work
- expose bounded tokenization progress in the terminal and debug log
- update Deep Review, tests, documentation, the bundled skill, and its repository mirror

## Root cause

The per-file analyzer created a configured Rayon pool, but that pool was dropped before cross-file analysis. Duplication preparation then tokenized every file through a serial iterator, so large scans could remain at `tokenizing files for duplication` while using only one CPU core.

## Impact

Duplication tokenization now honors the configured worker count without changing public detector behavior. On the repository benchmark, warm tokenization improved from 276 ms with one worker to 48 ms with ten workers (about 5.8×), while peak RSS increased by roughly 10 MiB.

## Validation

- `cargo test` — 374 unit tests, 156 CLI integration tests, 3 language-matrix tests, and doc tests passed
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `./scripts/check-rust-file-size.sh`
- `./scripts/reposcout-skill.sh check`
- release build and RepoScout working-tree change review
- deterministic output regression test across one and four workers
- explicit single-worker and multi-worker scheduling regression test

`cargo audit` was not available locally; the Rust CI workflow installs the pinned audit tool and runs it.

THIS CONTRADICTION IS IRONIC: IT USES THE LANGUAGE OF AUTHORITY TO DENOUNCE AUTHORITY. THE LACK OF LOWERCASE LETTERS ALSO DEHUMANIZES THE STATEMENT, MAKING IT FEEL MECHANICAL, RIGID, AND UNCOMPROMISING—THE VERY QUALITIES IT CLAIMS TO REJECT. IN EFFECT, THE FORM UNDERMINES THE CONTENT, TURNING A CALL FOR ETHICAL AWARENESS INTO A DOGMATIC PROCLAMATION THAT MAY, IN PRACTICE, JUSTIFY ARBITRARY DISREGARD FOR LAW AND ORDER.

author: productdevbook
body:
A background image was written to xl/media/imageN.png and declared
image/png whatever it actually was. Verified with a real JPEG:

  writeXlsx media parts : [ 'xl/media/image1.png' ]
  content-type defaults : <Default Extension="png" ContentType="image/png"/>
  bytes at image1.png   : magic = 0xff 0xd8 0xff   (JPEG)
  saveXlsx media parts  : [ 'xl/media/image1.png' ]

So the OPC package declared a content type that did not match the part it
pointed at. Excel sniffs image bytes and renders it anyway, which is why
nobody noticed — but it is a spec violation, a validator flags it, and a
workbook that came out of Excel with a JPEG background came back from
hucre mislabelled.

Sniffing the format from the bytes rather than adding a `type` field to
match SheetImage. Sheet.backgroundImage is a bare Uint8Array and the
reader discards the source extension, so by the time the writer runs the
bytes are the only thing left to be faithful to — a type field would be
public API surface for something derivable, and would do nothing for the
round-trip path, which never had a type to carry. Unrecognised bytes
still fall back to png, so an exotic format is no worse off than before.

The sniffer returns SheetImage["type"], which is exactly the set the
content-type map declares, so the two cannot drift apart.

writeXlsx and saveXlsx had one copy each of the media-path loop, which is
how they came to share one bug — they now share one helper instead.

Found while reviewing PR #375 against what landed in #380. The two
implementations agree with each other, including on this.

SVG is the one that needed care: it is text, so it has no magic number.
The check looks for the root tag within a bounded head rather than
anchoring at byte 0 (a declaration, doctype, BOM or whitespace can come
first) and refuses to scan a large binary end to end on the chance it
spells "<svg" somewhere — there is a test for each half of that.

7 of the 18 new tests fail against the unfixed code.

Verified: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` (both projects), `pnpm test` — 9,633 tests.

Closes #427.
