author: mehek-builds
body:
Follow-up to #154, which named this residue and did not close it.

## The defect

A requirements block that runs to the end of a posting with nothing to close it keeps the pay and EEO footer at weight 1. #154 estimated the cost from one subset. Measured board-wide it is not small: footer text sits inside a REQUIRED section on **5,839 of 22,138** active postings (26.4%).

Toast's "Field Sales Account Executive" is the funniest instance of a serious bug. Toast writes its benefits section as bread puns under "Our Spread* of Total Rewards", so `Toasters`, `Tofu`, `Baked` and `Recipe` were counted as things the employer required of a candidate, and the dashboard tooltip called them "the requirements Litos counted in this posting".

## Four additions, each counted before it was added

Over the 205,581 heading-shaped lines on the board, because this list has no shape guard beyond `isHeadingLine`:

| pattern | fires on | spellings |
|---|---|---|
| `total rewards` | 406 lines | 5 |
| `pay transparency` | 672 lines | 8 |
| `what we('?ll)? offer` | 119 lines (the contraction only) | — |
| `employment verification` | 70 lines | 5 |

The contraction is the same typed-regex-vs-scraped-text gap as the curly-apostrophe defect: `what we offer` was already here and missed "What we'll offer".

Plus `^disclosures:?$`, **anchored**.

## Two candidates measured and rejected

Recorded in the file so they are not re-proposed on the intuition that put them there.

**Bare `disclosures?`** fires on 202 lines and 4 of its 10 spellings are real work: "Prepare tax related disclosures for financial statements", "Manage subprocessor tracking and disclosures", "Experience negotiating non-disclosure agreements", "Data leakage and sensitive information disclosure". A tax accountant's requirement line is not a footer.

**LinkedIn tracking tags** are the single biggest unrecognised heading on the board: 3,705 lines, 328 spellings, and `headingCore` strips the `#` so they arrive looking like headings. Zeroing them is tempting and wrong as written: only 635 sit in the last 5% of their posting while **1,867 sit before the 80% mark**, so closing the section at the tag would zero real content on a third of them. They match nothing, so they close nothing, so they are harmless where they are. A test pins that.

## Effect

Measured against origin/main over all 22,138 active postings: the denominator changes on **617 (2.8%)**. What leaves is footer: `Zone Philosophy` (162), `Baked` (144), `Recipe` (132), `Disclosure` (69), `Total Rewards` (59), `Toasters` (48), `Washington Minimum` (47), `us-greenhouse-mail.io` (40).

**One drop worth reading**, because it touches `SKILL_LEXICON`: `compliance` leaves 52 denominators, all Figma sales postings, and it was coming from the benefits paragraph rather than any requirement. Checked before shipping, the same way ISSUE-026 checked `ai`.

## This is a partial fix, and the number is 9.4%

Footer-inside-requirements drops from 5,839 postings to 5,288: **551 closed**.

The remaining 3,015 are the harder half, where the footer arrives as PROSE with no heading-shaped opener at all ("The compensation range for this position will depend on where you reside..."). `NOISE_BLOCK` cannot reach those by construction: it needs 16 words or fewer and no terminal full stop, and these are long sentences. Closing them needs a footer sentinel that ends a scored section on a phrase rather than on a heading, which has a known false positive ("Knowledge of EEO and affirmative action reporting requirements" is a real requirement line), so it needs its own measurement rather than a quiet extension of this one.

## Tests

Five added. The fixture is deliberately rich on the requirements side: the first draft had three requirement lines, which left the posting unscorable once the footer was zeroed, so the salvage pass re-read the noise and handed `Tofu` straight back. That is the salvage pass working as designed, and it means a footer fix can only be observed on a posting that stays scorable without it.

Full suite **1594/1594**, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Removing the added vocabulary fails three of the five new tests.


## Code review (run pre-merge)

One finding, fixed in c06928b.

**24 postings become newly unscorable, and nothing recorded it.** Board-wide refusals go **1,583 to 1,606**. Verified correct rather than assumed: Samsara "Account Executive, Commercial - Mexico" scored on eight terms before this, four of which were `Tofu`, `us-greenhouse-mail.io`, `mail3.guide.co` and `Commitment`. Take the footer away and what is left is under the floor, so the posting refuses instead of printing a number built on a rewards paragraph and a mail domain. That is the trade `MIN_SCORABLE_TERMS` exists to make, and ISSUE-026 set the convention of recording this metric.

Checked and clean:

- **ReDoS** at the 60-char `isHeadingLine` cap, including the new anchored alternative.
- **Curly apostrophe**: `What we'll offer` with U+2019 matches, via the `headingCore` fold.
- **No theft** from the patterns tested after noise: `About You` still opens required, `Requirements` and `Preferred qualifications` unaffected.
- **Edge misses measured, not assumed**: `Disclosures :` (space before colon), `What we will offer` (uncontracted), singular `total reward` all have **zero** occurrences across the board's 205,581 heading lines. Unlike the NBSP case in #154, these are lexical variants rather than encoding hazards, so they are not the same class of latent risk.
- No SQL, auth, LLM-output, or shell surface. Scope clean: two files, both `jdMatch`.

**Cross-model pass unavailable.** Codex is rate-limited until Aug 8, so the adversarial pass was Claude-only, same as #154.

author: sheffchenk0
body:
## Why

Set-based classic sports report the games of each set on the period row, next to
the running sets-won tally. A live tennis match with the first set won 6:4 and
the second under way arrives from the feed as:

```xml
<sport_event_status status="1" match_status="201" scoreboard_available="true"
                    home_score="1" away_score="0">
  <period_score type="set" number="1" match_status_code="200"
                home_score="1" away_score="0" home_games="6" away_games="4"/>
  <period_score type="set" number="2" match_status_code="201"
                home_score="1" away_score="0" home_games="0" away_games="1"/>
  <scoreboard home_points="40" away_points="40" home_games="0" away_games="1"/>
</sport_event_status>
```

`home_games` / `away_games` had no place in `PeriodScore` — games existed only on
the scoreboard, which describes the set in progress and nothing else. The
attribute was therefore dropped while decoding, and a consumer was left with
`home_score`: the sets-won tally, identical on every row (1:0, 1:0, …). Rendering
a per-set row from it shows 1:0 where the set was 6:4.

It also cannot be reconstructed downstream. The scoreboard resets its games with
each new set, so once a set ends its score is gone from the live state, and a
consumer restarting mid-match has nothing to replay it from.

## What changed

- `GamesPeriodScore` on both the feed and the API `PeriodScore`, mirroring the
  existing rounds / kills / goals / points groups
- `HomeGames` / `AwayGames` as `Optional[int]` on `types.PeriodScore`, so absence
  stays distinguishable from a legitimate 0:0 at the start of a set
- mapped in both cache paths, feed and API

Additive only — no existing field changes shape or meaning.

## Tests

`internal/cache/period_score_games_test.go` drives the payload above through the
API path and asserts three rows: a completed set keeping 6:4, the set in progress
carrying 0:1, and a `map` period leaving games unset. It also checks the tally on
the same row stays readable, so the two numbers cannot be confused.

author: mayank-ppl
body:
Follow-up to #3588 (merged). Doc-only — no code changes.

Two separate concerns, kept in one PR because both are CLAUDE.md edits landing in the same session and neither is independently reviewable without the other's context. Happy to split if preferred.

## 1. The invariant behind #3588

Filed under the #3511 lesson, because it's the direct sequel on the same routes in the opposite direction: #3511 was a gate too *permissive* by default; this was a gate *refusing* on absent data.

`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/pages/[id]` answered 403 whenever no `x-tenant-id` resolved — page saves worked on the 3,907 visible books owned by a tenant and failed on the other **30,132**. Five points, each of which cost real time in the diagnosis:

- **Sibling handlers disagreeing about what absence means IS the bug.** The `GET` on that same route had always read a missing tenant as global scope, and said so in a comment; the six other global page writers apply no tenant filter at all. One handler of eight disagreeing with its own `GET` is drift, not policy.
- **Build the scope filter conditionally.** `{ id, tenantId }` with a null tenant matches missing-**and**-null in Mongo, so deleting the gate alone would have read as working on global books while never matching a tenant-owned page.
- **The two 403 bodies are load-bearing.** `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` (route scope gate) vs `{"error":"Forbidden - Insufficient role"}` (`withAuth`) was the *only* thing distinguishing a scoping bug from a permissions one.
- **A `curl` against a URL shape cannot establish what the client sends.** The issue was filed on a genuine 308 for `/api//pages/<id>` — a URL the app hasn't sent since #1880 collapsed `/api//` → `/api/` two months earlier. That wrong mechanism nearly aimed the fix at `getTenantSlug()`.
- **A grant the system cannot read is indistinguishable from no grant** (#3589).

## 2. Two stale deploy claims

**"Merging a PR does NOT deploy production" is wrong**, and acting on it wastes a ten-minute deploy per merge.

Verified 2026-08-04: #3588 merged at `08:00:18Z`, and `npx vercel inspect sourcelibrary.org` reported a new `target production / status Ready` deployment created within the minute, aliased `sourcelibrary-v2-git-main-…`. The project is git-integrated on `main`, and `post-deploy-warm.yml` runs the Cloudflare `purge_everything` + re-warm on the same push — so the merge path is fully covered.

The tell that the old text was stale was sitting in the workflow the whole time: its first step is **"Wait for Vercel deploy"**, which only makes sense if the push deploys.

`npm run deploy:prod` keeps its entry, rescoped to what it's still for: an out-of-band deploy with no push behind it, which gets no workflow run and therefore no purge. The "a failed `deploy:prod` may still have shipped" entry is untouched — still valid for that path.

Also adds a cross-reference: since a merge is now a production build, the **`entities` bulk-sweep interlock applies at merge time**, not only when someone runs `deploy:prod` by hand. That's the `/explore` prerender timeout that fails the build and, now, loses the deploy.

## Verification note

The prod behaviour of #3588 itself — an editor saving a page on a non-tenant book — still wants one browser check now that it's deployed, since it can't be tested anonymously (`withAuth` 401s before the scope gate is reached). Flagging rather than claiming it verified.

author: shyuan
body:
Adds `skills/stern-logs`, a skill that teaches an agent to drive [stern](https://github.com/stern/stern) for reading Kubernetes pod logs.

## Why

The failure mode this exists to prevent: stern follows by default, so a bare `stern <query>` in an agent context **never exits** — the tool call blocks until the harness timeout and the partial output may be discarded. On top of that the defaults (`--since 48h`, `--tail -1`, per pod) flood the context when the query widens.

So the skill is built around one Iron Law — every invocation carries `--no-follow` — plus a bounded default command shape, and a set of failure modes that read as "no errors" when they are not:

- an empty result exits 0 and prints nothing, so a non-matching query looks like a clean log
- a crash-looping pod's container is `terminated`, so a plain tail shows nothing
- `--max-log-requests` silently throttles (5 with `--no-follow`) or hard-errors (50 without)

## Layout

| file | contents |
| --- | --- |
| `SKILL.md` | Iron Law + rationalization table, default command shape, selection, gotchas |
| `references/recipes.md` | worked commands: crash loops, cross-namespace error hunts, ordering, `--stdin` replay, RBAC |
| `references/flags.md` | complete v1.34.0 flag table, config file, completion, install |
| `references/templates.md` | `Log` struct, template functions, JSON-log formatting |
| `ATTRIBUTION.md` | upstream is Apache-2.0; what to re-verify on a version bump |

`README.md` gains its row in the Skills table (repo invariant). No scripts — instruction-only.

## Verification

Flags, defaults and validation rules were checked against the stern source at v1.34.0 (upstream commit `3dd605b`), not just its README: `cmd/cmd.go` for the validation rules and `--max-log-requests` defaults, `stern/tail_utils.go` for the `Log` fields exposed to templates and `-o json`, `stern/resource_matcher.go` for supported `<resource>/<name>` kinds.

Behaviour tested against a local stern 1.34.0: the `--no-follow` + `--tail=0` rejection, exit 0 with no output on a non-matching query, `--stdin` with a `tryParseJSON`/`levelColor` template, `head` terminating the pipeline, and each flag combination used in the recipes (all pointed at a non-existent namespace, so no real log content was read).

## Review

Audited with `/skill-review` against its 22 anti-patterns. Fixed in `abea8ee` and `b073d96`: Naked Rule (Iron Law had no rationalization table), Redundant Duplication (three facts living in two files each), Nested Reference, Orphan Reference.

Known gap, tracked separately: the description's triggers have not been eval-tested. `"看一下 log"` is deliberately broad and may over-trigger on local application logs.

author: dwelle
body:
# feat: `ViewportStatusFrame`, hoist follow state, `currentUserControls`

## Summary

- Replaces the internal `FollowMode` component and PR #10926's `canvasNotification` prop with a single **`ViewportStatusFrame`** component/prop — one viewport-edge border + bottom-center badge, host-composed.
- **Hoists `userToFollow`/`followedBy` out of `appState`** to host-controlled state. The editor no longer decides who you're following — it only emits follow/unfollow *intents* (via `onUserFollow`, prop or imperative API) and renders whatever `userToFollow` the host passes back in.
- Redesigns `UserList`'s "who's here" UI: one merged dropdown (own avatar as trigger) instead of a separate `currentUserMenu` pill + `+N` overflow popover.
- Adds `currentUserControls`: host-rendered content in that dropdown (and now the mobile menu too), accepting either a node or `(isMobile: boolean) => ReactNode`.
- Ports `excalidraw-app`'s `Collab` to the new controlled model.

## Breaking changes

- `AppState.userToFollow` / `AppState.followedBy` removed. Use the new `userToFollow` prop (controlled) instead.
- `FollowMode` component removed; its badge/border is now whatever `viewportStatusFrame` the host composes (see `excalidraw-app/App.tsx` for the reference "Following X" badge).
- `onUserFollow` (prop and imperative API) now fires **only on user-initiated gestures** (avatar click, badge close, canvas pan/zoom/pointerdown breaking follow) — never on host-driven `userToFollow` prop changes. Consumers that relied on it firing for every state transition need to update.
- `canvasNotification` renamed to `viewportStatusFrame`; shape changed — `label`/`icon`/`background`/`color`/`onClose` now nest under `label`, and `border` is a required `false | string` (no default-color boolean variant).
- `currentUserMenu` renamed to `currentUserControls`.

## Details

- **`ViewportStatusFrame`** (`packages/excalidraw/components/ViewportStatusFrame/`): border overlay + badge, `role="status"`, real close `<button>`.
- **Follow-intent plumbing**: `App.emitUserFollowIntent`/`App.requestUnfollow` replace direct `appState.userToFollow` writes across `actionNavigate.tsx` (avatar click), the six zoom/fit actions in `actionCanvas.tsx`, and pan/pointerdown in `App.tsx`/`App.viewport.ts`. Laser pointer pointerdown is excluded — it's a presentation aid, not an edit, and shouldn't break follow.
- **`excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx`**: new `userToFollowAtom` + `setUserToFollow` funnel (handles leaving the old follow room before joining the new one); `followedBy` moved to a Collab class field. Own collaborator entries are now seeded with the local username (`setCollaborators`/`updateCollaborator`/`setUsername`) — collaborators never receive their own broadcasts, so without this the current user's entry had no username and got filtered out of `UserList`.
- **`UserList` redesign**: current user's avatar is always rendered as a pill (avatar + chevron), reserved its own slot so it's never hidden by or orphaned from overflow. Its dropdown always lists every collaborator (self included — "if you're alone, show just yourself") plus `currentUserControls` below a divider. Self's row shows `(You)` and is inert (no hover/click). Mobile menu gets the same `currentUserControls` content, inline. Fixed a layout bug where the trigger could wrap onto its own line when avatars didn't fit an integer number of slots.
- **Debug aid**: `excalidraw-app/debugCollaborators.ts` — `useSimulatedCollaborators` hook, dev-only, populates N static fake collaborators via `?collaborators=<N>` (one marked as the current user) for exercising this UI without a real collab room.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test:typecheck`, `yarn test:code` (lint), full suite (`yarn test:update`) all green
- [x] Manual: follow/unfollow via avatar click, badge close, canvas pan/zoom/pointerdown; followed user leaving the room auto-unfollows
- [x] Manual: `UserList` dropdown solo / with overflow / at various widths; `currentUserControls` on desktop and mobile
- [x] Manual: `?collaborators=N` debug flag

author: vinix24
body:
## Wat

De deur gooit zijn eigen routing-beslissing weg. `ExecutionPlan.digest()` maakt een canonieke dict en hasht die tot een permit-fingerprint, maar de dict zelf wordt nooit weggeschreven. De fingerprint bewijst **dat** er een beslissing was, niets bewaart **welke**.

## Wat er verandert

1. **`dispatch_plan.py`**: Extract `canonical_dict()` uit `digest()` — dezelfde dict die gehasht wordt, nu ook los opvraagbaar voor persistentie.

2. **`dispatch_cli.py`**: `_persist_route_decision()` schrijft de canonieke beslissing naar de bestaande `route_decisions`-stroom (NDJSON + per-dispatch JSON), met de fingerprint ernaast opgeslagen zodat de bewaarde beslissing achteraf tegen de permit verifieerbaar is.

3. **Best-effort**: faalt de schrijfactie, dan een expliciete WARN en de dispatch loopt door. Gebruikt `# vnx-silent-except:` marker.

## Buiten scope

`smart_router` aanzetten blijft Vincents beslissing. De opt-in flag is niet aangeraakt.

## Verificatie

- Alle 105 `test_dispatch_plan.py` tests groen
- Alle 126 `test_dispatch_cli.py` tests groen (6 nieuw voor OI-849)
- `canonical_dict()` matcht `digest()` voor alle 10 providers (parametrized)
- Fingerprint herbouwd uit opgeslagen dict == permit's `plan_digest`
- Faalpad: schrijffout → WARN, geen raise
- Dry-run schrijft NIET

body:
## What
Interim workaround: on SLES, install the MCR packages (`containerd.io`, `docker-ee`) with a direct `zypper -n install -y --allow-vendor-change` call instead of the generic `InstallPackage` helper, so the install succeeds on SLES cloud images that ship a distro-vendor `containerd` pre-installed.

## Why
On current SUSE SLES 15 cloud images, `containerd` is pre-installed from SUSE. The MCR `containerd.io` package set obsoletes/replaces it, which zypper treats as a vendor change; `zypper install -y` refuses that non-interactively and exits 4, surfacing as `package manager could not install containerd.io`. Reproduced on SLES 15 SP7 against both `stable-25.0` and `stable-29.2`; `--allow-vendor-change` resolves both.

## Why this is a workaround, not the final fix
The root cause is in the package-manager layer, not in launchpad: `zypper install -y` should allow the vendor change. That belongs in `k0sproject/rig`, whose zypper provider builds the install command. I've raised it upstream:
- Issue: https://github.com/k0sproject/rig/issues/417
- Draft PR: https://github.com/k0sproject/rig/pull/418

That upstream change is an RFC (open question on whether `--allow-vendor-change` should be a default or an opt-in option) and, even if accepted, won't land + tag + get vendored into launchpad in time for the v1.5.18 release. So this PR takes the **direct-zypper workaround in the SLES configurer as the interim fix**, deliberately bypassing rig's `InstallPackage` for exactly the calls that need the flag.

**Once the rig change lands and is vendored, this workaround should be revisited** — reverted back to the generic `InstallPackage` path (if rig makes it the default) or switched to rig's opt-in option (if that's the shape maintainers choose). Tracking that follow-up under PRODENG-3623 / the upstream PR.

## How
- Replace the two `InstallPackage` calls in the SLES `InstallMCR` path with `zypper -n refresh` + `zypper -n install -y --allow-vendor-change <pkg>` (preserving the prior refresh behaviour, non-interactive throughout).
- Wrap the underlying zypper error with `%w` so future package failures are diagnosable rather than swallowed.

## Testing
Validation was **manual/integration only** — this path runs live `zypper` against a SLES host and has no unit coverage in-repo (nor did the code it replaces). No automated tests were added or updated.
- `go build ./pkg/configurer/...`, `go vet ./pkg/configurer/sles/...`, and `gofmt` are clean.
- Manually reproduced the failure and verified the fix (`--allow-vendor-change` -> exit 0) on a standalone SLES 15 SP7 EC2 instance for both `stable-25.0` and `stable-29.2`.
- End-to-end coverage is exercised by the SLES leg of the smoke-test suite (`smoke-modern`).

## Links
- JIRA: [PRODENG-3623](https://mirantis.jira.com/browse/PRODENG-3623)
- Upstream root-cause fix: k0sproject/rig#417, k0sproject/rig#419

- [ ] Tests added or updated (N/A — live-host install path, not unit-testable in-repo; validated manually + via smoke tests)
- [ ] Docs updated if user-visible behaviour changed
- [x] No debug output or dead code left in

author: ldavti
body:
Closes #1008 (reopened after the staging screenshot).

## What the screenshot proved
Post-#1012 staging renders the **correct content** (Overview, sidebar — the render-level gate works) while the **address bar still reads `/sign-in`**. That combination means the router's internal location is `/` but `window.location` was overwritten afterwards by an external history write — prime suspect: the wallet-connect modal restoring its pre-open URL on close (the modal opens on `/sign-in`; by the time it closes, the router has moved to `/`, and the restore stamps `/sign-in` back into the address bar).

This desync is **invisible to the router and React** — no state reflects `window.location`, so none of the four previous redirect approaches (#921/#988/#1009/#1012's convention layer) could ever repair it: from the router's perspective everything already succeeded.

## Change
`useAuthRedirect` now self-heals the address bar: after handling the semantic redirect, it compares `window.location.pathname` against router state and — when they diverge — re-stamps the address bar with the router's href via `history.replaceState` (router state is the source of truth; `history.state` preserved). Short delayed re-checks (250 ms / 1.5 s) catch clobbers that land after the effect, e.g. during a modal close animation.

Failure containment stays layered: content correctness = render gate (#1012); URL convention = redirects; and now URL *integrity* = this self-heal.

## Tests
- The exact screenshot scenario: router at `/`, address bar clobbered to `/sign-in` → re-stamped to `/` with **no** router navigation.
- A late clobber (after the effect ran) caught by the delayed re-checks (fake timers).
- In-sync address bar → `replaceState` never called; all prior semantic-redirect cases unchanged.
- Full trustee suite: **57 files, 736 tests green**; tsc/eslint/prettier/build/lint-docs clean.

根因：VLAN/IFM 两个最早接入的模块注册的 XML namespace 是旧式 `urn:huawei:params:xml:ns:yang:huawei-<mod>`，与设备 YANG 包声明的 `urn:huawei:yang:huawei-<mod>` 不符。真机按声明校验即拒；模拟网元 namespace 宽容、回读按 local 名解析，全套测试均测不出（bgp-onboarding-deps 记忆早有预警，本次真机应验）。

## 改动

- `drivers/huawei.go`：VLAN/IFM namespace 常量改为设备声明值（BGP/NI 本就正确）
- `intent/cleanup.go`：硬编码 IFM namespace 改引常量
- **新增守护测试** `TestRegisteredNamespacesMatchDeviceYang`：以仓库内设备 YANG 包 `snd/ce6866p-yang/` 为真理源，遍历注册表逐描述符（含 per-node namespace map）校验；异名文件（openconfig 系）退回「namespace ∈ 设备包声明全集」。新注册模块自动纳入，封死此类盲区
- netconfsim 种子 / hwfix golden / 相关测试期望机械替换
- 记忆更新单独一提交（MEM04）

## 验证

- T07 红绿：守护测试先行，红灯精准命中 vlan/ifm 两模块，修后转绿
- `go test -race ./...` 后端全量全绿
- 前端零改动

author: chrisns
body:
## Summary
- `release/Dockerfile` cross-compiles `bb` as a single standalone binary for one `TARGET` build-arg (a zig target triple), same `zig cc` technique as the top-level and `web/` Dockerfiles. Unlike those, it isn't limited to what Docker/buildx has a platform for — zig can cross-compile for anything it has an LLVM backend and libc for, no QEMU involved.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` matrices over **29 targets** and publishes every binary as a GitHub Release asset:
  - **musl-linux (fully static, 20 targets):** the existing 6 Docker platforms plus aarch64_be, x86 (i386), riscv32/64, mips/mipsel (both ABIs), mips64/mips64el (N64 *and* N32 ABIs), 32-bit powerpc, big-endian powerpc64, loongarch64, and — because it worked and it's funny — a Qualcomm Hexagon DSP
  - **FreeBSD (3), NetBSD (1), OpenBSD (1):** native, dynamically linked — musl-style full static linking isn't available outside Linux
  - **Windows (2):** native PE, statically linked via mingw
  - **macOS (3... 2):** native, dynamically linked against libSystem
- `m68k` is the one target from `bb`'s own era excluded outright — zig has no working LLVM backend for it currently.

Reaching this far surfaced real portability bugs the 6-platform Docker matrix never hit (mips64 N64 ABI breaking autoconf's preprocessor detection, `pid_t`/`size_t` macro collisions, `malloc.h` not existing on BSD/macOS, `select()`/`fd_set` not existing on Windows, zig defaulting to `.obj` not `.o` for Windows, autoconf's `config.guess` not recognizing zig's Windows triple spelling, and the same Linux-driver-detection issue `web/patches` already worked around for wasm). Full detail in the commit message.

Every one of the 29 targets was validated end-to-end with `docker build` before going into the matrix — not just "should work by analogy."

## Cost / trigger note
This is a genuinely large matrix — 29 parallel Docker builds on every trigger. The workflow only fires on `workflow_dispatch` or pushes that touch `release/**`/the workflow file itself (not on every push to master), but wanted to flag the scale explicitly before this merges and runs for real.

## Test plan
- [x] Built all 29 targets individually via `docker build -f release/Dockerfile --build-arg TARGET=... --output type=local,dest=release/dist .`, confirmed correct binary format (`file`) for each
- [ ] Full matrix + release job on a real trigger

author: tsavo
body: ## Summary Process-floor measurement now uses the same deterministic ordinal-modulo partition law as the showcase surface. The process floor is a measurement instrument: exact corpus coverage is mandatory, while LPT is only a load-balancing heuristic. A floor that runs quickly over an incomplete cover is worse than a slower run over the complete pinned corpus, so process-floor coverage wins when the properties conflict. LPT remains available to package-suite callers. The process entrance now canonicalizes the relative-path roster and assigns ordinal modulo shard count. The focused tooth proves, rather than asserts, that four shards over a 65-file fixture have union equal to the corpus, total membership equal to 65, and pairwise-empty intersections. ## Invalidated historical claim Keaton measured the prior process plan at 1,042 unique reached, 379 omitted, and 405 duplicated memberships. Every process-floor number from run 30880776748, including R_silent=0, R_native=0, and R_timeout=0, was therefore over an unverified cover. Those values are not disproven, but they are not full-corpus claims. A fresh factory run on this plan must replace them before they are quoted as corpus results. ## Validation - Focused partition tooth: union, cardinality, and pairwise disjointness. - The pinned-corpus cover remains outstanding until a fresh factory receipt. ## Not claiming This PR does not claim a fresh process-floor measurement or repair the historical receipt. It changes the assignment law and leaves factory proof as a separate measurement. > [!NOTE] > ### Replace LPT-based sharding with exact lexical modulo-k partition in `apply_lpt_file_shard` > - [`apply_lpt_file_shard`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/7309/files#diff-722768a8db41f7e5bee7a5b826a61b0ebdc49edb27a8ff262303b2d68fd8c709) now resolves and de-duplicates input paths, sorts them lexically relative to the provided root, and selects paths where `ordinal % shard_count == shard_index`, replacing the previous delegation to `lpt_file_shards.filter_paths_for_shard`. > - `add_demand_table_arg` and `require_demand_table` are removed from the module; any callers will break. > - The tools path on module import now derives from `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]` instead of `resolve_repo_root()`, which may change which directory is added to `sys.path`. > - A new test in [`test_lpt_file_shards.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/7309/files#diff-476cac409fcde42de27754774c4f1f1f950deb7f2ea6114ef18c279bee9dd3a5) verifies that for 65 files with `shard_count=4`, all shards are disjoint and their union equals the full set. > - Risk: any code relying on the LPT-weighted distribution of `apply_lpt_file_shard` will now receive a different (lexical modulo) partitioning. > > > > Macroscope summarized 25ac86e. > >

author: lukeannison
body:
## Summary

The runtime compile (Gate 1) computes a declaration and drops it — nothing stores it, nothing serves it back. This is step 1 of the road ahead: give the compiled result somewhere to live and a way to be read back, without building the two-consumer write path (Gate 2 forwarding to the graph server) or the front-end editor.

- **New route** `POST /config/declaration/<kind>` (`kind` = structural | qualification | resolution), operator-only (same bearer key `POST /app/graph` already uses). Compiles the submitted files with the identical `compile(files)` the existing Gate-1 preview route calls, then durably stores the result in D1 under its own content-hash version and flips a "current" pointer to it.
- **New routes** `GET /config/declaration/<kind>/<version>` (public, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`) and `GET /config/declaration/<kind>/current` (public, `Cache-Control: no-cache`) — read a specific immutable version, or the latest without knowing the key.
- **Schema**: `worker/schema-declarations.sql` — `declarations` (one immutable row per `(user_id, kind, version)`) and `declaration_current` (the tiny, mutable pointer).
- **Receipt honesty**: `stored` now reflects a real durable write (`true`/`false`), never hardcoded. `engineAccepted` stays `null` — this route never calls Gate 2, so it never learns whether the engine accepted anything.

`worker/src/config.js` (the existing Gate-1-only preview route) is untouched — kept unauthenticated and side-effect-free exactly as its own header describes, so `scripts/check-isolate-conformance.mjs` needed no changes.

## What I chose, and why (design docs left this open)

`design-the-runtime-compile.md` describes storage/serving in general terms (§2.3, §4) but the concrete route shape for this slice — separate from the full two-consumer write path — isn't specified. I chose:

- **A new module (`declarations.js`) rather than extending `config.js`'s existing compile route.** That route is unauthenticated by design ("touches no storage... a session buys nothing but friction"); bolting durable writes onto it would make an open D1-growth surface. Persistence needed its own, gated route.
- **Write gated behind the existing operator bearer key**, read left public — mirrors the existing `POST /app/graph` (operator-gated write) vs. the app's public `presentation.json` fetch (no auth) that this is the direct successor to.
- **The "current" pointer flips on every successful Gate-1 store**, not held back for a second gate — there is no Gate 2 wired to this route, so holding back would mean never flipping at all. `engineAccepted: null` is what keeps this honest rather than implying acceptance.
- **Table keyed by `user_id`** (the operator's `GRAPH_USER_ID`) even though only one tenant exists today — matches the existing `graph_snapshots` convention and `design-the-runtime-compile.md` §2.3's own stated intent, without building any actual multi-tenancy logic (`config-is-per-user-not-per-server` stays unscoped, per the roadmap).

## What I refuted

- **First instinct: bolt storage onto the existing `/config/compile/<kind>` route.** Refuted on rereading that route's own header — it is unauthenticated specifically *because* it has no storage cost; adding storage there silently reopens a DoS surface the original design deliberately closed by staying side-effect-free.
- **First instinct: the idempotency test needed no scrutiny once it passed.** My initial in-memory D1 stub hardcoded dedup-on-insert regardless of the SQL text sent — meaning the idempotency test would have passed even with the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` clause deleted from the real code. Caught by asking what the stub would do under mutation *before* trusting the first green run; rewrote it to enforce a real primary-key constraint (throws on a duplicate key unless the SQL says `DO NOTHING`), then re-ran the mutation to confirm it actually catches the defect.
- **Assumed a separate "pointer-only" endpoint was required** to match the design doc's two-tier caching scheme literally. Refuted as unnecessary for this slice: nothing consumes a pointer-only response yet (the front-end is step 3, out of scope), so `GET .../current` resolves and returns the body in one call, with the correct no-cache header preserving the seam for later.

## Mutation transitions observed (four, each: broke it, red; restored, green — verified byte-identical to original after restore)

1. **Auth gate removed** (`operatorUser` check bypassed) → "an unauthenticated POST is refused" test failed. Restored → green.
2. **Idempotency guard removed** (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` deleted) → "posting the same files twice produces exactly one stored row" test failed (simulated `UNIQUE constraint failed`). Restored → green.
3. **Pointer update removed** → both "read 'current'" and "pointer moves, old version survives" tests failed. Restored → green.
4. **Declaration/dropped swapped on read** → round-trip byte-identity test failed. Restored → green.

## Verified against a real, live local Worker + local D1 (not just the Node-only test suite)

Ran `wrangler dev` locally against a real local D1 with the schema applied: unauthorized POST → 401 (nothing written); authorized POST → 200 with `stored:true` and a real `sha256-...` version; `GET .../current` → 200, correct body, `Cache-Control: no-cache`; `GET .../<version>` → 200, correct body, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; unknown version → 404; re-POST of identical bytes → same version, `stored:true`, no duplicate.

## What I could not confirm empirically

- **D1's real `ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING` / `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` semantics under true concurrent writes** (two simultaneous stores for the same version, or the pointer upsert racing itself). The local `wrangler dev` D1 and the in-memory test stub are both single-threaded within a request; no concurrency test was possible from this worktree. `compiled.version` being a pure function of content makes a race between two *identical* stores harmless by construction, but a race between the *pointer* upsert and a concurrent differing store was not exercised.
- **Production D1's actual row-size behaviour** near the 950,000-byte guard — inherited the same threshold `POST /app/graph` already uses, not independently re-measured for this table.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` (root): 1774 tests, 1772 pass, 0 fail, 2 todo (pre-existing, unrelated) — up from 1768/1766/0/2 before this change (6 new tests, no regressions).
- [x] `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` (worker/): bundles cleanly, ~137 KiB gzip.
- [x] Live `wrangler dev` + local D1 smoke test (see above) — real HTTP round trip, not just Node-level mocks.
- [x] Four mutation-proof transitions observed and reported above.
- [x] `config.js` and `scripts/check-isolate-conformance.mjs` untouched — no risk to the existing isolate-conformance CI job.

author: jeremytheocharis
body:
## Problem

CPU health flickers and is only dependent on average CPU at the moment. This stacked PR introduces the library the new calculation is built on.

## What we are shipping

- A caller — the CPU library in the next PR — declares just a **table**: what to measure and when to alert. This library executes it. Nothing in it is CPU-specific, so disk or memory can use the same machinery.
- The **engine** is the entry point and drives everything: the caller ticks it once per interval and gets back what fired.
- A **window** holds a series of **points** and applies a **reduction** to them, such as p95 or mean.
- A **latch** is hysteresis under another name: separate fire and clear marks, so a value resting on a threshold does not flicker the verdict.
- **Judging** and **ranking** order what fired, so when several signals fire at once the caller knows which cause to lead with.

## What we are NOT shipping

- Any CPU code — the sampler, the verdict table and the message are the next PR (#2686)
- The fsmv2 worker and the `USE_FSMV2_CPU` flag — later PRs on this stack
- Any consumer at all; this lands as a leaf package
- A changelog entry — no callers yet

author: nyanta-kun
body:
UmaConn の「Unexpected Memory Leak」モーダルダイアログの修正。PR #57 の調査中に発覚。

## 何が起きていたか

NVDTLab.dll は Delphi/FastMM 製で、NVLink を解放しないままプロセスが終わると
`DLL_PROCESS_DETACH` で **モーダルダイアログ**を出す。エージェントは `pythonw.exe` 起動で
閉じる者がいないため、プロセスはそこで止まったまま UmaConn COM を掴んで居座る。
次に起動したエージェントの NV 呼び出しがブロックされ、それがまたウォッチドッグの
`os._exit` を誘発する **自己増殖ループ**になっていた。

実測（2026-08-04）:

| 現象 | 実測値 |
|---|---|
| fetch-results の滞留 | 最大4本（16:35 / 16:46 / 16:52 / 16:56）。最古は **41分**居座り |
| realtime の `os._exit(1)` | 同日**3回**（15:17 / 16:17 / 16:40）。従来は月1〜2回 |
| 直後の起動 | `NVSetServiceKey: 60秒タイムアウト` = COM がブロックされている |

ダイアログの `TNVLink` の個数は生存インスタンス数と一致する。realtime は
main の `nv` と bg worker の `nv2` の2本を持つため **x2**、fetch-results 等は **x1**。

## 漏れていた経路は3つ

1. **`main()` がどのモードでも解放していなかった** — 解放がインタプリタ終了時まで
   先送りされ、そこがまさにダイアログの発火位置
2. **realtime の `_watchdog` は bg worker の `nv2` にしか停止通知を送っていなかった** —
   main の `nv` が必ず1本漏れる
3. **`_bg_watchdog` は素の `os._exit(1)`** — `nv2` と `nv` を2本とも漏らす（`TNVLink x 2` はこの経路）

2 については既に「os._exit だけだと TNVLink リークダイアログを表示する」というコメントが
入っていたが、対策が bg worker 側だけで不完全だった。

## 修正

- `release_nvlink()` を追加。`NVClose` → 参照破棄 → `gc.collect()` を1箇所に集約し、
  DLL 側の解放をインタプリタ終了時ではなく**その場で**確定させる。`NVClose` が投げても
  解放を止めない（ここで例外が抜けると `os._exit` 前の解放が丸ごと飛ぶ）
- `main()` のモード分岐を `_run_mode()` に切り出し、`try/finally` で全モード共通に解放
- `_exit_after_release()` に両ウォッチドッグを統一。`nv2` は生成したスレッド (STA) 自身に
  閉じさせる必要があるためキュー経由で依頼し、完了を Event で待つ（10秒でタイムアウトして
  main の解放へ進む）
- bg worker の `finally` でも `nv2` を解放。NVInit 失敗・例外・shutdown のどの経路でも残さない

## 検証

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| pytest | 7 passed（1回だけ呼ぶ / None を返す / NVClose 例外でも止まらない / 二重解放で落ちない / main から `_run_mode` が切り出されている） |
| ruff | All checks passed（main 比で新規指摘なし） |
| Windows 32bit Python 構文検査 | OK |
| **実機動作** | `17:26:09 [INFO] [release] main: NVLink を解放しました` を確認。fetch-results が滞留せず終了 |

滞留していた fetch-results は回収済み、realtime も新コードで再起動済み。

## 補足

`windows-agent/umaconn_agent.py` は `pillars.sh` の `pillar_of` では `jra` 判定だが、
実体は地方競馬 (UmaConn) の取込エージェント。柱判定は機械的に jra として扱っている。

body:
새 덤프(2026-08-04)를 별도 DB에 적재해 확인하다가, **DB 파트가 이미 만들어 둔 걸 제가 손으로 다시 만들고 있었다는 걸 발견**했습니다.

`SCHEMA_10~14`(2026-07-29, 강주호님)를 제 로컬과 통합 테스트에서 **한 번도 적재한 적이 없어서** 몰랐습니다.

```
admin_procedure    7건   서식 URL · 담당 기관 · 과태료 금액까지 들어 있음
law_precedent     32건   대법원 판결 원문 링크
policy_service    23건   융자 · 컨설팅 등 신청 가능한 지원사업
fn_accident_advice(업종, 재해유형, 중대여부)
```

제 상담 API가 사고 서술에서 **정확히 이 세 값을 추정**합니다. 맞물리게 설계된 것처럼 딱 맞아서 그대로 연결했습니다.

---

# 1. 하드코딩을 DB 데이터로 교체

| | 이전 (손으로 적음) | 지금 (`admin_procedure`) |
|---|---|---|
| 근거 조문 | ✅ | ✅ |
| **서식 다운로드 링크** | ❌ | ✅ |
| **담당 기관** | 일부 | ✅ 관할 노동관서 / 근로복지공단 |
| **과태료 금액** | ❌ "자료에 없음" | ✅ **미보고 3,000만원 / 미제출 1,500만원 이하** |
| 관련 판례 | ❌ | ✅ 대법원 판결 + 원문 링크 |
| 지원사업 | ❌ | ✅ 융자 · 컨설팅 + 신청 링크 |

## 과태료 금액 — PR #37 의 설명을 정정합니다 ⚠️

PR #37에서 **"법령 데이터에 형량 문장이 빠져 있어 금액을 쓸 수 없다"** 고 했는데, 정확히는 **`law_article` 에 없을 뿐 `admin_procedure.penalty` 에 있었습니다.**

프롬프트에 넣어 주니 모델이 지어내지 않고 정확히 말합니다.

**이전 (금액을 몰라서 회피)**
> 구체적인 벌금이나 과태료 액수는 자료에 나오지 않으므로 관할 지방고용노동관서에 확인하세요.

**지금 (실제 서버 응답)**
> 중대재해 발생을 지체 없이 보고하지 않으면 **3,000만 원의 과태료**가 부과될 수 있고, 산업재해조사표를 1개월 이내에 제출하지 않으면 **1,500만 원 이하의 과태료**가 부과될 수 있습니다 (산업안전보건법 제54조 제2항, 제57조 제3항).

형사처벌 조문(제168조·제170조)의 형량 문장은 여전히 `law_article` 에 없어서, 그건 계속 조문만 인용합니다. → 이승원님 요청 항목은 유효합니다.

## 실제 응답 (공장 프레스 끼임 사망)

```
행정 처리
  ▸ 작업 중지·근로자 대피      기한=즉시
  ▸ 중대재해 발생 보고         기한=지체 없이 | 관할 지방고용노동관서
                              위반 시: 미보고 시 과태료 3,000만원
  ▸ 사고 현장 보존             기한=조사 종료 시까지
  ▸ 산업재해조사표 제출        기한=발생일부터 1개월 이내 | 관할 지방고용노동관서
                              위반 시: 미제출 시 과태료 1,500만원 이하
                              서식: 산업재해조사표 (moel.go.kr 링크)
  ▸ 수사·처벌 대응 준비        기한=수사 착수 시
  ▸ 산재보험 요양급여 신청     기한=치료 개시 후 | 근로복지공단
                              서식: 요양급여신청서 (gov.kr 링크)
  ▸ 재발방지대책 수립          기한=노동관서 지정 기한
```

판례 3건(대법원 원문 링크) · 지원사업 5건 · 유사 재해사례 3건이 함께 나옵니다.

---

# 2. 왜 함수를 그대로 안 쓰고 나눠 읽는가

| 계층 | 어떻게 | 왜 |
|---|---|---|
| **행정** | `admin_procedure` 표 직접 | 함수가 기한과 조치를 한 문자열로 합침. 화면에서 기한·기관·서식을 **따로** 보여주려면 컬럼이 나뉘어야 함 |
| **판례** | `fn_accident_advice` 그대로 | "재해유형이 판결문에 나오는가"로 고르는 규칙이 함수에 있음. 다시 만들면 어긋남 |
| **정책** | `policy_service` 표 + 조건 하나 추가 | 아래 참고 |

## 지원사업에 분야 조건을 하나 더 걸었습니다

함수는 제목에 `예방` 이 들어가면 통과시킵니다. 그래서 이런 게 나옵니다.

```
▸ 사과 기상 재해예방 (전북특별자치도 장수군)   ← 공장 사망사고 안내에
   기타||현물 · 사과 기상재해예방 지원(동해, 서리피해 예방제)
```

`field` 로 산재 관련 세 분야(`행정·안전` / `고용·창업` / `보건·의료`)만 남기면 **나머지 9건은 그대로 남고 이것만 빠집니다.**

> 📌 **강주호님** — `fn_accident_advice` 의 정책 필터에 `field` 조건을 넣으시면 함수 쪽에서 해결됩니다. 지금은 백엔드에서 걸러 두었고, 테스트로 고정해 뒀습니다.

---

# 3. 코드값 API 추가 — `GET /api/references`

`SCHEMA_8` 이 만든 `v_ref_*` 뷰 주석에 이렇게 적혀 있습니다.

> 프런트 참조 도메인 뷰 — 백엔드 GET 엔드포인트 소스
> 프런트가 값을 하드코딩하지 않고 DB 값을 그대로 사용하게 함

**그런데 그 엔드포인트가 없어서** `API.md` 에 코드값 목록을 적어 두고 있었습니다. 뷰를 그대로 엽니다.

```json
GET /api/references
{
  "industries":  [{ "code": "제조업", "displayName": "제조업", "highRisk": true }],
  "sizeClasses": [{ "code": "5인 미만", "modelSizeClass": "5인 미만", "sortOrder": 1 }],
  "regions":     [{ "code": "부산", "displayName": "부산", "target": true }],
  "accidentTypes": [{ "code": "끼임", "displayName": "끼임" }],
  "workTypes":   [{ "industry": "제조업", "workType": "프레스 작업", "itemCount": 12 }]
}
```

업종 4 · 규모 10 · 지역 16 · 재해유형 24 · 작업종류 68 — **합쳐 122건이라 앱 시작 시 한 번 받아 두면 됩니다.**

`workTypes[].itemCount` 는 점검 문항이 업종당 수백 개라 작업 종류로 먼저 좁힐 때 "12문항" 처럼 미리 알려주는 용도입니다.

---

# 4. 제조업 유사 재해사례가 살아났습니다 🎉

2026-08-04 덤프에서 **제조업등 2,573건의 재해유형이 전부 채워졌습니다.**

| `industry_div` | 전체 | 이전 비어있음 | 지금 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 건설업 | 3,459 | 0 | 0 |
| **제조업등** | **2,573** | **2,573** | **0** |

어휘도 건설업과 같아서(추락 617 · 깔림 450 · 베임 241 · 끼임 219 …) **기존 매핑이 그대로 동작합니다.** "제조업은 분류가 안 돼 있어 표시할 수 없습니다" 안내를 걷어냈습니다.

## 매핑 구멍 하나 발견

코드값은 `깔림.뒤집힘` 인데 `sif_case` 는 `깔림` · `전도` 로 나뉘어 있습니다. 매핑이 없어서 **이 유형은 사례가 하나도 안 나오고 있었습니다.** 고쳤습니다.

---

# 5. 통합 테스트가 스키마를 절반만 싣고 있었습니다

`SCHEMA_8` 과 `SCHEMA_10~14` 가 적재 목록에 빠져 있었습니다. **DB에 있는 기능을 못 보고 지나친 원인**입니다. 전부 추가했습니다.

**테스트 55건 통과** (신규 6건)

| 지킨 것 |
|---|
| 행정 절차에 서식 링크 · 담당 기관 · 과태료 금액이 실린다 |
| 기관이 `-` 인 행은 화면에 그대로 찍히지 않는다 |
| 중대재해가 아니면 "즉시 작업 중지"가 빠진다 (과잉 안내 방지) |
| 판례와 지원사업이 실제 링크와 함께 나온다 |
| **농업 지원사업이 공장 사고 안내에 섞이지 않는다** |
| 프롬프트에 과태료 금액이 들어가 모델이 지어내지 않아도 된다 |
| 코드값 API 가 셀렉트박스에 필요한 값을 한 번에 준다 |
| 제조업도 유사 사례가 나온다 |

실제 PostgreSQL(새 덤프) + 실제 Gemini 키로 눌러 확인했습니다.

---

# 프론트엔드 (곽동헌님)

`backend/docs/API.md` 를 갱신했습니다.

- **2-1절** — 코드값을 하드코딩하지 마시고 `GET /api/references` 를 쓰세요
- **8-2절** — `administrativeSteps.items[]` 에 `agency` · `formName` · `formUrl` · `penalty` 가 추가됐고, `relatedPrecedents` · `supportPrograms` 두 배열이 새로 생겼습니다

화면에서는 이렇게 쓰시면 좋습니다.
- `formUrl` → **"서식 다운로드"** 버튼
- `penalty` → 경고색 뱃지
- `relatedPrecedents[].url` → 새 탭 (국가법령정보센터)
- `supportPrograms` → **"그래서 뭘 할 수 있나"** 에 대한 답이라 사고 안내 맨 아래 배치 추천

author: delpicorp
body:
Adds [dev-report](https://github.com/delpicorp/dev-report) as an external link, matching the other entries in that section. The skill lives in its own repository.

### What it does

You finish a long Claude Code session. A dozen files changed and several implementation decisions were made along the way, but the end-of-session summary is file names and function names — accurate, and written for someone reading the diff alongside it. Asking for it "simply" removes the reasoning too.

`/dev-report` explains the session in plain language instead: what was built or changed, why that approach was chosen, what is still unfinished or unverified, and what to do next.

Technical terms aren't stripped out — they're explained the moment they first appear, so the reasoning survives. Two rules do most of the work: every finding leads with the raw artifact (the actual log line, the actual count) before it gets explained, and the section on how a problem was solved has to name the option that was rejected and what would have gone wrong.

### Details

```
/plugin marketplace add delpicorp/dev-report
/plugin install dev-report@delpicorp
```

- Single skill — no agents, hooks, or MCP servers. About 380 always-on tokens.
- Explicit-only, so it does not fire on a casual "what did you just do?"
- Reports come out in whatever language the command was typed in. Aliases ship for Korean (`/개발보고`), Japanese (`/開発報告`), and Spanish (`/informe-desarrollo`). File paths, function names, and log lines always stay in their original form.
- Two worked example reports ship in the repo (illustrative, not real customer sessions).
- MIT licensed. Disclosure: I'm the author.

Happy to reword or move the entry if it fits better elsewhere.

author: kbenestad
body:
Three defects that together made `mdcms config` section edits look like they did nothing and `mdcms build` look broken.

## 1. `mdcms build` could write a `nav.yml` no YAML parser can read

`_emit_value()` — the scalar emitter behind `generate_nav_yml()` — quoted a value only when it was empty, contained `:`, `"`, `'` or `#`, or spelled `true`/`false`/`null`, and when it did quote it escaped `"` but not `\`.

```
title: "C:\Users\me — setup"     # invalid escape sequence → file fails to parse
title: [2026] Roadmap            # parses back as a flow sequence, not a string
title: - dash lead               # parses back as a block sequence
```

Once `nav.yml` was unparseable the renderer's js-yaml load failed and the navigation went blank — which is what "the build stopped working" looks like from the browser.

**Fix:** values are emitted as properly escaped YAML scalars (backslashes, quotes, control characters), and the decision to quote is made by round-tripping the string through the parser — anything that fails to parse or comes back as a different value or type is double-quoted. `_emit_code()` shares the same logic. Verified against 36 awkward inputs; all round-trip exactly.

## 2. `mdcms config` silently deleted `nav.yml` contents when it could not be parsed

The section editors read the file with `read_nav_yml()`, which deliberately degrades to an empty nav so `mdcms build` can recover (it regenerates page entries from disk anyway). The editors don't regenerate anything — they write back what they read — so an empty read plus a save meant deletion. Reproduced on the `showcase` sample site: adding one section took `nav.yml` from 146 lines (5 sections, 24 pages) down to a single section and no pages, with no warning.

**Fix:** added `read_nav_yml_for_edit()`, which raises instead of returning an empty nav, and switched every section editor to it. The `mdcms config` summary now prints `sections: unreadable — <reason>` instead of `sections: 0`, and the Manage sections menu reports the error and returns. `mdcms build` stays tolerant (CI must not break on a damaged file) but its warning now spells out which section metadata it is about to lose.

## 3. A page's frontmatter `sort:` was ignored once the page was in `nav.yml`

`build_page_nav()` computed `sort = existing.get("sort") or primary.get("sort") or 100`, preferring whatever was already in `nav.yml`. Since the first build writes the frontmatter value there, that value was pinned forever — changing a page's sort, by hand or through `mdcms config` → Manage pages, never moved it in the nav. This contradicts `docs/reference-nav.md`: "Page `title`, `sort`, `section-id` — these are always taken from frontmatter."

**Fix:** order reversed. `nav.yml`'s value now only applies to pages that declare no `sort:` at all.

## Also

- `set_config_block()` left `config.yml` without a trailing newline after writing `default-category` / `categories`.

## Verification

- All eight sample sites build clean, and their `nav.yml` files are byte-identical after rebuild — the emitter change causes no churn on existing content.
- `read_nav_yml` → `generate_nav_yml` round-trip is stable for all eight.
- Section add / rename / re-sort / set-parent / visibility / pagination all survive a subsequent `mdcms build`.
- Page sort change through `mdcms config` now reaches `nav.yml` on rebuild.
- A deliberately corrupted `nav.yml` is left intact (146 lines before and after) instead of being wiped.
- `pyflakes` clean apart from the three pre-existing `fetch-deps` `NameError`s already tracked in `docs/knownbugs.md`.

## Version

Bumped to **v0.8.2** (patch — fixes only) across `mdcms.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `app/config.yml` and `app/index.html`, and re-synced `app/index.html` into all eight sample sites per `CLAUDE.md`. `docs/unreleased.md` and `docs/knownbugs.md` updated.

author: blas1n
body:
A measurement, committed as a test, that de-risks item 30 sub-item D before it is built.

## Why

D recovers a stale asset path — the kind embedded in a JS string literal like `const NEXT_SCENE = "assets/scenes/level2.ron"` — by asking the index where that path's asset went. That needs **something to record the move**, and today only orphan recovery does. A rename made while the watcher is running records nothing: `drain_asset_changes` drops the source path because it no longer `is_file()`, and only reloads the destination.

So before designing D around "the index remembers former paths", the question is whether the information exists at all.

## Measured

It does — we were discarding it. `notify-debouncer-full`'s `FileIdMap` stitches the backend's two halves into a single event carrying **both** paths, old first:

```
Modify(Name(Both)) paths=[".../assets/models/thing.txt", ".../assets/models/renamed.txt"]
```

## What the test asserts, and what it deliberately does not

It asserts the **pairing** — that some event names both the old and the new path, old first — not the exact `EventKind`. A backend is entitled to spell a rename differently; it may not drop the old path, because that is the only thing making a stale reference recoverable.

This matters cross-platform, and getting it through CI is half the point: I measured on Windows, and asserting a Windows-only fact as universal is a mistake this effort already made once (PR #1754's predecessor). If Linux reports renames differently, this test says so here rather than after D is built on the assumption.

Failure is silent otherwise: a rename that loses its old path still looks like an ordinary change to the destination, so nothing would look wrong until a recovery quietly stopped working.

## Test Plan

- [x] `bsengine-asset`: 86 → 87, run 3 consecutive times (timing-dependent; 1.42–1.43 s each)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [ ] CI answers the Linux question

author: erikenobipicks
body:
## Problema

Al programar partidos para **hoy** con "programar", no aparecían: `/pinpon_hoy` seguía diciendo "No hay lista de partidos cargada para hoy".

Dos causas:

1. **Guard bloqueante.** `_pinpon_activar_programados` hacía `if hoy in activados: return`. Si el día ya se había activado una vez (p. ej. por la mañana ya habías marcado resultados), `2026-08-04` quedaba en `pinpon_prog_activados` y **cualquier partido programado para hoy después se quedaba invisible para siempre**.
2. **Nunca se publicaban ese día.** Aunque no estuviera bloqueado, al programar partidos de hoy cuando **ya había pasado** la hora de publicar (07:00), había que esperar... al día siguiente.

## Arreglo

1. **Quitado el guard `hoy in activados`.** Es redundante: al activar, los picks se retiran de la cola (`pinpon_programados`), así que en barridos siguientes ya no se reencuentran. Ahora programar más partidos para hoy tras la primera activación **sí los publica** (se fusionan en el calendario del día sin duplicar).
2. **Publicación inmediata.** `_pinpon_programar` publica al momento los partidos de **hoy** si ya pasó la hora de publicar (07:00). Los de **días futuros** siguen esperando a su hora, como antes.

### Comportamiento
```
programar (captura/lista con partidos de hoy, a las 10:22)
→ 🏓 Programados 5 partido(s).
  • 2026-08-04: 5 partido(s)
  Los de hoy ya pasaron la hora de publicar (07:00): los publico ahora.
→ (se publica el calendario en el canal oficial + free, y saltan los avisos)
```
Los partidos con hora ya pasada quedan igualmente markables (mismo comportamiento que el modo registrar).

## Cambios
- **`handlers.py`**: `_pinpon_activar_programados` (sin guard por día) y `_pinpon_programar` (activación inmediata de hoy).

## Pruebas
- `py_compile` OK en `handlers.py`, `db.py`, `main.py`.

  join in loadSaves.

author: tobyhede
body:
Closes #13.

`4/4` and `4/4 + 3/4` are written into storage on a first run as ordinary Presets, and from that write on they are renamed, replaced and deleted like any other. "Built-in" stops being a kind of Preset.

It was never one concept. It was five rules that existed only because those two Presets were not stored: a frozen list of two names standing as the source of truth, an identifier derived from the name because it had to survive a reload without being written anywhere, a reserved-name rule refusing the user a save under either, a discard rule dropping any stored entry that used one, and a second `apply-preset` payload shape carried through `validPayload`, `leavesUnchanged` and `apply`. All five are deleted rather than relocated — nothing moves to the caller, because after the first write there is no second kind of Preset to tell the first apart from.

## The predicate

Seeding an empty list would put the examples back the moment a listener deleted the last one, which is the change undone. So the question is *never written* against *written and now empty* — a distinction `localStorage` already draws, returning `null` for a key never written and `"[]"` for one deliberately emptied, and one that is trustworthy only because nothing writes `polynome-presets-v2` speculatively.

It lives in `createStoredPresets`, which takes the raw stored value: `null` seeds, a string is parsed and repaired through `createSavedPresets`, and unparseable JSON empties rather than seeds, because a value this version cannot parse is still evidence that something wrote it. Put in `app.js` the predicate would be reachable only from a browser test.

The issue names the key `polynome-presets`; that one is retired, and the live key is `polynome-presets-v2`. The argument is unchanged, only the literal.

## What else falls out

`apply-preset` carries a Configuration and nothing else. The collapse is safe because both branches already agreed on identity — one built from an id-free literal, the other stripping identifiers before rebuilding. A name is now a malformed payload and therefore a `TypeError`, and `preset-not-found` goes with it, since only the name branch could produce it.

`choices.presetNames` and `describeConfiguration().selectedPreset` were already dead. Neither reached the interface: `app.js` destructures the other five choices, and the panel marks selection through `describePresets`, which is the only thing handed the stored list. Both were read by `test/configuration.test.js` alone.

## One defect found in review

The preset heading kept a hardcoded `2` from `index.html`, and `renderPresetPanel` does not run while the panel is closed, so the count was only ever corrected once the panel had been opened. That literal was safe while two built-ins were guaranteed and is not now — deleting both and reloading read "2 presets" over an empty list. `renderPresetCount` is separate for the same reason the early return exists: counting is `savedPresets.length`, and none of the describing work that return avoids is needed to know it.

## Decision record

ADR-0010 records the decision, including what a wholesale storage clear does: it leaves the key absent, so an open tab seeds again. That is the intended answer — clearing this origin returns it to a first run, and from inside the page nothing distinguishes that from a browser opening Polynome for the first time. It is not a deletion undone, because deleting leaves `"[]"`, a written key, which is never seeded.

ADR-0003 and ADR-0006 are left as written, per the precedent ADR-0009 sets; ADR-0010 is where the correction is read from. **The number `0010` is a proposal** — `AGENTS.md` requires renumbering to one above the highest on `main` before this merges.

## Verification

`npm run check` passes: Biome clean apart from two warnings pre-existing in `test/accessibility.test.js`, TypeScript clean, 182 unit tests, 50 browser tests, coverage at 96.96% lines / 90.11% branches / 95.59% functions against ratchets of 95 / 87 / 94.

The manual audio checks in `AGENTS.md` gained a precondition: a profile the examples have been renamed or deleted in needs its preset key cleared before check 1 has anything to listen to.

author: os-zhuang
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5179

## 采纳了 issue 里允许的「声明式 retention」反驳路线

issue 的裁定给了两条路(适配器内清理 / 声明式 retention),并要求走后者时说明理由。本 PR 走声明式,理由是三条硬事实,不是偏好:

1. **ADR-0057 §3.3 明写「一个平台级 reaper,不是 N 个插件各扫各的」。** `LifecycleService` 由 engine 插件无条件注册(`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:288`,注释原话:"a declared retention that drives no sweeper is dead surface"),每个有数据引擎的 kernel 都在跑,默认每小时一次。同包的兄弟表 `sys_job_run` 早就是这么做的(`retention: { maxAge: '30d' }`),`sys_job_queue` 是这一族里唯一漏掉的。在适配器 poll 循环里再造一个清理器,等于给同一张表加第二个扫除者。
2. **`retention.onlyWhen` 就是为这种表造的。** spec 里它的 describe 原话:"for tables that interleave live workflow state with terminal history"。`sys_job_queue` 正是这种表 —— pending/running 是活的、completed 是历史、dlq 等人看。reaper 已经把它并进删除条件(`lifecycle-service.ts:654 → :783`),且已有回归用例(`lifecycle-service.test.ts` 的 "merges retention.onlyWhen into the reap filter (mixed tables, #2834)")。
3. **该表的写入方是适配器自己,不是用户数据** —— 这正是无人值守删除在这里安全、而对业务表不安全的原因;窗口写在对象定义上,运维能看见,还能经 `lifecycle` settings 命名空间按环境覆盖,不用改代码。

## 落地内容

`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-job-queue.object.ts`:

```ts
lifecycle: {
  class: 'transient',
  retention: { maxAge: '7d', onlyWhen: { status: 'completed' } },
}
```

- **只清 `completed`。** `pending`/`running` 是未投递的活儿,`dlq`/`failed` 是死信队列,存在的意义就是等人处理(`listFailed` / `replay` / `purgeFailed` 仍是唯一出口),**任何年龄都不自动清**。
- **用 `retention` 不用 `ttl`。** TTL 没有行过滤器,而 dlq 行同样会写 `completed_at` —— 一个 `ttl: { field: 'completed_at' }` 会把死信队列一起吃掉。
- **`class: 'transient'`(workflow / ephemeral state),不是 `telemetry`。** 按 ADR-0057 §3.6,`telemetry`/`event`/`audit` 类在注册了 `telemetry` datasource 的部署里会被**改路由到另一个库**(engine `getDriver` 第 3 步,优先级高于 manifest 的 `defaultDatasource: 'cloud'`)。把一个还在投递的工作队列换库是迁移,不是清理;`transient` 按 §3.6 明确留在主库。

## 保留窗与去重窗口的关系(代码注释里写死了,不只在这里)

去重是拿终态行的 `created_at` 跟 `idempotencyWindowMs`(默认 24h)比,reaper 的 cutoff 用的是**同一根 `created_at` 轴** —— 所以「保留窗 ≥ 去重窗」就等价于「去重还需要的行一定还没被清」,两条规则之间没有时钟偏差。7d 给了一周的投递历史可查,对默认去重窗有 7 倍余量。

这条不变量现在是**被强制的**,不是巧合:`DbQueueAdapter` 读对象上声明的窗口(新导出 `completedRetentionWindowMs()`),构造时若 `idempotencyWindowMs` 比它长就直接抛错并报出两个数字 —— 而不是等几天后冒出重复投递、日志里一行都没有。注释落在三处:对象定义、`DbQueueAdapterOptions.idempotencyWindowMs`、`publish()` 的去重点。

## 关于 PM 补充里的两点

- **批量上限**:声明式路线下清理不是逐行删,而是每次 sweep 一条 `DELETE ... WHERE created_at < ? AND status = 'completed'`(`lifecycle-service.ts:780`),不存在「一次 poll 删 N 行」的循环。REAP_GUARD 的 500×20 分批只用于注册了 reap guard 的对象。这是 `sys_activity`(14d)、`sys_job_run`(30d)这些量级更大的表一直以来的姿态,没有为本表另立一套的理由;若认为首扫存量表的单条大 DELETE 需要分批,那是 LifecycleService 对**所有** lifecycle 表的共性问题,已另开 finding(见下)。
- **日志不吵**:LifecycleService 每次 sweep 只打**一行**聚合 info(`[lifecycle] sweep: N policy(ies) applied, ~M rows reaped, ...`),而且注释原话就是 "cleanup must not re-feed the tables it drains"。本表只是被计入这行既有日志,没有新增 logger,也不会随 poll(秒级)刷屏。

## 测试

新增 `packages/services/service-queue/src/job-queue-retention.test.ts`(10 例),其中 `sweep()` 忠实镜像 reaper 的 where 构造(`{ created_at: { $lt: cutoff }, ...onlyWhen }` + `multi: true` + 系统上下文),并且**读声明本身**而不是把窗口再抄一遍:

- 声明钉死:`class` / `maxAge: '7d'` / `onlyWhen` 恰好是 `{ status: 'completed' }` / 无 ttl / 无 archive;
- 保留窗 ≥ 默认去重窗(有人调短声明就红,而不是等生产出重复投递);
- 长跑:60 天 × 每天 publish→completed→sweep,**每一步**行数 ≤ 8(不做策略则是 60 行永久残留);
- 十年前的 dlq / failed / pending / running 行一律不被清,dlq 依然可 `listFailed`;
- 去重窗口内(23h)的 completed 行经 sweep 后仍在,重复 publish 仍被去重返回同一 id;
- 超过保留窗后行被清,同 key 重新被接受(此时早已出了去重窗,这是去重契约本身,不是破坏);
- 30 天没人处理的 pending 行 sweep 动不了,handler 一注册照常投递。

命令与结果见报告;`plugin-email`(队列消费方)全量 170 例一并跑绿,未受影响。

author: delpicorp
body:
Adds [dev-report](https://github.com/delpicorp/dev-report) as an external link, matching the other entries in that section. The skill lives in its own repository.

### What it does

You finish a long Claude Code session. A dozen files changed and several implementation decisions were made along the way, but the end-of-session summary is file names and function names — accurate, and written for someone reading the diff alongside it. Asking for it "simply" removes the reasoning too.

`/dev-report` explains the session in plain language instead: what was built or changed, why that approach was chosen, what is still unfinished or unverified, and what to do next.

Technical terms aren't stripped out — they're explained the moment they first appear, so the reasoning survives. Two rules do most of the work: every finding leads with the raw artifact (the actual log line, the actual count) before it gets explained, and the section on how a problem was solved has to name the option that was rejected and what would have gone wrong.

### Details

```
/plugin marketplace add delpicorp/dev-report
/plugin install dev-report@delpicorp
```

- Single skill — no agents, hooks, or MCP servers. About 380 always-on tokens.
- Explicit-only, so it does not fire on a casual "what did you just do?"
- Reports come out in whatever language the command was typed in. Aliases ship for Korean (`/개발보고`), Japanese (`/開発報告`), and Spanish (`/informe-desarrollo`). File paths, function names, and log lines always stay in their original form.
- Two worked example reports ship in the repo (illustrative, not real customer sessions).
- MIT licensed. Disclosure: I'm the author.

Happy to reword or move the entry if it fits better elsewhere.

author: mickamy
body:
Adds the SCRAM-SHA-256 client valet uses to authenticate against an upstream PostgreSQL server. This is the one piece of the proxy that could not be borrowed: valet speaks raw wire messages rather than using a driver, so `pgx` cannot do it.

Verified against the published vectors in RFC 7677 section 3. That test is what matters most here — if the key derivation, the proof, or the auth message assembly were off by a byte, valet would authenticate against nothing.

## Package boundary

`internal/pgauth` depends on nothing from `pgwire`. It deals in the payloads the exchange carries; the caller wraps them in `SASLInitialResponse` and friends. Keeping it separate is what makes the RFC vectors replayable on their own.

## A failed exchange is over

`ErrAuth` documents that retrying with the same credentials is never safe, and the state machine now enforces it. Every failure — a rejected proof, a malformed server message, or a step called in the wrong order — moves to a terminal state, so a client cannot be driven into a second attempt.

The out-of-order case is deliberate rather than incidental. It spends no nonce and touches no server, so it could be argued as recoverable. But it means the caller's own state machine has lost track of where it is, and a client that carried on from there would be authenticating on behalf of code in an unknown state. Starting over costs nothing, since a `SCRAMClient` serves one exchange either way.

## Validation is stricter than libpq, on purpose

libpq accepts any iteration count above zero and any salt length. Both are cheap to exploit offline against a proof captured from the wire, so valet draws the line differently:

- **Iterations must be 4096 to 1000000.** 4096 is what RFC 7677 names for SHA-256 and what PostgreSQL defaults to; the error names `scram_iterations` so an operator can find the cause. The upper bound matters because the derivation runs before anything about the server has been verified — an unbounded count lets one hostile upstream occupy a core per connection attempt.
- **The salt must be at least 16 bytes.** With one byte there are 256 candidate keys per password, which is not a search. PostgreSQL generates 16, and requiring it also keeps `crypto/pbkdf2` from refusing the derivation in FIPS 140-only mode.
- **Reserved and duplicate attributes are refused.** RFC 5802 section 5 requires failing on `m=` rather than ignoring it. Duplicates are rejected for the same reason startup parameters reject them: two parsers disagreeing about which copy counts is something to aim at. Unrecognized keys are still accepted, since the RFC reserves those for extensions.
- **A server-final carrying both a signature and an error is refused.** Guessing which half of a self-contradicting answer to believe is worse than declining.

## Mutual authentication is not optional

`Complete` reports whether the server proved it knows the password. A caller must check it rather than treating `AuthenticationOk` as sufficient: a server that answers the client-final-message with `AuthenticationOk` and no `AuthenticationSASLFinal` leaves valet having proved itself to a server that proved nothing back, which is what an attacker relaying the connection would arrange.

## Two limits worth knowing about

Both are recorded in the package documentation, because each is a reason a connection can fail that no error message explains on its own.

**Channel binding is not implemented.** Where an upstream advertises both `SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS` and `SCRAM-SHA-256`, an attacker between valet and the database can strip the `-PLUS` offer and valet will complete the plain exchange without noticing. It cannot even signal the downgrade, since the `y` gs2 header is a claim of support it does not have. Until `-PLUS` lands, TLS certificate verification on the upstream connection is the only defense there, and therefore not optional.

**SASLprep is not applied.** Normalization would mean a dependency on `x/text/secure/precis`, which is not yet worth one binding. Passwords are used as given, which matches PostgreSQL for ASCII and for any password the server also fails to normalize. A non-ASCII password requiring normalization will not authenticate.

## Tests

Mutation checks confirm the guards are actually pinned: reverting `%q` to `%s`, shrinking the nonce, removing either iteration bound, dropping the identity escaping, or dropping the terminal-failure latch each fail the suite. Every case in the failure tables asserts on the message as well as the sentinel, so a case cannot pass by failing an unrelated check earlier in the function.

author: rukadeakshay01
body:
**Stacked on #332 — merge that first.** Base is `eeschema-directive-text`, not `main`: a netclass label's row shows its text, which only exists in the model after #332.

Ports the `m_netNavigator` tree (`MakeNetNavigatorNode` + `GetNetNavigatorItemText`) and `SelectNextPrevNetNavigatorItem` behind **Tab / Shift+Tab**. A node per net, a leaf per item on it, each described in words — *"Symbol 'R1' pin '1' (A)"*, *"Wire from (a, b) to (c, d)"*. Clicking a leaf selects the item it names.

## Two things that read like their neighbours and are not

- **Tab and Shift+Tab wrap.** `SelectNextPrevNetNavigatorItem` walks past the end to the beginning and back. **Previous/Next Marker (#347) deliberately does not.** Both stepping rules are in this codebase now, and a test pins each against the other — this is exactly the kind of pair that gets "unified" by accident later.
- **A graphic line names itself.** A line that is neither wire nor bus resolves to *"Graphic line not connectable"* rather than being dropped, so a tree that somehow holds one explains itself instead of showing a blank row.

## Scope notes

Upstream groups a net's leaves by sheet path; we work on the open sheet like the rest of our connectivity, so that level would have exactly one child and the leaves sit directly under the net.

The **View > Panels > Net Navigator** entry did not exist here, and that was *not* inventory drift — upstream gates it on the `m_IncrementalConnectivity` advanced config, which is off by default. We always have connectivity, so it is always offered.

`netOfItem` is included for **Find in Net Navigator** (#76), which now has nothing else left to build on.

## Verification

12 tests, mutation-checked four ways (no wrap → 1 fail; `~` pin name shown → 1; graphic line dropped → 1; tree unsorted → 1). The sort mutation initially survived because the fixture's nets happened to come out in name order; a net whose label is last in the file and first alphabetically now pins it.

Full CI: biome exit 0, `pnpm -r typecheck` clean, 3446 tests, designer build ok.

author: guilhem-lm
body:
## Summary

An emoji in a flow step summary kept its unzoomed pixel size when the flow graph canvas was
zoomed, so at high zoom it looked far too small next to the words beside it.

The cause is in Gecko, not in our code. On macOS, Firefox resolves emoji to Apple Color Emoji,
which is a bitmap (`sbix`) font, and it rasterizes those glyphs at a size that ignores an
ancestor's `transform: scale()` — which is exactly how `.svelte-flow__viewport` implements canvas
zoom. Text outlines re-rasterize at the scaled size; the bitmap emoji glyph does not.

Confirmed Firefox-only: Chrome scales the emoji correctly at every zoom level (measured ink
height 22px → 36px going 1.0× → 1.6×, in step with the zoom). Narrowed on an isolated test page
to the transform itself — scaling the same label by `font-size` instead of by `transform` renders
correctly, and *every* variant that used `transform: scale()` reproduced the bug, including with
`will-change: transform`, `translateZ(0)`, and `text-rendering: geometricPrecision`. So no CSS
property on the existing text fixes it; the emoji has to stop being a bitmap glyph.

The fix bundles Noto Color Emoji, whose COLR glyphs are vectors and therefore scale like any
other text, and appends it to the app-wide font stack after Inter.

## Changes

- Bundle Noto Color Emoji in `frontend/static/fonts/`, split into 10 files by `unicode-range`
  exactly as Google Fonts serves it. Client-side, a chunk is only fetched when a page renders an
  emoji in that range — verified in the browser that loading the flow editor with one 🚀 fetches
  **1 of the 10 chunks** (118 KB), and a page with no emoji fetches none. Note the 2.0 MB total is
  nonetheless embedded in every binary and image: `static_assets.rs` serves `frontend/build/` via
  `rust_embed`, which bakes in all ten chunks regardless of what clients request.
- Add the ten matching `@font-face` blocks to `frontend/src/lib/assets/app.css`, next to the
  existing self-hosted Inter face, with the Firefox constraint recorded.
- `frontend/tailwind.config.cjs`: `main: ['Inter', '"Noto Color Emoji"', 'sans-serif']`. This is
  the single app-wide source of truth — it reaches `html` through the `addBase` call in the same
  file. Noto sits *after* Inter, so it only ever picks up codepoints Inter lacks.
- `frontend/src/routes/+layout.svelte`: same stack on the toast wrapper, which has its own scoped
  rule rather than inheriting.
- Include the SIL OFL 1.1 license text alongside the font files.

Beyond the reported bug, this also gives emoji a consistent appearance across operating systems
and fixes Linux clients, many of which ship no color emoji font at all and render tofu boxes today.

## Screenshots

Flow graph at default zoom and zoomed in, both after the change:

![pr-default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/agent-screenshots-internal/main/shots/glm/emoji-in-flow/1785831684-pr-default.png)

![pr-zoomed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/agent-screenshots-internal/main/shots/glm/emoji-in-flow/1785831686-pr-zoomed.png)

These are Chrome, which never exhibited the bug — they are evidence of no regression, not of the
fix. The bug is a compositor-level artifact: Playwright's Firefox screenshots re-render from the
display list rather than reading back the compositor, so they showed the emoji scaling correctly
even before this change. The fix itself was verified by hand in a real Firefox.

## Known limitation (pre-existing, not introduced here)

`assets/app.css` is exported by `@windmill-labs/components`, but `files` is `["dist", "package"]`
and `svelte-package -o package` never copies `static/`. So the published stylesheet references
font files the tarball does not ship — that is already true on `main` for
`url('/Inter-Variable.woff2')`, and these `@font-face` blocks follow the same pattern.

For embedders this means the emoji chunks 404 and the browser falls back to the system emoji font,
i.e. exactly the pre-PR behaviour; `font-display: swap` means nothing blocks on it, and
`unicode-range` means only the ranges actually used are requested. Making the URLs
package-resolvable means moving both Inter and Noto under `src/lib/assets/` and changing how the
SvelteKit app resolves them — worth doing, but as its own change rather than inside an
emoji-scaling bug fix.

## Test plan

- [x] In **Firefox**, open a flow with an emoji in a step summary and zoom the canvas in and out —
      the emoji scales with the text at every zoom level. Confirmed by hand; this is the one check
      that cannot be automated, since Playwright's Firefox screenshots re-render from the display
      list and were green even before the fix.
- [x] On a page with one emoji, exactly one chunk is fetched, not all ten (measured via
      `document.fonts`); a page with no emoji fetches none.
- [x] Chrome renders the flow correctly with the new stack (no regression).
- [ ] Safari smoke test.
- [ ] Eyeball a couple of emoji-heavy non-flow surfaces (AI chat, item summaries, markdown) — the
      app-wide stack changes emoji appearance there too, which is intended but worth a look.
- [ ] Render a keycap sequence (`1️⃣`, `#️⃣`): Inter covers the digit and `#` while chunk 2 carries
      U+20E3 and U+FE0F, so the cluster spans two fonts. Expected to be fine via cluster-aware
      matching, but it is the one case where the Inter-first ordering could bite.

When proxy building adds only pre parent call code to a method – without any post code – and the method declares a `void` or `never` return type, the generated proxy method contains the pre code but no call to the original method: the original implementation is silently skipped.

This change renders the parent call (without a return statement, which is not allowed for these return types) like the branch for pre and post parent call code already does.

Note for the upmerge to 9.2: the unit test `noParentCallIsRenderedForVoidAndNeverReturnTypesIfOnlyPreParentCallCodeExists` introduced with #3596 documents the old behavior and needs to be inverted – the `ProxyMethodGeneratorTest` introduced with this change covers the corrected behavior and will conflict with the file of the same name from #3596.
