author: licheer-zte
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #92244: both the core model-directive path and the **Telegram model-picker button callback** invoked `applyModelOverrideToSessionEntry` without `preserveAuthProfileOverride`. Switching to a non-default model therefore **unconditionally deleted** `authProfileOverride`, `authProfileOverrideSource`, and `authProfileOverrideCompactionCount` — even when those fields were set by a non-picker source (session-level override, CLI flag, env var). The user saw "Model changed to X" with no warning that their auth-profile override was silently destroyed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared mutator (`applyModelOverrideToSessionEntry`) already supports `preserveAuthProfileOverride`: when set and no explicit `profileOverride` is supplied, the destructive branch that deletes the auth-profile fields is skipped. Both call sites simply never passed it. The fix keys preservation off `isDefault` — an explicit reset to the default model is the one case where clearing the auth-profile override is intended; any other model switch keeps a non-picker override (and still updates it when the request carries an explicit `profileOverride`).

Changed call sites:
- `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.ts` — core directive path (`preserveAuthProfileOverride: !params.request.isDefault`)
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-model.runtime.ts` — the Telegram picker button callback named in the report (`preserveAuthProfileOverride: !isDefaultSelection`)

## User Impact

Before: selecting a different model via the Telegram picker (or a model directive) silently removed a session's auth-profile override and its source/compaction metadata, breaking profile-bound auth for later turns with no error surfaced.

After: switching models keeps the existing auth-profile override. Only an explicit reset to the default model clears it. Explicit profile selection still updates the override exactly as before.

## Evidence

### New regression test (core path)
`src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts` — "keeps a non-picker auth-profile override when switching to a non-default model (#92244)": entry with `authProfileOverride: "openai:work"` / source `cli` switches from the default (anthropic/claude-opus-4-6) to openai/gpt-4o; asserts both the override and its source survive.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/model-picker/
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  25 passed (25)
```

### Telegram callback path
`bot-handlers.callback-model.runtime.ts` now passes `preserveAuthProfileOverride: !isDefaultSelection` into the same mutator, so the Telegram button path (the exact user action named in the report) no longer deletes non-picker auth-profile overrides.

### Intentional behavior preserved
The pre-existing test "resets to default and clears auth plus a provider-incompatible runtime" (explicit `isDefault: true` selection clears auth) still passes — included in the 25 above.

body:
The Users tab hides accounts holding a platform role — and with them the only role editor in the product, so an Ally staffer could not be granted a consumer-app role through the UI. INTERNAL made this worse: it joined SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES, so it was both excluded from the list and filtered out of the role picker, leaving the intended "INTERNAL alongside LEARNER" shape unreachable.

- New super-duper-admin-only filter, "Platform accounts → Include Ally staff & super admins", off by default. It is hidden from everyone else rather than 403-ing on click, since the backend only accepts the opt-in from that tier. The platform roles join the Role filter only while those accounts are listed, and are dropped again when the opt-in goes away so the list can never come back empty for an invisible reason.
- INTERNAL is now assignable. Only the two tier roles are withheld, via TIER_MANAGED_ROLES, because the Super Admins tab owns those with its own confirmations and self-lockout guards.
- Those tier roles are held out of the picker, shown read-only ("Super duper admin is kept — change that in the Super Admins tab"), and re-added to every change-roles payload, resolved against the full role list. Without this, granting LEARNER to a super duper admin would have demoted them: change-roles replaces the whole set, and the picker never showed the tier.
- The modal also states that consumer-app roles only surface content assigned to that account's organization, which is what a learner on a platform account actually sees.

author: mrcsin
body:
## Problem

The in-app grid-style editor (`GridStyleEditorViewModel`) was the last unlocalized operator surface in the error-localization roadmap. Its `ErrorMessage` was built by **joining raw `.Message` strings**, bypassing `ReasonLocalizer` entirely — `ReasonLocalizer` wasn't referenced in `StyleEditor/` at all. So a load / validate / save failure rendered English regardless of UI culture. The editor opens *after* startup (culture established), so there's no reason to leave any of it English — leaving loader errors English while validator errors were Russian would show one panel in mixed languages depending on whether the file was missing or a color was malformed.

## What changed

Type all **8** grid-style error producers and route the three `ErrorMessage` join sites through `ReasonLocalizer.Localize`:

| Producer | Typed errors |
|---|---|
| `GridStyleValidator` | config-missing, section-missing (unifies `colors` + generic), orientation-invalid, key-missing, invalid-hex-color |
| `GridStyleLoader` | config-not-found; **load-failed** (Rule-B envelope) |
| `GridStyleWriter` | **save-failed** (Rule-B envelope) |

Each gets a `ReasonLocalizer` arm, en/ru resx + Designer, and a coverage sample. The join sites localize by type and fall through to `.Message` for anything not yet typed. English base messages stay byte-identical except the two Rule-B headlines, which drop the `: {ex.Message}` tail.

**Two design points worth calling out:**
- The orientation error **carries its two expected values as properties** — `GridOrientationValues` is `internal` to Core and invisible to the UI localizer, so the arm can't reference it.
- The dropped exception detail rides `CausedBy(ex)` and is logged at **both** consumers of the shared loader: the editor view model (`LogWarning`) and the **startup** path in `Program.cs` (`Log.Error`). Without the startup sink, a malformed `grid_style.yaml` at launch would lose its parse detail entirely.
- `ReportSaveException` drops its raw tail to the already-localized `Resources.SaveFailed` — the exceptions reaching it are pre-write pipeline throws, not file-write failures, so naming a file would mislead.

**Scope:** pure localization. Issue #118 (the editor's structural refactor — declarative 60-field map, async `Save`, `HexColor.Parse` removal) is independent and untouched; only the three join sites move. After this, the operator-facing error surfaces are fully typed — the startup config load (before culture exists) and the two PLC malformed-wire diagnostic edges remain English by design.

## Verification

- `dotnet build SemiStep.slnx` — 0 warnings; `dotnet test` — 1685 passed, 0 failed; `dotnet format` clean.
- `ReasonLocalizerTests` pins each of the 8 types' ru render + the en `Localize == .Message` pins; `CoreErrorLocalizationCoverageTests` auto-enrolls the 8 public errors; `ResourceSyncTests` enforces en/ru/Designer key + placeholder parity.
- `GridStyleEditorViewModelTests.LoadAsync_MalformedHexColor` overlays a corrupted color on the shipped config and asserts `ErrorMessage` is the exact Russian hex sentence (a regression to raw `.Message` fails it). Two log-sink tests assert the `CausedBy` exception reaches the log — removing the sink call fails them.
- `GridStyleEditorFacadeTests` assert `GridStyleLoadFailedError`/`GridStyleSaveFailedError` retain their exception on the nested `.Reasons`.
- Review chain: comprehensive (5 agents, all OUTCOME ACHIEVED) → smells → comment audit → critical, all clean after fixes. The reviews caught an untested log sink (added tests), a doc overreach ("sole English-by-design surface" — qualified against the PLC edges), and a `Path`→`FilePath` rename.
- **Manual test (operator):** passed.

```

0ab4468 docs(test): drop misleading Rule-B comment in localizer test
4143204 refactor(l10n): rename GridStyleConfigNotFoundError.Path to FilePath
70409ad test(l10n): cover grid-style exception log sink; fix doc overreach
44a75bf test(l10n): cover grid-style error localization end-to-end
79c7adf feat(l10n): type grid-style file-IO errors
```

author: clarkemoyer
body:
Three rows from Conductor run 90. Ledger goes **L110 / 109 rows → L113 / 112 rows**.

## The rows

**L111 — a mutation that breaks the syntax exits 1, and so does a guard that fired.** Mutation-reviewing #1056 I neutered the orphan check by rewriting `problems.append(` into `problems.extend([] and [`. Unbalanced, so the module raised `SyntaxError` and the run exited **1 with zero `FAIL` lines** — which through the exit code alone is indistinguishable from "the guard detected the planted defect". It credits a check that never ran, in the reassuring direction. CLAUDE.md already has the general form (a test asserting a non-zero exit must also assert on the output); the corollary is that it applies to the **reviewer's own** mutation. Predict which tests will redden, by name, before applying it.

**L112 — two parsers over one file drift apart silently.** `_ROW` was `L\d{2}`, so once the ledger passed L99 it matched only the `L10` prefix of a three-digit id, demanded a separator where the third digit was, and stopped matching at all. Eleven rows (L100–L110) went invisible to five checks including the guard-path existence check. Measured on `main` at `3aaad32`: **109 rows in the file, 98 parsed**. Coverage fell and the suite got *greener*. The fix that holds is not a wider regex — it is asserting the two parsers agree on the id **set**, which is what #1056 shipped and what this row cites.

**L113 — a saturated cap looks exactly like satisfied demand.** Open `github-actions` Dependabot PRs across 62 FFC-EX repos: 17 zeros, one 2, four 3s, five 4s, **35 at exactly 5, none above 5**. Five is `open-pull-requests-limit`. A mode sitting on the configured ceiling with an empty tail is a limit being enforced, not demand tapering — so "no new Actions updates lately" was the mechanism having stopped in 35 of 62 repos. Filed as #1057.

author: sandeepmalhotragithub
body:
Accounts holding a platform role (SUPER_ADMIN, SUPER_DUPER_ADMIN and now INTERNAL) are filtered out of GET /v1/users so a tenant's user list only shows that tenant's own people. That exclusion also removed the only route to their roles: with no row there is no role editor, so Ally staff could not be given a consumer-app role (LEARNER, COUNSELOR…) through the admin UI at all — the sole option was a hand-rolled call to assign-role.

- GET /v1/users accepts includePlatformAdmins=true, which drops the exclusion. Honoured only for callers holding view:super-duper-admins; anyone else gets a 403 rather than a silently ignored parameter. Absent or non-"true" values keep today's behaviour exactly.
- GET /v1/users/me now returns `roles` alongside the collapsed `role`. Both web clients already read it: the priority list behind `role` cannot express a multi-role account, so a staffer holding [INTERNAL, LEARNER] arrives as LEARNER and no super-admin gate accepts them.

No migration and no new endpoint — role editing already exists at POST /v1/authorization/change-roles.

author: emmanuelmathot
body:
Closes #71.

## The problem

`GeoZarrParams.multiscale_levels` defaulted to `0`, so unless a testbed config said otherwise the GeoZarr arm produced a **flat, full-resolution store with no overviews**. Two consequences, both raised on the CNES side ("GeoZarr a aussi des overview", review comment #21):

1. It isn't a representative GeoZarr — an overview pyramid is the direct analogue of COG overviews.
2. It skewed the benchmark. TiTiler had to pull full-resolution chunks and downsample them for every zoomed-out tile, so the D2 §6 display numbers measured the *missing pyramid*, not the format.

## Default-on

`multiscale_levels: auto` (the new default) coarsens by `/2` while the shorter side stays ≥ 256 px — the same rule GDAL follows for COG overviews. A 10980 px MAJA band gets 5 overview levels; the 512 px CI fixture gets 1, so the deployable path exercises pyramid generation. An explicit integer overrides; `0` still writes the flat store, kept deliberately as the comparison case that quantifies what the pyramid buys.

## Which spec

The issue asked for GeoZarr 0.4 + an OGC tile-matrix-set. **That's not what this does.** GeoZarr 0.4 is deprecated and GeoZarr v1 — which will assemble the Zarr conventions — hasn't landed, so there's no GeoZarr version to claim conformance to. The store targets the published conventions directly, declared in `zarr_conventions`:

| Convention | What it carries |
| --- | --- |
| [`multiscales`](https://github.com/zarr-conventions/multiscales/blob/v0.1/README.md) | the `layout`: which group holds each level, which level it was `derived_from`, the relative `scale`/`translation` that derivation induced, `resampling_method: average` |
| [`spatial`](https://github.com/zarr-conventions/spatial/blob/v0.1/README.md) | `spatial:transform` (rasterio/affine coefficient order), `shape`, `bbox`, `dimensions`, `registration` |
| [`geo-proj`](https://github.com/zarr-conventions/proj/blob/v0.1/README.md) | the **native** CRS as `proj:code`/`proj:wkt2` — nothing reprojected to web mercator |

The documents come from [`zarr-cm`](https://github.com/zarr-conventions/zarr-cm) rather than being hand-rolled, so each convention's uuid, pinned schema URLs and validation stay that package's business to track. It's pure Python on `typing-extensions`, so it's in `dev` too and the metadata is unit-tested in CI without the geo stack.

What's ours in `geozarr_multiscales.py` is only the geometry: pyramid depth, per-level geotransform decimation, cell-centre coordinates, and the **GDAL ↔ rasterio/affine coefficient-order conversion** — a trap that silently shifts every coordinate if confused, so there's a test pinning it.

Every level group *and* the array inside it carry their own grid. The convention lets a group's description stand in for its arrays, but xarray drops dataset attributes when a variable is selected out — and a tile server addresses a variable.

## Two bugs this surfaced

- Every level was getting the **native** geotransform copied onto it, mislocating each overview by its decimation factor.
- `compression_ratio` sized "uncompressed" from the base array while `size_bytes` counted every level, so the pyramid's cost read as poor compression. Both now count every level.

## Size ↔ display, made visible

New `GeoZarrLayout.overview_bytes`; `summary.md` states what share of the store is pyramid, or flags a single-level store as not display-comparable. COG is larger partly *because* it carries overviews, so this is what makes the size comparison like-for-like.

## Reader metadata

`SourceObject.standard_name` joins `nodata`/`scale_factor` — the delivered rasters name the CF quantity nowhere. MAJA reflectance vs `quality_flag` masks, S1 RTC gamma0.

## ⚠️ Breaking: no CF georeferencing in the output

`spatial_ref`, `grid_mapping` and `_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS` are **gone**. The conventions are the only place the grid lives, and Zarr v3 names an array's axes in its own `dimension_names` field (which is what `spatial:dimensions` refers to).

[rioxarray 0.22+](https://github.com/corteva/rioxarray/releases) reads the conventions natively, so `.rio.crs` / `.rio.transform()` still work on every level — hence the `rioxarray>=0.22` bump in the `geozarr` extra. An older reader expecting a CF grid mapping will not georeference the output. This harness's own display metric now selects tiles from `proj:code` + `spatial:transform`.

## Verification

- **282 tests pass**; 221 + 31 skipped in a CI-shaped env (`dev` extras only), ruff clean.
- Store metadata round-trips through `zarr_cm.extract_many` with **nothing left over**, revision detected, all three documents validate.
- rioxarray georeferences levels 0/1/3 at both dataset and array level: same ground extent, cells doubling.
- The runner's store-walking path is exercised against nested level groups.

## Not included

Acceptance items 4–5 — re-measuring display/size and refreshing `consolidated-metrics.md` — are lab runs against CNES data plus an edit in the study repo. The issue wants them run **together with the zstd-on-COG codec-matched re-run**; the code is ready for that.

author: keyurgolani
body:
**Stacked on #436 (S129).** §1.4 decision 1 / R3 am.

## 🔴 The classification and the engine had no words in common

§1.4 says *"fail-open vs fail-closed is classified **per gate**"*, and the classification existed as data (`FAIL_OPEN_GATES` + `gate_failure_mode`). Measured:

```python
set(firepath.GATE_ORDER) & FAIL_OPEN_GATES  ==  set()
```

**Empty.** The set listed the per-trigger **cap keys** a person edits (`cost_cap`, `rate_cap`, `max_runs_per_hour`, `duty_gate` — the `GATE_KEYS` vocabulary), while the fire path walks **gate names** (`incident`, `screen`, `quiet`, `duty`, `budget`, `claim`, `yield`, `capability`).

Two vocabularies for two real surfaces, and the classifier only answered for one — so **every gate the engine actually runs resolved to `"closed"`**, including `duty` and `incident`, both of which are required to fail **open**.

## The gates were right; the classifier was wrong

Driven rather than assumed — the code could equally have been the bug:

| gate | driven behaviour | classifier said |
|---|---|---|
| `duty` (unregistered provider) | **allows** — *"the fire proceeds"* | closed ❌ |
| `incident` (unreadable flag) | **allows** | closed ❌ |
| `budget` (unreadable) | **refuses** | closed ✓ |

All three behaviours are correct. The table describing them disagreed in two of three cases, and **nothing outside tests read the table**, so nothing caught the drift.

A fourth instance of this program's signature defect, in its most self-referential form: **the inert control here was the description of the controls.**

## Both spellings resolve now

Rather than renaming one side. A person's trigger config says `duty_gate`; the fire path's gate is `duty`. Both are correct in their own surface, and a classifier that answered for only one is what produced this.

Adds a `FAIL_CLOSED_GATES` set so the security fences are **explicit** rather than implied by absence, with a test that the two sets never overlap — a gate in both would resolve by lookup order, the ambiguity S71 found in `fuse`.

## A real conflict in the plan, resolved explicitly

§1.4 groups *"budget/storm-guard checks"* as fail-open. §3.6 says *"the budget check is fail-closed — an unreadable budget is not an unlimited one"*, and the code follows §3.6.

Those are **two different questions wearing one word**:

- the per-trigger **cap keys** (`cost_cap`, `rate_cap`) fail **open** — a hung probe must not stop every automation
- the fire path's pre-claim budget **read** fails **closed** — an error is not an allowance

Both are now written down, so the next reader does not re-derive which clause wins.

## The tests assert against BEHAVIOUR, not the table

A table-vs-table test would have passed before this fix. These drive the real gates. **Reverting the change turns 4 red**, including the two behaviour-verified ones.

A completeness test also requires every `GATE_ORDER` entry to carry a stated direction, so a gate added to the walk without one fails instead of silently reading closed.

## Gate

`make lint` green. Full `pytest -n 4 --dist worksteal`: **15879 passed, 29 skipped, 13 xfailed**, zero failures. Verified merge-clean against `main`.

author: ehxuban11
body:
`train(..., cuda_graph=True)` went from 2 families to 24, across five tasks. ## What - New per-family specs: yolox, yolo7, yolo9_e2e, yolonas, picodet, rtmdet, fomo, nafnet. - Three shared mixins in `libreyolo/models/base/`: - `classify_cuda_graph.py`: resnet, convnext, mobilenetv4, efficientnetv2 - `semantic_cuda_graph.py`: segformer, lingbotvision - `detr_cuda_graph.py`: dfine, deim, deimv2, rtdetr, rtdetrv2, rtdetrv4, ec - `TrainGraphManager.invalidate()` + `BaseTrainer.invalidate_cuda_graph()`, for families that change what the captured region computes mid-run (YOLOX enables its L1 branch at mosaic close). - Capture now logs randomness-drawing layers inside the graph once. ## Two bugs fixed - **`cuda_graph=True` was a silent no-op for dfine, deim, deimv2, rtdetrv4 and ec.** Those trainers copy `_train_epoch` and called `on_forward` (eager) instead of `_forward_train` (routed). Nothing errored; capture never engaged. - **Re-capture was impossible.** `make_graphed_callables` rebinds `module.forward` in place; dropping a graph without restoring it makes the next capture's warm-up replay the dead graph inside the new capture and permanently disables the feature. ## Measured (RTX 5070 Ti, Windows, AMP, fastest of 24 steps) fomo 3.63x, mobilenetv4 2.74x, efficientnetv2 2.44x, yolo9-t 1.99x, yolo9_e2e 1.76x, yolo9_p2 1.49x, nafnet/resnet 1.25-1.26x, picodet 1.22x, deim/rtdetrv4 1.18x, yolonas 1.17x, dfine/deimv2/rfdetr/rtdetrv2/ec 1.15-1.16x, convnext 1.15x, yolox/segformer/rtdetr 1.12-1.13x, rtmdet 1.10x, yolo7/lingbotvision 1.04-1.05x. End to end, YOLO9-t on 406 images, 20 epochs, dataloader and validation included: 428.4s -> 367.7s (1.16x), mAP50-95 0.6394 both arms, per-epoch losses identical. The win tracks how much of a step is network rather than loss, and is largest at small batch. Phase split at 640/b8: yolo9-t network 84% (ceiling 6.1x), yolox-t 31% (1.5x), rtmdet-t 26% (1.3x). SimOTA is 69% of a YOLOX step. ## Numerics: needs a call before merge The old contract was "enabling `cuda_graph` never changes training numerics". That is now false in two places, both inherent: - **rtmdet**: `share_conv=True` aliases the head convs across all 3 pyramid levels, so those 2 weights' gradient is a 3-term sum. Eager and graphed sum in a different order; under fp16 that differs in the last bits. 137 of 139 gradients stay bit-identical. - **segformer**: stochastic depth inside the captured region. A replayed graph consumes the generator on its own schedule, so it does not reproduce the eager draw sequence. Statistically equivalent, like a different seed. I softened the doc rather than the code. The alternative is to keep the contract absolute and drop those two, costing 1.10x (rtmdet, 1.24x at b4) and 1.12x (segformer). **Product call, not a technical one.** Every other family is bit-identical, except fomo and lingbotvision at 1 ULP of float32. ## Normal precision (amp=False) Every family still captures at fp32. Speedups shift, because fp32 kernels run longer so a step is less launch-bound: | Family | AMP | fp32 | | --- | --- | --- | | mobilenetv4-s b16 | 2.74x | 3.61x | | fomo-s b16 | 3.63x | 3.06x | | yolo9-t b8 | 1.99x | 1.69x | | yolo9_e2e-t b8 | 1.76x | 1.52x | | picodet-s b8 | 1.22x | 1.15x | | dfine-n b4 | 1.16x | 1.13x | | yolox-t b8 | 1.13x | 1.08x | | nafnet-s b8 | 1.26x | 1.08x | | resnet-18 b16 | 1.25x | 1.05x | | rtmdet-t b8 | 1.10x | 1.04x | | yolonas-s b8 | 1.17x | 1.03x | | rtdetr-r18 b4 | 1.12x | 0.99x | **The parity guarantee is AMP-only, and the doc now says so.** At fp32 these families do not reproduce their own eager runs: two identical seeded eager YOLO9-t runs diverge 36% relative over 20 steps, YOLOX-t 2.6%. cuDNN picks a nondeterministic weight-gradient algorithm for some fp32 convolution shapes (measured: two back-to-back wgrads on one 8x64x160x160 conv differ by 3.2e-7 relative), and TF32 off does not fix it. Capture is not what removes reproducibility there. ## Step-0 per-parameter evidence Both arms provably hold identical weights at step 0. Loss delta is **exactly zero for all 24 families**, and **no BatchNorm buffer differs** anywhere. Gradients bit-identical: yolo9 583/583, yolo9_p2 775/775, yolo9_e2e 693/693, yolox 219/219, yolonas 460/460, picodet 369/369, yolo7 271/271, deimv2 298/300, rtmdet 173/177. D-FINE, DEIM and RT-DETRv2 look alarming (112/400, 113/422, 95/312) until the identical comparison runs eager against eager: 116/400, 117/422, 98/312. Those families reproduce barely a quarter of their own gradients; capture moves 3 or 4 more out of several hundred. The encoder-boundary split is sound. ## Edge paths now tested - `amp=False` capture - layer freezing (frozen params exercise `allow_unused_input`): bit-identical to eager - resume from checkpoint: re-captures, keeps training - capture raising OOM: exactly one warning, run finishes eager with the eager losses - gradient accumulation (`nbs`), where `zero_grad` runs once per window rather than per micro-batch - per-epoch validation with a live graph ## Check - `tests/unit`: 5068 passed, 0 failed. - New `tests/e2e/test_cuda_graph_training_families.py`: 49 tests, all pass. Per-family it asserts capture actually engages (every failure mode here degrades to eager silently), and holds the loss trajectory to the family's own eager-to-eager spread plus a documented per-family tolerance. Plus gradient accumulation, live-graph validation, and the YOLOX mosaic-close switch. - `tests/unit/test_cuda_graph_training.py`: +23 tests for invalidation, forward restoration, stochastic-layer detection, and the three mixins' gating. - `ruff`: 137 errors before and after; the new files are clean. ## Not verified - One box only: Windows, RTX 5070 Ti, torch 2.11+cu128. Nothing run on Linux or Ampere/Hopper. Failure mode there is a warning plus eager fallback, not broken training. - Resume-from-checkpoint with a live graph. - DDP and distillation stay excluded, as before. - Non-detect tasks on multi-task families (rfdetr seg/pose, ec seg/pose, dfine segment, rtmdet segment, yolonas pose) stay eager, gated. - Six DETR families default to `multi_scale=True`, where a graph may never capture in a short run. Documented; `multi_scale=False` for the full speedup. - `skills/run-rf100vl-benchmark/SKILL.md` still says `cuda_graph: true` is "bit-identical". True for the YOLO families, not for the DETR families or rtmdet. Not edited here: a recipe change orphans banked epochs. ## Code provenance All code in this PR is original, written for this PR, or a refactor of existing LibreYOLO code moved to a new boundary: - New files (`libreyolo/models/base/classify_cuda_graph.py`, `semantic_cuda_graph.py`, `detr_cuda_graph.py`, `tests/e2e/test_cuda_graph_training_families.py`): original. - `libreyolo/models/yolox/nn.py`: existing YOLOX head code split into `forward_train_maps` with no behavior change, plus two constant allocations moved onto the target device. The surrounding YOLOX implementation's provenance (Megvii YOLOX, Apache-2.0) is unchanged and already recorded in the notice files. - `libreyolo/models/yolo7/net.py`, `segformer/nn.py`, `lingbotvision/nn.py`: existing loss tails split into named methods, no behavior change. - Everything else: new methods on existing trainers, and additions to `libreyolo/training/cuda_graph.py` and `trainer.py`. No third-party code is introduced, adapted, or derived in this PR, so no notice-file changes are required.

Greptile Summary

 The PR extends training CUDA graph capture across detection, classification, semantic segmentation, point detection, and restoration families, while adding graph invalidation and safe eager-forward restoration. - Adds shared classification, semantic, and DETR encoder capture adapters plus family-specific capture specifications. - Routes copied D-F

author: jedrazb
body: Adds `DocxEditor.ContextMenu`, an example that customizes every part of the React adapter, and — following from what building that exposed — removes a large stubbed surface from the `Editor` contract. ## What's here **`DocxEditor.ContextMenu`.** Right-click opens Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, Select All, Link and Comment, each greyed out with the engine's own reason. Composes like the toolbar and menu bar: a row child replaces that row in place, `hidden` removes it, `preset={false}` starts from nothing, `ContextMenu.Item` adds a host action. Its rows *are* the menu bar's rows, reused rather than reimplemented, so a row looks and behaves the same in both. **Four new commands** — `selectAll`, `copy`, `cut`, `paste` — plus `snapshot().selectionCollapsed` and `useEditorCommand` accepting a raw `EditorCommand` rather than only a `ChromeSlotId`. **`examples/igloo/`** — `bun run dev:igloo`. Every `DocxEditor.*` part re-skinned, re-iconed and re-labelled under one theme. Most of it is `--doc-*` token overrides rather than component rewrites, which is the point. **Opt-in icons** on menu-bar triggers and on the colour split controls. Every other control took an `icon`; those didn't. **`useDocxSource`** — opening a document in one call instead of thirty lines of fetch + font loading + composition + cancellation. It holds the document back until fonts settle, because layout measures with them and releasing bytes first paginates on the fixed fallback and then re-paginates, which reads as the text jumping. `@docx-editor.dev/fonts` gains `defaultFonts()`, pairing the load and the face registration that had to be called together by hand. Both demos move onto it; the vite flagship loses 39 lines. ## The removals `hitTest`, `resolvePointer`, `dispatchInteraction`, `getInteractionFrame`, `getDisplay`, the caret and selection rect readers, `getScrollGeometry`, `getAccessibilityObservation`, the `display` event, `EditorHost.onDisplay`, the `pageContent` query, and `contracts/geometry.ts` with its published subpath. `contracts/interaction.ts` goes from 599 lines to 86. Every one was a stub with **zero callers**. They were removed rather than filled in because the honest-empty rule does not extend to them: `getComments()` returning `[]` is a true statement about a document, but `hitTest` returning `null` is indistinguishable from "you clicked the page margin", so no caller could tell unimplemented from answered. `getPageGeometry` was the cluster's one real consumer — both Vue rulers — and it returned `[]`, so **those rulers had been rendering nothing**. It is now implemented, in content pixels rather than layout points. Pointer interaction is untouched throughout: it never went through the facade, and the hit-test algorithm stays in `layout/semantic-hit-test.ts` where the surface calls it. ## Review Four expert reviews ran against the diff — core correctness, React hooks, security, dead code. No vulnerabilities. They found a number of real defects, several in code whose own comments argued it was correct, all fixed in `399d70870`: - `useEditorCommand` keyed its memo on the command's `type`, so two commands sharing a type returned stale state while `execute` ran the live one — the control rendered one thing and did another. - The context menu never took focus (it called `focus()` while still `visibility: hidden`), so its entire arrow-key layer was dead. - View mode gated commands but not the keyboard: the pages layer stayed `contentEditable`, so a "read-only" document still drew a caret, opened an IME, and told a screen reader it was writable. - `cut` deleted the selection even when the clipboard write was synchronously known to be impossible. - The context menu's merge algorithm was a third copy that had diverged — no Fragment unwrap, so a host mapping over its overrides got a duplicate row. Extracted and shared with the menu bar. ## Rebased onto `docx-editor-v2` The base landed `setEditingMode` (`editing` / `suggesting` / `viewing`), which supersedes the two-state `setMode` this branch had added — dropped, along with `snapshot().mode` and the React/Vue prop effects driving it. Merging the two surfaces exposed two defects in the base's mode handling, both fixed here: - The viewing gate refused **every** command, so a reader could not `selectAll` or `copy` the document a viewer exists to show. It disagreed with the construction-time `mode: 'view'` path, which has always gated on `mutating`. Viewing now refuses mutating commands only. - `setEditingMode` left the pages layer `contenteditable`. The engine refused the write, but the browser still offered one. The DOM affordance now follows the mode, at mount and at runtime. ## Notes - React-only, staged in the parity contract and the export-divergence note; the engine half is shared. - Breaking, marked `!`. npm has `0.0.1-placeholder`, so nothing downstream is affected. - Verified in the browser throughout. Core 2991 pass / 0 fail; React 233 pass (up from 199 on the base); Vue 9 pass. The 6 React and 8 Vue failures are pre-existing: each was reproduced identically on an untouched `origin/docx-editor-v2` worktree, and none is in a file this branch changes. `check:public-docs-surface` is likewise red on a clean v2 tree. - **CI did not run on this PR.** `ci.yml` triggers only on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, so no v2 PR is verified by it. Everything above was run locally: `typecheck`, all three suites, `api:extract` + `api:check`, and the export-parity, editor-contract, parity-contract and adapter-css-thin gates. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: doreen-admin
body:
## Summary
- `derive_searchable_relation_fields()` (`helpers/schema_helpers.py`) used to read a standalone `x-relationship.searchField`, declared independently of the `labelField` that actually renders on screen for that FK — nothing stopped the two from drifting apart (the field shown could differ from the field actually searched). It now derives the same `{relation, field}` list from `labelField` itself, sharing its origin with cmd_548's CSV-import full-match (`build_label_expression`) — the searched field can never disagree with the displayed field again.
- Only string-typed, non-dotted `labelField` elements qualify: `enum` fields (translated on-screen label vs. untranslated stored value — same trap as cmd_493), date/time, number, and CUID-pattern id fields are excluded. A composite `labelField` (`[f1, f2]`) is evaluated per element.
- `validate.py` (Section 14) now rejects, by entity/field name, any schema that still declares `searchField` — it has no effect post-retirement, and silently ignoring it would leave the schema author believing search still works.

author: loicmathieu
body:
## Summary

### 1. Skip redundant flowable resolution

Fixes the redundant executor work reported in #9008: a running flowable's resolveNexts()/resolveState() was being re-evaluated on every executor cycle, even on cycles where the resolver could only return empty (e.g. an If task's resolveNexts() was called 4 times per execution, 2 of them wasted). Each call also rebuilds a `RunContext`, which runs an outputRepository.findByExecution() query — so every wasted call is a wasted DB query too.

Adds `ExecutorService.canChildrenProgress(execution, parentTaskRun)`: a flowable can only produce a new child, or terminate, when it has no child task run yet or at least one child has terminated — every FlowableUtils.resolve*Nexts/resolveState implementation already returns empty/absent otherwise, so this guard never hides real work.
Skips the whole RUNNING-flowable block in handleFlowableTasks (RunContext included) when the guard says no child can progress.
Known limitation: once any child has terminated the guard stops helping, so a Sequential of 5 tasks still re-resolves on every cycle from task 2 onward. This removes the redundancy at the head of each flowable, not all of it.

Verified with LOGGER_LEVELS_IO_KESTRA_EXECUTOR=DEBUG tracing on IfTest.ifTruthy: 4 resolveNexts calls → 2,

### 2. Dispatch a newly-created root task run in the same executor cycle

`ExecutorContext.withTaskRun` used to only append new task runs to a separate `nexts` list, merged into the execution by `onNexts()` only after `process()` returned. That meant `handleWorkerTasks` could never see a task run created earlier in the same pass, costing a full executor cycle (execution-store lock + queue round-trip) between e.g. `handleNext` creating the flow's first task and `handleWorkerTasks` dispatching it to RUNNING.

- `withTaskRun` now merges new task runs into the execution as soon as they're produced, and sets `executionUpdated` directly on that merge.
- `onNexts()`'s own merge logic is now dead code (its one caller always passes an execution already merged into) and has been stripped back down to its one remaining job: the CREATED → RUNNING transition.

**Why this PR doesn't also reorder `handleFlowableTasks` before `handleWorkerTasks`** (which would collapse the *second* redundant cycle too, per #9008): It breaks every `Loop`-based test. The `Loop` case inside `handleFlowableTasks` transitions its own CREATED task run straight to RUNNING as it spawns sub-executions. Running `handleWorkerTasks` after that would leave the Loop task run RUNNING with no attempts (`handleWorkerTasks` only attaches the first RUNNING attempt to task runs it finds still CREATED), which crashes `LoopExecutionEventMessageHandler.terminateLoop()` (`attempts.getLast()` on an empty list) the moment the first sub-execution finishes. It would need either splitting `handleFlowableTasks` into a reorderable "compute nexts" half and a position-sensitive "custom executor logic" half, or making `Loop`'s spawn logic not bypass `handleWorkerTasks`'s attempt-injection.

Verified with `LOGGER_LEVELS_IO_KESTRA_EXECUTOR=DEBUG` tracing on `IfTest.ifTruthy`: 9 executor cycles → 8 (the `handleNext`-creates / `handleWorkerTasks`-dispatches pair now collapses into one; the `handleFlowableTasks`-creates / `handleWorkerTasks`-dispatches pair does not, for the reason above).

## Test plan

- [x] Same regression test as #17832 (`IfTest.shouldResolveFlowableOnlyWhenItCanProgress`) — flowable-resolution count unchanged at 2
- [x] `io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.IfTest` — 8/8 passing
- [x] Full `io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.*` suite — 123/123 passing (including the 5 Loop-based classes that failed with the full reorder before it was reverted)
- [x] `H2RunnerTest` — 99/99 passing
- [x] `H2RunnerRetryTest` — 21/21 passing

Closes #9008

author: lbm364dl
body:
Port of the mojibake half of #382, re-landed on current `main`. Child of the polity migration epic #458.

Item 2 of the issue -- the "duplicate Réunion spellings" -- is **not** touched: it was withdrawn by its author as a misread of the intentional short-versus-canonical pattern (`182 Reunion / Réunion`, exactly like `223 Turkey / Türkiye` and `167 Czech Republic / Czechia`). Both spellings are meant to be there.

## What was wrong

Three territory names shipped corrupt in the published area tables: the UTF-8 bytes of an accented letter decoded as a pair of Latin-1 characters in `inst/extdata/harmonization/regions_full.csv` and `polities_cats.csv`.

## Evidence it reproduced on `main`

Scanning every character column of all 55 shipped `data/*.rda` datasets, on this branch before any change:

```
  dataset               column     value
1 polities_cats         iea        CÃ´te d'Ivoire
2 polities_cats         water_area CÃ´te d'Ivoire
3 polity_area_crosswalk area_name  CuraÃ§ao
4 regions_full          name       CuraÃ§ao
5 regions_full          iea        CÃ´te d'Ivoire
6 regions_full          iea        Netherlands Antilles / CuraÃ§ao
7 regions_full          water_area CÃ´te d'Ivoire
8 regions_full          Lassaletta CuraÃ§ao
TOTAL: 8
```

Eight cells, three names, three published tables -- one more table and three more columns than the issue reported.

## What I changed

- **`data-raw/_labels.R`** (new): `repair_mojibake()` takes the Latin-1 bytes back out and re-reads them as UTF-8 (`iconv` cannot mend this in one call: `"UTF-8"` to `"latin1"` returns the string unchanged and the reverse double-encodes it). The round trip is only accepted when the result is `validUTF8()`, so a string that merely happens to contain U+00C3 is left alone. `repair_table_labels()` applies it across **every character column**, not a hand-picked label list -- the corruption also sits in `iea`, `water_area` and `Lassaletta`.
- Its own file because **two** data-raw scripts read the same vendored CSV: `harmonization_tables.R` builds `regions_full` and `polities_cats` from it, and `table_mappings.R` re-reads it as `regions_full_raw` to build `polity_area_crosswalk`. Repairing in one left the other corrupt.
- Repaired on **read**, not in the CSVs, which are vendored and would then diverge from their source -- the same override-on-read pattern `manual_area_prefixes` already uses.
- Regenerated `regions_full.rda`, `polities_cats.rda`, `polity_area_crosswalk.rda`.
- New sweep in `tests/testthat/test_datasets.R`.

Only the mojibake part of #382's `_labels.R` is ported. Its `blank_zero_sentinels()`, `fill_adb_region()` and `polity_prefix` changes belong to other sub-issues and are left out.

### One thing to know about the `.rda` rebuild

`polity_area_crosswalk` was rebuilt from the **committed `data/polities.rda`** rather than from the local polities gpkg. The gpkg has drifted to 740 polities against the committed 603, so re-running `data-raw/table_mappings.R` as written would have dragged 137 unrelated upstream polities into an encoding fix. The committed `polities.rda` is exactly the input that produced the committed crosswalk, so this isolates the change -- and the diff below proves it did.

## How I verified

**1. The rebuild changed the eight corrupt cells and nothing else.** All 55 shipped datasets compared before/after by value:

```
### DIFF polities_cats
  col iea        : row 84  CÃ´te d'Ivoire -> Côte d'Ivoire
  col water_area : row 84  CÃ´te d'Ivoire -> Côte d'Ivoire
### DIFF polity_area_crosswalk
  col area_name  : row 521 CuraÃ§ao -> Curaçao
### DIFF regions_full
  col name       : row 131 CuraÃ§ao -> Curaçao
  col iea        : row 115 CÃ´te d'Ivoire -> Côte d'Ivoire
                   row 136 Netherlands Antilles / CuraÃ§ao -> Netherlands Antilles / Curaçao
  col water_area : row 115 CÃ´te d'Ivoire -> Côte d'Ivoire
  col Lassaletta : row 131 CuraÃ§ao -> Curaçao
```

The other 52 datasets are value-identical (six had byte-level compression churn only and were reverted, so the diff carries three `.rda` files, not nine).

**2. Re-running the original scan finds nothing.** `NO MOJIBAKE FOUND`.

**3. No numeric output can move, and that is measured rather than asserted.** Dumping the derived area lookups before and after -- `.get_polities()` in both directions plus `.current_area_lookup()` -- gives identical row counts (266 / 266 / 265) and exactly one changed cell in each, `279,CuraÃ§ao,999` becoming `279,Curaçao,999`. Nothing in `R/` reads `iea`, `water_area`, `Lassaletta` or `FAOSTAT_name`; they are documented columns only. The single name-to-code join in the package, `get_primary_residues()` via `add_area_code(name_column = "area")`, has no `Cura` string anywhere in its `crop_residues` source, so no row changes match status. Nothing sorts or de-duplicates on a label: `.get_polities()` arranges by `polity_end_year`, `polity_start_year`, `area_code`, and `.current_area_lookup()` by codes and years.

So the change is confined to string labels. **A full-pipeline magnitude comparison against `main` was not run** -- the argument that none is needed is the mechanical one above, not a measurement of built output.

**4. The test fails without the change.** Against pre-fix data it reports 7 offending columns and fails 4 assertions:

```
-- 1. Failure: published area tables carry no mojibake
length(offenders) (`actual`) not equal to 0L (`expected`).
  `actual`: 7
mojibake in area labels: regions_full$name (CuraÃ§ao); regions_full$iea (CÃ´te
d'Ivoire, Netherlands Antilles / CuraÃ§ao); regions_full$water_area (CÃ´te
d'Ivoire); regions_full$Lassaletta (CuraÃ§ao); polities_cats$iea (CÃ´te
d'Ivoire); polities_cats$water_area (CÃ´te d'Ivoire);
polity_area_crosswalk$area_name (CuraÃ§ao)
-- 2-4. Failure: "Curaçao" %in% regions$name / "Côte d'Ivoire" %in% regions$iea
        / "Curaçao" %in% crosswalk$area_name  is not TRUE
```

The sweep covers all 85 character columns of the four published area tables and has a non-vacuity guard, so a fourth instance fails CI rather than being found by eye. Non-ASCII literals are `\uXXXX`-escaped, as `R/scrape_faostat.R` already does for `Türkiye`.

**5. Gates.** `air format` clean; `lintr::lint_package()` with the CI config reports **no lints**; `test_datasets.R` 546 pass / 0 fail; `test_code_names.R` 26, `test_polities.R` 24, `test_polity_output_coverage.R` 82, `test_harmonize.R` 12 -- all pass. No roxygen docs touched.

## Note on severity

It was latent, not live, and that was checked rather than assumed: no alias resolves on either spelling of Curaçao, so there was no correct label for the corrupt one to fail to match. It was a trap all the same -- area 279's `FAOSTAT_name` is `NA`, so the corrupt `name` was the only label it had, and an alias added later under the correct spelling would have missed in silence.

Closes #399

author: nirdrang
body:
A reviewer's maintained "this green is unearned" tag is now the item agent's own judgment call, not a founder escalation.

## What happened

The old rule reserved one dismissal for the founder: when a reviewer keeps insisting a passing test claims more than it proves, the item agent could fix the finding freely but could not dismiss it alone. The rule fired for the first time today. By the time the question reached the founder, the item agent had already done everything a judge needs — the facts were undisputed by every party, both fix routes had been tried or rejected for written cause across three agent generations, and the second reviewer had independently endorsed the fix as sound.

The founder's answer: "this is a judgement call to the orchestrator." Folded here as the standing rule.

## The rule now

The item agent rules a maintained residual terminal itself, under two conditions that are not optional:

1. **The reviewer's maintained disagreement is recorded verbatim next to the ruling and stays visible in the pull request body.** A ruling may overrule the objection; it may never erase it.
2. **The ruling states what the green does claim and what it does not**, so the residual is a documented boundary rather than a swallowed defect.

Escalation to the founder remains for what was always theirs: a finding that contradicts ratified text, and scope growth.

Prose-only change — one paragraph in the skill.

author: liamriddell
body:
56 warnings, now zero: 23 unused imports or parameters, and 33 uses of `any`.

## Unused imports and parameters

Mechanical, with two exceptions worth naming:

- **`VMBuiltins` keeps its `EngineContext` import** behind a scoped disable. A `{@link}` in `pluginFunctionRegistry`'s deprecation note points at it, and a dangling documentation link is worse than the warning.
- **`ExpressionEngine`'s `const value = await resolver`** dropped the binding but kept the await. The await is the point there; the batcher re-reads the value from cache.

## The `any` casts

They fell into three groups.

**Unnecessary.** `PrecedenceParser` passed `this as any` to parselets — but `Parser` is a type alias for `PrecedenceParser`, so `this` already satisfied it. `ParseletRegistry` reached for `.category` through `any` although both parselet interfaces declare it.

**Genuinely optional shapes**, now described rather than erased: binding powers a parselet may or may not expose, the `timedOut` marker a Value carries only after an async resolution gives up, the `expression`/`details` fields only some diagnostic events carry. Each is a named type at one site instead of a cast at every access.

**One was hiding a defect.** The worker's `serializeToken` copied five of `Token`'s eight fields — dropping `typeId`, `text` and `lineBreaks` — then cast the result back to `Token` through `any`. The type promised fields the main thread never received, which is exactly why consumers read `lineBreaks` with a `?? 0` fallback. It now copies all eight, so the declared type is true and those fallbacks are no longer load-bearing.

## Two knock-on fixes

Typing `ConstantInfo.value` honestly as `number | string | bigint` (its `type` field has always included `"bigint"`) broke the playground build, which is what I wanted it to do:

- `engineShared` needed the `VmStackValue` import it was already using
- `ConstantsExplorer`'s helpers now take `ConstantInfo["value"]` rather than a hand-written narrower union, so the next widening surfaces as a compile error instead of a missing case

## Verification

oxlint reports nothing. `npm run verify` (4041 tests), `test:full` (4397 tests, 190 suites), both `typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc`, build, smoke, comment style, doc coverage, and a clean playground build.

author: ajatprabha
body:
Part of #87. Independent of #163, which does the same pass over the core package. Disjoint files, either order.

## What changed

Every exported doc comment and the four package comments in `ferrytest`, `driver/env`, `driver/kv` and `driver/yaml`.

| package | ADR mentions in `go doc -all` | package comment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ferrytest` | 51 -> **0** | 8 -> 58 lines |
| `driver/env` | 10 -> **0** | 30 -> 33 lines |
| `driver/kv` | 18 -> **0** | 52 -> 58 lines |
| `driver/yaml` | 10 -> **0** | 83 -> 56 lines |

719 insertions against 917 deletions over 28 files.
Three package comments grew because they had almost no user-facing content to begin with; the per-identifier docs shrank hard, which is where the deletion is.

`ferrytest`'s package comment was eight lines explaining why the package ships from core rather than from a module of its own.
That is a decision, and its reader cannot act on it.
It now defines the vocabulary a driver author needs, names the four consumers, and states both stability promises including the one with teeth: **a minor upgrade of ferry can make a driver that passed yesterday fail today, and that is intended.**

## `Plane.Kinds`

It gets the longest field comment in the package, deliberately, because it is the thing this build has got wrong twice - once in the tickets for #84 and #86, once in a driver that followed them.

It now says outright that it is not what `Get` returns, that a flattening plane still carries `Bool` and `Number` because a bool written to it comes back as the same bool, and that omitting them **demands a store that refuses every boolean and every port number**.
`Plane.Open` says fresh on every call is the requirement rather than the convention, with a worked closure.
`Plane.Except` says an excepted value routes to the refusal half, so it buys a loud refusal the driver has to actually make rather than a skip.

## Drivers

The three driver packages now read like their READMEs, which is the voice the owner signed off on.

`driver/kv`'s experimental warning stays first and still says both halves: neither the Go API nor the storage spelling is stable, and nothing has run against a real store.

`driver/yaml`'s merge documentation gained the unknown-tag drop, which the README documented and the godoc omitted entirely - the two disagreed and the godoc was the optimistic one.

`driver/kv`'s `Sink` said staging is what makes a failed dump leave the store untouched, which reads stronger than the code is: `Commit` does not roll back a partial failure, it continues past a failed `Put` and reports all of them. That is deliberate, and the doc now states the limit.

## READMEs

All three ended with a promise that the package documentation carried the full reasoning.
This PR makes that false, so all three now point at pkg.go.dev for the reference and `docs/adr/` for the reasoning.
Nothing else in them changed.

## How this was verified

**The change is provably comment-only.**
Every `.go` file was reparsed without `parser.ParseComments`, so the AST carries no comment nodes, and reprinted.
Diffed against `main`, the only difference in the whole tree is the addition of `ferrytest/example_test.go`, and there are **zero removed or altered lines** in any existing file.

All four packages: 0 ADR mentions, 0 issue references, 0 em dashes in the diff.
`go build`, `go test` in all four modules, `go test -race`, `make check` and `make lint` all green.

One deletion worth naming: `Artefact` carried a note that its shape is provisional pending an owner ruling in #109.
That is addressed to the owner rather than to a driver author, who cannot act on it.
#109 is open and titled for exactly this, and `surface_test.go` still records it, so the signal is not lost.

author: yschimke
body:
## Summary

meshcore-mobile's republish **failed**, and it's self-inflicted by the annotation work:

```
Error: merge-catalog-section: asset 'annotations/index.json' differs between the two
       catalogs — refusing to overwrite …/out/annotations/index.json
```

`copyAssets` treats every nested file as a per-component asset that must be byte-identical or absent. `annotations/index.json` is neither — it's a **map** keyed by preview and reference id, so a host catalog and a folded section legitimately carry different copies.

## Why it appeared only now

meshcore folds `compose-m3-meshcore` in as a Material 3 tab, so two catalogs meet at fold time. The collision stayed hidden while meshcore's *host* manifest was empty — an empty manifest isn't written at all, so only one file existed. design-parity#277 made the host manifest non-empty (the sticker-id fix), and the very next run aborted.

So the failure is a direct consequence of the preview layer starting to work.

## The fix

Union the two maps instead of comparing bytes. The folded section's components become tabs in the host, so their annotations belong alongside the host's — not replacing them, and not blocking the fold.

**Host entries win a key collision.** The fold is additive, and a borrowed catalog must never silently redefine an id the host already published. A test pins that direction so a future refactor can't quietly invert it.

## Test plan

Two regressions added to `merge-catalog-section.test.mjs`:

- **Unions both manifests** — reproduces the exact failure (both sides carrying a manifest) and asserts the merged result has both preview keys and keeps the host's reference layer.
- **Host wins a collision** — same id on both sides resolves to the host's entry.

The pre-existing "refuses to overwrite a differing asset" test still passes, so ordinary per-component assets keep their strict byte-identity guard; only this one map is special-cased.

Full driver suite: **418 tests passing**.

## After this

Re-dispatch meshcore's `design-artifacts.yml`. This was the last blocker between the merged chain and a compare page with both columns annotated.

author: kg-bot
body:
## What & why

OAuth login needs a browser, so it can't run in CI or on headless machines — and the docs advertise a GitHub-Actions template-sync workflow that a browser flow can never satisfy. Token auth already worked internally (`auth.type: 'token'`) but there was no command to set it; you had to hand-edit `config.json`. This was the originating customer's literal ask on ticket 35EZG2.

author: matthewyjiang
body:
## Summary

Ship the hashline edit stack end state: sole `edit` tool, chainable snapshots, session recovery, and grep tags.

- Replace `edit_file` / `apply_patch` with hashline `edit` (PUT/CUT against original line numbers).
- `read_file` always returns `[path#TAG]` + `N:line` for UTF-8 sources.
- `grep` content mode mints `[path#TAG]` and hashline `N:text` rows for edit chaining.
- TAG is 4-hex (low 16 bits of FNV-1a), matching the oh-my-pi wire size.
- Session `SnapshotStore` shared across coding tools records full-file text + seen lines on read/grep/write/edit.
- Stale tags remap when the store still holds the tagged snapshot and anchors move by one consistent offset; otherwise fail closed with a bounded live snapshot.
- Seen-line checks reject edits of anchors the model never saw under that TAG (with a short reveal).
- Parser accepts case-insensitive PUT/CUT and lenient ranges (`N-M`, `N..M`).
- Hashline metrics: tag mismatch, recovery ok/fail, unseen reject.
- Success payloads stay chain previews; unified diffs stay on tool metadata.

### Not in this cut

- Block ops (`N*`), registers, `REM`, `MV`
- Create/delete via hashline (still `write_file`)
- Persistent cross-restart snapshot store
- Per-line wire hashes

## Validation

```text
cargo fmt --all
python3 scripts/check_architecture.py
cargo clippy -p rho-agent-tools -p rho-providers --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test -p rho-agent-tools --lib --locked
cargo test -p rho-coding-agent --locked --test automation_cli
```

All passed.

## Test gate

- [x] Followed `rho-test-selection` (failure mode, owner layer, gap).
- [x] Each new test names a distinct **failure mode** (user-visible or contract bug).
- [x] Each new test has one **owner layer** (pure unit / SDK contract / PTY / OS).
- [x] No existing test already covers that failure mode at a better layer.
- [x] Interactive TUI behavior uses a **PTY scenario** by default; new `crates/rho/src/tui` unit tests are pure logic or justified below.
- [x] Cases share one test function per rule (tables), not twin functions per literal.
- [x] Asserts use structured values; string `.contains` only for redaction, wire format, or security escaping.
- [x] No locks on help text, statusline chrome, labels, or other copy.
- [x] No wall-clock sleep used for synchronization; no known-flaky timing races.
- [x] Nearby weaker or duplicate tests were removed or merged when practical.

### New tests

| Failure mode | Owner layer | Why existing coverage is not enough |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hashline parse must accept replace/insert/cut, lenient ranges/keywords, and reject block/register ops | Pure unit | Grammar + lenience |
| Apply must honor original line numbers and reject stale tags / overlaps | Pure unit | Apply semantics |
| Snapshot store must fuse identical content, keep colliding texts apart, and LRU-evict paths | Pure unit | New session store |
| Remap recovery must rewrite anchors after uniform drift and refuse changed anchors | Pure unit | New recovery |
| `edit` must recover via store when tag is stale but anchors still map | Tool | Store + apply path |
| `edit` must reject unseen anchors from partial reads | Tool | Seen-line guard |
| Grep content mode must mint full-file tags and hashline rows | Pure unit | Grep chain contract |
| `edit` / `write_file` / `read_file` chain previews and multi-file commits | Tool / SDK | End-to-end paths |

### PTY exception (if any)

```text
N/A - presenter wiring and tool contracts; no new interactive chrome behavior that needs a PTY scenario.
```

## Breaking changes

- `read_file` text/source output is hashline (`[path#TAG]` + numbered lines).
- `grep` content mode output is hashline-shaped (`[path#TAG]` + `N:text`).
- `edit_file` and `apply_patch` are removed; use `edit` / `write_file`.
- TAG width is 4 hex digits (was 8 on intermediate branch cuts).

## Next-major debt

None for dual API shapes. Capability aliases for removed tool names, if any, stay greppable as `NEXT_MAJOR` where already marked.

author: gyuminlee-repo
body:
## Why

Three things this release finishes, all from the same root: MAME assumed the expected list was a KURO export laid out in plate order, and built machinery to police that assumption instead of letting the operator state it.

The backend half landed already (#234, #235). This is the half the operator touches.

## What

**A. The operator names the variant column.** A file picked as the expected list is inspected, and when it is not a KURO export the sheet and variant column become choices, with the auto-detected column pre-selected. The KURO `SourceColumnPanel` convention is followed: `__auto__` is a first-class item in the same Select, so auto-detection is a choice you can return to rather than a mode you fall out of. Two things from that panel are not carried over: MAME reads a label and has no ranking axis, and `inspect_variant_source` returns no rows, so there is nothing for a preview table or an Apply button to act on. The chosen values ride on `validate_inputs` and both `analyze` calls through one helper, because validation and the run reading different rows is the failure this whole release is about.

**B. Build well layout is gone.** Nobody confirms 96 rows by eye. Nothing is lost: the draft layout is inferred by the analyze handler whether or not that button was ever pressed. The `well_layout` RPC parameter and the store field stay, because a project autosaved with a confirmed layout must still restore it and still outrank a sample map.

**C. The plate-order finding stops blocking.** Once the operator points at a sheet and a column, refusing to run because two sheets disagree argues with the person who just said which one to read. The finding is silent when the selection is explicit, informational otherwise, and `missing_from_expected` is still reported either way, because a mutant on the plate with no row shifts every later well and no selection makes that visible. The escape text no longer mentions the button removed in B.

**D. One activity source axis instead of two routes.** The selector is no longer "which EVOLVEpro route" but "where the activity numbers come from", stated with the fact that NGS verdicts are used either way.

**E. Janus autosave actually writes.** #234 added the automatic export but `device9` refuses without a `liquid_class`, so every run was reporting `missing_liquid_class`. The dialog settings move into the store and ride along on `analyze`, and the outcome is shown rather than swallowed: path and row count when saved, nothing-to-write when skipped, the reason verbatim when it failed.

## Honest limits

D is not a single panel. The upload path joins round genotype and the plate-layout path calls `build_evolvepro_input`; they are different backend contracts, and the genotype path has no RPC filling the current round, so rendering both under one source would add a second export that writes an empty file. The axis was renamed and both capabilities kept; folding them into one panel needs the upload source moved onto the `build_evolvepro_input` contract first. The Agilent handling from v0.13.27, WT-block normalisation and the round-1 baseline choice, is untouched inside `BuildEvolveproInputPanel`.

`janus.ts` imports the store, so the pure settings helpers were split into `janusSettings.ts` before the store started importing them back. This codebase has hit that module-eval cycle before.

## Verification

```
node scripts/i18n-lint.mjs          ok
node scripts/i18n-parity.mjs        ok, 10 locales x 2,359 keys (-20 removed, +12 added)
node scripts/sync-check-groups.mjs  41 passed, 14 warned, 0 failed
node scripts/gen-whatsnew.mjs --check   up to date
node scripts/sync-check.mjs         PASS [version-sync] aligned: 0.15.6
```

New vitest coverage: the auto-detected column is pre-selected, the mapping hides for a KURO export, all three requests carry the same values, the plate-order finding no longer gates the run and is absent when the selection is explicit, the Janus outcome renders, and `buildWellLayout` is gone from the store.

`tsc` and `vitest` were not run locally (shared-folder repo on WSL, where `pnpm install` replaces the Windows `node_modules`), so CI is the first check on both.

Version lands once at 0.15.6, with one CHANGELOG section covering this change and the two `v0.15.5.1` merges that carried no entries of their own, and `whatsNew.generated.ts` regenerated.

author: wmp
body:
## Linked discussion / issue

None. This PR follows an external audit and the documentation review performed after that audit. No repository Discussion or issue was opened beforehand.

## Summary

Adds `docs/system-invariants.md` (773 lines): a catalog of 24 cross-layer invariants — conditions that must hold regardless of which controller, cron or import path is involved — each with a stable ID, a named source of truth, a named enforcement mechanism (or the honest word "none"), concurrency scope, retry and crash semantics, required test kind, and a status of `enforced`, `partial`, or `unenforced`.

Adds `docs/concurrency-and-idempotency.md` (398 lines): the decision procedure for *which* protocol a concurrent write should use (atomic delta, unique index, conditional update, upsert, pessimistic lock, advisory lock, idempotency key — in that preference order), a mechanism inventory of every lock currently taken in `backend/src`, and a gap register of writers whose protocols disagree.

Adds two ADRs:
- `0001-scoped-db-single-database-door.md` records why `withScopedDb` is the only database entry point and — the part most often misunderstood — states plainly what it does *not* give a caller (protection against a concurrent writer of the same row).
- `0002-invariant-catalog-and-enforcement-ranking.md` records the decision to catalog invariants at all and the six-level enforcement ranking (compiler type → lint rule → database constraint → source-scanning test → single-site test → prose) that the whole series follows.

**Why the repository needs this.** The audit that produced this content found the same small set of concurrency defects independently rediscovered in more than one place — an atomic balance delta and an absolute balance recompute both writing `accounts.current_balance` with no shared protocol, a holdings replay implemented two different ways in two files, a comment claiming an atomic increment where the code does a plain read-modify-write. Each of these was locally reasonable and globally wrong, and nothing in the repository stated the cross-layer rule a reviewer could have checked the change against. This PR is that missing document.

**What it defines.** The full text of `docs/system-invariants.md` and `docs/concurrency-and-idempotency.md`, as written, checked line-by-line against the current `backend/src` and `database/schema.sql` (see Documentation verification below). It does not define new behavior; it describes behavior that exists today, including where that behavior is a defect.

**What is currently enforced vs. not.** Of the 24 invariants: 2 are `enforced` (refresh-token rotation via a pessimistic lock; the one-active-MNY-import-per-user partial unique index), 4 are `partial` (a logout's truthful reporting; attachment metadata-resolves-to-bytes; backup completeness; one-cron-effect-per-tick), and the remaining 18 are `unenforced` — meaning the system can violate them today, with the specific violating code cited in the entry. This PR does not change that count. It is the measurement, not the fix.

**Why documentation alone does not close these gaps, stated plainly per this series' shared decision:** an entry marked `unenforced` — for example INV-BALANCE-001, which documents that `accounts.current_balance` has three incompatible writer protocols on one column — remains an open implementation defect after this PR merges. Fixing it is a separate, future PR that would then flip the status field and delete the citation of the violation, per the "Using this catalog" section this document itself specifies.

**Alternatives considered and rejected**, per ADR 0002: writing the same rules as unstatused prose (rejected — a document that doesn't distinguish intended from actual behavior is exactly how the false "atomically increment" and "under lock" comments this audit found came to be believed); fixing the findings without a catalog (rejected — several were independently rediscovered and fixed in parallel efforts that didn't know about each other, which the catalog's existence is meant to prevent going forward); tracking invariants in the issue tracker (rejected — an issue closes and becomes invisible; an invariant's status needs to be checkable during review years later).

## Scope

This PR contains Markdown documentation only:

- `docs/system-invariants.md` (new, 773 lines)
- `docs/concurrency-and-idempotency.md` (new, 398 lines)
- `docs/adr/0001-scoped-db-single-database-door.md` (new, 88 lines)
- `docs/adr/0002-invariant-catalog-and-enforcement-ranking.md` (new, 108 lines)

It does not change:
- application runtime behavior;
- database schema or migrations;
- API contracts;
- frontend components;
- CI workflow execution;
- any other file's content — no existing document is edited by this PR (the `CLAUDE.md`-family pointers to these new documents are PR 4).

## What reviewers should check

1. Confirm every `enforced` invariant (INV-AUTH-001, INV-IMPORT-001) names a real, currently-present mechanism — the pessimistic lock in `backend/src/auth/token.service.ts`, and the partial unique index `idx_import_jobs_one_active_per_user` added by `database/migrations/135_import_jobs_single_active.sql` and mirrored in `database/schema.sql`.
2. Confirm the `partial` and `unenforced` statuses match the current source — in particular INV-BALANCE-001's claim that three incompatible protocols write `accounts.current_balance`, and INV-HOLDING-002's claim that `holdings.service.ts` and `net-worth.service.ts` replay a stock SPLIT differently (multiplicative vs. additive).
3. Confirm the retry/crash-semantics fields for INV-IMPORT-002 accurately describe the window *after* `writeAll`'s transaction commits — this is the entry the branch's own history says was corrected once already ("Correct two invariants the review caught"), and it is the one this series' verification treated as the highest-stakes single claim in the document (see Findings below for one wording nuance worth a second look).
4. Confirm the concurrency mechanism-choice table in `docs/concurrency-and-idempotency.md` §2 and the lock inventory in §8 list only mechanisms that actually exist — five pessimistic/advisory lock sites are named by file and line; confirm no sixth exists that the document should also list, and no listed one has since been removed.
5. Confirm cross-references between `system-invariants.md`, `concurrency-and-idempotency.md`, and the two ADRs resolve to files that exist on this PR's base (they do — both ADRs are in this same PR).

## Findings from documentation verification

Verification against the current source (detailed methodology below) found the mechanism-and-status claims in both documents to be accurate, with **one factual error that recurred in two places, corrected in this PR before opening it:**

- **Cron cadence.** Both `docs/system-invariants.md` (INV-OCCURRENCE-001) and `docs/concurrency-and-idempotency.md` §8's gap register described `processAutoPostTransactions` as running "every 5 minutes." The actual `@Cron` schedule, confirmed at `backend/src/scheduled-transactions/scheduled-transactions.service.ts:152`, is `"5 * * * *"` — minute 5 of every hour, i.e. **once per hour**, not every five minutes. The underlying claim (no lock, no CAS on `next_due_date`, no unique constraint, so two replicas on one tick can double-post) was correct and unaffected; only the cadence phrase needed fixing, in both locations, and has been.

One additional item worth a second look, not a required change: the "comment above `runImport`" quoted in INV-IMPORT-002 and in `concurrency-and-idempotency.md` §4 is, more precisely, a module/class-level doc comment on `MnyImportService` immediately preceding the class declaration in `backend/src/import/mny/mny-import.service.ts`, rather than a comment attached to the `runImport` method signature itself. The comment's text and the argument built on it are both accurate; only its exact location is slightly more specific than "above `runImport`" s

author: wu-changxing
body:
## What

`SessionStorage` defaults to a bare relative path **and creates the directory**:

```python
def __init__(self, path: str = ".co/session_results.jsonl"):
    self.path = Path(path)
    self.path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
```

`host()` builds it with no argument, so this is on the hosting path. Measured on a project whose `host.yaml` says `trust: strict`, from a subdirectory, on `main` after #663:

```
storage path      : .co/session_results.jsonl   <- sub/.co, not the project's
decoy .co created : True
trust now reads   : None
```

Two costs:

1. **The session history goes where no later run looks.** An agent restarted from the project root does not see the turns it just served.
2. **The created `.co/` is a decoy.** `#660`/`#661`/`#663` made everything walk *up* to the project, and the walk stops at the nearest `.co/`. From then on the subdirectory's empty one answers for `host.yaml` and the trust lists — a project configured whitelist-only runs as `careful`, admitting contacts and accepting invite codes.

`#663` fixed this shape in plan mode and in `co skills copy --to-project` and missed this one: **every test constructed `SessionStorage` with an explicit path**, so nothing exercised the default.

## The guard

Rather than fixing the third creator and assuming it is the last, this adds a standing check: each entry point a hosted agent touches early — session storage, an Agent, a Logger, a skill lookup, a trust check, plan mode, the permission whitelist — run in a subdirectory of a real project, in its own interpreter, asserting no `.co/` appears.

Two things were verified about the guard itself:

- it **fails** when the fix in this PR is reverted (otherwise it is decoration)
- its subprocesses import **this repo**, not the installed `connectonion`. Without that they imported the released 1.5.11 and reported three creators that are already fixed here — a green-looking measurement of the wrong package.

## Also

The path is now resolved rather than relative, so a tool calling `os.chdir` cannot move the history mid-run. `host(co_dir=...)` passes its own `co_dir` so an explicit one still wins.

`test_host_session.py::test_default_path` asserted the relative path; updated to the resolved one, same directory, with the reason recorded.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_the_session_history_belongs_to_the_project.py`, 18 cases, proven to fail first. Full suite **4348 passed**.

author: hamehrabi
body:
CON-007 forbids telemetry, so the kit is structurally unable to observe its own failure rate in the field. This set is the only substitute — and the only way to answer *"did rewording that question help?"*, which for a product made entirely of prose is every question worth asking.

## Built

- **36 answer scripts** in the specified proportions: 16 happy, 10 edge, 6 adversarial, 4 must-refuse
- **5 repository fixtures**, including the awkward ones — populated `spec/`, read-only, existing `CLAUDE.md`
- **11 deterministic scorers**
- **An engine that takes scorers as input**

## The engine/scorer split is the point

Adding a scorer means adding an entry to `ci/scorers.mjs` and touching nothing else. There's a test that **invents a scorer and runs it through the untouched engine**.

Get this wrong and every experiment becomes a harness change — an hour each, forever.

## No model-graded scorer, deliberately

Grading a model-driven system with a model drifts on both sides at once, and the drift is invisible **because both sides move together**. Eleven of thirteen deterministic is a decision, not an accident.

## `todo_density` is reported but not gated

Q-014 stays open until ten real runs exist. Guessing the threshold now would **invent the definition of "hollow"** — the one thing that metric exists to detect.

## Two cases worth reading

**EV-027** expects the intake to *proceed* on someone building a keylogger. Without a case testing that boundary, a future change could quietly make the kit judgemental about its users' products — degrading output for projects it disapproves of, with nobody deciding that.

**EV-036** refuses *even though permission was granted*. REQ-F-026 is a design rule, not a consent rule.

Every script is labelled **INVENTED** — they cover what I thought of, not what a real developer does.

## Not done, and recorded rather than implied

**The golden workspaces do not exist.** The harness has never been fed a workspace produced by a real intake. Generating 36 means 36 full runs, and a single Round-1 run took minutes of model time.

**FF-003…FF-008 and FF-010…FF-014 therefore stay unwired**, and the merge gate still runs only stages 1 and 2. The traceability matrix says so.

The machinery is complete. The measurement has not been taken.

**277 tests pass.**
