author: benjamin-pasic-symphonygroup
body:
## Problem

Interns with no workspace could see another workspace's tickets.

`User.workspaceId` is the workspace a user last switched to — a pointer, not proof of
membership. Every ambient-workspace endpoint trusted it with no membership check, so a
non-member got the pointed-at workspace's tickets, categories and statuses in full. Only
per-resource reads (`getTicketById`) verified access.

The pointer goes stale because admins/mentors bypass membership entirely: `switchWorkspace`
sets it for admins without creating a member entry, and demoting them to intern removes the
bypass while leaving the pointer behind. The mass role change to intern turned this from
latent into live.

## Fix

- `resolveActiveWorkspaceId` in `helpers/workspaceAuthz.js` — admins keep the query/body
  override, admins and mentors keep their ambient pointer, everyone else needs an active

author: adityarajsingh-git
body:
## What

Makes the split deploy (client on Netlify, API on Render) configurable via env vars: the client API base comes from `VITE_API_URL`, and the server refuses to boot outside dev/test without `MONGODB_URL`. Adds a README Deployment section.

## Why

The API base URL was hardcoded to `/api/v2` and only worked behind the Vite dev proxy — a split deploy would send every request to the static host. And a deploy that forgot `MONGODB_URL` booted "healthy" and then failed on every DB-backed route; failing at boot is the same fix already applied to `JWT_SECRET`.

## Changes

- `client/src/lib/api.ts` — `BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || "/api/v2"`. `||` rather than `??` on purpose: copying `client/.env.example` leaves the var defined-but-empty, which must still mean same-origin.
- `client/src/vite-env.d.ts` (new) — Vite client types + typed `VITE_API_URL`.
- `client/.env.example` (new) — documents `VITE_API_URL` incl. the build-time-baking caveat.
- `server/src/config/env.ts` — `resolveMongoUrl()` with the same dev/test allowlist as `resolveJwtSecret()`; every other `NODE_ENV` throws at boot.
- `server/.env.example` — `MONGODB_URL` requirement + `CORS_ORIGIN` comma-separated multi-origin syntax (no spaces).
- `README.md` — Deployment section: Render settings for the API, Netlify settings for the client, env vars for both.

## Testing

- `client/src/lib/api.test.ts` — 3 new tests: absolute base when `VITE_API_URL` set, `/api/v2` fallback when unset, empty-string treated as unset. 117/117 green; `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) passes.
- `server/tests/env.test.ts` — 5 new tests: production/staging boot failure without `MONGODB_URL`, production boot with it, dev/test boot without it. 112/112 green; `npm run typecheck` passes.
- CORS multi-origin verified against the real app via a throwaway supertest script: `CORS_ORIGIN="https://sn2.netlify.app,http://localhost:5173"` reflects each listed origin and omits the header for unknown origins.

## Risk

- `VITE_API_URL` is baked in at build time — changing it on Netlify requires a rebuild, not just a redeploy (documented in README).
- Deploys on staging/qa/preview `NODE_ENV`s that relied on booting without `MONGODB_URL` will now fail at boot — intended, but a behavior change.

author: mahyarj
body:
Closes #99

## What

`getPlanBounds` padded each opening by half its own thickness only, so a door's
90° swing arc — radius equal to the *opening's length* — fell outside the content
box. A perimeter door opening outward got sliced by the export edge, and **Fit**
cropped it too.

Doors now contribute the exact extent of what they draw. New
`getDoorSweepPoints` (`src/geometry/itemGeometry.ts`) returns the hinge, both
leaf tips, and any of the swing circle's four axis-aligned extreme points
(`hinge ± radius`) that fall **inside the swept quadrant** — tested by requiring
a non-negative dot product with both quadrant edge vectors. `getPlanBounds`
includes those with zero padding (they are already-drawn positions).

## How it satisfies the acceptance criteria

- [x] **Full drawn extent** — the AC's exact case (wall `(0,0)–(400,0)` t=10, door
      `offset 100`, `length 80`, swinging −y) now returns `minY: -80`.
- [x] **Box stays tight** — same case keeps `maxY: 5` and `minX`/`maxX` at
      `-5`/`405`. Padding the hinge by the radius on four sides was explicitly
      rejected; only the swept side grows. Exact numbers pinned in `bounds.test.ts`.
- [x] **Both `hingeEdge` × both `swingSide`, plus a 45° wall** — covered in
      `bounds.test.ts`. The 45° case is the one that matters: there the arc's own
      `hinge.x + radius` point (neither tip) sets `maxX`, so tips alone would be
      wrong.
- [x] **Windows audited and pinned** — `getWindowGeometry`'s rect and midline do
      stay within half the item's thickness of the wall centerline, so the
      existing per-endpoint padding already covers them. No bounds change needed;
      a test asserts a window inside its wall's thickness adds no extent.
- [x] **A perimeter door exports whole** — `exportSvg.test.ts` pins the `viewBox`
      (`-45 -120 490 165`; the `y` was `-45` before) and asserts every sweep point
      clears all four edges by the full margin. Both PNG and SVG frame off
      `buildExportSvg`.
- [x] **`EXPORT_MARGIN` unchanged at 40** — asserted by a test.
- [x] **No regression without doors** — no existing test changed; walls-only and
      walls-plus-windows bounds are identical to before.
- [x] `npm run check && npx tsc -b && npm test` pass.
- [x] **No README change.**

`computeFitView` needed no change — it inherits the corrected bounds.
`docs/DECISIONS.md` records why the quadrant-extreme test beats both "just the two
tips" and "pad the hinge by the radius", and why the fix belongs in the bounds
rather than the margin.

## Testing

`npm run check && npx tsc -b && npm test` → Biome clean, `tsc -b` clean,
**27 files / 342 tests passing**.

I also confirmed the new tests actually catch the bug: with the door branch in
`getPlanBounds` disabled, 4 of them fail (e.g. export height `90` instead of
`165`), while the window and no-door tests still pass.

author: sefalk
body:
Fixes #45.

## The symptom is real; the stated cause is not

#45 proposes to "mirror `check-python-linting.py`". That cannot be applied as
written: **neither checker contains diff logic** — both take `--files`. The
branch-delta resolution lives in the four stop hooks. So acceptance criterion 4
("base-branch resolution matches `check-python-linting.py`") is unsatisfiable
literally; its *intent* — do not add a second resolver — is what this PR
implements: the hooks pass the merge-base they already resolve into the checker.

The real defect is granularity: `check-python-quality.py` reported **every**
function in a file it was handed. In WIT #3105 a one-line registry change
therefore demanded ~90 lines of NumPy docstrings on six unrelated methods,
blocked three commit attempts, and ended in a recorded deviation. There was no
correct path — only out-of-scope edits or bypassing a HARD gate.

## What changed

`--diff-base REF` restricts reporting to functions whose line span intersects
the branch diff against that ref. Decorator lines count as part of the function.

Three deliberate choices:

- **The default did not change.** The issue proposed diff scoping by default
  with whole-file behind a flag. That is inverted here: a caller who forgets
  the flag would otherwise get a silently *weaker* HARD gate.
- **No second base-branch resolver.** `resolve_base` only verifies a ref; it
  deliberately does not compute a merge-base. The hooks own that policy.
- **Unresolvable history fails wide, not narrow.** Shallow clone, missing
  branch, or no repository at all → whole-file scan with a `NOTICE:` line,
  never a silent pass. Untracked files are scanned whole for the same reason:
  no diff can speak for them.

Ignore hygiene follows the same scope, but a suppression predating the branch
is reported as `ADVISORY:` instead of blocking — visible without punishing the
author for inherited debt. A suppression added in an *earlier phase of the same
branch* still blocks: it is after the merge-base, so the branch owns it.

## Evidence

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test-quality-gate.ps1` (new, 15 cases) | 15/15 |
| `test-lint-gate.ps1` | 21/21 |
| `test-hooks.ps1` | 63/63 |
| `test-hooks-integration.ps1` | 7/7 |
| Mutation | 7/7 killed |

Each test builds a throwaway repository with a real base branch — the #37
lesson about tests that silently inherit the developer's working tree.

**On the one mutant that survived at first:** swapping `cat-file -e {base}:`
for `HEAD:` changed nothing, because a file merely absent from the base is
already reported as wholly added by `git diff`. The probe's only real job was
the *untracked* case, where both refs miss alike — an equivalent mutant. Rather
than annotate it, the probe was replaced by the condition it actually tests
(`git ls-files --error-unmatch`), which also removed dead code for tracked
files. The mutant is no longer expressible and its replacement dies.

Plan: `docs/plans/fix-2026-08-04-quality-gate-diff-scope.md`

## Contribution 2: mechanism lineage audit of the current frontier

Verified by marker inspection after `hilbert sync` of `55d2752`, before this submission:

## Contribution 3: negative results from this seat (so others don't repeat them)

All verified on the ranked runner unless marked local:

- Witness-generation heterogeneous scheduling (E-cores), fine and coarse claim granularity: −1.5% / −0.69% — the phase is compute-bound; E-cores dilute it.

body:
## Что

Раздел `docs/research/filesystem-cache.md` описывал подключение `filesystem_cache` к **существующей** таблице через in-place подмену диска, но в репозитории не было кода, который это воспроизводит. Этот PR добавляет такой стенд.

## Изменения

- **`deploy/scripts/fscache-inplace-swap.sh`** (хост-скрипт) + цель **`make fscache-swap-demo`**. Против локального стека он:
  1. настраивает «сырой» s3-диск и создаёт на нём таблицу с данными;
  2. показывает, что чтения **не** кэшируются;
  3. делает in-place подмену: переименовывает сырой диск в backing, ставит `cache`-диск под **тем же именем**, переносит крохотную директорию метаданных при **остановленном** узле;
  4. показывает, что те же парты теперь кэшируются (cold с S3 → warm из кэша), row count и checksum не изменились, ни один парт не двигался.
- Скрипт **прибирает за собой** на выходе (trap) — стек остаётся в исходном состоянии.
- README и research-док теперь ссылаются на команду.

## Проверка (на локальном кластере)

```
==> 2. baseline: reads are NOT cached (raw s3 disk)
    cold: 0.00 B from S3, 0.00 B from cache
    warm: 0.00 B from S3, 0.00 B from cache
==> 4. verify: same parts, now cached, data intact
    cold: 28.73 MiB from S3, 12.66 MiB from cache
    warm: 0.00 B from S3, 28.73 MiB from cache
    rows: 300000 -> 300000   checksum: unchanged
```

Прогонялось end-to-end; после выполнения рабочее дерево и стек чистые (артефактов в контейнере не остаётся). Только shell + Makefile + doc-пойнтеры, Go-кода и coverage это не касается.

author: daniiiil1
body:
## Summary

- makes every gripper conversion parameter injectable while preserving the existing no-argument API;
- derives the default finger length from the exact Xacro geometry (`0.9 * 0.19011 m`) instead of the rounded `0.171 m` duplicate;
- validates non-finite and physically inconsistent calibration values at construction time;
- documents metres, radians, actuator-percent units, and the deliberate absence of clamping;
- removes stale comments that described a 0.125 m aperture and incomplete opening-angle information;
- adds regression coverage for round trips, extrapolation without clamping, custom geometry, invalid calibration, and Xacro/Python consistency.

## Root cause

`GripperConversion` carried an independent rounded copy of geometry from `stretch_gripper.xacro`. Nothing failed when one side changed, so the Python conversion and robot model could silently drift.

The new test evaluates every `stretch_gripper*.xacro` under `stretch_description/batch` (22 files at present) and compares the fingertip geometry with the conversion default. A future geometry change will therefore either update the helper deliberately or supply robot-specific constructor values.

The legacy `status_to_all()` velocity calculation is intentionally unchanged. Stretch Body supplies actuator velocity in rad/s; converting it to fingertip angular velocity requires the robot-specific actuator-to-percent derivative and should be handled separately rather than guessed in this geometry-only fix.

## Validation

```text
PYTHONPATH=hello_helpers/src python3 -m unittest discover -s hello_helpers/test -v
Ran 6 tests in 0.016s — OK
```

`git diff --check` also passes.

author: benitoric
body:
## Resumen

Nueva lógica de estados para la columna **Estado** del listado de Jugadores:

- **Activo**: ficha médica vigente (no vencida) y sin lesión.
- **Inhabilitado**: ficha médica vencida o sin cargar.
- **Lesionado**: con lesión activa registrada.
- **Inactivo**: dado de baja — siempre prevalece sobre el resto.

Cada jugador muestra siempre su etiqueta de estado en la columna, con color propio (Activo celeste, Inhabilitado amarillo, Lesionado rojo, Inactivo gris). Se agrega el chip de filtro **Inhabilitados** y el orden por columna Estado sigue el ranking activo → inhabilitado → lesionado → inactivo. La ficha individual muestra el mismo estado derivado.

## Implementación

El estado se deriva en el frontend (`estadoJugador()` en `src/helpers.js`): la base sigue guardando `activo`/`lesionado`/`inactivo` y la condición de inhabilitado sale del estado de la ficha médica ya calculado por `fichaMedica()`. Una ficha que vence dentro de los próximos 30 días sigue contando como vigente (jugador activo).

## Cambios

- `src/helpers.js`: `estadoJugador()` y mapa de etiquetas `ESTADOS`.
- `src/pages/Jugadores.jsx`: filtro, chips, orden y etiqueta de la columna Estado sobre el estado derivado.
- `src/pages/Ficha.jsx`: la etiqueta de estado usa el estado derivado.
- `src/styles.css`: badge `inhabilitado` y ajuste de anchos de columna para la etiqueta más larga.

## Verificación

- `npm run build` sin errores.
- Capturas con Playwright (móvil 390px y escritorio 900px) con datos que cubren los cuatro estados: ficha vigente → Activo, ficha vencida → Inhabilitado, sin ficha → Inhabilitado, lesión activa → Lesionado, baja → Inactivo.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Three registry-conformance bugs surfaced by the new conformance corpus (harvested from
uv / pip / pypa-packaging / warehouse / opencontainers distribution-spec — see
artifact-keeper-test#333), found → fixed → unit-tested on one branch.

Fixes #3114
Fixes #3115
Fixes #3116

**pypi `<base href>` proxy bypass (security)** — an upstream `<base href>` on a proxied Simple
index re-anchored our root-relative rewritten download URLs onto the upstream origin: proxy
bypass, upstream-host disclosure, and broken air-gapped installs. `rewrite_upstream_urls` now
strips `<base>` before rewriting. Same class as #2801, for the `<base>` vector.

**pypi PEP 658 core-metadata not advertised** — `build_simple_project_response` served
`<file>.metadata` but never advertised `core-metadata` on wheel entries, so pip and uv never
used the metadata fast path and downloaded whole wheels to resolve. Now advertised for `.whl`
only; sdists unchanged.

**oci manifest push-by-digest not verified (integrity)** — `handle_put_manifest` computed the
body digest but never compared it to a digest-form reference, so a mismatched-digest manifest
PUT was accepted (201) instead of rejected with 400 `DIGEST_INVALID`. Guard added, firing only
on `sha256:` references so tag pushes are unaffected, matching the existing blob-completion path.

Also included: a path-traversal guard rejecting unsafe upload filenames, which partially
addresses #3107 (the filename-sanitization half; the `validate()`-wiring half remains open), and
seven commits of net-new pypi/oci unit tests built from the same corpus.

## Regression test (required for `fix/*` PRs)

- [x] This PR is a `fix/*` AND adds/updates a test that would have caught the bug
- [ ] N/A — this is not a bug fix

Each fix landed with a unit test that is RED on `main` and GREEN here:
`test_rewrite_upstream_urls_neutralizes_base_href` and
`test_build_simple_project_response_json_advertises_core_metadata_for_wheels`. The OCI
manifest-digest guard is covered behaviorally at the DTF level by the adopted
distribution-spec conformance tier.

## Test Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated (if applicable)
- [x] E2E tests added/updated (if applicable) — conformance corpus in artifact-keeper-test#333
- [x] Manually tested locally
- [x] No regressions in existing tests

`cargo test --lib api::handlers::pypi::tests` → 221 passed, 0 failed (2 new tests plus all
existing pypi tests). The OCI change compiles clean in the same build.

## API Changes
- [ ] New endpoints have `#[utoipa::path]` annotations
- [ ] Request/response types have `#[derive(ToSchema)]`
- [ ] OpenAPI spec validates: `cargo test --lib test_openapi_spec_is_valid`
- [ ] Migration is reversible (if applicable)
- [x] N/A - no API changes

No new endpoints or schema types. The changes correct the response bodies and status codes of
existing PyPI and OCI routes toward their governing specs.

## Not included (follow-ups)

Upload `validate()` wiring (behavior-changing, #3107), PEP 440 version ordering (#3106), and the
OCI Referrers API (#3108) and cross-repo blob mount (#3109) feature gaps. The `canonical_version`
leniency fix (#3111) ships in the stacked round-2 PR.

body:
### Motivation
- Restore correct saving and applying of grid column order in `frmProceed` after a recent incorrect change caused positions to be ignored on restart. 
- Prevent popup-menu instability and deadlocks caused by rebuilding FMX control children while a native popup is opening. 
- Preserve existing INI format and width/visibility storage while making order persistence reliable.

### Description
- Capture order from the enumerated `Grid.Columns[]` sequence (use `Position := I`) so the visual enumeration is recorded reliably. 
- Apply saved order by resolving columns by their stable `Name` and assigning `Index` in a left-to-right sequence after widths/visibility are applied to avoid index-shift issues. 
- Make the "Столбцы" popup permanent and build its child items once at initialization via `BuildGridColumnsMenu`, then synchronize checkmarks on popup using `Items` rather than creating/freeing FMX `Children` at open time. 
- Add static regression tests covering capture/apply logic, popup behavior, and bump `APP_VERSION` to `1.0.63`, and update release notes accordingly.

## Intent

Make Hermes Agent a first-class Firstmate primary Captain's Assistant while keeping every crewmate visible through the Herdr backend; preserve existing harness behavior and block invisible delegation.

## What Changed
- Added a new Hermes primary integration: `.hermes/plugins/firstmate-primary/` plugin (`__init__.py`, `plugin.yaml`) and `bin/fm-hermes-primary.sh`, letting Hermes Agent act as a first-class Captain's Assistant primary.
- Extended spawn/backend/session-lock/harness-process libs (`bin/fm-spawn.sh`, `bin/fm-backend.sh`, `bin/backends/herdr.sh`, `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-harness-process-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh`) so every crewmate stays visible through the Herdr backend and delegation cannot happen invisibly.
- Added coverage for the new behavior (`tests/fm-hermes-primary.test.sh`, `tests/fm-hermes-harness.test.sh`, `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh`, plus updates to `fm-backend-herdr`, `fm-backend`, `fm-session-start`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile` tests) and updated docs (`docs/supervision-protocols/hermes.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/codex-app-backend.md`, `README.md`) to describe the new primary and fix stale duplicate backend lists.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The Hermes-primary integration (plugin, process-identity helpers, session-lock/harness-detection wiring, and docs) is additive, gated behind strict scope checks (persistent-CLI launch shape, cwd==root, valid state dir), fails closed on ambiguity, blocks delegate_task and unsafe watcher-arm shapes, explicitly refuses Hermes as a crewmate/secondmate runtime in fm-spawn.sh, and is backed by targeted tests (fm-hermes-primary.test.sh, fm-hermes-harness.test.sh, fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh) that assert exactly these behaviors; existing harness protocols and herdr crewmate-visibility contracts are left untouched.

author: tomerwave
body:
## Version

**0.6.0, not 0.5.1.** `policy/unused-suppression` now rejects `severity: off`, `only-in` and `allow-in` as invalid configuration, so any repository that had switched that rule off has a config that **no longer loads**. That is breaking, even pre-`1.0`.

## The trap that caught the last release, caught again

`crates/godlint-cli/Cargo.toml` still asked for `godlint-core = { version = "0.5.0" }`. `check-release.py` refused the tag until it matched — the same gate, catching the same mistake, one release later. Worth noting it earns its keep every time.

## Two entries moved to Internal

Two `### Changed` entries opened with *"Nothing a user can observe"*. That is exactly what the `Internal` category exists to withhold — the release body is the section verbatim and reaches people who will never read this repository. Both predate the category, which shipped in this same cycle.

Announced: **1 Added, 13 Changed, 8 Fixed.** Withheld: **8 Internal.**

## What ships

**Added** — every rule takes `only-in` and `allow-in`: the paths it applies to, and the exemptions inside them.

**Changed, the user-visible ones** —
- `policy/unused-suppression` reports a directive that silences nothing whatever the reason, and cannot switch itself off.
- A stale `.github/accepted-drift.md` declaration fails rather than printing a notice.
- The drift gate reads an exit status instead of matching an error message.
- Suppression matching grouped by file; reading and parsing runs on every core (2.66× on a large tree).

**Fixed** — the action's job summary appears when there are findings, which is the only time it was ever for; `maintainability/function-nesting` no longer charges a function for a closure it returns; `ci/no-silenced-failure` reads `True` and `TRUE`; and several gates stopped taking a proxy for the thing they check.

## Verification

`godlint --version` → **0.6.0**. 887 tests / 0 failed, clippy 0 warnings, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `godlint check .` no findings, 2,099 validator checks, `check-release.py v0.6.0` passes.

`.github/accepted-drift.md` is absent, so nothing needs deleting after publication — `docs/releasing.md`'s post-release step is already satisfied.

## Tagging

**I have not created the tag.** Exact version tags are admin-only by ruleset, and creating one publishes to crates.io, npm and PyPI, which cannot be undone. Merge this, then create `v0.6.0` when you want the release to go out.

author: cyberk1ng
body:
Health imports were failing on device, and Settings → Advanced → Health Import gave no sign of why. This fixes the subsystem and rebuilds the page.

## The queue deadlock

`_start` drained the delta queue with no `try/finally` and no per-item guard, so the **first** type that threw escaped the loop and left `running` permanently `true`. From then on the queue accepted types that nothing would ever process again: every health import for the rest of the session silently did nothing, dashboards kept rendering whatever was already stored, and nothing was logged. `getWorkoutsHealthDataDelta` had the same shape — its guard flag was set before an unguarded fetch and cleared only on the line after it — and the same outcome.

Both now clear their flag in a `finally`, and a failing type is logged and skipped rather than taking the drain with it.

## Concurrent HealthKit authorization

HealthKit presents **one** authorization sheet at a time; a second `requestAuthorization` raised while the first is on screen replaces it, and what the user sees is a sheet that appears and vanishes before it can be answered. That is reachable with no user error at all — opening a dashboard schedules a background delta per chart while the settings page starts an import on tap.

Every path into the plugin now goes through a single serialization gate (`_serialized`), and the delta path asks for authorization **once** instead of twice. The gate's baton is released in a `finally` and never completes with an error, so a failing import propagates to its own caller without wedging the ones behind it.

## Also fixed

- **Core sleep was silently dropped.** The set of stages duplicated under the generic `SLEEP_ASLEEP` type named `SLEEP_ASLEEP_CORE` — not a value of the plugin's enum. Deep and REM matched by luck; core (Apple's `SLEEP_LIGHT`, the largest stage of a typical night) did not, so the "Asleep" chart showed roughly half of every staged night. A test now asserts every member of the set resolves to a real `HealthDataType`.
- **`Health.configure()` was never called**, though the plugin documents it as mandatory; it is what populates the cached device id, which the Android BMI path dereferences unconditionally. `HealthService` now owns the handshake, once per service, and does not cache a failed one.
- **Android-only companion permissions were requested on iOS.** `Permission.activityRecognition` has no iOS strategy at all, and `Permission.location` raised an unrelated Location prompt in front of the HealthKit sheet.
- **A type that resolves to nothing** is now reported as `noMatchingTypes` and logged, instead of importing nothing in silence — which was indistinguishable from a broken import.
- Every import outcome is logged under `LogDomain.health` with a sub-domain, so the next failure is diagnosable from the logs.

## The page

Imports return a `HealthImportResult` rather than throwing, so one failing type cannot abort a batch and the page has an outcome to render. The old page fired every import without awaiting it and rendered nothing afterwards — a success, an empty range and an outright failure all looked identical.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Mobile, dark** | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/before/health_import_mobile_dark.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/after/health_import_mobile_dark.png) |
| **Mobile, light** | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/before/health_import_mobile_light.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/after/health_import_mobile_light.png) |
| **Desktop, dark** | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/before/health_import_desktop_dark.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/after/health_import_desktop_dark.png) |
| **Desktop, light** | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/before/health_import_desktop_light.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/after/health_import_desktop_light.png) |

A row per data family saying what it will import, quick ranges, and an Import all action. The end date no longer defaults to *tomorrow* — the import capped every request at the current instant anyway, so it only ever misrepresented the range. On desktop the page states that there is no health store rather than offering six buttons that quietly do nothing.

**After a run** — this state has no "before", because it did not exist:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matthiasn/lotti-docs/main/pr-screenshots/health-import-subsystem/after/health_import_results_mobile_dark.png)

A row reports its own sample count, an empty result, a permission refusal (with where to fix it), or a failure, in the alert ramp's success/warning/error tones. It shows a spinner while working and cannot be started twice.

## Testing

**100% line coverage on every changed file (473/473)**, 167 tests across five files mirroring their sources.

Every regression test was re-run with its fix reverted to confirm it fails — a passing test that survives the revert is not testing anything:

| Reverted | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `_start` guard | `a throwing type does not wedge the queue for the session` |
| `SLEEP_LIGHT` in the duplication set | `duplicates HealthDataType.SLEEP_LIGHT as generic SLEEP_ASLEEP` |
| Single authorization on the delta path | `maps BLOOD_PRESSURE to systolic and diastolic` |
| `_serialized` gate | `two concurrent imports never overlap in the health plugin` |
| Workout guard `finally` | `clears the guard flag and reports when the fetch fails` |
| `noMatchingTypes` reporting | `an unresolvable type is reported, not silently skipped` |
| `Health.configure()` handshake | `every read method configures the plugin first` |
| Android-only permission guard | `asks for nothing on a non-Android platform` |
| Authorization inside the `try` | `reports failed when authorization itself throws` |
| Controller error guard | `a throwing import becomes a failed result, not a stuck row` |

A skeptical review of the branch caught the last two before this PR opened: `authorizeHealth` sat outside the `try` in `_fetchHealthData`, so a throwing `requestAuthorization` escaped the result contract and left a row spinning forever with no way to retry — 100% *line* coverage did not catch it, because the line is covered by the success path and only the throwing case was missing.

## Docs

- `knowledge/features/health_import.md` — new concept covering the queue, the gate, the delta semantics and the sleep duplication, with the queue lifecycle as a state diagram; linked from the features index and from `dashboards.md`.
- CHANGELOG under 1.0.1 + matching `metainfo.xml` entries.
- The manual page (`sync-and-data/health-import`) updated in English and all 10 translations.
- New labels added to all 11 translated ARB catalogs (`en_GB` unchanged — spelling-only exception, and it already omitted every `settingsHealthImport*` key).

## Not verified

Everything here is reasoned from the code and pinned by tests; **none of it has been run against a real HealthKit store.** The reported symptom (blood pressure importing nothing, the sheet flashing) matches the queue deadlock and the double authorization, but if it persists, the new per-outcome logging under `LogDomain.health` is what will say why.

## Known, not fixed

`_fetchHealthDataDelta` anchors a composite type's start date on `actualTypes.first` only, so for `BLOOD_PRESSURE` a diastolic gap can never refill once systolic is ahead of it. Pre-existing; called out rather than folded into this change.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Builds on top of the already-merged **PR #3** cloud-sync dedup fix.

The seed report ships per-customer **summary stats** (`spent`/`visits`/`firstVisit`/`lastVisit`) that already represent each customer's known transaction history. PR #3 hardened the **receipt** guard so exact-receipt re-imports no longer double-count. But importing an M-Pesa statement whose rows fall **inside a customer's known date window** still double-counts those rows on top of the seed summary — revenue, visits and dates all inflate, because those rows have *different* receipts the guard doesn't recognize.

This PR adds a **seed-data duplicate guard** layered on the receipt guard.

## What changed

1. **`isSeedDuplicate(tx)`** — returns `true` only for a *dated* row that matches a **non-new** (seed/baseline) customer with non-zero summary stats and falls inside the customer's **frozen snapshot window** (`seedFrom`/`seedTo`) — *not* the live `lastVisit`, which imports keep extending. No-date, no-match, `isNew`, and **rebuild-mode** (`visits===0 && spent===0`) rows all return `false`.
2. **`isSeen(tx, opts)`** — the **receipt guard** (`transactionKey` / `txKeyNoTime`) is checked **first**; only rows whose receipt is *not yet* in `DB.seen` fall through to `isSeedDuplicate`. `opts.seedGuard === false` disables the seed fallback.
3. **`importTransactions` / `backfillTransactions`** call `markSeen(tx)` **on every skip** so a seed-covered receipt is recorded and caught by the receipt guard next time. `backfillTransactions` passes `{seedGuard:false}` — history-only, so seed rows still enter per-customer history.
4. **`showPreview`** stamps `seedDup: isSeedDuplicate(r)` and renders a **“SEED — already counted”** badge. `dup` is the receipt-only check so the SEED badge surfaces and seed rows flow through to `importTransactions` for marking (reported revenue excludes them so the log never shows double-counted amounts).
5. **`seedDB()`** stamps `seedFrom`/`seedTo`; **`load()`** migrates existing saves by name-matching `SEED_CUSTOMERS` so the frozen window is backfilled on first run.

## Guard ordering (req. 6)

> The guard only fires for rows whose receipt is **NOT** yet in `DB.seen` (receipt guard checked first), and uses the **snapshot window**, not the live `lastVisit`.

`isSeen` checks the receipt map first and returns early; `isSeedDuplicate` reads `cust.seedTo` (the frozen seed value), falling back to `lastVisit` only when the snapshot is absent.

## Verification

- All 4 inline `<script>` blocks re-parse cleanly (Node `new Function`).
- 15/15 unit checks on the guard logic: no-date, inside/outside/boundary window, no-match, `isNew`, rebuild-mode, snapshot-vs-live-`lastVisit`, receipt-first ordering, and the `{seedGuard:false}` opt-out for backfill.
- 6/6 checks on the preview badge + import-filter semantics (SEED badge renders; seed rows reach `importTransactions` to be `markSeen`'d).

## Files

- `index.html` — guard + preview + seed snapshot/migration (+70 / −9)

author: tjmcdonough
body:
Three ways into the product and no memory of which one worked. A returning
visitor had to re-derive their own account from scratch every time, and a
wrong guess on an OAuth provider doesn't fail — it mints a second account.

This puts a **Last used** badge in the top-right corner of whichever control
you got in with last: `Continue with Google`, `Continue with GitHub`, or the
email `Sign in` button.

## How

Better Auth ships the mechanism — the `lastLoginMethod` plugin. Two decisions
worth naming:

**The cookie is written on the provider callback, not on the click.** A
hand-rolled version can only write it when the button is pressed, because the
OAuth flow navigates the browser away — which badges a method the user
abandoned at the consent screen. The plugin writes it on success only.

**The cookie is read server-side, in the page.** Both auth pages are already
`force-dynamic` and already resolve `providers` server-side, so the badge rides
the same path. The documented client helper (`getLastUsedLoginMethod()`) runs in
the browser, and `social-buttons.tsx` is `"use client"` — the server would render
no badge and the browser would add one, which is a hydration mismatch and a
visible flash on every load.

`LAST_LOGIN_METHOD_COOKIE` is passed *into* the plugin rather than assumed from
its default, so the writer and the two readers are one symbol with no second
string to typo. No migration and no new env var — `storeInDatabase` stays off,
the cookie is the whole store.

## Deliberate decisions

- **The email badge is on `/sign-in` only, not the `/sign-up` create form.**
  "Last used" over a control that creates a new account is a wrong signal. The
  *social* buttons are badged on both pages — they're one control that signs in
  or up through a single call, so on `/sign-up` the badge is what steers a
  returning user off making a duplicate account.
- **On a shared browser the badge reflects whoever signed in last, not the
  current visitor.** It's a hint, never a lock — all controls stay equally
  available and unmodified. It discloses only *which method*, no identity or
  email. Google, Slack and GitHub all behave this way. `clearLastUsedLoginMethod()`
  on sign-out would remove it, at the cost of the feature: surviving sign-out is
  the entire point.
- **An unrecognised cookie value badges nothing.** The plugin also writes
  `passkey`, `magic-link` and `siwe` for methods this app doesn't offer, and a
  provider whose credentials get pulled must not leave a badge floating where its
  button used to be. The gate fails to the plain sign-in page everyone has today.

## Accessibility

The badge sits *outside* the `<button>` element, so it doesn't join the
accessible name (`Continue with Google`, not `Continue with Google Last used`).
Tabbing moves between controls and would skip it entirely as static text, so the
badged button carries `aria-describedby` pointing at it. It's `pointer-events:
none` — it can never eat a click meant for the button under it. Positioned inside
the corner rather than overhanging the edge: the buttons sit 8px apart and an
overhanging badge lands on the one above it.

## Edge sweep

Walked D4/D5/D8/D9/D10/D11/D13 — **0 unhandled**. The one that mattered was D11,
producer/consumer wiring: the plugin writes a cookie and the pages read it, joined
only by a string. Verified against the plugin source that it writes
`config.cookieName` verbatim with no `__Secure-` prefix under `useSecureCookies`
— that prefix would have made the badge silently never appear in production only,
while working perfectly in dev.

The cookie is `httpOnly: false` by design (the client is meant to be able to read
it), which means the browser can also write it. Nothing from it is ever rendered:
it selects which fixed control carries a fixed label, and a value naming no
control selects none. There's a test for that.

## Activation sweep

No dead-ends. The change is net-positive on scent — it converts "which of these
three did I use?" from recall into recognition. The no-cookie state is byte-for-byte
the page that ships today.

## Validation

`/ship` is exempt from the full gate, but this ran:

- Typecheck: PASS (all 7 packages)
- Lint: PASS (3 pre-existing warnings, none in these files)
- Tests: PASS — 52 across `__tests__/auth` + `__tests__/ui`
- Prettier: PASS
- Full suite + build: CI

**Wants one manual check after deploy**, because no local test can drive a real
OAuth round-trip: sign in with GitHub, reload `/sign-in`, confirm the badge is on
the GitHub button.

author: janithjay
body:
### Purpose

Fixes two issues preventing `sign in` in the `@thunderid/nuxt` SDK and quickstart sample app:
1. **Session Cookie Resolution**: `getSessionCookieName()` and `getTempSessionCookieName()` in `packages/nuxt/src/runtime/server/utils/session.ts` evaluated static property access (`CookieConfig.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and `CookieConfig.TEMP_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`), which returned `undefined`. This caused session cookies to be saved under the literal cookie name `"undefined"` instead of the configured vendor prefix (e.g. `__thunderid__session`).
2. **Token Request Configuration**: The default token endpoint auth method (`client_secret_basic`) caused token exchange to fail with an `unauthorized_client` error when the Identity Provider expected credentials in the request body. Configured `tokenRequest.authMethod` to `client_secret_post` in `samples/nuxt/quickstart/nuxt.config.ts`.

### Approach
- Updated `getSessionCookieName()` and `getTempSessionCookieName()` in `packages/nuxt/src/runtime/server/utils/session.ts` to call static methods `CookieConfig.getSessionCookieName(vendor)` and `CookieConfig.getTempSessionCookieName(vendor)`.
- Configured `thunderid.tokenRequest.authMethod: 'client_secret_post'` in `samples/nuxt/quickstart/nuxt.config.ts`.


### Related Issues

- fixes https://github.com/thunder-id/thunderid/issues/4568

author: nilsmeier1812
body:
## Summary

Implements a complete HTTP-JSON bridge for live arm pose execution, allowing external projects to command the G1 robot arms without requiring ROS. The system supports both joint-space and Cartesian pose targets, with full planning and collision avoidance.

## Key Changes

### New Components
- **`arm_api.py`**: HTTP server node (`:8770`) that bridges HTTP requests to ROS topics. Handles request validation, status tracking, and response delivery with optional waiting for completion.
- **`arm_command.py`**: Wire format parser and validator for arm commands. Shared by both the HTTP bridge and ROS controller to prevent format divergence. Supports two command types:
  - `joints`: Direct 7-DOF joint angles per arm (rad)
  - `pose`: Cartesian hand pose (position + orientation) with automatic IK solving
- **`arm_cli.py`**: Reference CLI client using only Python stdlib (no external dependencies), demonstrating the API and serving as a copy-paste template for integration.

### Documentation
- **`ARM_API.md`**: Complete API reference covering all endpoints, request/response formats, status states, HTTP codes, and security considerations.
- **`ARM_API_HOWTO.md`**: Step-by-step practical guide with code examples in Python, JavaScript, curl, and direct ROS usage.

### Enhanced Pose Storage
- **`pose_store.py`**: Major refactor for persistence and organization:
  - Moved storage from volatile `$HOME` to bind-mounted repo (`data/arm_poses.json`) to survive container restarts
  - Added category/folder support for organizing poses
  - Implemented schema versioning (v1→v2 migration)
  - Automatic legacy file migration from old location
- **`ui_interface.py`**: New `PoseSaveDialog` consolidates name, category, and component selection into a single dialog instead of sequential prompts.

### Controller Integration
- **`arm_controller.py`**: 
  - Added `/g1pilot/arm_command` subscription for live pose commands
  - Added `/g1pilot/arm_command/status` publisher for command feedback
  - Added `/g1pilot/pose_store/save/status` publisher for save operation feedback
  - Tracks command request ID and source for proper status attribution
  - Refactored `_on_pose_save()` to use shared `arm_command.parse_save_command()`

### IK Solver Enhancement
- **`ik_solver.py`**: Added offline IK solving capability (`solve_offline()`) for one-shot pose targets, complementing the existing servo-based approach.

### Launch & Build
- **`manipulation_launcher.launch.py`**: Added conditional launch of `arm_api` node
- **`setup.py`**: Registered `arm_api` as entry point

## Security & Design Notes

- **Default binding**: `127.0.0.1:8770` (localhost only) — requires explicit `bind_host` configuration and `auth_token` header for network exposure
- **No security bypass**: All safety gates (E-Stop, ENABLE MANIPULATION, collision, limits) remain in `arm_controller` — the bridge cannot circumvent them
- **Shared validation**: Both HTTP and ROS paths use identical `arm_command.parse_*()` functions to prevent format divergence
- **Atomic file operations**: Pose storage uses write-tmp-then-rename for safe concurrent access
- **Status tracking**: Each command gets a unique ID; status messages are attributed to the correct requester via `/g1pilot/arm_command/status`

## Use Cases

1. **External planning systems** compute arm poses and execute them without ROS infrastructure
2. **Web dashboards** or mobile apps control the arm via standard HTTP
3. **Pose management** with persistent storage across container restarts and organizational categories

author: bbekshr
body:
Closes the S70 asymmetry: `app/api/server/[slug]/refresh-score/route.ts` has guarded advisory
reconciliation on the score write landing since S51, but `bots/compute-scores.ts` — the far higher
volume writer (~1,000 servers/night vs one maintainer click) — did not.

## The bug

`bots/compute-scores.ts` logged the `servers` UPDATE error and then reconciled anyway. A failed
UPDATE (57014 statement timeout, transient PostgREST 5xx) plus a scan reporting zero advisories
closed **every** open `security_advisories` row while `cve_count` and `score_security` kept the old
CVE penalty. The result is a page that contradicts itself: `components/server/Hero.tsx:36` counts
advisory ROWS and says "No known CVEs", while `components/server/SecurityPanel.tsx:138` reads the
`cve_count` COLUMN and still shows N. Nothing self-heals it — the next scan re-derives `cve_count`
from OSV, not from the closed rows.

The bot's exposure is strictly **wider** than the route's: it passes `closeOn: 'success-or-pending'`,
under which `lib/advisories.ts`'s early return never fires, so a `'pending'` scan closes rows too.

## The change

- The reconcile now sits in the `else` arm of `if (updateError)`, mirroring the route's guard.
  Deliberately `if/else` and **not** `continue` — a `continue` would skip the 300ms OSV politeness
  sleep on precisely the run where every write is failing.
- New `serverUpdateFailures` counter, disjoint from `advisoryWriteFailures` (whose own comment scopes
  it to reconcile failures only).
- `run.addUpdated()` gated on the write landing, so `bot_runs.servers_updated` counts writes that
  actually happened (precedent: `bots/sync-registry.ts` / S66).
- `run.setSummary` now reports `attempted` **and** `scored = processed - serverUpdateFailures`. A
  1000-server run where every write fails previously reported `scored: 1000`; it now reports
  `attempted: 1000, scored: 0, serverUpdateFailures: 1000`.
- `bots/freshness-probe.ts:42` cross-file line citation corrected (`369-377` → `410-417`).

`process.exitCode` is deliberately unchanged — the no-exit-code policy is documented in the bot and
its open question is backlog row M10. This PR does not decide it.

## Verification evidence

qa-verifier ran the bar twice: once on `8f69cb5`, then again on `fb8f7f0` after the review-board
fixes, because a diff that changes after verification is unverified.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 1 warning — pre-existing `app/admin/page.tsx:246`, tracked as S2/S7, count unchanged |
| `npm test` | **298 passed / 23 files** (`main` baseline: 297) |
| `npm run build` | **Exempt, not run** — verified surface is `bots/**` + `__tests__/**` + `BACKLOG.md` only, with no non-comment import of the bot anywhere under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`. A real-env build prerenders ~1,000 server pages against a 5 GB Supabase egress ceiling, so it is not run speculatively. |

Feature check: no reachable path from `updateError != null` to a `reconcileAdvisories` call (one call
site, inside the `else`; no `continue`/`break` between the UPDATE and the guard). Summary arithmetic
verified against a hypothetical all-fail run. The corrected line citation was re-read and matches the
policy comment's true first and last line exactly.

## Review board

Four agents in parallel (correctness, regression, security/data-integrity, qa-verifier), each told to
refute the diff. All findings resolved:

- **CONFIRMED ×3 — "the added test does not exercise the changed file."** Correct, and stated plainly
  here rather than papered over: no file under `__tests__/` can import a `bots/` module (module-scope
  `main()`; `bots/lib/supabase.ts` throws without service-role env). **S70's acceptance criterion
  explicitly allows a documented manual trace, and that is the branch being claimed for the bot.**
  The added test pins the *shared* guard shape on the route half — which was itself unpinned by any
  test until now (a `if (false)` mutation of it left the whole suite green on `main`). Filed **M17**
  to extract a `lib/` seam so the bot arm becomes lockable.
- **CONFIRMED ×2 — the run summary overstated.** Fixed (`attempted` vs `scored`, above).
- **CONFIRMED — stale cross-file line citation.** Fixed and re-verified.
- **PLAUSIBLE — `movedSlugs` should not be gated.** Accepted, and it reversed a CEO decision. The
  asymmetry is decisive: over-revalidating costs one entry in an already-batched POST; under-
  revalidating leaves `/compare/...` stale for its full 7-day ISR TTL, and because postgrest-js
  resolves with `{error}` rather than throwing, a lost response *after* a commit produces exactly
  that. Reverted to `main`'s unconditional placement.
- **PLAUSIBLE ×2 — the guard comment overstated.** Corrected in place: "the next run retries" is true
  only when the write did not commit (a lost response after a commit stamps `score_computed_at` and
  defers the reconcile by up to `SCORE_STALE_DAYS`), and the comment now names what the safe branch
  gives up — `reconcileAdvisories` is the only *creator* of advisory rows as well as the only closer,
  so a newly published CVE goes unrecorded that night. That trade is deliberate: a false-green
  verdict is worse than a delayed disclosure, and an upsert-only mode is not a safe alternative
  because the upsert writes `adv.status` and can itself close a row.

## Deviations from plan

- The architect stage was skipped; the CEO wrote the build plan from the research brief. The board
  then refuted one call in it (`movedSlugs`). Recorded in the retro rather than filed.
- Two out-of-scope defects were **found and filed, not fixed** — finding and fixing do not share a
  diff. `app/api/submit/route.ts:239-284` is the third writer of this class and is *worse*: it never
  destructures the UPDATE's `error` at all, then reconciles unconditionally. Its "provable no-op"
  comment covers the close half only; the row-creating upsert half still runs.

## Records

BACKLOG S70 → `in-review`; M17 and M18 appended; cycle facts folded into
`docs/org-memory/codebase.md`; micro-retro appended to `docs/org-memory/retros.md`. Only Status was
changed on the existing row — no Priority or criteria edited, no rows deleted.

## ⚠️ Protected path — needs your `human-approved` label

The **Protected-path guard is RED by design**: this PR adds one test case to
`__tests__/refresh-score-advisories.test.ts`, and `__tests__/**` is a protected path under
CLAUDE.md §5 (test assertions are the verification bar). `Type-check / Lint / Test` is green.

No production code under a protected path is touched — `bots/**` is not protected. I have not added
the label and will not; applying it is yours.

author: tdjager
body:
Sets `cooldown: default-days: 5` on both update blocks in `.github/dependabot.yml`.

## What this actually changes

Dependabot has applied a **three-day cooldown by default since 2026-07-14**. So this is 3 → 5 days, not 0 → 5. The explicit setting also pins the choice, so a later change to that default cannot silently shrink the window.

Five days is measured against how fast the registry compromises of the past year surfaced: chalk/debug, shai-hulud and the keyv/cacheable maintainer hijack of 2026-08-04 were all detected within hours to days. With `interval: weekly` the practical delay is *at least* five days and at most until the next weekly run.

Cooldown covers **version** updates only — Dependabot security updates are exempt and keep opening immediately.

## Two limitations, both recorded in the file

1. Cooldown keys off the age of a **new release**. An attacker who repoints an existing tag or version at malicious content (the tj-actions/changed-files pattern, CVE-2025-30066) never triggers a version-update PR, so cooldown never sees it.
2. **The `pip` entry does not govern what CI installs.** CI runs `uv sync` from `uv.lock`, and Dependabot's pip updater does not maintain `uv.lock` — that needs `package-ecosystem: uv`. Cooling down the pip entry is harmless but protects less than it looks like it does. Switching ecosystems is a behaviour change, so it is left out of this PR and marked with a `TODO` in the config instead.

## Note

Opened from a fork (`tdjager/zad-cli`) — I do not have push access to this repo, so the workflows on this PR need a maintainer to approve them.

author: dennie-seth
body:
Produces the missing **simulation results artifact** for T-0099. The card shipped the sim harness + tests but never actually ran the sim to generate data. Base `develop`.

## What existed vs what this adds
`sweeps.py` ran the nine invariant scenarios once at a fixed compressed-time config and printed a table — it never swept a parameter grid or exported anything, and no results artifact had ever been committed. This adds `sim/run.py` (+ `test_run.py`, `sim-tuning-sweep` entry point): a deterministic (seed 42) grid-sweep runner over the open tuning brackets from `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, and writes the data out.

## Headline findings (full detail in `tools/sim/results/RESULTS.md`)
1. **INV-6 (rarity instance cap) never violated** across all 38 runs — cap enforcement is robust in both brackets.
2. **Held-bleed duration (E-1) is the parameter with real signal.** Under hoarder stress, fast held bleed (60–75 min) → ~6–9% INV-7 violations vs ~101–106% at the slow end; world-bleed sub-range has no measurable effect. **Recommend held bleed 60–75 min, world bleed kept at full 48–72h.**
3. **T-1 / T-2 show no differentiating signal** — and the sweep surfaced *why*, which is worth attention: unlock decay is applied in the engine but **never read by any invariant check** (T-2 results byte-identical at every value), and **INV-8’s "world-anchored" heuristic conflates "currently held" with "extinct"** (flat violation rate regardless of collapse duration). Recommend holding both at bracket midpoints (collapse 3 weeks, unique-unlock decay 7 days) *for now*, but those two are real coverage gaps worth follow-up cards.

## Artifacts
- `tools/sim/results/RESULTS.md` — full writeup, tables, method, limitations
- `tools/sim/results/tuning_sweep.{json,csv}` — raw 38-row data
- `tools/sim/src/sim/run.py` + `tests/test_run.py` — the runner + tests
- `tasks/T-0099.md` — new `## Results` section pointing at the artifact

## Checks
`pytest` 80 passed (was 73), `ruff` clean. TDD for the new runner. Authored Dennie Seth + `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

Clarifies failed patch replacements where `old_string` and `new_string` are identical. The existing behavior correctly performed no edit, but its terse error did not explain how to form a valid replacement.

author: shahednasser
body:
## Summary

**What** — Enables the react-router v6 `future` flags that the admin dashboard actually depends on, ahead of the react-router v7 upgrade. One file, +22/−1.

```diff
  const router = createBrowserRouter(routes, {
    basename: __BASE__ || "/",
+   future: {
+     v7_relativeSplatPath: true,
+   },
  })

- <RouterProvider router={router} />
+ <RouterProvider router={router} future={{ v7_startTransition: true }} />
```

**Why** — These flags become the default in react-router v7. Turning them on while still on v6 means the v7 bump is a dependency change rather than a behavioural one, and it isolates any behavioural regression to *this* PR instead of the version bump.

**How — and why only two of the six**

Rather than enabling all six documented flags, each was checked against whether the dashboard uses the feature it governs:

| Flag | Governs | Usage in the dashboard | Enabled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v7_relativeSplatPath` | relative paths inside splat routes | 1 splat route — the `*` catch-all rendering `no-match` | **yes** |
| `v7_startTransition` | wraps every router state update in `React.startTransition` | applies regardless of features used | **yes** |
| `v7_fetcherPersist` | `useFetcher` lifecycle | 0 uses of `useFetcher` | no |
| `v7_normalizeFormMethod` | `formMethod` casing on router `Form`/`submit` | 0 — all 126 `<Form>` usages are the dashboard's own `components/common/form`; nothing imports `Form` from `react-router-dom`, and there are no `submit()`/`method:` calls | no |
| `v7_skipActionErrorRevalidation` | revalidation after a route `action` errors | 0 route `action`s — all 24 `action:` keys are data-table selection callbacks | no |
| `v7_partialHydration` | `fallbackElement` → `HydrateFallback` | see below | no |

`v7_partialHydration` is excluded for a different reason than the rest. The dashboard *is* a data router with loaders (supplied by `lazy:` modules re-exporting `loader`), but it has no root `HydrateFallback`. Enabling the flag makes react-router warn on **every initial page load**:

```
No `HydrateFallback` element provided to render during initial hydration
    at DataRoutes … at RouterProvider …
```

This was caught by actually running the dashboard, not by reading the docs. Adding a `HydrateFallback` is a prerequisite for enabling the flag, and belongs in its own change.

One API detail worth recording: **`v7_startTransition` is not a router option.** Its type lives on `RouterProvider`, and passing it to `createBrowserRouter` is a compile error:

```
error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and
'v7_startTransition' does not exist in type
'Partial<Omit<FutureConfig, "v7_prependBasename">>'.
```

That type is also why the router-side list is complete at these flags: `v7_prependBasename` is applied automatically by data routers and isn't user-settable.

**Testing**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test` | 14 files / 107 tests passed — unchanged from before this PR |
| `turbo run build --filter=@medusajs/dashboard` | 10/10 tasks pass |
| `prettier --check` | clean |
| Built output sets only the two intended flags | `v7_relativeSplatPath: true`, `v7_startTransition: true`; `v7_partialHydration: true` appears 0 times |
| Admin dev-server + HMR smoke (all 9 `virtual:medusa/*` families, add/remove regeneration, `/__open-in-editor` 403) | 21/21 passing |

Verified end-to-end against a real Medusa app with these packages linked locally: rebuilt the dashboard, redeployed into the app, restarted `medusa develop`, and confirmed the served bundle contains only the two flags.

**Known gap:** the runtime navigation pass for `v7_startTransition` (rapid navigation between `lazy:` routes, deep navigation + browser Back) was not completed — the browser tooling wouldn't connect. Static verification is clean and the dashboard's own test suite is unchanged, but that behavioural check is outstanding. It is re-covered by the full manual matrix in the react-router v7 phase, when these flags become defaults anyway.

---

## Checklist

- [ ] I have added a **changeset** for this PR — changesets for this upgrade land together on the umbrella PR, so the release notes read as one change
- [x] The changes are covered by relevant **tests** — dashboard suite unchanged at 107 tests; dev-server/HMR smoke at 21/21
- [x] I have verified the code works as intended locally
- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable

---

## Additional Context

Part of the staged Vite 5.4.21 → 7.3.6 upgrade, targeting the `chore/update-vite` integration branch. This phase is deliberately independent of Vite: it de-risks the later react-router v7 bump, and can be reviewed and reverted on its own.

author: fcecin
body:
# fix(ci): make CI green again — master, PR, daily, pre-release, release assets

## Description

Master's `ci.yml` has not run since **2026-06-26**: every push produced a run
with **zero jobs**. `release-assets.yml` has **never** produced an artifact —
three runs in its whole history, all failed. `ci-rln-simulator.yml` last passed
**2026-05-22**. The nightly macOS builds have been red the entire time.

None of that was visible, for two compounding reasons. The e2e job that would
have caught the code regression only runs on `pull_request`, so a master
breakage surfaces as *everyone's PR is red* rather than *master is broken*. And
master's own `ci.yml` run aborted at startup before scheduling anything, so it
had nothing to report.

Every fix below was reproduced first, then verified on a fork where `push`,
`workflow_dispatch` and `pull_request` could all be exercised. Several were only
reachable after the previous one was fixed — `release-assets` alone had six
defects stacked behind each other.

## Changes

### `ci.yml` — master CI was dead for six weeks

The interop `uses:` pointed at `@SMOKE_TEST_2026.06.25`, an **annotated** tag.
GitHub cannot resolve that workflow's own nested
`./.github/workflows/test_PR_image.yml` through an annotated tag, and on `push`
it aborts the whole run before scheduling a single job:

```
Invalid workflow file: .github/workflows/ci.yml#L203
error parsing called workflow ... nim_waku_PR.yml@SMOKE_TEST_2026.06.25
    (source tag with sha:928c6cde)
 --> "./.github/workflows/test_PR_image.yml" : workflow was not found.
```

`pull_request` tolerates it, so only master was affected. Introduced by PR 3983
(2026-06-26), which switched the ref from `SMOKE_TEST_STABLE` — a **lightweight**
tag that resolves fine — to the annotated one. Bisected: `4ba5710a` = 9 jobs,
`26098d76` = 0 jobs.

Pinned to the tag's commit. **Push run went from 0 jobs to 11.**

### `persistency.nim` — the one red job once CI ran again

With CI repaired, master's push run was green except `send-api-e2e-tests`, which
segfaulted at `test_s24_ephemeral_message_with_reachable_store`. Two defects:

`reset()` cleared the global before calling `close()`. `let p = gPersistency`
compiles to a bare pointer copy with **no incref** (confirmed in the generated
C), so that dropped the last reference and freed the object before `close()`
walked its `jobs` table. Now it closes first, then clears.

The singleton is also created on whichever pooled FFI worker thread starts a
node and released on whichever one stops a later node. Under `--mm:refc` the GC
heap is per thread, so that release frees into the wrong heap. `GC_ref` pins it
for the process lifetime.

### `ci-daily.yml`, `pre-release.yml`, `release-assets.yml` — no toolchain

All three went from checkout straight to `make`, with no Nim/Nimble on the
runner, so macOS died on `make: nimble: No such file or directory`. ubuntu
survived only because its image ships a usable nim. `ci.yml`'s build job had it
right all along; the other three never did.

### `pre-release.yml` — permissions decided by a repo setting

`logos-delivery-js/.../test-node.yml` declares `actions: read, checks: write`.
Neither caller granted anything, so the repo-wide default decided, and with a
read-only default the run dies at startup before scheduling any job. Declared
explicitly on both callers, so it no longer depends on a repo setting.

### `ci-rln-simulator.yml` — contract pin drifted from the submodule

The node started calling `getRecentRoots()` in PR 3903 (2026-06-04); the
workflow kept deploying hardcoded contract `e75ac913`, which does not define it.
Every `eth_call` reverted, every publish was rejected as RLN-invalid, and the
fleet never reached a publishable state. The commit is now derived from
`vendor/waku-rlnv2-contract` so the two cannot drift again.

### `release-assets.yml` — five more, each hidden behind the last

- **static build had no dependency paths.** `--skipParentCfg:on` skips the
  repo-root `config.nims` that includes `nimble.paths`, so the compile died on
  `cannot open file: chronicles`. The dynamic build always passed `off`.
- **built and shipped libwaku, which no longer exists.** No Makefile target, no
  `library/libwaku.nim`, no `library/libwaku.h`, no nimble task. `make libwaku`
  resolves to "Nothing to be done", produces nothing, and packaging then failed
  on the missing files. Deleted (-48 lines).
- **macOS packaged headers from a path that never existed** —
  `./liblogosdelivery/liblogosdelivery.h`; they live in `library/`. The Linux
  branch was already correct.
- **`dpkg-deb` rejected the version.** Debian versions must start with a digit
  and our tags are `vX.Y.Z`, so `Version: v0.38.1` is invalid. This would have
  failed on every real release tag, not just here.
- artifact names embedded the raw ref, which breaks `tar` on any branch dispatch
  (harmless for tags, but it made the workflow untestable before merging).

### `tests/simulator/rln-e2e-test.py` — one sleep, deliberately

The upstream test is left intact except for a commented 10-second settle
between `WARMUP` and `PROPAGATION`. The startup flake it bridges is a **node
bug, not a test bug**: REST relay publish returns 200 even when gossipsub has
an empty mesh and drops the message outright — the handler discards the
`NoPeersToPublish` error that `node.publish` already reports, and checks only
the timeout. Observed in CI as the publisher's first two messages reaching
0/5 receivers while everything ~6s later reached all of them. So `WARMUP`'s
publish-until-200 gate can pass while the sender's mesh is still forming, and
single-shot `PROPAGATION` judges a publish that went nowhere.

The proper fix (surface zero-peer publishes as 503; then the sleep and the
flake both disappear) is an API behaviour change and gets its own PR rather
than riding a CI one.

### Review polish

A fork-side review pass added, in the same spirit:

- `pre-release.yml` reads `$GITHUB_REF` / `$RELEASE_NAME` from the environment
  instead of splicing `${{github.ref}}` into the script.
- `release-assets.yml` checkout bumped `v2` → `v4`.
- The synthesised Debian version squashes characters dpkg forbids (branch
  names can carry underscores).
- `AGENTS.md` no longer documents the removed `make libwaku` target.
- `reset()`'s docstring no longer claims to clear a "Teardown provider" it
  never touched.

## Notes

Verified on a fork, per workflow:

| Workflow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` on `push` | 0 jobs, startup failure | **11/11 green** |
| `ci.yml` on `pull_request` | `send-api-e2e-tests` segfault | **11/11 green** |
| `ci-rln-simulator.yml` | 2/3 scenarios, aborted at WARMUP | 5/6 bare (PROPAGATION startup flake = the REST zero-peer bug); **6/6** with the 10s settle bridge |
| `ci-daily.yml` | macOS instant death | macOS builds; only red is the Discord notifier, which needs a secret a fork lacks |
| `pre-release.yml` | macOS red, js-waku red | all 3 build legs + both js-waku green; only red is release creation, which a fork cannot do |
| `release-assets.yml` | never produced an artifact | both macOS legs green; ubuntu deb re-testing |

Behaviour changes a reviewer should consciously accept:

- **Interop ref is now a commit, not a tag.** Bumping `SMOKE_TEST_*` no longer
  moves CI automatically; the pin must be updated by hand. That is the cost of
  the fix — GitHub cannot resolve the nested ref through an annotated tag.
- **The RLN simulator now follows the submodule** rather than a hardcoded
  commit. Intended, but moving the submodule now moves the deployed contract.
- **`GC_ref` leaks one small object per `reset`.** Deliberate, and far cheaper
  than corrupting another thread's heap.
- **Tagged releases will start producing artifacts again** for the first time
  since 2026-05-07, and will no longer include a `libwaku` asset.

No workflow triggers were touched: zero changes to `on:`, `schedule:`, `cron:`,
`push:`, `pull_request:` or `workflow_dispatch:` anywhere i

body:
Closes #4346.

### Description
This PR executes a massive omnichannel revenue initiative by engineering an algorithmic "In-Store Availability" pipeline. Cara is rapidly expanding its physical brick-and-mortar retail footprint. However, the current e-commerce website operates as an entirely isolated digital silo. Customers frequently browse online but prefer to buy in-store to avoid shipping delays or to try the item on first. We were completely failing to leverage our digital traffic to drive physical retail sales. We needed to engineer a system to seamlessly bridge the digital and physical retail experience.

### Changes Made
- **API Integration:** Upgraded the backend API architecture to integrate directly with the physical Point-of-Sale (POS) inventory database (`/api/inventory/retail`).
- **Component Engineering:** Engineered a highly interactive `<InStoreTracker />` React component prominently injected onto the PDP.
- **Geolocation Pipeline:** The frontend engine now utilizes the browser's native Geolocation API (or gracefully accepts a manual zip code input) to mathematically determine the user's physical coordinates.
- **Dynamic Curation & UX:** The backend mathematically queries the physical inventory of the 3 closest Cara retail locations. It returns the exact stock status for that specific SKU/Size variant. The UI dynamically renders a high-urgency call to action: *"Available today at the SoHo Flagship store (1.2 miles away)."*

### Impact
- **Omnichannel Conversion & Foot Traffic:** By engineering this localized tracking pipeline, we transition from an isolated e-commerce site to a holistic, omnichannel retail engine. We instantly capture high-intent buyers who need the item immediately but don't want to wait for shipping. This drastically drives foot traffic to our expensive physical retail locations and significantly increases overall brand conversion by meeting the customer exactly where they want to shop.

author: dhoulb
body:
## Summary

Fixes the local `bun run test:firebase` failure on macOS, diagnosed as a **startup race**: `firebase emulators:exec` can launch the test script a beat before the emulator's Java socket actually binds. When that happens every request fails with an instant `ECONNRESET` and the whole suite burns through (in ~34ms) before the port opens. Diagnostics that confirmed it: with a long-running emulator, `curl` and `bun -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/')"` both succeed on the same machine that failed under `emulators:exec`.

Fix: before registering the emulator-backed tests, poll the emulator endpoint until it responds (100ms interval, up to 10s), throwing one clear "emulator is not accepting connections" error if it never does. Free when the socket is already up — verified 41/41 against the emulator.

Also documents a second, separate finding in the firebase README: the emulator host must stay pinned to `127.0.0.1` (as `firebase.json` already does) because the emulator's socket is IPv4-only and Bun's `fetch` resolves `localhost` to `::1` **without falling back to IPv4** — unlike curl — so `localhost` fails with `ECONNRESET` even against a healthy emulator. That no-fallback behaviour may be worth reporting upstream to oven-sh/bun.

body:
## What & why

Two small pieces the MoonTerminal chart panel needs.

**`MoonTabItem` label centring.** A tab is laid out at an explicit width, but its
row carried no justification, so the label sat against the left padding and read
as mis-aligned whenever the text was shorter than the box — visible on every
short tab name. An unbalanced top margin pushed it a further 2px below centre.
The label now owns the flexible middle of the row: `flex_1 + min_w_0` lets a long
label clip inside the tab instead of pushing the badge and close button out of
it, and `justify_center` centres it in the space that is left.

**`chart-candlestick` icon.** Consumers offering candle display settings label
that control with a typographic glyph, which reads as a separator rather than a
button. This adds the Lucide icon so they can use an icon slot.

## How to verify

- `cargo check -p moon-ui-components` and the repo guardrails script.
- Visual: any `MoonTabStrip` with tabs wider than their labels — the label sits
  centred, and a label longer than its tab clips rather than displacing the badge
  or the close button.
- The icon is consumed downstream as `icons/chart-candlestick.svg`; it is picked
  up by the embedded asset set with no registration step.

Consumed by the companion MoonTerminal PR, which must merge after this one — the
icon path there is an unchecked string, so its CI passes with or without this.

author: kaloudis
body:
# Description

Fixes the remaining missed-accounting path from external security report FND-004 (NWC budget enforcement).

The report's headline finding, a check-then-act race where N parallel `pay_invoice` requests could each pass the budget check before any debits landed, was already closed by #4303 (per-service payment queue) and #4305 (pending amounts reserved inside `canSpend`). Verification against master also showed its reconcile-miss claim is now fail-closed rather than an escape: an unreconciled pending activity stays counted in `pendingSpendSats` indefinitely.

One claim survived verification as a real residual hole. In `handleLightningPayInvoice`, `finalizePayment`, the only place a settled spend is debited via `trackSpending`, was gated on finding the settled payment in the refreshed payments list:

```ts
if (payment) {
    await this.finalizePayment({ ... });
}
```

If the payment settled (preimage in `TransactionsStore`) but the list lookup missed, the handler returned success with a valid preimage while recording **no activity at all**: neither `totalSpendSats` nor `pendingSpendSats` ever saw the amount, so the spend permanently escaped the connection budget. Miss windows: payments lists windowed at 100 entries on busy nodes, node indexing lag immediately after settlement, backends with incomplete `listPayments` (CLN's missing-entries lists are a known issue), or a failed refresh. The cashu path had the same `if (payment)` gate after the melt had already been confirmed successful.

## What changed

- `stores/NostrWalletConnectStore.ts`: budget accounting no longer depends on the payments-list lookup. The lightning success path finalizes whenever a preimage is in hand (`payment || preimage`); the cashu path finalizes unconditionally once the melt has succeeded. When the list lookup misses, the activity record is synthesized from request-side state (invoice, payment hash, preimage, amount, fee).
- `utils/NostrConnectUtils.ts`: new `buildSettledPaymentFallback()` builds that settled `Payment`/`CashuPayment` record. Passing `decoded: null` into `finalizePayment` was not an option; the `BaseModel` constructor throws on null data.
- `utils/NostrConnectUtils.test.ts`: unit tests for the fallback builder (lightning and cashu shapes, settled-payment semantics, optional-field tolerance).

When the lookup succeeds, behavior is byte-identical to before. The fallback only fires in the window where the spend previously escaped accounting.

body:
Three inbox changes, all approved by Antonio ("ship everything left if it's safe").

## 1. Deleting an email now bins our own copy too — 180-day recoverable bin
Since the Own-Inbox capture landed we hold our own copy of every email body and attachment. Deleting only moved the Gmail side; our copy was kept for ever with no notion of deletion.

- Deleting stamps a bin clock. The copy stays **readable** the whole 180 days — Gmail empties its own Trash at ~30, so past that ours is the only copy. That is the point.
- Restoring clears it, **including a restore done inside the Gmail app** — without that, the sweep would destroy the only copy of a live email at day 180.
- A nightly sweep erases past-retention copies: **storage objects before the rows**, because the rows hold the only pointers to the bytes.
- **Delete forever** (Trash only, confirm, no undo) erases our copy immediately for junk. It deliberately does **not** hard-delete in Gmail — our grant is `gmail.modify`, which cannot; the first version called it anyway and would have 403'd *after* flagging our copy for destruction. It is also **per message, not per thread**: a trashed thread routinely picks up a live reply later.

Council (5 core + Security + Data-Migration) found **5 blockers, several data-destroying** — all fixed. Sandbox QA then found a **6th they all missed**: the catch-up sweep never drained (stamped 180, then 0 for ever, leaving 65 trashed copies unbinned). Fixed and re-proven.

Proven on the deployed sandbox build: drain to zero, the restore direction, a real end-to-end purge (stored file went 200 → gone, all rows removed, other copies untouched), and the purge cron refusing an unauthenticated call.

## 2. Search suggestions as you type
Search matched **whole words only** — on production `anto` matched 0 rows while `antonio` matched 2,473, so a dropdown would have sat empty while you type. Prefix matching on the word under the cursor is the feature, not a garnish.

Operator queries (`from:`, `has:`) stay on the live-Gmail Enter path — a keystroke must never cost Gmail quota (the 2026-08-02 self-rate-limit incident). A failing suggest never breaks the search box.

## 3. Compose left the open thread frozen
Antonio forwarded 9 PDFs and saw no attachments on the sent email. Nothing was lost — all 9 were captured 8 seconds after the send. The reply box has always refreshed the open thread after sending; Compose only ever refreshed the list.

## Not included, deliberately
Full-body search. 22,744 bodies are stored but not indexed, so a word buried deep in an email is still unfindable. Its own job, its own decision.

## Database
Both migrations are **already applied to production** by Antonio (DDL before code).

Suite 8,029 green; lint, types and build clean.

## Summary
- Builds on #486's `assign_field_value`/`replace_unsupported_character_and_retry` (which recovers from characters the packet PDF template's Helvetica font can't encode by transliterating them, e.g. "ń" -> "n") to fix a gap: for characters with **no glyph in the font at all**, HexaPDF raises `MissingGlyphError` with `glyph.name` set to the font's generic `".notdef"` placeholder rather than a real Adobe Glyph List name -- so the existing `GlyphList.name_to_unicode` lookup returned `nil` and the fill still crashed.
- Real-world example: a stray `U+FE0F` (VARIATION SELECTOR-16) left behind by a mobile keyboard's emoji autosuggest misfiring while typing “I". It's invisible, has no emoji attached to strip via `strip_emojis` (which only strips a variation selector *following* an actual emoji character), and isn't caught by `LatinScriptValidator` since variation selectors are Unicode script `Inherited`.
- Fix: for `MissingGlyphError`, recover the actual failing character from `glyph.str` directly instead of round-tripping through `glyph.name` -> AGL lookup. The other recovery path (`HexaPDF::Error` "no codepoint for :name", used when the glyph is real but the font's encoding table has no free slot) is unaffected -- there's no glyph object on that error, so it still resolves the character via `GlyphList.name_to_unicode`.
