body:
## Summary

- Makes `admin.timothystl.org` installable ("Add to Home Screen" / "Install admin.timothystl.org"): registers a service worker (`/sw.js`) alongside the manifest that already existed, plus the `apple-mobile-web-app-*` meta tags iOS reads instead of the manifest. The worker deliberately does **not** cache the shell or intercept `fetch` — every screen here (a gym hold queue, a payroll period, held mail) is only as good as its last request, and serving a stale cached copy offline would let staff act on numbers that are already wrong.
- Adds a **Notifications** toggle to the sidebar footer, hidden until the client confirms the browser actually supports the Push API. Subscribing POSTs the browser's push subscription to `/api/push/subscribe`, stored in a new `push_subscriptions` table (`admin/db.js`, `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped).
- Implements Web Push (RFC 8291 aes128gcm content encoding + RFC 8292 VAPID) by hand in `admin/webpush.js` — Cloudflare Workers has no room for the `web-push` npm package, which shells out to Node APIs Workers doesn't have. The derivation (HKDF info strings, header layout, per-record nonce math) is copied from the real `web-push`/`http_ece` reference implementation rather than reconstructed from memory.
- **First trigger wired up**: a held Filtered Mail submission (`/api/contact`, `/api/prayer`) now pings every subscribed device via `ctx.waitUntil(pushToAllSubscribers(...))` — never awaited, so a push failure can't fail a real visitor's submission.
- Documents the required manual step (`VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` / `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` Worker secrets) and the design decisions in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Verification

Since there's no live device or push service to test against in this environment, correctness is verified with an **independent round-trip**: `admin/webpush.test.mjs` encrypts a payload with `admin/webpush.js` (WebCrypto), then decrypts the raw bytes back using a *separately written* implementation of the same spec built on Node's `crypto` module, and asserts the plaintext matches. The VAPID JWT signer was likewise checked against an independent DER-signature verification. Both passed.

- [x] `node admin/webpush.test.mjs` — aes128gcm round-trip OK
- [x] Every `admin/*.js` imports cleanly as ESM (the project's own CI check, since `node --check` alone has missed template-literal breakage before)
- [x] `node --experimental-loader ./test/html-loader.mjs test/admin-redesign.test.mjs` — 633 passed (boots the real Worker against real SQLite)
- [x] `node test/shell-layout.test.mjs` — 33 passed, including "no script errors" in a real browser

## Manual step required after merge

`VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` must be set as Worker secrets (`wrangler secret put VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY --name tlc-newsletter-admin`, same for the private key) before the Notifications toggle will actually work — until then `/api/push/vapid-public-key` answers 501. author: sstern42
body:
Implements a rearm delay for the Salary Expectations trap to prevent players from laying multiple traps in rapid succession. Without this, a single trap placement could function like a machine gun if clicked repeatedly in the same second.

## Changes

- **GameScene**: Added `trapReadyAt` object to track when each trap type becomes available again, measured from placement rather than detonation to cap how often the action can be attempted
- **GameScene**: New `trapWaitRemaining()` method returns milliseconds until a trap type is ready, zero when available
- **GameScene**: New `startTrapDelay()` method applies the cooldown and emits events for UI feedback
- **GameScene**: Updated trap placement to check cooldown before allowing placement and emit 'trap-waiting' event if still cooling
- **UIScene**: Added `waitingTraps` Set to track which trap types are currently cooling down
- **UIScene**: New `available()` method checks both affordability and cooldown status
- **UIScene**: New event handlers for 'trap-waiting', 'trap-waiting-started', and 'trap-ready' to grey out buttons during cooldown
- **UIScene**: Updated button refresh logic to grey selected buttons while cooling, and updated hover logic to respect cooldown
- **UIScene**: New `showTrapWait()` method displays remaining seconds in warning message
- **towers.js**: Added `rearmDelayMs: 4000` to Salary Expectations definition
- **copy.js**: Updated Salary Expectations blurb and added 'trapWaiting' message to HUD copy

The cooldown is set when the trap is placed (not when it detonates), so it acts as a cap on how often the placement action can be attempted regardless of player timing. Button greying provides immediate visual feedback that the trap is unavailable.

## Summary

\`type BasisTransform = AngledFacetMap\` in \`emodeconnection/port.py\` is a hard `SyntaxError` on Python 3.10/3.11 -- this package declares \`requires-python = ">=3.10"\`, and the PEP 695 statement form of type aliases is Python 3.12-only syntax (not deferred by \`from __future__ import annotations\` the way annotation-only syntax is).

Reproduced against a real 3.10.16 interpreter before fixing. \`typing.TypeAlias\` (PEP 613, available since 3.10) is the portable equivalent -- same explicit "this is a type" declaration, works everywhere the package claims to support.

Note: this branch (\`port-offset-pinning\`) was already merged into \`dev\` via #30; this PR only adds the one fix commit on top, so the diff is just the one file.

author: adnenlaplateforme
body:
`/admin/events` portée sur la maquette « Planning & Workshops », et la première
action de cette maquette branchée sur le serveur.

**Dépend de [marsai-back#26](https://github.com/adnenlaplateforme/marsai-back/pull/26)**
pour `GET /events/:id/bookings`. Le reste de la page fonctionne sans.

## `b456571` — la maquette

La page devient un planning — en-tête, deux tuiles de synthèse, un onglet par
journée — au lieu d'une table de lignes. `EventRow` et son `window.confirm`
laissent la place à `EventCard`, dont le dialogue de suppression **compte les
réservations qu'il va emporter** : `booking.event_id` est en ON DELETE CASCADE,
supprimer l'atelier efface les inscriptions sans qu'aucun mail ne parte.

`eventSchedule.js` tient la mise en forme, sans réseau, testé tel quel comme
`juryDistribution.js` :

- les deux langues sont lues côte à côte puis recollées par `mergeTranslations`.
  `GET /events?lang=` filtre sur la traduction : un événement saisi en anglais
  seulement est absent de la réponse française et disparaîtrait du planning.
- la journée se calcule sur la date locale et non `toISOString()` : un atelier
  de 22 h tomberait le lendemain en UTC, sous le mauvais onglet.
- une conférence libre rend `null` et non `0` places prises — « 0 inscription »
  ferait passer une salle ouverte à tous pour un atelier boudé.

Deux correctifs sur la page de création, qui ne pouvait pas fonctionner : elle
n'était routée nulle part, et son payload partait en chaînes là où le schéma zod
attend deux entiers et un booléen — 400 garanti à chaque envoi.

## `e6a49d0` — la liste des participants

Le panneau n'est monté qu'au clic : une journée compte plusieurs cartes, charger
les inscrits de chacune à l'affichage ferait autant de requêtes pour un contenu
que l'admin n'ouvrira peut-être jamais.

`participantsCsv.js` fabrique le fichier côté client — le serveur n'a pas à
produire un second format de la même donnée — et reste pur. **Ses trois
précautions répondent chacune à un cas réel :**

- la marque d'ordre des octets, sans quoi Excel lit le fichier en ANSI et
  massacre les accents ;
- l'échappement RFC 4180 : « Martin, épouse Durand » couperait la ligne en deux
  colonnes et décalerait tout le fichier ;
- l'apostrophe devant un champ commençant par `=`, `+`, `-` ou `@`.
  **`POST /bookings` est une route publique** : un prénom saisi `=1+1` est à la
  portée de n'importe qui, et un tableur l'exécute à l'ouverture.

La date s'écrit `2026-07-01 12:30`, en heure locale et non localisée :
« 01/07/2026, 12:30 » porte sa propre virgule et ouvrirait une colonne de plus.

## Tests

**94 verts, 9 fichiers** (74 → 94), lint propre, `vite build` OK.

Un défaut d'affichage trouvé par le test : sans nom, la ligne montrait l'adresse
deux fois. C'est le composant qui a été corrigé, pas l'assertion.

## Ce qui reste désactivé, à dessein

« Modifier » garde son bouton inerte et sa raison en clair — le formulaire
d'édition n'existe pas encore. Un admin doit pouvoir distinguer « pas encore
livré » de « en panne ».

author: lexus2016
body:
Follow-up to #1678 (issue #1673).

#1678 staggered most evolution stages onto distinct minute offsets, but three
pairs still fire in the same wall-clock minute — which is the whole point of
#1673, since that is when their provider calls overlap:

| pair | collides at |
|---|---|
| `ci-diagnosis` × `postmortem-miner` | 06:00 |
| `ci-diagnosis` × `research` | 09:30 |
| `funnel` × `integration` | 07:40 |

`ci-diagnosis` kept `*/30`, which fires at :00 and :30 and so lands on whatever
else uses those minutes; `funnel` sat on :40, which `integration` already owns on
odd hours.

- `ci-diagnosis`: `*/30` → `12,42`
- `funnel`: `40 7` → `25 7`

Both offsets are unused by any other evolution job.

## The test asserts the invariant, not a list of offsets

`tests/scripts/test_evolution_cron_stagger.py` expands every schedule to its full
`(hour, minute)` firing set and intersects every pair. A schedule may then move
freely as long as it does not land on an occupied minute.

The alternative — a per-job "is this off :00?" assertion — goes stale on the
first legitimate schedule change and still never names the pair that actually
collides. That is also why #1677, which took that approach for three named jobs,
is closed as superseded: it would have passed against all three collisions above.

Two guards come with it:
- the cron directory is discoverable (a wrong path would make the check
  vacuously pass);
- every schedule parses as five fields (a malformed one would drop out of the
  intersection silently).

**Verified:** 17 passed. Run against the pre-fix schedules, the collision check
fails and names all three pairs.

body: ## Source A bug found while auditing the org-settings/config-resolution area: `apps/web/src/components/settings/organization-form.tsx`'s org URL/slug field was a live, editable input. ## Why a maintainer wants this When the org-scoped `/api/:org/...` route migration shipped (#3272), `ORGANIZATION_UPDATE` (`apps/api/src/tools/organization/update.ts`) was deliberately changed to reject slug updates, with the comment: "Slug is intentionally NOT updatable: it anchors org URLs (`/api/:org/...`) and renaming would silently invalidate every saved URL." This is also documented as a repo-wide invariant in `CLAUDE.md`'s API Path Convention section ("Org slugs are immutable ... so URLs remain stable"). But the actual Settings → General page never went through that tool — it calls Better Auth's own `organization.update` endpoint directly via `useOrgAuthClient()`, and that endpoint (in the vendored `@decocms/better-auth` package) happily accepts and persists a `slug` change (only checking uniqueness). So any org admin could rename the org's slug from Settings, silently invalidating every bookmarked `/$org/...` link, saved `/api/:org/...` API integration, and webhook built against the old slug — the exact failure the tool-side fix was meant to prevent. ## The fix Made the URL/slug field in `OrganizationForm` read-only (plain text, not a form input), removed `slug` from the form schema and the `Better Auth` update payload, and dropped the now-dead "navigate to new slug on rename" logic. Added an i18n description explaining why (en + pt-br). Net diff: -61/+16, mostly deletions (dead validation, dead navigate-on-rename branch, an unused i18n placeholder key). ## How to verify - Open Settings → General for an org: the URL field now renders the slug as static text, not an editable input. - `rg -n 'slug' apps/web/src/components/settings/organization-form.tsx` — only the two read-only display sites remain (`org.slug` and the query-key cache invalidation). ## Checks run locally - `bun run fmt` — clean - `cd apps/web && bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean - `bunx oxlint` on the 3 changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors Full CI (lint, full typecheck, test suite) validates the rest. --- ## Summary by cubic Make the organization slug on Settings → General read-only to prevent breaking `/api/:org/...` URLs and integrations. Removes slug update paths so the UI matches the invariant that org slugs are immutable. - **Bug Fixes** - Render the org slug as static text with a brief explanation (en, pt-br). - Remove `slug` from the form schema and the update payload sent to `@decocms/better-auth`. - Delete slug validation and navigate-on-rename logic; keep cache invalidation only. Written for commit 6a1ac71b078e4f51ed1c0ad62dcbdf6517287840. Summary will update on new commits.

author: bensaadamine
body:
The photos were reduced to a strip down the right edge — about a fifth of the banner — because the veil went fully opaque until 60% of the width. This widens what you see to roughly 37%, and it does so without putting the title at risk.

Copying `LandingHero` verbatim was the obvious move and it does not survive contact with these images. It ends its veil at 60% (`lg:w-3/5`), which works there because its text column stops short of that and the photo behind it is a white desk. Here the text column runs to 59% and two of the three photos are dark at that point: measured against the real pixels, the title came out at 1.0:1 — invisible, not merely low.

So the veil now holds solid to 40% and fades to 85% instead of stopping dead at 60%. Fading later, rather than staying opaque longer, is what buys both things at once: worst case rises to 6.0:1 while more of the image shows than before. The setting comes from sweeping twenty combinations against the actual photos and keeping the one with the most visible image that still clears 4.5:1 with room to spare — 35%/85% reaches 39.7% visible but only 4.95:1, too close to the floor to trust at an 8px sampling step.

Below `lg` the photo stays hidden. The text spans the full width there, and any veil opaque enough to protect it hides the photo anyway.

author: renesenses
body:
## Bug (forum, Mika — Beoplay A9 MK IV via DLNA)

Lancer un titre TIDAL (FLAC) vers un renderer DLNA strict renvoie
`UPnPError 714 "Illegal MIME-type"` sur `SetAVTransportURI`, et la lecture
échoue sans aucun repli. Le même titre passe en CAST.

**Cause prouvée par le log du testeur** : le Sink du renderer (protocolInfo)
déclare le FLAC sous l'étiquette `audio/x-flac` (et supporte `audio/wav`,
`audio/L16;rate=44100;channels=2`), mais **pas** `audio/flac`. Or Tune annonce
le MIME littéral `audio/flac` dans le DIDL/`SetAVTransportURI`. Le décodeur
strict (B&O / Lyngdorf) rejette l'annonce → 714, alors qu'il sait décoder le
flux.

## Fix — **réactif** (chirurgical, zéro régression latence)

La 1ʳᵉ tentative `SetAVTransportURI` annonce `media.mime_type` **inchangé** —
comportement actuel exact. **Le chemin heureux (Sonos & co) ne fait aucun
`GetProtocolInfo`** : zéro round-trip / zéro latence ajoutée en nominal. La
sonde du Sink et les retries n'ont lieu **que si un 714 survient réellement**.

Sur un vrai 714 : une **seule** sonde `get_protocol_info()`, puis au plus deux
retries :

**(a) Orthographe exacte du Sink** — `advertised_mime_for_sink(desired, sink)`
(fonction pure testée) : si le MIME désiré n'est pas listé tel quel mais qu'un
alias connu l'est (`audio/flac`↔`audio/x-flac`, `audio/mpeg`↔`audio/mp3`,
`audio/wav`↔`audio/x-wav`), on ré-émet avec l'étiquette réellement listée par
le Sink (ex. `audio/x-flac`). C'est ce volet qui résout le cas Beoplay.

**(b) Repli PCM** — `fallback_mime_from_sink(sink)` : si le 714 persiste, on
ré-émet une dernière fois avec un MIME PCM listé par le Sink (préférence
`audio/wav` puis `audio/L16`). Les renderers stricts filtrent sur le MIME
annoncé mais décodent au contenu, donc un libellé accepté laisse passer les
octets FLAC réels.

Sinon → renvoie l'`Err` 714 comme aujourd'hui. **Total : ≤ 1 sonde Sink +
2 retries, et uniquement sur 714.**

## Fichiers

- `tune-core/src/outputs/dlna.rs` :
  - `play_media` : 1ʳᵉ tentative avec MIME inchangé ; boucle réactive (sonde +
    retry exact + retry PCM) déclenchée **seulement** sur 714.
  - `didl_metadata_mime()` : variante de `didl_metadata` acceptant un MIME
    explicite (l'ancienne signature 2-args est conservée pour les tests).
  - Helpers purs `advertised_mime_for_sink`, `fallback_mime_from_sink`,
    `sink_entry_base_mime`.
  - 5 tests unitaires (réécriture x-flac, exact inchangé, alias absent
    inchangé, mpeg→mp3, fallback wav>l16>none).

## Vérification

- `cargo check -p tune-core` : OK.
- `cargo test -p tune-core outputs::dlna::tests` : 25 tests OK.
- Pas de renderer Beoplay réel disponible : validation = unit-test + cargo check.

À porter sur `main` après merge.

body: ## Summary PR Hygiene could say which PRs were *badly kept* but not which ones *mattered*. GitHub knows nothing about priority, so the Jira key the hygiene pass already extracts is used to join each PR to its ticket, and a PR is called out when the ticket is high priority **and** its status says the code is already somewhere it can hold up a release. ```python critical_in_flight(prs, tickets): keyed = prs[prs.jira_key != ""] # no key -> no priority to read merged = keyed.merge(tickets[["key", "priority", "status"]], on jira_key, how="inner") return merged[priority in CRITICAL_PRIORITIES and status in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES] ``` Two judgement calls, both taken from the status/priority names this instance actually uses (64 tickets match today): - `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` = dev env, code review, review, design review, review in staging, ready for production. **"In Progress" is excluded** — that means the code is still being written, not that it is queued behind a review. - `CRITICAL_PRIORITIES` includes `urgent`, `critical` and `blocker` alongside `high`/`highest`, so renaming the top priority in Jira does not silently empty the tab. Rendered as the first tab of PR Hygiene with a matching tile, sorted longest-idle first (the useful order: it is the sitting, not the existence, that costs a release), with the ticket key linking through to Jira. The join uses the unscoped ticket frame on purpose — a PR belongs to the org regardless of which team or person the dashboard is filtered to. An empty result reads as a success message rather than a blank table, and a PR whose key points at a ticket outside the loaded window simply drops out of the join rather than being guessed at. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c17119c8657c4eccbc4a7205d8e37981 Requested by: @avosmod8 ---

author: modiparv
body:
First two surfaces of the product frontend brief — the show-me checkpoint before TODAY / PIPELINE / export-compare / OUTREACH / IC MEMO.

## SCREEN — `/app/screen.html`
- Filter rail → live count → results table. The count is the brief's **three-way honesty split**: matched / failed filters / **could not be measured** — the third always visible, one click to view those companies.
- Live filters (what the store supports today): sector as SIC divisions with readable names, revenue/employees/net-assets bands, region (country + locality), company age, **owner age** (mechanical date arithmetic on public PSC birth month/year), screening mode, outstanding security interests, staleness cutoff, watchlist-only.
- **Phase-2-dependent filters are present but inert** — EBITDA, margin/growth/gearing, ownership class, succession detectors, distress, plausibility — each labelled `not_reached` with the reason on hover. They will enable as the machinery lands; until then they never pretend to run.
- Sortable columns, keyboard navigation (↑/↓/Enter), saved screens and watchlist stars (browser-local storage; no auth by design).

## COMPANY — `/app/company.html`
- Six at-a-glance tiles (revenue, EBITDA, margin, employees, owner age, ownership class) — each traceable or carrying its precise absence state.
- Staleness callout, trajectory matrix with per-period age headers, **succession read stated as register observations** (never conclusions), beneficial owners + officers with approximate ages, full security interests with holders, mechanical peer set (same division, nearest by net assets), fetched-documents history with parse status and register links, coverage panel.

## Data & plumbing
- Exporter gains registered addresses, PSC birth month/year, officer roster, full charges with secured parties (dataset 6.5 MB raw).
- TRACE ported to `/app/trace.html`; landing CTA now points at the screen. Ops viewer untouched.

## Honest-conflict note (per house rules)
EBITDA, margin, growth, gearing, score, ownership class, distress language and plausibility flags do not exist in the store — they are Phase 2. Everywhere the brief asks for them, the UI shows the designed slot with `not_reached` and the reason, never an invented value.

body:
## What's in this release

Phase 2 of the analyzer work: fix the solc coverage gap, add 4 semantic detectors, re-run all 60 TVL projects, triage the new HIGH findings.

### Coverage-gap fix
- Root cause: solc-on-PATH is a version dispatcher (`solc_versions/solc`). Real causes of the silent coverage gap were **not** pragma pins but:
  1. **"Stack too deep"** on large contracts → added a viaIR retry.
  2. **Missing vendored dependency imports** → added a longest-suffix remapper fallback.
- Whole-project compile: **26/60 → 51/60 OK**. Full CLI run: **22/60 → 44/60 projects with findings, 447 total** (was 121).
- 15 native solc binaries added locally (0.5.7..0.8.28); binaries are gitignored (re-downloadable via `binaries.soliditylang.org`).
- 9 projects documented as unanalyzable (version-pin mixes, pre-viaIR stack-too-deep, Vyper-mislabeled .sol, malformed source).

### New semantic detectors (`smart_analyzer/detectors/semantic.py`)
- `value_flow` — balance-delta / fee-on-transfer crediting
- `callback_reentrancy` — token-receiver-hook reentry (0 TVL fires; corpus TPs only)
- `integer_truncation` — divide-before-multiply value loss (0 TVL fires)
- `oracle_taint` — oracle reads feeding value-moving ops

Invariants held throughout: **pytest 21 passed, corpus recall 138/138**.

### Triage
All 21 new-detector HIGHs (ValueFlow 16, OracleTaint 5) plus top pre-existing-detector HIGHs are **DISMISSED** (standard-token atomicity, governance-set Chainlink feeds, permissionless-by-design entry points). No confirmed exploits — an honest null result, consistent with Phase 1. Verdicts in `opencode_artifacts/exploit_pocs/poc_verdicts.md` (Phase 2 section).

### Artifacts
- Canonical ranking now run3: `opencode_artifacts/ranked_findings.md/.json` (447 findings, HIGH 178 / MED 205 / LOW 64, 44 protocols).
- `STATUS.md`, `ROADMAP.md` (Phase 2 DONE), `REPORT.md` updated.

## Notes
- Git identity for the new commit: `Fatima-yo <castiglionemaldonado@gmail.com>` (matches existing repo history).
- The ~250MB solc binaries and Foundry `out/` are intentionally not committed (see `.gitignore`).

author: jzhao234
body:
TLDR: one cancelled turn could permanently disable the disk quota, a huge
run_python response could eat host memory without limit, a wedged bridge
could freeze a whole container's tool calls, routine teardown logged fake
errors, and crashed runs leaked temp files forever. All five fixed.

Problem, one by one:

1. The pool cached the --storage-opt boot probe with a sync.Once. A first
   probe running under an already-cancelled context fails without learning
   anything about the storage driver, but the Once latched that "unsupported"
   answer for the process lifetime — every later container ran with NO
   writable-layer quota.

2. runPython read the bridge's response line with a bare ReadBytes — no size
   cap, unlike bash output (BashOutputCaptureCap). The bridge caps its own
   stdout/stderr/result captures, but `vars` extraction is unbounded, so a
   cell returning a huge variable inflated host RSS with no ceiling.

3. The bridge exec had no WaitDelay, and terminateBridgeLocked's post-kill
   wait on cmd.Wait() was unbounded — while holding c.mu. Anything keeping
   the exec client's pipes open (the exact hazard BashWaitDelay documents)
   blocked every bash, run_python, and file op on that container forever.

4. close()/killContainerNow suppressed "already gone" kill errors by matching
   three phrases podman no longer emits for the common case. Killing an
   exited-but-not-yet-removed container actually says "can only kill running
   containers. <id> is in state exited: container state improper" (verified
   verbatim on podman 5.8.2), so the routine exit-vs-`--rm`-removal race
   logged a spurious "kill unconfirmed" error every time it happened.

5. The bridge-script and seccomp temp files written into BridgeDir are only
   removed on the graceful close path, so every crash leaked them into the
   directory permanently — there was no sweep, unlike containers, which
   PruneOrphanedContainers reclaims at boot.

Fix:

1. ProbeStorageOptSupport now reports (supported, conclusive); a probe cut
   short by its context is inconclusive. The pool memoizes only conclusive
   determinations (mutex + done flag instead of the Once): an inconclusive
   probe safely omits the layer quota for that one container and the next
   creation re-probes.

2. The response line is read through readCappedLine, which stores at most
   bridgeResponseCaptureCap (= BashOutputCaptureCap) bytes and drains-but-
   counts the rest to the delimiter — cappedBuffer's store-then-discard
   semantics applied to the response stream. Overflow fails the call with an
   explicit truncation error; because the drain leaves the stream framed, the
   session is kept (no reset, no poison), mirroring bash truncation being
   non-fatal to the sandbox.

3. The bridge exec now carries WaitDelay = BashWaitDelay, and the post-kill
   wait is bounded by bridgeReapTimeout (5s). Past the bound the bridge state
   is cleared anyway and the abandoned Wait finishes on its own once the
   WaitDelay force-closes the pipes.

4. The suppression lists are unified into containerAlreadyGone, which also
   matches the state error — but only for the dead states (exited/stopped).
   A paused container is frozen, not gone, and keeps counting as unconfirmed.
   killContainerNow already treated "not running" as cleanup-confirmed; the
   new marker is the same condition in podman's current wording, so exited
   now correctly confirms #796 cleanup there too.

5. PruneOrphanedBridgeFiles sweeps BridgeDir at boot (wired next to the pool
   build in buildSandboxPool), matching only the two CreateTemp patterns —
   now shared constants so the sweep and the writers cannot drift — and only
   regular files older than 1h, so a start still in flight here or in a
   sibling instance sharing the directory is never raced. Deleting a LIVE
   container's script is harmless regardless: the bind mount pins the inode.

Not touched: close()'s stats-drain bound (already landed in #951) and the
host-executor's parallel bridge paths (test-only fixture, not a boundary).

Tests: each fix carries a regression test that was mutation-checked — the
Once-style latch, reverting to the unbounded ReadBytes, dropping the reap
bound and the WaitDelay, dropping the kill-state markers, and dropping the
sweep's age bound were each reintroduced and caught. The reap-bound test
needed a readiness handshake on stderr: signalling the fixture before its
grandchild exists kills the shell too early to reproduce the hang. Package
suite is race-detector clean; the 23 podman-gated integration tests fail
on this host for want of the sandbox test image — identically at the base
commit, verified by stash.



**Testing caveat:** the 23 podman-gated sandbox integration tests fail identically on this host and on `dev` (`981fc98`) — no sandbox image available here, verified by running the suite on both trees. Unit coverage is new and green.

author: hahwul
body:
`^V` cycles WS → HTTP/1.1 → HTTP/2 on a Repeater tab holding a handshake, and h1 ⇄ h2 on
every other non-gRPC tab. Nothing drew it. The key was discoverable from the Help overlay
and from the footer of one pane in one mode, so a tab that could be asked three different
questions looked like a tab that could be asked one — the same shape as the refusal the
override itself just removed.

THE CHIP. ` ^V:WS ` / ` ^V:h1 ` / ` ^V:h2 ` on the TARGET band, naming the transport `^R`
will dial. It hit-tests as a button (`chrome_hit` → `:transport`) and cycles on click, like
every other border chip.

WHY THE BAND, NOT THE REQUEST BORDER. That border was the first try and it does not fit:
at 100 columns the request column is 49 wide, and ` ^R:SEND `, ` ^L:CL `, ` ^U:PRETTY ` and
the mode chip already fill it to within three cells of the card title. A fifth badge pushes
the chain past `min_x`, and the chain drops its LEFTMOST first — the ` ↵:NOR ` chip, which
is the one that reports whether typing will edit or navigate. The TARGET band is full
width and already holds the rest of "how do we connect": the URL and the SNI override.

THE DRESS. `Frame.state_badge` — a right-chained badge that reports STATE rather than
on/off, so it carries its own colours instead of `toggle_badge`'s lit/muted pair. For a
chip whose NAME is the state there is no "off", and muted grey reads as a disabled control.
Two dresses: the resting fill at rest, and the `^R:SEND` gold when the operator has
overridden auto-detection. A handshake tab that will NOT speak WebSocket is the one thing
on that band worth interrupting a glance for. No functional colour is spent — the palette
keeps green/yellow/red for HTTP status, and this uses the existing accent/gold vocabulary,
so all 28 themes follow for free.

THE TITLE. The request card said "HANDSHAKE (h1)" and "REQUEST (h2)" because nothing else
carried the transport. Now something does, so the title says only what the card IS in its
pane, and the transport is named once. That is not just de-duplication: the badge chain
measures its left stop FROM the title, and those five columns were exactly what pushed an
h2 tab's own ` ↵:NOR ` chip off a 100-column terminal. An overridden handshake tab is
titled REQUEST, not HANDSHAKE — `^R` sends an ordinary request and reads a response,
MESSAGES is gone, the split is one card again. The chip carries the other half by naming
both ends (` ^V:WS→h1 `), so the tab is still not mistakable for a plain one, which is what
the old title was for. `→` measures one column; the specs pin the chip's last live cell and
the dead one after it, because the badge geometry counts characters, not display width.

THE OVERLAP. The SNI marker placed itself at `right - " SNI ".size - 1` and was drawn
AFTER the mode chip — which is inside the mode chip's cells. Setting an SNI override
painted over the right five columns of ` ↵:NOR ` and left a truncated chip behind. Making
room for the transport chip meant chaining that band's chrome (mode → SNI → ^V) through one
pure geometry both the draw and `chrome_hit` read, so this went with it.

VERIFICATION. `spec/tui/repeater_transport_chip_spec.cr`: the three-state cycle, the
hit-test in both shapes, both dresses asserted against `bg_at`, the gRPC tab that draws no
chip because `^V` refuses there, the SNI/mode/transport cells staying disjoint, and the
request border keeping its own badges in h1 and h2 alike. TUI suite green; the full suite's
only failures are the eight that need port 8070 free.

author: shawnwelsh
body:
## Summary

- **Tidy** (row 3, page 2) sweeps a cohort of sessions off the deck — Consoles, Windows, or All — from a timed picker. Swept sessions **keep running** and stay tracked, so the 30s re-scan can't drag them back; they return at the **end of the row** the moment you type into one. Nothing is ever ended.
- **Reboot works.** It previously killed the deck for good. The bridge used to spawn a detached restarter just before exiting — that restarter had to outlive its dying parent and repeatedly didn't (a plain detached spawn, then WMI `Win32_Process.Create`), leaving the deck dead with no way back but a manual `Start-ScheduledTask`.
- `run-bridge-hidden.vbs` now **supervises**: it waits on the bridge and relaunches on any exit, so Reboot is simply `process.exit(0)` and nothing has to survive it. **Crashes self-heal for free.** Reboot also moves to page 3.
- A confirmed reboot **takes over all 15 keys with REBOOTING** before teardown starts. The frame ships first and the plugin holds the last frame it received, so it stays up for the whole outage instead of leaving a normal-looking deck that has silently stopped responding. It self-clears if the restart never took.

### Root cause, for the record

The old launcher ended in `sh.Run "...", 0, False` — *don't wait*. That single `False` orphaned the node tree, made the task "complete" in seconds, and left nothing watching to restart anything. Three tempting explanations were investigated and **disproven**: a Task Scheduler job-object kill, `Win32_Process.Create`'s ~2048-char limit (WMI accepted 1642 chars, rv=0), and EDR blocking `-EncodedCommand` (a direct encoded spawn ran fine). The real lesson is architectural: never restart a service by spawning something that must outlive the dying parent — supervise from outside.

## Files Changed

**Deck behaviour** — `layers.ts` (Tidy key, cohort picker, REBOOTING screen, page 3), `controller.ts` (picker routing, page cycle, deferred reboot), `registry.ts` (`hidden` flag, `sweep()`, `wake()`, pager math), `http/hooks.ts` (wake on `UserPromptSubmit`)
**Reboot/infra** — `scripts/run-bridge-hidden.vbs` (supervisor loop with backoff + crash-loop cap), `index.ts` (supervised exit path), `config.ts` (`supervised`, `canReboot()`)
**Rendering** — `render/tile.ts` (bin icon), `shared/protocol.ts` (icon union)
**Tests** — `sweep.test.ts` (new), `registry.test.ts`, `reboot.test.ts`

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm test -w @conn/bridge` — **323 passing**, 23 files
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean on `packages/shared` and `packages/bridge`
- [x] VBS syntax + loop + give-up logic exercised against the real file before deploy
- [x] `CONN_SUPERVISED` verified to propagate through `cmd -> npm -> node` with no trailing-space corruption
- [x] **Live:** bridge killed outright, returned unaided in 5.5s with all 5 sessions re-adopted
- [x] **Live:** deck's Reboot key confirmed end-to-end on hardware
- [x] Icons checked as rendered PNGs at 144px and at the deck's real 72px downscale

author: jzhao234
body:
TLDR: the web tier now really binds 127.0.0.1:3000 (the docs always said it
did), redirect targets and the Secure-cookie decision come from the
configured public origin instead of client-supplied x-forwarded-* headers, a
dead backend shows "can't reach the chat server" instead of reload-looping
between /chat and /login, throttled logins say so instead of claiming the
server is down, and the vendor-named login prop no longer leaks into
white-label RSC payloads.

Problem:
- deploy/fleet-web.service runs `npm run start` -> `next start`, which
  defaults to 0.0.0.0, while the Caddyfile, the unit header, and bootstrap
  all promise 127.0.0.1:3000. On a box without firewalld, :3000 is directly
  reachable past Caddy — and the web tier trusts x-forwarded-proto/host, so
  a direct plain-http login mints a session cookie without Secure and
  redirects can be steered to an attacker-chosen host.
- getRedirectUrl/isSecureRequest trusted x-forwarded-* unconditionally even
  though every deploy has a canonical origin (NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN,
  written by bootstrap).
- The chat bootstrap treated ANY failed /api/session or /api/conversations
  response as session expiry. A down backend answers 502 through the proxy
  routes while the cookie is still valid, so /chat redirected to /login,
  the middleware bounced straight back to /chat, and the two pages reloaded
  in a loop.
- The login route folded the verify endpoint's 429 (rate limit, Retry-After
  60) into the generic "server isn't reachable" bucket.
- elcanoLoginEnabled — a vendor name — was serialized into the RSC payload
  of every white-label login page even when the feature is off.

Fix:
- web/package.json start script passes -H ${FLEET_WEB_HOST:-127.0.0.1};
  FLEET_WEB_HOST in fleet-web.env overrides it for TLS terminated on
  another host (documented in the unit header + bootstrap's no-domain
  hint). Unit changes are comment-only, so update.sh's functional-diff
  check stays quiet; the behavior change ships with the web rebuild.
- getRedirectUrl/isSecureRequest use NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN when it is
  set and parseable, falling back to the previous header behavior when it
  is not (local dev over plain http keeps working).
- New classifyBootstrapFailure distinguishes 401/403 (redirect to /login)
  from everything else; chat-experience shows a full-page "Can't reach the
  chat server" retry card on cold boot and keeps the cached transcript on
  warm revalidation. Settings pages already gated on 401 and are untouched.
- /api/auth/login maps upstream 429 to /login?e=throttled and the card
  renders "Too many sign-in attempts. Try again in a minute." — matching
  the backend's Retry-After: 60.
- elcanoLoginEnabled renamed to magicLinkLoginEnabled everywhere (it gates
  the external magic-link handoff, not the password form). No behavior
  change.

Tests:
- web: auth.test.ts pins canonical-origin-over-headers and all fallbacks
  (2 cases fail on the old code); bootstrapFailure.test.ts pins the
  401/403-vs-502/503/504 contract; api/auth/login/route.test.ts pins the
  429->throttled mapping (fails on the old code) plus server/invalid/CSRF;
  login-card.test.tsx renders the throttle + unreachable copy and carries
  the prop rename. Full suite: 85 files / 866 tests green; tsc --noEmit
  and eslint clean.
- go: build ./... and vet -tags fleet_host_executor ./... clean;
  admincli/boxdoctor/httpapi tests pass. Podman-gated sandbox integration
  tests not run (no podman here).



**Operator note:** an operator fronting the box with their own proxy must now set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and rebuild the web app, since redirects prefer the configured canonical origin over `x-forwarded-*`. `bootstrap.sh`'s hint covers the another-host case; the same-box custom-proxy flow is worth calling out in release notes.

**Follow-up candidates (not in scope):** `web/src/app/lib/oidc.ts` (redirect_uri) and `web/src/app/lib/csrf.ts` (expected host) still derive from `x-forwarded-*`. Not exploitable once the tier is loopback-bound, but now inconsistent with `auth.ts`.

author: yoichi-kaneko
body:
## 背景

YAMAPの山行計画ページが Next.js 構成へ作り替えられ、`fetch_plan.ts` が依存していたクラス名（`Plan__Table` / `Plan__ActivityRecord` / `CheckPoints` など）がDOMから消滅していました。その結果、スキルの出力がセクション見出しだけの空応答になっていました。

```
概要
--------
計画データ
--------
移動計画
```

ページ取得（Playwright）自体は成功しており、失敗していたのは cheerio によるセレクタ抽出です。現在のクラス名はハッシュ化された CSS Modules 形式のため、クラス名ベースの抽出は今後も壊れ続けます。

## 対応

DOMのスクレイピングを廃止し、ページに埋め込まれた `__NEXT_DATA__`（`props.pageProps.plan`）の計画データを正として読み取る方式へ移行しました。

- **通過時刻**: `arrivalTimeInSeconds` はペース倍率100%の素の値のため、`round(区間秒 ÷ (paceMultiplier/100) ÷ 60)` で区間ごとに分へ丸めて累積（画面表示と一致する計算）。近似値である `timeMultiplier` は使用しない
- **距離・標高差**: YAMAPの表示に合わせて切り捨て（距離は小数第1位、標高は整数）
- **ラベル**: コース定数・ペース倍率の判定閾値をYAMAP側の実装に合わせて移植（`≤11 やさしい / ≤24 ふつう / それ以上 きつい`、`≤70 ゆっくり / ≤90 ややゆっくり / ≤109 標準 / ≤129 やや速い / それ以上 速い`）
- **待機条件**: データが初期HTMLに含まれるため `networkidle` → `domcontentloaded` に変更（高速化・安定化）
- **ブラウザのクローズ**: `try/finally` 化し、抽出失敗時のリークを防止
- **エラー処理**: `__NEXT_DATA__` 欠落・JSON解析失敗・計画データ不在（非公開／削除）をそれぞれ明示的なメッセージで通知
- **概要に計画タイトルを追加**: 各モードが「山名・山域を取得」用途で使うため
- **日出・日入は取得対象外**: JSONに含まれず、他モードからの参照も無いため今回のタイミングで収集対象から除外（天気系は `get_openweather_forecast` が担当）

装備品・食料など新たに取得可能となった項目は、コスト面を考慮して従来どおり対象外としています。

## 検証

実際の計画ページで実行し、**画面表示と全項目が一致**することを確認しました。

- タイム 26時間56分（表示 26:56）／距離 42.4km／のぼり 4887m／くだり 5129m／コース定数 118（きつい）／ペース倍率 110%（やや速い）
- 全51チェックポイントの通過時刻が表示と完全一致（1日目 8時間45分 / 2日目 10時間42分 / 3日目 7時間29分）
- 宿泊地（`stayType: sleep`）も `（宿泊地）` として正しく出力
- `/printing` 付きURL、不正URL（エラー）、存在しないコード（エラー）の3ケースも期待どおりの挙動
- `tsc --strict` 型チェック通過、`pnpm test` 41件パス

## ドキュメント更新

| ファイル | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/fetch_yamap_plan/SKILL.md` | 概要を「レンダリング済みHTMLから抽出」→「埋め込みJSONから抽出」に更新。抽出項目を実出力に合わせて具体化、注意事項の「CSSクラス名の変更」→「`__NEXT_DATA__` の構造変更」、日出・日入が対象外である旨を追記 |
| `README.md` | スキル実行時の注意・YAMAPサービス表・ディレクトリ構成の「スクレイピング」表記を実態に合わせて修正 |
| `.claude/coding_agent.md` | `src/yamap/` の説明と `setup:browsers` のコメントを更新 |

  * 計画概要、日別の行程、移動計画を含む詳細なレポートを表示します。

author: tsadoq
body:
Closes the five-member artifact chain by shipping the beat behind `roadmap.md` — the one member the substrate named but nothing wrote.

The beat reads `spec.md`'s `REQ` ids and writes a roadmap of `ITEM` rows, each scored with Intercom's RICE and paired with a Shape Up **appetite** that is never an input to the score. Sequence is derived rather than sorted by score, and dates, quarters and sprints are banned throughout.

## What ships

| Path | |
|---|---|
| `skills/product-roadmap/SKILL.md` | Three-condition refusal gate on its upstream, plus re-run behaviour |
| `skills/product-roadmap/references/rice-template.md` | The member's shape: two tables, RICE units, appetite |
| `skills/product-roadmap/references/product-roadmap-principles.md` | Five red-flag clusters `product-review` reaches with no edit |
| `skills/product-artifacts/references/artifact-family.md` | `roadmap.md`'s sections → `## Scored items`, `## Sequence`, `## Risks` |
| `tests/guarantees.py` | `listing_total_chars` 2000 → 2666 |
| `pyproject.toml` | One `testpaths` entry |

## Notes for review

- **`## Sequence` is a strict prefix of the `## Sequencing` it supersedes**, so a pinned-order assertion alone would pass against a document that never dropped the placeholder. The contract test pins supersession as well as order. Any later beat emitting this section inherits the collision.
- **The budget ceiling moves by policy, not correction.** Only the share term of the derivation changes — a quarter to a third — on the ground that a plugin claiming a third of a shared listing is defensible where a half is not. No per-plugin share is documented anywhere, so the term is this repo's own convention. Floored, not rounded: `200,000 × 0.01 × 4 / 3 = 2,666.67`.
- **Three comment corrections rode along in `guarantees.py`**: the overflow mechanism drops *descriptions of least-invoked* skills rather than whole entries; the four-chars-per-token figure is relabelled as this file's approximation; and a `v2.1.105` citation came out, the CHANGELOG carrying no matching entry.
- **WSJF, MoSCoW and Kano ship cited** as alternatives. ICE is dropped — a documented search found no first-party source.
- `.claude/settings.json` carries an accumulated local-dev allowlist. Say the word and I'll split it out.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

1. The rubric constants in the new contract test are the **fifth cross-module copy** of one block. Two implementers verified this as material and both correctly declined to fix it, since extraction needs a shared harness under repo-level `tests/`.
2. `test_description_budget.py` still states the wrong overflow mechanism in its preamble and failure message; `test_product_review_contract.py` still says "One rubric ships today" when five do. Assertions correct in both, only the prose is stale.

## Verification

`pytest` 303 passed / 2 skipped (304/1 with `tiktoken`), `ruff check lib skills` clean, `mypy --strict` clean. Every task was built test-first — red observed before green — and each diff audited against its planned target files.

body:
> *"1 swim(s) have a place that disagrees with the points awarded."*

That told a submitter there was a problem and **nothing about where it was** — leaving them to
guess which of 55 events to open in Meet Maestro.

The auditor already knew. `auditPlacePoints` returns the event number, description, swimmer,
team, place, points awarded, and the points that place *should* pay. All of it was going into
`evidence`, which nothing renders — which is the same as not having it.

Findings now carry an optional `items` list that the front end renders, so the same warning
reads:

> **1 swim(s) have a place that disagrees with the points awarded.**
> Usually a disqualification or an exhibition swim that was never reconciled into the placings…
> - Event 38 · Girls 11-12 50m Backstroke — Carroll, Harper G (GG) placed 3rd but scored 0, where 3rd pays 1

**Generic rather than special-cased.** Two other findings had the same "named in the title,
useless in the body" shape and now use it too: an unknown team code, and a team that scored
zero, both list which.

Capped at 12 lines with "…and N more", so a badly-reconciled meet cannot bury the rest of the
page.

Against the real `2026-07-13 GG v WYCC` file — the meet from the report — through the running
stack and in the browser. 85 app-tier tests, archive replay green.

author: mikeneaton
body:
Gap #1 of the three the owner's gem walkthrough exposed. **Workshop-managed** — the control is a toggle on the react layer.

## The problem

> *"I want the number update to follow that same timing."*

It couldn't. A badge's digits come from React state, so they snap to the new value the instant the reducer commits. The plate could pop, but the number had already changed — the pop **decorated** a number rather than **delivering** it.

## Three decisions

**A hold is a DELTA, not an absolute.** *"Show two less than you currently are"*, not *"show 4"*. An absolute goes stale the moment anything else touches the unit — a second buff, a trade, an unrelated re-render — and a stale absolute is a badge showing a number that was never true. A delta stays correct under all of them.

**The cue holds, the def releases.** Only the cue knows the number (it reads the delta off the buff event); only the author knows the moment. So the hold is automatic, and delivering it is a **"Carries the number"** toggle on a react layer — released at that layer's peak, *per recipient*, so a cascade delivers each unit's number in turn rather than all of them on the first pop.

**An unclaimed hold must not be permanent.** Every def authored before this exists — and every def that doesn't opt in — would otherwise leave a badge wrong forever. So holds carry a TTL and read as absent once expired, and `destroy()` delivers anything still owed when an effect is cut short.

It fails **open**. A stat badge is load-bearing information, and the rule this codebase keeps re-learning is that a silent wrong answer costs more than a loud absence.

## Render path

`Card` subscribes **per-uid** via a primitive snapshot (mirroring the existing `getSpellBuffSeq` pattern), so a card with nothing held reads 0 and never re-renders when some other card is gemmed. The withheld value drives the digits **and** the up/down colouring, so a badge is never internally inconsistent.

## Known limits, shipped deliberately

- A **stack** (two Rubies on one body) is held as one total and delivered whole by the first gem — the badge steps once, not twice. Splitting needs a partial release, which needs the def to know the per-gem amount.
- **Combat only.** The shop path needs the delta on `RubyLandedFx`, a sim-side field (Kevin's ownership).

## Verification

18 unit tests over the store — including the TTL fail-open, that a fresh hold after expiry doesn't inherit the dead delta, and that the snapshot is primitive so `useSyncExternalStore` can't loop. `rubiedLandsIn` now carries the summed delta with a test pinning it; losing it would silently make every hold a no-op.

Gate: `typecheck` (pkgs + web) ✅ · `lint` 0 errors ✅ · 3837 tests ✅ · `build:web` ✅

## Next

Gaps #2 (per-layer traversal, so gems can volley while badges cascade) and #3 (rubies routed through bindings, so avenge and battlecry can differ) — both in flight.

author: jzhao234
body:
TLDR: three bundle-manifest interpolation defects. An env-file override of a
${VAR:-default} MCP env/header key was silently ignored on the standalone
paths — it now wins. A correctly escaped $${ literal in a connector value was
expanded anyway — it now survives. And ${FLEET_WORKSPACE:-...} / :? spellings
slipped past the reserved-token guard — they now fail the load with an error
naming the contract.

Problem: the manifest interpolates at bundle load, which runs BEFORE
config.Load applies the .env file (the load must run first so EnvVarNames can
seed the .env allowlist). Three consequences for connector values:

- ${VAR:-default} baked its default into the runtime manifest before the .env
  file existed in the process env, and EnvVarNames — scanning the
  post-interpolation values, where the token no longer exists — never
  registered VAR, so the env-file value was dropped by the allowlist too. The
  operator's override lost to the literal with no signal anywhere (the
  fleet#706 residual; docs/MCP-BUNDLE-ENV.md carried it as a known follow-up,
  and elcano-config#32 is blocked on it).
- The $${ escape was consumed by the load pass, whose "${...}" output the
  spawn-time pass then expanded — blanking the author's escaped literal.
- The reserved-token guard matched only the bare ${FLEET_WORKSPACE} spelling,
  so a :- form resolved from the process env (an exported FLEET_WORKSPACE
  could hijack it) or baked its default, silently defeating the launch-time
  workspace substitution; a :? form told the operator to export the var — the
  opposite of the contract.

Fix: chose "make the override apply" over "fail loudly" — the deferred-bare-
token design already names catalog-build time (after the .env load) as the
correct resolution point for connector values, so extending it to the :-/:?
forms removes the silence AND gives operators the env-or-default semantics
the syntax promises, where failing loudly would have left the .env file a
second-class home for connector config. Load now re-sources mcp_servers
env/headers and http_tools headers from the raw manifest (the load pass still
validates them: an unset ${VAR:?...} or a non-bare reserved token fails the
load), and the spawn-time pass handles the full form set — $${ escape,
${VAR}, ${VAR:-default}, ${VAR:?msg}, reserved tokens preserved verbatim — as
the single substituting pass for those fields. EnvVarNames extracts names
with the op-aware sourceEnvRefs so defaulted refs survive the .env allowlist,
and excludes the reserved tokens, which are not process-env vars. expandExpr
rejects every colon-suffixed reserved-token spelling. Deliberately unchanged:
${VAR:?...} still validates at load against the pre-.env env, and non-map
fields (server urls, branding, providers) still resolve at load — both noted
in docs/MCP-BUNDLE-ENV.md, which is updated to match.

Issue #902 (validate-config accepts manifests that fleet serve rejects): the
premise does not hold at HEAD — validate-config has always loaded through
clientconfig.Load, whose strict decode is the same one serve boots through,
and an unknown branding field fails both with the identical '[line:col]
unknown field' error (verified empirically on this tree; at the incident's
ebd63f0 the branding.logo field did not exist yet, so the green validate must
have come from a newer binary than the serve that crash-looped — version
skew, not a decode gap). TestCheckManifestUnknownFieldFailsLikeBoot now pins
the invariant end to end. This resolves issue #902; leaving the close to a
human on the PR.

author: snissn
body:
## Objective

Wire the existing vector-partition coordinator and shard service into a production-owned topology constructor without importing the M8 harness.

Closes #4014

## Design

- Validate live catalog placement and leader hints, concrete address-family-compatible owner endpoints, complete member-specific routing for locally served groups, endpoint uniqueness, normalized shard-service limits, the router source, and replicated lifecycle authority before serving.
- Start shard listeners only for declared partition owners; coordinator-only nodes remain supported.
- Reuse a bounded TCP connection pool per endpoint sized to configured shard concurrency, reconnect once after a transport loss, and route bounded leader retries to known node endpoints.
- Bound accepted shard connections separately from each dispatcher pool, derive distinct request/response wire-frame caps from the logical shard limits, join cancellation watchers before pooling sockets, and own listener, connection, dispatcher, and coordinator shutdown with partial-construction rollback in both production and M8 topologies.
- Expose a copied readiness/status snapshot.
- Preserve the existing request, response, fanout, deadline, cancellation, read-proof, generation-pin, and failure contracts.

## Boundaries

- No user-facing vector API; #4016 owns that layer.
- No rebuild/invalidation orchestration; #4017 owns that layer.
- No operations bundle or default enablement; #4018 owns that layer.
- No new storage format, Raft architecture, or ANN algorithm.

## Validation

- `GOWORK=off go test ./TreeDB/nativewire -count=1`
- `GOWORK=off go test ./TreeDB/nativewire -run 'TestVectorPartitionProductionTopology|TestVectorPartitionProductionEndpointMatchesListener' -count=100 -timeout=120s`
- `GOWORK=off go test -race ./TreeDB/nativewire -run 'TestVectorPartitionProductionTopology|TestVectorPartitionProductionEndpointMatchesListener' -count=10 -timeout=180s`
- `GOWORK=off go test ./TreeDB/nativewire -run 'TestVectorPartitionShardSearchTCPDerivesSeparateFrameBoundsV1|TestVectorPartitionShardSearchTCPServerBoundsRequestAndFailedResponseFramesV1|TestVectorPartitionProductionEndpointMatchesListenerAddressFamilyV1' -count=100`
- focused transport/topology selector with `-race -count=10`
- `GOWORK=off go vet ./TreeDB/nativewire`
- Windows and Darwin `go test -c` cross-compiles
- `GOWORK=off go test ./cmd/... -count=1` (at `8a9408c9b` before the final endpoint-validation patch)
- `git diff --check`

Coverage includes two-group generation-pinned TCP search, local and remote owners, member/leader-hint/address-family/hostless endpoint validation, truthful shared-listener rejection, connection reuse and reconnect, multi-pool accepted-connection admission, M8 dispatcher ownership, cancellation-watcher joining, request/response frame-limit alignment and failed writes, cancellation/deadline/disconnect behavior, incomplete topology refusal, partial-start rollback, shutdown, restart, and closed-path failure without partial neighbors. Build-file selection covers the fallback socket implementation on JS, Plan 9, and WASI.

## Performance

The existing 10k M8 production-topology test was run three times on merged main and this candidate with identical inputs:

| revision | runs | median | max RSS |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| merged main | 48.09s, 47.83s, 49.81s | 48.09s | 379,776 KiB |
| candidate | 48.97s, 49.23s, 48.85s | 48.97s | 376,576 KiB |

The +1.8% median wall delta is inside the observed run spread; peak RSS is 0.8% lower. No material regression is evidenced. The deterministic transport tests separately prove one accepted connection for repeated requests and successful reconnect after an idle close.

After the review-driven bounded-pool correction, the same current-head 10k test passed three consecutive runs in 146.883s total (48.96s/run) with 381,056 KiB peak RSS, materially unchanged from the candidate evidence above. Deterministic coverage also proves parallel leases up to the configured endpoint limit and context cancellation while saturated.

## 问题

`ProcessSheetServiceImplTest#pinnedBomPackagingRequirementsScaleInNativeUnits` 反射调用 `finishedOutputQuantity(ProcessSheetRowRequest)`，而该方法在 **#1898（2026-07-27「preserve Workflow BOM SKU and family reporting」）** 就被多产出的 `finishedBomOutputs` 取代并删除（返回 `(productTypeId, quantity, unit)` 三元组以支持一次报 N 个成品）。

于是这条抛 `IllegalState: Method not found`，**从 7-27 起一直红**。

## 改动

断言意图逐字不变：成品产出数量按**原生单位**取值（10 box 就是 10，不做质量折算）。改为解析 `finishedBomOutputs` 的唯一一条产出，并顺带钉住 `unit` 与 `productTypeId` —— 比原来只断言一个数字更能说明「单产出报工解析成什么」。

## ⚠️ 更值得关注的：为什么能红 8 天

CI 的 `java-build-test` 只有两步：

```yaml
- name: JPA repository query startup gate
  run: mvn -B test -Dtest='*RepositoryQueryValidationTest'

- name: Package exact-commit deploy artifact
  run: mvn -B package -Dmaven.test.skip=true    # 无测试选择器时
```

**Java 单测套件在 CI 里从来不整体跑。** web-admin 侧有全量 vitest 闸（332 files / 2474 tests，每次 push 和 PR 都跑），Java 侧没有对等的闸 —— 所以任何 Java 测试烂掉都不会被发现，除非有人恰好手工跑到。

本 PR 只修那条断言；要不要给 Java 加全量测试闸是另一个决定（正在实测 main 上全量 Java 测试的健康度，先知道基线有多少红，再决定闸怎么加 —— 直接加闸可能会把一堆既有红暴露成"挡所有人的红"）。

author: inth3shadows
body:
Closes #204. Deferred out of #202 on purpose — moving the measurement stack in the same commit as the codec leaves no clean before/after. This is that change, with the numbers.

## The problem

`capture._find_record_list` kept the strict identical-keyset rule after #202 widened what the tabularizer folds. A payload where two thirds of the rows carry `line` bucketed as `compact-json` with **no record list**, while the codec folded it. Everything reading that function — `classify_shape`'s buckets, `measure`/`report` coverage, `policy_gen`'s auto drop-path generation, `dropeval`, `fluency.questions` — skipped exactly the traffic union-schema tabularize was built for.

`transforms.is_tabularizable` is now the single canonical "would the codec fold this" rule, and capture uses it.

## Measured

Synthetic runecho-shaped payloads (3 × 40 symbols): shape bucket `compact-json` → **`array-of-records` 3/3**, `extract_records` **0/3 → 3/3**, drop-path **0/3 → 3/3**.

End to end, `terse policy generate` over a runecho-shaped corpus now emits `↳ drop-candidate symbols[].body (~96% of tokens, 100% unique)` where it previously emitted nothing — the same shape the regression test carries, so it is auditable from the branch.

On the **tracked bench corpus, exactly one payload moves**: `gh_issues`, from no-record-list to `array-of-records`. That is the same payload, and the same nested non-uniform array, that #202 moved 32.7% → 38.8%. The other eight payloads' generated questions are byte-identical.

## The identical-key-set guarantee is gone, and that was the real work

`extract_records` used to promise callers could index every record by `records[0].keys()`. Three consumers relied on it and would now `KeyError` on a record missing a key: `fluency`'s column pickers, `gen_questions`, and `dropeval`. They take the intersection now, via the `_intersection_cols` helper the nested-record path **already had**, rather than a second copy. That is also the semantically right answer: a column some records lack cannot be the subject of *"for the record whose id is X, what is Y?"*. `probes` needed no change — it walks `rec.items()` and already counts per-field presence.

## What review caught

Three of the four findings were in work this PR added:

1. **The consumer fix was pinned by nothing.** Reverting both call sites to `list(records[0].keys())` failed **zero** tests — while genuinely raising `KeyError: 'extra'` from `gen_questions` and dropeval on a nested non-uniform payload. Three tests added; two fail under that revert.
2. **The invariant test was a tautology.** `test_shape_classifier_and_codec_agree_on_every_bench_payload` compared `is_tabularizable` against itself and never called `compress_structure`. It passed with the classifier fully reverted to the strict rule, *and* passed with the codec's union branch disabled while the classifier stayed correct — i.e. green through exactly the regression it is named for. The oracle is now the codec's real output (compress, then look for a `__terse_table__`), verified to fail under that second mutation. Scoped at `compress_structure` rather than the wire, since `compress_with`'s emit-only-if-smaller can ship plain minify for a payload that did tabularize.
3. **"Nothing that predates #204 changes" was false.** `_intersection_cols`' original caller, `_nested_record_group` (#71), by construction only ever sees non-uniform child lists — exactly where sorted and first-seen differ — so its id/target column choice *does* move: a structure payload with `sym` before `path` now enumerates `sym` where it enumerated `path`. Same information, different question. The claim holds only for uniform lists, which is what keeps the bench corpus at one changed payload. Corrected in the docstring and CHANGELOG.
4. **Stale comments**, in a PR whose premise is that a stale comment hid a bug: `_nested_record_group` still called `extract_records` the "STRICT uniform" extractor and pointed at a rationale this PR deleted; `test_non_uniform_dict_list_is_not_array_of_records` attributed its exclusion to uniformity when the density gate is what actually excludes it. Both corrected, and that test now also asserts the positive case.

Also replaced the CHANGELOG's `1,949 → 861 tok` figure — measured on a throwaway synthetic not present in the branch, so unauditable — with the `policy generate` result above.

Review separately fuzzed ~7,000 non-uniform/sparse/shuffled-key payloads across 11 entry points and found **no missed consumer**: 0 exceptions on this branch, 0 on main.

1217 passed, ruff + mypy clean.

author: jayminwest
body:
Pinned ref moves from `v0.13.1` to `v0.13.2`.

Every file in this diff is derived — `bun run sync:upstream` wrote all of it from warren at `v0.13.2`. Review the changelog delta and the docs diff, not the mechanics.

The nightly sync run https://github.com/jayminwest/warren-site/actions/runs/30890644917 built this branch and passed the full gate suite, but could not open the PR (Actions lacked PR-create permission at the time — now enabled). Opened manually; see #6.

Upstream compare: https://github.com/jayminwest/warren/compare/v0.13.1...v0.13.2

<details><summary>warren v0.13.2 release notes</summary>

### Security

- **Agent output can no longer terminalize its own run** — stream
  events now carry a parse-boundary provenance tag (`origin`,
  `src/core/wire.ts`). The K8s pod-log parser classifies an
  unattributed NDJSON line as `origin: "agent"` and downgrades its
  self-declared `stream: "system"` to `"stdout"`, and terminal
  detection refuses agent-authored events outright — so a crafted
  `{"kind":"state_change","stream":"system","payload":{"type":"agent_end"}}`
  line printed at the pod log no longer reaps the run as `succeeded`.
  Warren's own in-pod emitter stamps the marker, so legitimate
  claude-code `result` / pi `agent_end` envelopes are unaffected
  (warren-6646).
- **Route params can no longer traverse out of a directory**
  (warren-7c1e). `matchRoute` percent-decodes every `:param`, but the
  `([^/]+)` capture constrains only the raw pathname and `URL.pathname`
  preserves `%2F` — so `POST /runs/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpwn/salvage` decoded
  to `../../etc/pwn`, which the salvage intake joined straight onto the
  salvage directory. Any bearer holding `dispatch` could write up to
  32 MiB of its own bytes to an arbitrary path. The router now refuses a
  param that decodes to a path separator or a NUL, and a new
  `salvageBundlePath` resolver re-checks containment at the sink.
- **A malformed percent-escape no longer crashes the request pipeline**
  (warren-7c1e). `/runs/%ZZ/cancel` raised `URIError` out of
  `matchRoute`, which `handleRequest` calls outside its try/catch, so
  the connection dropped instead of returning warren's error envelope.
  Such a path is now a plain 404.
- **Salvage events no longer publish the host bundle path to spectators**
  (warren-7c1e). `salvagePath` is a `REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS` member, but
  `reap.workspace_salvaged` and `reap.workspace_salvage_recorded` served
  the identical absolute path to anonymous readers as `bundlePath`, and
  `reap.workspace_salvage_failed` carried it again inside raw git stderr.
  `bundlePath` / `salvagePath` now censor on the key, and the
  salvage-failed payload joins the body/log split. `rescueRef` stays in
  the clear — it is a branch name holding the already-public run id.
- **Path-mode previews move to a dedicated origin** (warren-3f8a) so
  agent-authored preview code can no longer read the operator token out
  of the UI's `localStorage`. A dedicated listener on
  `WARREN_PREVIEW_PORT` (default bind port + 1) serves nothing but the
  preview proxy; the warren origin answers `/p/...` with a 308 redirect.
  The unix-socket transport keeps legacy same-origin mounting and warns
  at boot. `/preview/config` discloses the preview port so the UI and PR
  annotations render the real URL.
- **`targetBranch` on `POST /runs` is now a validated push target**
  (#754) — a dispatch-capable bearer can no longer aim a run's push at
  an arbitrary branch such as the project default.
- **`POST /runs/:id/steer` validates `priority`** against
  `INBOX_PRIORITIES` instead of casting an arbitrary string past the
  type (#757), and **agent runtime ids are validated against
  `KNOWN_RUNTIME_IDS`** so an unknown runtime can no longer slip through
  agent upsert (#758).
- **`.warren/config.yaml` fails closed** (#759) — one unknown key used
  to silently drop the whole config, including the admission caps it
  carried. Unknown keys now surface instead of erasing their siblings.
- **Security headers on every response** plus `Vary: Authorization` on
  projection-dependent routes (#750), and the **per-client event-stream
  cap no longer trusts client-supplied forwarding headers** for its
  client key (#751).
- **Public-projection leak sweep** — `reap_failed` / `spawn_failed`
  events no longer leak absolute host paths and raw subprocess stderr
  (#752); `reap.workspace_destroyed` and `watchdog.terminal_reconciled`
  payloads no longer re-leak `burrowId` / `burrowRunId` (#748, #749);
  `plan_runs` and `plan_run_children` are now field-projected for
  spectators instead of served whole (#747); and anonymous
  `GET /runs/:id/events` no longer materializes the entire run
  transcript in memory per request (#710). Acceptance scenario 39 grew
  matching assertions for plan-run fields and path-bearing event kinds
  (#753).

### Added

- **Seeds integrity guard** for `.seeds/issues.jsonl` (warren-a71f,
  #716), plus post-merge dedupe that keeps terminal states
  (warren-b3be, #761).
- **Alpha logo/icon branding variants** and generator updates
  (warren-1d14).

### Changed

- **SPEC.md is retired** (warren-6fe3, #720–#741). Its living contracts
  were salvaged into `docs/design/` records — preview environments,
  plan-run coordinator, scheduler, warren-config loader,
  runtime/supervisor/durability, agent composition + pi runtime — and
  its V1 goals and security posture folded into `ACCEPTANCE.md` and
  `SECURITY.md`. All code and doc references now point at the design
  records or `docs/http-api.md`.
- **`AGENTS.md` is the canonical agent instruction doc**; `CLAUDE.md`
  is now a symlink to it (warren-b771, #742). A docs dedup/conflict
  sweep aligned README, ROADMAP, PHILOSOPHY, and CONTRIBUTING (#743).
- **Cross-repo dispatch is fully removed** — plan-run coordinator and
  dispatch routing (warren-deed, #721), the dispatch-prompt builder
  (warren-702e, #724), `seedProjectId` in the spawn path (warren-fd42,
  #725), the target-project resolver and `extensions.repo` schema key
  (warren-2967, #727), the cross-repo UI surface (#729), and
  `execution_project_id` on `plan_run_children` (warren-7c67, #731).
- **Finalize contract cleanup** — dead `closeSeedId` deleted (#745) and
  the remaining holdouts generalized (#746).
- **`src/ui` migrated to TypeScript 7** and the jscpd duplication
  ratchet tightened from 3% to 1.3% (#744).
- **K8s repo-cache is opt-in, default off** (warren-554f, #719), and
  the event bridge drops the remaining per-delta noise events
  (warren-ef12, #714).
- **CI action bumps** — docker buildx/build-push/login/qemu and
  actions/checkout moved to their next majors (#700–#705).

### Fixed

- **In-pod salvage reaches the control plane again** (warren-7c1e).
  `POST /runs/:id/salvage` was missing from
  `RUN_CALLBACK_ROUTE_PATTERNS`, so the run-scoped token every pod
  carries (warren-57fd) was refused 403 on the one route that banks a
  run's otherwise-unrecoverable commits before the `emptyDir` dies. The
  route now sits in the allowlist, still pinned to its own run id and
  still refused once that run is terminal.
- **K8s pod-log follow honesty** — the follow's half-open blind window
  is bounded (warren-029d, #717) and the pod exits non-zero when the
  in-pod finalize never delivers (warren-4d6a, #718), closing the
  warren-3047 silent-discard root cause. `warren run` no longer races
  burrow finalize under the local runtime either (warren-2909, #713).
- **Healer routing and retry accounting** — `projectMapping` no longer
  routes by case-insensitive substring match, so a short project name
  can't shadow a longer one (#764), and the retry cap is no longer
  computed over only the 500 most recent `heal.dispatched` events
  (#762).
- **Plan-run correctness** — `promptTemplate` must contain `{seed_id}`
  or the dispatch is refused (warren-b3be, #761); `plan_run_children`
  and `run_previews` writes now go through transition tables instead of
  accepting any state jump (#760).
- **Reap PR seed

body:
Phase 3b of the PyQt6 port (#27) — completing the code side, with both recommendations you picked.

## The thing that actually needed proving

The app had never been run under PyQt6. Phases 1–3a established that it *should* work; this establishes that it *does*.

Under `QT_API=pyqt6` and `QT_API=pyqt5`, identically:

```
binding            : PyQt6 6.11.0   |  PyQt5 5.15.14
resources loaded   : 11/11          |  11/11
addFolder icon     : True           |  True
result window      : True           |  True
details dialog     : True           |  True
about box          : True           |  True
problem dialog     : True           |  True
deletion options   : True           |  True
recent (QAction)   : True           |  True
prefs->options     : True           |  True
menu actions built : 6              |  6
```

Full suite: **835 passed, 6 skipped on both.** `run.py` runs its real event loop and exits 0 on both.

## Binding layout

- `requirements.txt` → **PyQt6** (default) + qtpy
- `requirements-pyqt5.txt` → the **fallback**

CI gains a PyQt5 leg that **uninstalls PyQt6** rather than setting `QT_API`, so it exercises qtpy's own selection with only PyQt5 present — what a user on the fallback actually has. It asserts the selection took (`qtpy.API_NAME == 'PyQt5'`) so a silently-wrong binding fails loudly rather than quietly retesting PyQt6.

## The Linux exclusion is gone

`requirements.txt` carried `PyQt5 ...; sys_platform != 'linux'` because PyQt5 lacked usable Linux wheels. **PyQt6 ships manylinux wheels**, so Linux installs a binding like everything else.

The practical effect is the point: **the Qt tests now run on the Linux legs**, which previously skipped them entirely. That was the coverage gap that let `--full-verify` ship unreachable from the GUI, and it's now closed on every platform.

Qt wheels bundle Qt but not the system libraries it links against — even the offscreen platform plugin links libEGL and libxkbcommon — so the Linux legs install `libegl1`, `libgl1`, `libxkbcommon-x11-0`, `libdbus-1-3`. A missing one surfaces as a plugin load failure, not a Python error, so it's documented in the README for bare Linux images generally.

## One CI trap caught while writing it

The fallback leg is also `ubuntu-latest` + `3.12`, so both `Upload coverage report` and `Upload Artifacts` would have matched it and collided on artifact name (`coverage-xml`, `modules 3.12`). Both are now excluded from that leg.

## Docs

README gains a "Qt bindings" section covering the default, the fallback, `QT_API`, and the Linux system libraries; `pyqt5-dev-tools` and `python3-pyqt5` are gone from prerequisites. HANDOFF's test counts and platform table were stale — refreshed, and the table now notes every platform runs the Qt tests.

## What's left of #27

**Packaging** — and that half cannot be verified here, since nobody can run a frozen build. It belongs with #10. `requirements-extra.txt` still pins `pyinstaller<6.0`, which has no 3.14 build; widening it without a real packaging run is exactly the trap #10 exists to avoid.

author: redscaresu
body:
Two small follow-ups after v0.2.0.

## 1. `release.yml`: emit a combined `SHA256SUMS`
The release only shipped per-binary `<name>.sha256` files, so the README's
`shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` verify step had no manifest to check against
(v0.1.0 had one from the old manual build; v0.2.0 lost it).

Each matrix leg builds in isolation and can only see its own binary, so this
adds a `checksums` job that:
- `needs: build-and-release` (waits for all four legs),
- pulls the four `.sha256` assets back off the release with `gh release download`,
- concatenates them (sorted by filename) into `SHA256SUMS`,
- attaches the manifest to the release.

`SHA256SUMS` is a plain concat of the already-generated per-binary sums, so it
stays consistent with them by construction.

## 2. `AGENTS.md`: name the ephemeral `--purpose` convention up front
Adds a one-line pointer (not a duplicated recipe — `goldfinger guide` stays
canonical) so an agent developing a fleet change knows to `mirror --purpose
<name>` into a fresh, timestamped, never-auto-deleted snapshot. Reaches
`CLAUDE.md` too via the symlink.

## Note
`release.yml` only runs on `v*` tag pushes, so the `SHA256SUMS` change isn't
exercised until the next release tag. `make check` is green; no Go code changed.
