author: jzhao234
body:
TLDR: `sudo fleet update` rebuilt the sandbox image into root's podman
store, which the fleet service (running as its own unprivileged user)
can never see, and only rebuilt when the Containerfile's content
changed. A client bundle that merely renames its image tag therefore
booted clean and broke on the first tool call. Root-run builds now land
in the service user's store, and the rebuild triggers on the tag as
well — including when the expected tag is simply absent.

Problem:
- update.sh step 4 ran scripts/build-sandbox-image.sh as root (fleet
  update chowns, installs into /opt/fleet, restarts systemd), and that
  script did a plain `podman build`. Root's rootful store is a separate
  namespace from the User=fleet unit's rootless store — the one
  bootstrap.sh deliberately builds into via runuser — so every rebuild
  through fleet update was a no-op for the running service.
- The rebuild gate compared only the Containerfile hash
  (.fleet-state/sandbox-containerfile.sha256). A bundle renaming
  manifest sandbox.tag with a byte-identical Containerfile (omnicom-
  config just renamed fleet-sandbox-example → fleet-sandbox-omnicom)
  skipped the build; fleet does not verify the image at boot, so the
  box comes up healthy and every sandboxed tool call then fails asking
  podman for a tag that was never built.
- doctor's remediation hints (boxdoctor.go "sudo fleet update (rebuilds
  the bundle's sandbox image)", doctor.sh "build it: sudo fleet
  update") were untrue on both counts.

Fix:
- The store fix lives in build-sandbox-image.sh, not update.sh, so
  every root caller benefits (fleet update, an operator following
  doctor's hint, the documented manual invocation): when run as root
  with the unit installed, the build re-runs as the unit's User= —
  resolved via `systemctl show -p User`, FLEET_SERVICE_NAME selecting
  the unit — under runuser with the unit's HOME/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (the
  service user is a nologin system account with no login session;
  /run/<user> is tmpfs and is recreated the way the unit's
  RuntimeDirectory= would), cd'ing to that HOME first because rootless
  podman re-execs and chdirs back to a cwd the user may not enter.
  bootstrap.sh keeps its own runuser path: it builds before the unit
  is installed, so it cannot resolve User= from systemd.
- New `--print-tag` query mode prints the resolved <name>:<tag> from
  the same manifest read the build uses (no podman, no side effects).
  update.sh gates on that tag — recorded in
  .fleet-state/sandbox-image.ref next to the hash stamp — and also
  rebuilds when the tag is missing from the service user's store,
  probed through the same runuser environment (sandbox_podman). An
  empty recorded ref (pre-upgrade box) is treated as no-signal rather
  than a rename so the fleet doesn't mass-rebuild; the absence probe
  still heals those boxes, including images stranded in root's store
  by pre-fix updates.
- The post-build dangling-layer prune moves to the store the build
  actually targeted (it previously pruned root's).
- doctor.sh's fallback hint now names a root invocation that works
  (`sudo … build-sandbox-image.sh`); boxdoctor.go's "sudo fleet
  update" hint was verified true after the fix and left as-is, keeping
  the Go and shell messages aligned. Stale "only when the Containerfile
  changed" descriptions in update.sh, admincli, and OPERATORS.md
  updated to match.

Tests:
- New in internal/admincli: TestBuildSandboxImagePrintTag and
  TestBuildSandboxImagePrintTagRenamedBundle run the real script and
  assert tag resolution (the renamed-bundle case is the omnicom
  regression — it fails on the previous code, which had no
  --print-tag); TestBuildSandboxImageTargetsServiceStore and
  TestUpdateSandboxGatePresent pin the load-bearing delegation/gate
  lines the way the existing bootstrap guard tests do.
- go build ./..., go vet ./... (one pre-existing internal/tools vet
  failure, present at HEAD), go test ./internal/boxdoctor
  ./internal/admincli all pass; update.sh --dry-run plan inspected.
- bash -n and shellcheck on the three touched scripts: no findings
  beyond the two already present at HEAD.
- A real podman build could not be exercised in this environment; the
  runuser build path is untested end-to-end here.



**Verification caveat:** a real podman build and the `runuser` delegation could not be exercised end-to-end here (no usable podman). The delegation was stub-exercised with fake `systemctl`/`runuser`/`podman` and asserted byte-consistent with `bootstrap.sh`'s existing path; `--dry-run` step-4 plans were inspected.

**Real-world trigger:** omnicom-config renamed its sandbox tag with a byte-identical Containerfile, which is exactly the case the old hash-only gate skipped.

author: jaxtothemax
body:
The app deploys to two places and only one deploys itself: `web/` goes to Vercel the moment `main` changes, `worker/` goes to the droplet only when a person copies a file onto it. Nothing in the repo said so, and nothing did the copying.

When the wallet-identity change merged today, Vercel shipped the new front end within the minute, the worker stayed as it was, and **Connect XRPL wallet** answered `unknown method findOrCreatePlayerByWallet` in production. Neither half was broken — they disagreed. The gap is the defect, not the code on either side of it.

`worker/deploy.sh` does what the runbook said to do by hand, and refuses the ways it goes wrong:

- won't install a checkout whose worker still reads `players.email` in nineteen places over a schema that no longer has the column — the outage, run in reverse
- backs up the worker binary and a full `pg_dump` to `/root` before touching either, and prints both restore commands at the end
- skips the migration when `players.email` is already absent, so a second run is not a second flush
- stops on first error rather than half-migrating; fails loudly if the worker doesn't come back or its RPC surface is still the old one

The header states the ordering rule for any future change touching both halves: **worker first, then let Vercel take the web app.**

## Usage

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Megawatt-Solutions/Megawat---XRPL-Make-Waves.git /tmp/mw
bash /tmp/mw/worker/deploy.sh
```

## Testing

As far as a laptop allows. `REPO` auto-detects the checkout from the script's own location, verified both from the repo root and by absolute path from `/tmp`. All four checkout guards exercised against real inputs: the old worker (rejected, `email/verified x19`), a missing migration, a nonexistent `REPO`, and the current worker (accepted). Everything past the `/etc/spreadcast/worker.env` read needs the droplet.

author: yasinsheikh8
body:
This is the fix for the *root cause* behind "LiteAPI didn't respond", not a cosmetic addition.

Suppliers reject an incomplete location — LiteAPI needs city **and** country. The field collected free text, so a bare "Lisbon" went out incomplete and came back rejected. Picking a suggestion writes `Lisbon, PT`, which round-trips unambiguously every time.

Free text still works and is still resolved against the same table. The list removes the guesswork rather than replacing the fallback.

A test asserts that contract directly:

```ts
// Whatever the list puts in the box must resolve to a complete location.
for (const suggestion of suggestDestinations("lis")) {
  const resolved = resolveDestination(suggestion.value);
  assert.equal(resolved.countryCode, suggestion.countryCode);
  assert.equal(resolved.source, "explicit");
}
```

## Details

**No endpoint.** Suggestions come from the local table — a few KB, so there's no request to wait on, nothing to debounce, and nothing to fail mid-search.

**A real combobox, not a div that looks like one.** Arrow keys move the active option, Enter takes it, Tab accepts the highlighted one, Escape closes, and `aria-activedescendant` tells a screen reader what's highlighted. Without that it's unusable by keyboard.

**Alternate spellings match but collapse.** `munch`, `münch` and `münchen` all find Munich, and the list shows **one** row rather than offering the same city twice under two spellings.

## Two defects the browser run caught

- The option's accessible text was **"LisbonPortugal"** — the separator was a CSS margin, and a screen reader reads `textContent`. The comma now lives in the text.
- The results heading read **"8 stays in Lisbon, PT"**, leaking an ISO code at users. The aggregator now returns the resolved city and the heading uses it.

Neither was visible in a screenshot. Both came from asserting on real output.

## Verified in a browser

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Suggestions appear while typing | ✓ |
| Mouse click writes `Lisbon, PT` | ✓ |
| ArrowDown + Enter writes `Barcelona, ES` | ✓ |
| `role=combobox`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant` | ✓ |
| Escape closes the list | ✓ |
| Search from a suggestion reaches results | ✓ |
| Heading shows "8 stays in Lisbon" | ✓ |

**77 tests**, up from 70. Typecheck and build clean.

- **Basic CI on pull requests**: new `lint.yml` workflow runs bash/PHP/Python/JS syntax checks on every PR, now that PRs are required to reach `main` (branch protection) but nothing was automatically checking them.

Bumps `version.txt` to 1.22.0.

## Test plan
- [x] Functional test (not just syntax): confirmed the backup file is created, contains the actual live config, has correct 0o600 permissions, and the update still completes successfully with the new stage inserted
- [x] This PR itself is the first live test of the new lint.yml workflow

body:
## Summary

- route BYO-key OpenAI extraction through graphiti-core 0.29.3's public client contract, preserving retries, tracing, structured response adaptation, and token tracking
- make the default embedded graph derive from the resolved memrelay home, scope config discovery to `MEMRELAY_HOME`, and preserve explicit config/env graph overrides
- cancel borrow-host calls by terminating and awaiting only the process tree rooted at memrelay's spawned PID (Windows Job Object with exact-PID fallback; POSIX process group)
- avoid expected Ladybug duplicate-index ERROR diagnostics by checking index metadata first while propagating real FTS failures and closing failed opens
- give the self-observation smoke one absolute drain budget, a finite configurable timeout, and deterministic cancellation cleanup; raise the documented default to 1200s based on the observed 927.7s successful extraction
- replace stale smoke guidance with current Copilot/OpenAI status and correct detached-daemon log instructions

## Finding disposition

- **Fixed:** BYO-key tuple crash, graph relocation/data isolation, borrow-host process leakage, Ladybug duplicate-index diagnostics, and smoke timeout accounting/cleanup.
- **Already fixed on main:** daemon startup no longer uses the historical 10-second timeout. Current code has adaptive 30-second warm / 120-second cold readiness windows, `MEMRELAY_READY_TIMEOUT`, honest timeout messaging, and `<MEMRELAY_HOME>/logs/daemon-startup.log`. No speculative lifecycle constants were changed; stale docs were corrected.
- **Live status:** prior Copilot borrow-host extraction and self-observation exclusion passed. The OpenAI adapter failure is covered hermetically here, but no paid live OpenAI call was made, so the runbook does not claim live OpenAI revalidation.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest -q` — 1289 passed, 4 optional cloud-backend skips
- focused cancellation/timeout suite after final edge refinements — 24 passed
- `ruff check src tests scripts`
- `ruff format --check src tests scripts`
- `git diff --cached --check`

All validation was hermetic; no Copilot, Claude, OpenAI, or other paid inference calls were made.

## Residual risk

Windows process-tree ownership uses pywin32 Job Objects (available through the existing Windows runtime dependency) and falls back to `taskkill /PID <spawned-pid> /T /F` if job setup or termination fails. The fallback remains exact-PID scoped and never kills by process name.

author: voidspooks
body:
Closes #513.

`LastUpdatedAt` on the score-progress query took the newest `events` row of any action, while the status backfill in `0048scoresstatus.go` counts only `created` and `updated`. A score row whose only provenance is an out-of-band load therefore reported the load's timestamp while `questionsupdated` stayed 0, so the two read the same events and disagreed about them.

The lateral now carries the same action allowlist. An allowlist rather than a `<> 'imported'` exclusion, so a `deleted` event, or any action added later, cannot bump the timestamp either.

## The comments were the other half of the ticket

`scoreprogress.go` described history loaded from outside the app as carrying no events at all, while `0048scoresstatus.go` described it as carrying `imported` provenance events. Both statements are about environments rather than about the code, and neither is checkable from this repo, so I rewrote the `scoreprogress.go` side to state the rule instead: imported provenance is not an edit, whether or not a given environment records it. That holds either way and is what the query now enforces.

`0048scoresstatus.go` is untouched. It is the side already stating that rule, and it is an applied migration.

## Scope beyond the ticket's file list

`openapi.yaml` is a regeneration, not a hand edit. swag sources the `lastupdatedat` description from the struct field comment, so editing that comment moves the spec. Description text only, no schema or contract change, and `redocly lint` is clean at the usual 8 warnings with 2 explicitly ignored.

`_test_data_empire.sql` is a comment-only change. The data is unchanged, and it remains the fixture this fix is tested against. The old comment justified the imported events by saying last-updated shows the import instead of blank, which is the behavior being removed here, so it would have documented the opposite of the code.

## Visible behavior

A row whose entire event history is non-edit now reports no `lastupdatedat` instead of the load's timestamp. The field is `omitempty`, so it is absent rather than null. On the dashboard such a row's tooltip stops reading "Last updated <import date>" and falls through to its state-based text, and in `aggregateScores.ts` its `lastUpdatedMs` becomes -1, which puts it back in the tie where the has-score tie-break decides. That is the invariant the comment at `aggregateScores.ts:95` says the chosen-call logic depends on.

Rows with a genuine in-app edit are unaffected, since the edit is the newest matching event either way. The counts do not move at all; this changes only the timestamp.

## Tests

New `TestScoreProgressLastUpdatedIgnoresImportedEventsIntegration` drives the real `FindScoreProgress` path and asserts an imported-only system reports a nil `LastUpdatedAt` while still reporting its answers. It resolves its subject systems from the events table rather than hardcoding ids, so it cannot pass vacuously against a data call that simply has no events, and it mirrors the query's own exclusion of decommissioned systems. Verified to fail against the unfixed lateral, where it returns the import timestamp rather than nil.

`TestBuildScoreProgressSQL_Shape` gains one assertion pinning the action filter. The existing `TestImportedScoresKeepProvenanceWithoutDoneStatusIntegration` is unchanged and still passes; it pins the status half.

## Gate

`make test-unit` green across all 12 packages, run with `-count=1` rather than from cache. `make test-integration` green. `make test-e2e` ran 197 with 0 failures. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks both green, no `--no-verify`.

Snyk and the deploy checks will show red here: this is a fork PR and those jobs need org secrets. Expected, and they pass once the branch is pulled in-repo.

author: jasonleetucker-code
body:
First remediation pass against the [2026-08-04 decision-intelligence audit](https://github.com/jasonleetucker-code/riskittogetthebrisket/blob/main/docs/audits/decision-intelligence-audit-2026-08-04.md) (merged in #701): **Phase 0 of that plan, plus two Critical findings that were giving users wrong numbers.**

This is **2 of 43 Critical** and does not attempt the other 171 Critical/High findings. Scope is deliberate — see "What this does not do".

## Phase 0 — make a board change measurable

The audit's plan opens with a blocking prerequisite: with 173 fixes to land, an intended repricing and a regression look identical unless you can measure them.

- **`scripts/golden_board.py`** captures every decision-bearing field (value, rank, tier, confidence, market-gap, source coverage) from a contract built through the real `build_api_data_contract` on a *pinned* input export.
- **`scripts/board_diff.py`** reports value moves with percentile spread, rank churn and label flips, plus `--expect-no-value-change` for phases that must move labels only.
- Baseline committed at `tests/fixtures/golden/baseline.json`.

**`tests/conftest.py` — finding Q-1.** `test_data_contract.py` is removed from `_LIVEDATA_MODULES`. The module is 100% synthetic (every test builds input from `_minimal_raw_payload()`; no reference to `exports/`, `CSVs/` or `data/`), yet the filename-keyed exemption moved **33 tests covering the core blend** into the non-blocking advisory tier — so a real regression in `build_api_data_contract` could not fail a PR. Verified: 33 pass in 1.4s.

## T-3 / C-2 — stop discounting pick years the market already prices

Both ingested markets price the **next** class **above** the imminent one, because an unknown pick carries option value:

```
ktcSfTep      2026 Early 1st 5595 | 2027 7061 | 2028 5122
idpTradeCalc  2026 Early 1st 5554 | 2027 7052 | 2028 5034
```

`offsetDiscounts` assumes smooth `1.00/0.82/0.66/0.53` decay. Composing the two published **2027 firsts 18% and 2028 firsts 34% below what both markets agreed** — biasing every trade involving future capital the same way: sell futures cheap, buy futures expensive.

The discount now applies only to years the pipeline **synthesised** by cloning a nearer year (`_SYNTHETIC_FAR_FUTURE_PICK_NAMES`) — the one case where it does real work.

**Measured on the live board** (`board_diff`, pinned 2026-08-04 export):

| | |
|---|---|
| 2027 tiers | **+22.0%** |
| 2028 tiers | **+51.5%** |
| 2029 tiers | unchanged (still 0.53 — synthesised) |
| values moved | 21, all picks |
| ranks re-sorted | 649 |
| pricing swap | 3 underpriced 2028 4th-rounders enter at ranks 413–584, displacing 3 ~1115-value rows at rank ~675 |

### This reverses a prior product decision — please look here

Two tests asserted the old ordering, one calling the opposite *"the audit's most prominent inversion"*. I **rewrote rather than deleted** them, with the evidence recorded in place.

The market's own numbers do not support the old rule: KTC prices **2028 Late 1st at 4026 vs 2026 Late 1st at 3942**. An unknown future first can become an early one if that roster collapses; a known 2026 slot cannot. So the "inversion" was the market, and the blanket discount was the overcorrection.

What I kept is the part that survives: a speculative 2028 tier still must not outvalue the **1.01 of the class about to be drafted**.

If the product deliberately wants to be more conservative than the market on future capital, that is legitimate — but it belongs in a calibrated, documented adjustment, not a prior stacked on a price that already encodes the year. **This is the one change here I'd most want a second opinion on.**

## W-1 — the FAAB pool counted draft picks as free agents

The bid desk's share-of-pool denominator filtered only on *"is this name on a roster"*. Picks are never on a Sleeper roster, so every pick passed the filter and the best one set `top_pool_value`.

Simulated against the live board with a realistic 12-team roster exclusion:

| | denominator | standard bid |
|---|---|---|
| before | **7,799** (a first-round pick) | **$8** |
| after | **1,914** (best actual free agent) | **$21** |

Every recommended bid was **2.7–3.0× too low** — on the number users act on to win a contested claim.

**This raises exposure to W-2, which is NOT fixed here.** The bid is still a *share of the best wire asset* rather than an absolute anchor, so the top-of-wire player now always draws ~30% of budget. The fix still improves discrimination — previously every free agent was a tiny fraction of a first-round pick, so a 1,914 player and a 500 player were nearly indistinguishable — but W-2 needs a replacement-level anchor and is the next required step. I did not invent a constant to paper over it.

## Also

`test_refit_path_characterisation.py` parsed `_LIVEDATA_MODULES` by splitting on the first `)`, so it broke on a parenthesis inside a comment. Now parses to the frozenset's closing brace, like its sibling in `test_livedata_policy.py`.

## What this does not do

**41 Critical and 130 High findings remain open**, including the trade verdict naming the wrong winner, `/edge` labelling all 36 tight ends SELL, the IDP board being IDPTradeCalc ±15%, and the circular Hill-curve holdout. The audit's Part B sequences them; the IDP re-fit in particular needs a real fitting run with validation, which this pass does not attempt.

## Verification

- Full blocking tier: **5,768 passed, 26 skipped** (`pytest -m "not livedata"`)
- `ruff check` clean; `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files
- Board effect measured with the harness this PR adds, not asserted
- The committed baseline reflects post-change state, so the next phase diffs against it

body:
## Summary

Adds structured usage + cost tracking for all audio-native providers (openai, gemini, xai, nova, qwen, livekit).

- **`UsageRecord`** (`src/tau2/data_model/usage.py`): normalized per-provider usage event — token counts with text/audio/cached splits, audio-seconds, TTS characters — with `delta` vs `cumulative` semantics (last-value-wins per scope for running counters like Nova totals, xAI audio-minutes, LiveKit STT seconds) and a `billable` flag (xAI reports tokens but bills per audio-minute).
- **Versioned pricing table** (`src/tau2/voice/pricing.py`): rates verified against official provider pricing pages (Nova marked UNVERIFIED — AWS pages are JS-rendered); unknown model → cost `None`, never a silent `$0`; litellm fallback for cascaded LLM legs.
- **Surfacing**: per-response records ride on agent message chunks (`usage`/`cost`); session-level `SessionUsage` lands on `SimulationRun.agent_usage`, and `agent_cost` derives from it. The usage ledger survives `disconnect()`, with cumulative meters flushed at disconnect.
- **Fixes along the way**: Nova `usageEvent` camelCase aliases (previously dropped all fields), `get_cost()` one-side-`None` no longer nukes the other side, `$nan` avg-cost display renders "n/a", nova added to `--audio-native-provider` CLI choices, `--max-steps-seconds` passthrough in `run_multiple`.

## Testing

- 29 new unit tests (`tests/test_voice/test_usage_pricing.py`): wire-format parsing per provider, delta/cumulative aggregation, pricing math, unpriced-vs-free semantics. Regression sweep green (259 passed in test_streaming/test_voice; 64 in llm_utils/results/orchestrator/checkpoint).
- New `TestUsageReporting` in the horizontal provider suite: one spoken turn must produce billable usage records that price to cost > 0. Passed live for openai, gemini, xai, qwen, livekit, livekit-thinking (nova blocked on expired local AWS SSO).
- End-to-end: 1-task 60s `run_multiple` sims across 5 providers — every saved sim has `agent_usage` + `agent_cost`, and per-chunk costs reconcile exactly with session cost (openai $0.085, gemini $0.036, xai $0.050 = 60s × $0.05/min, qwen $0.059 on qwen3.5-omni-plus-realtime, livekit $0.031 incl. per-leg STT/LLM/TTS breakdown).

body:
Closes the Phase 0 blockers so recall-echo can produce measured claims. RE-31 (Phase 1) is stacked on this branch.

## What's here

**Runtime backend** — embedded vs server is now a config choice (`[graph] mode`, previously a dead key) via `surrealdb::engine::any`; both backends compile in. Lock collisions became a named `GraphError::Locked` with bounded retry instead of a raw SurrealKV panic.

**Serve daemon** — every graph command and hook goes through a per-memory-dir unix-socket daemon that auto-starts on first use (no opt-in, no fallback paths, per design decision). It holds the one embedded store and the lazily-loaded embedder, idles out after `[serve] idle_timeout_secs`, and is crash-only. Admin ops take exclusive ownership via an enforced admin lock. This unblocks concurrent access — the failure that killed the benchmark pilot in June.

**LazyEmbedder** — the ONNX model loads on first embedding op, not on every graph open. Also fixed a test hang (untimeouted HuggingFace download during `init`).

**Golden retrieval tests** (`tests/query_golden.rs`) — 10 tests pinning recall@k ordering, confidence weighting, decay-floor edge exclusion, scoring-weight sensitivity and 1-hop expansion semantics, so Phase 2's retrieval work cannot silently regress them.

v3.11.1 (SessionEnd hook fix + the repo's first CI test job) shipped separately from this branch and is already on crates.io.

## Audit remediation

Three parallel auditors (quality / performance / security) reviewed the branch before this PR; 16 findings fixed in a92a64b — socket-directory hijack, peer authentication, config-driven filesystem mutation, protocol bounds, real mutual exclusion for admin ops, dead-daemon retry, and hook-path daemon reuse. Details in that commit message.

## Not here

The LongMemEval baseline report (`docs/benchmarks/baseline-2026-08.md`) lands as the final commit before merge — the run is in progress. AC4 stays open until then.

author: doralevich
body:
One new file, `scripts/test-telegram-channel.mjs`. Nothing in the app changes.

## Why

Channels rests on one question that can't be answered from this repo: Hermes authenticates webhook deliveries with its own subscription signature, Telegram authenticates with a `secret_token` it echoes in a header. If those don't line up, Hermes rejects everything Telegram sends and no amount of UI fixes it.

`api.agent37.com` and `api.telegram.org` are both blocked from the build environment, so I can't run this myself. The script exists so whoever can doesn't have to reconstruct the sequence from a chat message.

## What it does

Exactly what the dashboard's connect button does:

1. Validate the bot token (`getMe`)
2. Create or reuse the public port on `8644` with prefix `webhooks` (handles the 409)
3. Point the bot at `{origin}/webhooks/{subscription}` via `setWebhook`

```bash
AGENT37_API_KEY=sk_live_... INSTANCE_ID=ab12cd34ef \
BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC-DEF... SUBSCRIPTION=telegram SIGNING_SECRET=... \
  node scripts/test-telegram-channel.mjs
```

Then message the bot and run `CHECK=1`, which reads `getWebhookInfo` and names which of three outcomes happened:

| Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **rejected** | Hermes refused the delivery. Its own error text is printed — that's the thing worth sending back; a 401/403 means the auth schemes don't line up, a 404 means the subscription path is wrong. |
| **delivered but silent** | Telegram is happy; Hermes isn't routing to the agent or isn't replying. Hermes-side config. |
| **working** | Turn Channels on. |

`CLEANUP=1` unhooks the bot and deletes the public port — a test bot left pointed at a real instance is the kind of thing nobody remembers a week later.

## Safety

Use a throwaway bot. `drop_pending_updates` is set on both the hook and the cleanup, so it won't replay a backlog into a live agent. The script reads credentials from the environment and never writes them anywhere.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes
- Ran it with no environment set: exits on the missing-variable guard rather than making a call

Not verified: the script has never completed a run, because this environment can reach neither host it talks to. Its two API calls mirror the ones in `lib/agent37.ts` and `lib/channels/telegram.ts` that ship in the app.

author: ipv1337
body:
## Why the open PRs are red

`osv-scan` waives a finding only when a change touches **no** dependency manifest — and a dependency bump touches a lockfile by definition. So #1379, #1380, #1382, #1383 and #1384 each fail on the same **24 pre-existing advisories** they did not introduce, while unrelated PRs pass straight through the identical set. The nightly scheduled scan on `main` has been red on this set too (it also fails closed). Fixing the baseline is what unblocks them.

Diagnosis credit to @Beacon; this PR is the remediation.

## What this fixes

10 advisories, 16 affected package instances, 0 critical / 10 high / 14 medium. Source: run [30897730701](https://github.com/VitruvianSoftware/vitruvian-core/actions/runs/30897730701), job `osv-scan`.

| Advisory | CVSS | Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr | 7.7 | ip-address | 10.1.0 / 10.2.0 | 10.4.0 |
| GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 | 7.5 | brace-expansion | 1.1.16 / 2.1.0 / 2.1.2 / 5.0.5 / 5.0.8 | 1.1.18 / 2.1.4 / 5.0.9 |
| GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 | 7.5 | fast-uri | 3.1.2 / 3.1.3 | 3.1.5 |
| GHSA-22jq-vg5j-6vgg | 6.9 | ip-address | 10.2.0 | 10.4.0 |
| GHSA-4xrf-jv44-h6hh | 6.9 | ip-address | 10.2.0 | 10.4.0 |
| GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp | 6.3 | postcss | 8.4.31 / 8.5.10 | 8.5.23 |
| GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239 | 5.3 | hono | 4.12.32 | 4.13.0 |
| GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524 | 4.8 | undici | 6.25.0 / 6.27.0 | 6.28.0 |
| GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm | 4.8 | undici | 6.25.0 / 6.27.0 | 6.28.0 |
| GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 | 4.2 | undici | 6.25.0 / 6.27.0 | 6.28.0 |

**`osv-scanner.toml` is untouched.** Nothing here is suppressed or re-baselined — it is fixed.

## How

Every one of these is a **transitive** dependency; none is declared in any `package.json` here, so there is no direct version to bump. `docs/dependency-versioning/javascript.md` names exactly this case — *"If you truly need to force convergence ... (a security fix)"* — and prescribes a root pnpm override.

The overrides are keyed **per major** (`brace-expansion@1` / `@2` / `@5`) rather than by bare package name, so each major line is pulled to its own patched release instead of collapsing five call sites onto a major their parents never declared. Values are ranges (`^1.1.18`), not pins, so ordinary patch updates keep flowing.

`policy-library` is not a pnpm workspace member — Pulumi's CrossGuard runner installs it with npm from its own `package-lock.json` — so it gets the equivalent npm `overrides` block and a regenerated lock.

### `pulumi/library/ts/package-lock.json` is deleted, not bumped

This is the one judgement call in the PR, so please push back if you disagree. Nothing reads that file:

* `tools/copybara/copy.bara.sky:424` already calls it *"a stale in-tree lock (pnpm is used at the root)"* and lists it in `origin_only_exclude`, so it is never migrated; the mirror keeps its own copy via `standalone_only`. Deleting it in-tree cannot reach the mirror.
* Its root entry contradicts its own `package.json` (`@types/node ^22` vs `^26`, `@pulumi/gcp ^8.0.0` vs the catalog's `^9.31.0`, literal ranges where the manifest now says `catalog:`) — so `npm ci` against it could not succeed today regardless.
* `pulumi/library/ts` is a pnpm workspace member; its `BUILD` lists only `package.json` as `srcs`, and no BUILD / workflow / Dockerfile runs `npm ci` in that directory.
* Dependabot's npm ecosystem is root-only (`.github/dependabot.yml:96`), so nothing was maintaining it either.

It was a scan surface and nothing else, and it would have drifted red again next month. Removing it clears 7 of the 24 findings permanently.

## Verification

Run at `0d794868`, with the real gate:

```
$ bash tools/osv-scan/osv-scan.sh          # osv-scanner v2.4.0
✓ no unaccepted advisories across 105 scanned sources
```

That run had no diff base, so `dep_manifests_changed()` failed closed and the gate was in **full blocking mode** — the strict verdict the nightly gets, not the waived PR path. The working tree was clean afterwards, so the read-only assertion holds.

Lockfile sync re-checked with the same hermetic pnpm `tidy-check` uses:

```
$ bazel run -- @pnpm//:pnpm install --dir . --lockfile-only
$ git diff --exit-code -- pnpm-lock.yaml   # no diff
```

Tests: `//oauth-user-inspector:unit_tests` and `//packages/design-system:lib_typecheck_test` pass (`oauth-user-inspector` is the only direct consumer of any bumped package — `postcss ^8.5.21`, satisfied by 8.5.23). Broader local `bazel test` runs died on this machine's Bazel server (memory) and on the Swift toolchain (no Xcode), both unrelated to this change — CI covers the rest.

## After merge

Pushing `pnpm-lock.yaml` to `main` triggers `dependabot-lock-rebase.yml`, which requests a rebase of every open Dependabot npm PR automatically. The five blocked PRs should go green on their own; I'll confirm and nudge any that don't.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`pulumi/examples/go-foundation/policy-library/package-lock.json` is outside Dependabot's root-only npm scope, so nothing maintains it — it will drift red again. Worth either bringing it into `dependabot.yml` or deciding it should not be a scanned surface. I'll open a separate issue.

## Related issues

**Closes #1191** — *"Dependabot cannot update pulumi/library/ts: 48/48 update jobs fail on corepack, 41 open alerts (1 critical, 19 high) are unfixable."* I found that issue after writing the patch, and it independently confirms the deletion above from the other direction: Dependabot classifies `pulumi/library/ts` as an npm ecosystem *solely because* that `package-lock.json` exists, then corepack intercepts (the root declares `packageManager: pnpm`) and every job dies. 48/48, silently, since the directory was grafted. So the file was not merely unread — it was actively generating 41 of the repo's 214 open Dependabot alerts (19%) for a lock nothing installs from. Removing it deletes the ecosystem misclassification at the root rather than working around corepack.

That also retires the concern #1191 raises about the `osv-scanner.toml` baseline: several entries were accepted for one quarter *"on the assumption the advisories would get patched during the quarter,"* which for this directory was structurally impossible. Those advisories are now gone rather than waiting on an expiry.

**Unblocks the "remediation deadlock" in #1385 §2.** That issue notes #1383 is the `npm-minor-patch` group PR that would fix several of these — but #1383 is itself blocked by them. This PR breaks the cycle from outside the dependabot set, so #1383 no longer has to be the fix. #1385 §1 (cross-ecosystem false positives — Go-only PRs blocked by npm advisories) is a separate gate-scoping defect and is **not** addressed here; it stays open on its own merits. Worth noting it is now largely dormant in practice, since the npm advisory set it fired on is empty.

author: quinnjr
body:
Cargo says nothing about a directory it was never told to care about. A crate in neither `members` nor `exclude` is not a workspace member, so every whole-workspace build, test and clippy run skips it, and `scripts/publish.sh` — which walks `members` — never publishes it. Nothing reports it; the crate simply stops being covered.

## Why this exists

Three incidents in one cycle, all the same root cause:

| Crate | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `armature-h1` | Absent from `members`, so the publish script never saw it. `armature-core` requires it, so publishing core would have failed against a dependency that wasn't on crates.io. Caught by hand, mid-release. |
| `armature-fuzz` | Stayed a submodule after its targets moved into `armature-core/fuzz`; accumulated failing CI once workflows were generated per directory. |
| `armature-session` | Reached **0.3.0** having never been built, tested, linted or published. Adding it to `members` immediately surfaced two clippy denials that had been there the whole time. |

## What it checks

Both directions:

- a crate directory cargo does not account for
- a `members` entry whose directory has gone

The second is checked **before** `cargo metadata` runs. Cargo refuses to load the workspace at all in that state and reports only `failed to read <path>`; running cargo first would leave that branch unreachable — which is exactly what my first draft did, and I only noticed because I tested the failure path rather than assuming it.

Crates that opt out by declaring their own `[workspace]` are not flagged. The `<crate>/fuzz` crates do that deliberately, being nightly-only.

## Verification

Both failure paths were verified by reproducing the real incidents, not by reading the code:

```
$ python3 scripts/check-workspace-membership.py          # current tree
OK: 66 packages, every armature-* directory accounted for.

$ # armature-session removed from members
These crate directories are in neither `members` nor `exclude`:
  armature-session
exit=1

$ # a members entry with no directory
These `members` entries have no Cargo.toml:
  armature-ghost
exit=1
```

The script is standalone so it runs locally too, and parses the two arrays textually rather than pulling a TOML dependency into CI.

## The defect (player-facing)

**Heart of Aeonia (76412) was emitted grantable in the Caelid bundle.** The game hides that grace's asset behind Commander O'Neil's defeat flag (EMEVD common event 9005810, gate `1049380800`, `m60_49_38`); force-lighting it on lock receipt warps the player onto a disabled bonfire inside his arena. It is now withheld and lights on the kill, as vanilla does. **The emitted-set delta of this whole PR is exactly `{76412}`** (61 -> 62 withheld flags).

## Reproduction first

Woke the oracle against fresh main (`ad3b884`) + the ensured bundle: **12 flags absent from `_BOSS_GATED_GRACE_FLAGS`** (`76412 76415 76419 76422 76509 76524 76823 76853 76862 76930 76945 76960`), **76412 emitted** -- same list as the 2026-08-04 audit measurement.

## Per-flag adjudication (gen's defect, not the oracle's)

Per gf-grace-straddle the oracle was tried first: every one of the 12 is a real `InitializeCommonEvent(_, 9005810, gate, ...)` row in its own tile's EMEVD, the asset-entity joins to BonfireWarpParam on the same tile, and each gate is that tile's GameAreaParam boss-arena defeat flag (`game_areas.tsv`) -- except 76422's, the Radahn-defeated global `310`. The oracle is acquitted; gen's 37 was complete only for the 380-file corpus of 2026-07-06, which predates the m60_/m61_ tile decompiles (bundle now: 587).

| flag | grace / gate | was |
|---|---|---|
| 76412 | Heart of Aeonia / 1049380800 (O'Neil) | **EMITTED -- the fix** |
| 76415, 76419, 76524, 76823, 76862, 76945 | Sellia crypt, Redmane plaza, Castle Sol rooftop, Ensis, Forsaken Graveyard, Church of the Bud | already withheld via `arena_graces.tsv` -- classification only |
| 76422, 76509, 76853, 76930, 76960 | Radahn, Fire Giant, Bayle, Scaduview/Gaius, Scadutree Base | moved from the `_ARENA` hand list (union-neutral) |

Nothing left needing an in-game check: all 12 settle on datamined evidence, written beside the entries in `gen_data.py`.

## Direction of error

Wrongly-withheld would be worse than wrongly-grantable, so explicitly: 9005810 lights each grace ON its gate flag in vanilla; Caelid keeps 37 graces; every front door is unchanged (`region_open_flags.py` body identical); gen_data hard-fails a regen whose front door lands in the skip set. Old seeds keep their baked grace list (bundle is slot_data), so the fix reaches new seeds only.

## The oracle runs in CI now

Dark cause was **positional path resolution** (two dirnames up = `_ap/worlds` under the harness), not artifacts -- fixed with the `find_repo_root` walk-up like every suite #361 woke. Ledger row `DEV_BOX_ONLY -> TESTS_JOB`; census family `grace-skip-oracle-known-red-244` (5) deleted; counts **re-measured** in the harness layout: 1555 passed / 77 skipped (re-measured after rebasing onto #364/#365), census green, `gf_suite_ledger --check` green.

**Rule 11:** `Regression244` pins the motivating case artifact-free -- (a) none of the 12 in `REGION_GRACE_POINTS` (fails on reclassify-back + regen), (b) all 12 in `_BOSS_GATED_GRACE_FLAGS` (fails on the frozenset revert itself). Both watched red under mutation before restoring the fix; the 5 pre-existing oracle tests fired on the same mutations.

## Rides along

* ~~A commit fixing main's red `gf_suite_ledger --check`~~ -- dropped on rebase: #365 landed the ledger row for `goods_hold_cap` while this branch was being built. (NB the dead `find_repo_root` import in that suite is still there on main and its ledger reason describes a walk-up that never runs -- cosmetic, noted here rather than churned.)
* Regen: exactly one module body moved (`region_graces.py`, Caelid -76412); the rest is the `inputs_hash` trailer + the three HTML page stamps (verified hash-only). No contract change, **no version bump**, gitlink untouched. Changelog + blurb grew under the open v0.3.4 window (rule 14).

Closes #244.

## Problem

PostgreSQL R11 against KubeBlocks main froze with both database Pods `5/5 Running` while the Cluster and Component stayed `Creating`. Every Pod repeatedly reported:

```
roleProbe code=-1: only exec action is supported: notImplemented
RoleProbeNotDone / primary is not present
```

The tested addon exact was main `5fa53f531defe335cd044723ebb854e6f4de4dbe`; its ComponentDefinitions still declared `roleProbe.http` for dbctl. The frozen failure-events artifact is SHA256 `9755c786fb6cec11d6f25e407b95bcbf4736b00af8404901e7581599c4e05db7`.

## Fix

- Call the same localhost dbctl `/v1.0/getrole` endpoint through `roleProbe.exec`.
- Bind the action to the existing `postgresql` lifecycle container so all lifecycle exec actions keep one execution image/container contract.
- Use `curl --fail --silent --show-error`, preserving the plain role token on stdout and converting non-2xx responses into probe failures.
- Advance the chart to `1.2.0-alpha.2` because ComponentDefinition lifecycle actions are immutable.
- Add a structured rendered-manifest contract test for all six PostgreSQL ComponentDefinitions.

author: gabdank
body:
Three commits, reviewable and revertible independently. The first is the one this branch was opened for; the other two came out of a colleague's terminal output while reviewing it and are unrelated to it — bundled here on request rather than split into their own PRs.

What ties them together is the shape of the defect: in each case the record said something the evidence did not support.

---

## 1. `hasSuppl: N` believed from a record Europe PMC holds without the files

`suppl_flag_is_authoritative` decides whether Europe PMC's `hasSuppl: N` can be believed as "this article has no supplements". It distrusted the flag for preprints and for articles Europe PMC does not hold, and stopped one case short: an article Europe PMC holds **only as a non-open-access record**, where it has the metadata and none of the supplementary files. There `hasSuppl: N` is a true statement about Europe PMC's holdings and a false one about the article.

When the guard returns True, `need_supplements` is False, so no tier is ever asked for supplements and the manifest records the confident status `none_listed`.

**Measurement.** `10.1038/s41586-026-10510-x` (Nature, paywalled) — `inEPMC=Y, inPMC=Y, hasSuppl=N, isOpenAccess=N`, `PMC13186389` not in the PMC Open Access subset. Recorded `complete pdf=ok suppl=none_listed files=0`, while `landing.html` — the page the browser tier had already loaded and saved for the PDF — lists `MOESM1` through `MOESM13`. The tier had thirteen supplement links in hand and never looked, because the question was already settled.

**Change.** One condition, plus the third case in the docstring with the DOI and the measurement:

```python
if ids.is_open_access is False:
    return False
```

`is False` rather than a falsy test: an absent `isOpenAccess` means unknown, a different claim from a measured N.

**Cost.** Paywalled indexed articles now get a supplement search instead of a confident `none_listed` — more browser-tier work on exactly the papers that already need the proxy. That is the correct trade. Open-access articles that genuinely have no supplements still get `none_listed`, pinned by test rather than asserted.

**Live verification.** `complete pdf=ok suppl=fetched_unverified files=13`, all thirteen MOESM files on disk. `fetched_unverified` rather than `fetched` is correct — the set came from scraping a page, not an archive member list.

**Corpus scan.** Over all 36 `corpus/*/manifest.json`, exactly one article has the affected shape and it is this one. No other re-fetches are implied.

---

## 2. Advice that outlived the obstacle it described

A tier that hits PMC's proof-of-work page says "the browser tier is required for them"; the browser tier bounced off NCBI's bot check says "re-run with `--headed` to collect these supplementary files". Both were glued onto the problem line, so both survived into a finished record even when a later tier had since fetched every supplement from the publisher.

**Measurement.** `10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.038` finishes `complete pdf=ok suppl=fetched_unverified files=6` and still printed both sentences. All six files match the hand-fetched hashes in `manual_fetch.yaml` byte-for-byte:

```
mmc1.pdf MATCH   mmc2.xls MATCH   mmc3.pdf MATCH
mmc4.xls MATCH   mmc5.pdf MATCH   mmc6.pdf MATCH
```

Nothing was missing. The 13 files "behind NCBI's proof-of-work page" are PMC's rendition of the same deposit — redundant, not lost. The output was asking for a headed run over files already on disk.

**Change.** `SourceResult` separates the two. What a tier ran into is a problem and stays in the manifest unconditionally, because it is a record of the run and stays true. What to do about it is `suppl_advice`, which `fetch_publication` emits only when the run ends with supplements still outside `store.SUPPL_SETTLED`. Silencing advice on an *unresolved* obstacle would be the worse failure, so that half is pinned too.

Before and after on the same DOI:

```
- ! 13 supplementary file(s) are behind NCBI's proof-of-work page; the browser tier is required for them
- ! PMC served a bot check to the headless browser; re-run with --headed to collect these supplementary files
+ ! 13 supplementary file(s) are behind NCBI's proof-of-work page
+ ! PMC served a bot check to the headless browser
```

---

## 3. A missing config file, defaulted to in silence

Both CLIs default `--config` to the bare name `config.yaml`, resolved against the current working directory. Run either from a subdirectory — a per-ticket folder under the repo is the case that prompted this — and every key falls back to the built-in defaults, including `corpus_dir`. The fetch then writes to a corpus the extract stage will not read, and nothing says so: the run reports `complete`, writes real files and exits 0.

A `note:` on stderr, matching `_warn_if_no_session` in shape and reason. Not an error and not a failure, because running on defaults is legitimate when deliberate; stderr so it cannot corrupt piped output.

---

## Verification

- **815 passed, 10 skipped** — baseline on `main` is 811; five new tests, two existing tests updated to the split rather than weakened.
- `ruff check --select F manuscript_harvest tests` clean.
- **Each new guard was broken and the corresponding test confirmed to fail**, then restored. For the `hasSuppl` guard the failure was on the paywalled row only — the open-access and unknown rows kept passing, so it pins the new behaviour without masking the old.
- Two live proxy runs, both against ground truth where ground truth exists.

One thing I should flag as *not* attributable to this branch: on my machine `10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.038` also went from `failed`/`expected_but_missing`/0 files to `complete`/6 files. That is environmental — ScienceDirect did not serve a stub page this time — not an effect of any commit here.

author: akshatagarwl
body:
Fixes #156

## The problem

`Tab.astro` dropped the panel inset with `[&:has(>pre)]:p-0`. That rule is right for a panel that *is* a code block — the fence owns its own frame, so insetting it again double-pads it. But `:has(>pre)` also matches a panel holding a fence **and** prose, so the prose lost its padding too. Combined with `[&>:last-child]:mb-0!`, a trailing paragraph ended up flush against the panel border with zero space on any side, and lost its left inset so the text started hard against the frame.

## The fix

```diff
-    "px-4 py-3 [&:has(>pre)]:p-0 [&>:first-child]:mt-0! [&>:last-child]:mb-0!",
+    "px-4 py-3 [&:has(>pre):not(:has(>:not(pre,template)))]:p-0 [&>:first-child]:mt-0! [&>:last-child]:mb-0!",
```

`p-0` now applies only when the panel contains nothing but fences. A mixed fence+prose panel keeps the inset, consistent with every other code-block host (CodeGroup, Steps, Callout, Card, Accordion) per the note in `theme/entry.ts`. I added an explanatory comment above the element, since the selector is hard to read and the `template` exclusion is non-obvious.

## Why `template` must be excluded

When `icon` is set, `Tab.astro` renders a `<template data-blume-tab-icon>` that stays a **permanent child of the panel** — `Tabs.astro` *clones* it into the trigger (`trigger.appendChild(icon.content.cloneNode(true))`) rather than moving the node. So a code-only panel with an icon legitimately has a non-`pre` child, and the naive "is the fence alone?" tests break:

| Selector | Code-only tab **with** `icon` | Code-only tab, **two** fences |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:has(>pre):not(:has(>:not(pre,template)))` | matches (correct) | matches (correct) |
| `:has(>pre:only-child)` | **no match — double inset** | no match |
| `:has(>pre:only-of-type)` | matches | **no match — double inset** |

Excluding `template` handles both cases, which is why this isn't written as `:only-child`/`:only-of-type`. The comment records this so it doesn't get "simplified" later.

## Test plan

Verified on this branch with Tailwind 4.3.3:

- **The selector genuinely compiles.** Built `apps/docs` and grepped the generated CSS — the comma inside the nested `:not()` survives:
  ```css
  .\[\&\:has\(\>pre\)\:not\(\:has\(\>\:not\(pre\,template\)\)\)\]\:p-0:has(>pre):not(:has(>:not(pre,template))){padding:0}
  ```
  The old bare `[&:has(>pre)]:p-0` rule is no longer emitted, and `.px-4`/`.py-3` are intact.
- **Both branches behave**, checked by matching the compiled selector against `Tab.astro`-shaped markup in a DOM engine with `:has()` support: code-only / code-only+icon / multi-fence → `padding: 0`; fence+trailing prose / prose+fence / fence+prose+icon / prose-only → `px-4 py-3`. The `:only-child` and `:only-of-type` regressions in the table above were confirmed the same way.
- `bun run typecheck` — 3/3 tasks pass, 0 errors.
- `bun run check` (`ultracite check`) — 0 warnings, 0 errors, formatting clean.

author: sepehr-safari
body:
You were right, and I fixed the wrong container the first time.
[#133](https://github.com/zig-nostr/plaza/pull/133) kept the preview's text
inside its **card**, measured that, and called it done. The report said
**window**.

Measuring at the narrowest size the window allows, rather than the size it
opens, found two separate causes.

## 1. The floor was seven pixels too small

Every screen needs **687px**: a 56pt rail, the 620pt reading column, and the
11pt scrollbar gutter the virtualList reserves. `app.zon` declared **680**.

The floor was set in #44. The feed became a virtualList later, the gutter came
with it, and nothing moved the floor. The narrowest window the app allowed had
been too small to hold its own content ever since. The link preview is where a
reader *sees* it, because it is the only thing at the column's right edge with a
border of its own to be cut in half.

## 2. A stranger's name can be 354px wider than your window

Display names, NIP-05 handles and profile names arrive over a relay bounded only
by the buffers that receive them, 64 and 128 bytes. Rendered at those lengths:

| | measured past the window edge |
|---|---|
| feed NIP-05 handle | **354px** |
| profile name | **403px** |

`identityBlock`'s comment said `grow` would make a long name ellipsize inside
the block. It does not. `grow` hands out spare space and never takes any back,
so a name wider than the row keeps its width and pushes the handle, the time and
the card's right edge out of the window. That is the same sentence #133 wrote
about the link card, forty lines away in the same file. I fixed the instance in
front of me and did not look for the others.

## The part that took longest to find

A definite width has to be on the **text element**. Same run, same viewport:

| where the width was put | measured right edge |
|---|---|
| nowhere | 1054 |
| grandparent column | 1054 |
| direct parent column | 1054 |
| the `paragraph` itself | bounded |

Single-line text measures at its natural width whatever its ancestors are, and
the default ellipsis cannot elide without a box to be too small for.

## The rule, rather than another comment

`build.zig` now reads `.min_width` out of `app.zon` and hands it to the tests.
The sweep renders **all eight screens at exactly that width**, with every
stranger-supplied field filled to the capacity of its buffer, and fails naming
the offender and the number. The floor and the layout cannot drift apart
silently again, which is the only reason this survived as long as it did.

## Verified

- 331 tests green, `zig fmt --check` clean, `native check` reports the manifest valid
- red first: the sweep failed at 680 with `7px past the edge`, and at buffer-length content with `354px` and `403px`
- each fix reverted by value and required to fail: lowering the floor back to 680, widening the column to 660 (caught, `17px past the edge`), and removing each of the three load-bearing text widths (three findings each)
- one width I added is **not** individually load-bearing: the feed's display-name leaf. 64 characters happens to fit today's type scale. It shares the row's budget so the arithmetic stays true if that scale changes, and I would rather say so than imply it was measured overflowing

author: kirkwaiblinger
body:
<!--
👋 Hi, thanks for sending a PR to typescript-eslint! 💖
Please fill out all fields below and make sure each item is true and [x] checked.
Otherwise we may not be able to review your PR.
-->

## PR Checklist

- [x] Addresses an existing open issue: fixes #8255 
- [x] That issue was marked as [accepting prs](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22accepting+prs%22)
- [x] Steps in [Contributing](https://typescript-eslint.io/contributing) were taken
- [ ] If this PR used AI assistance, I followed the [AI Contribution Policy](https://typescript-eslint.io/contributing/ai-policy/)
   - *_This PR currently contains a lot of AI slop! This is intentional. It's in prototype stage for now, for reviewers to comment on viability and limitations of the rule, not intended for final review yet. I did handwrite quite a few of the test cases, especially as I found various mistakes in the implementation. I also had the AI generate a good chunk of test cases._*

## Overview

I hacked away at this with Claude to see if such a rule is practical. I would encourage checking the branch out and playing with the rule to see what you think, especially regarding unresolved lint reports.

If the rule seems viable, and we finish speccing it out, I'll go in and deslopify the PR.

At a high level, this rule implements the ideas discussed in #8255.
- `using disposable = makeDisposable();` marks the disposable as used.
- `makeDisposable()[Symbol.dispose]();` marks the disposable as used.
- `return makeDisposable()` (in a disposable-returning function) marks the disposable as used
- `acceptsDisposable(makeDisposable())` marks the disposable as used

and one of these must occur in every reachable code path.

- `makeDisposable().property` does _not_ handle a disposable.
- `foo.disposableProperty` does _not_ "produce" a disposable. Only function/constructor calls "produce" a new disposable that needs to be handled.
- Things like `makeDisposable1() || makeDisposable2()` and similar operators are correctly handled, I think. In the `||` case, the overall node produces a disposable that must be handled, no matter which branch it's from, _because disposables are always truthy_. Similarly, `makeDisposable() && whatever` is _never valid_, because if a disposable is produced from `makeDisposable()`, it is immediately floating/unhandled, because it would always be truthy, and would be discarded by the `&&`.
- I made `makeDisposable() satisfies WhateverType;` be considered unhandled (unless of course the overall expression is handled), since the `satisfies` expression just transparently passes the value through without changing the type.
- I made `makeDisposable() as WhateverType;` the same as `satisfies` for now, but I think that's probably incorrect. `foo() as SomeDisposable` should probably "produce" a disposable, and `makeDisposable() as NotADisposable` should probably "handle" the disposable (due to asserting it never was a disposable).

Some big findings:
1. [All built-in iterators are Disposable nowadays](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Iterator/Symbol.dispose) (this was a surprise to me). Therefore, iteration is a valid way of handling iterable disposables.
   - `Array.from(iterable)` isn't implemented yet, but all the bult-in syntaxes, i.e. `for...of`, `const [foo] = iterable`, `yield* iterable`, etc. are handled.
   - The disposable iterators situation _also applies to iterator helpers_. So, something like 
      ```ts
      [1, 2, 3].values().map(value => value + 1).find(value => value === 2);
      ```
      causes many lint reports for now. This is something we'll have to find a way to handle. 
1. Some node.js types do not play well with this rule.
   - `setTimeout()` being disposable is a prime example
   - But also _each line_ of 
      ```ts
       const child = childProcess.spawn(command, args, {
         ...options,
         shell: process.platform === 'win32',
         stdio: 'inherit',
       });

       child.on('error', e => reject(e));
       child.on('exit', () => resolve());
       child.on('close', () => resolve());
       ``` 
       causes a report, since each line returns a disposable.
      
1. We have _lots_ of lint reports in the test code, since lots of the vitest spy/mock objects are disposable. I haven't dug deeply into whether we reasonably could/should refactor the tests to use disposable style, or whether they should be considered problematic false positives. 

1. To address some of the above issues, I wonder whether we should use a heuristic, along the lines of: `disposable.methodReturnsDisposable()` should _not_ be considered a new disposable needing to be handled for the sake of this rule. As long as _either_ `disposable` or `disposable.methodReturnsDisposable()` is handled, both are considered handled. (This would address the `child.on()` calls, and most of the iterator helpers).
1. We probably need to hardcode iterator helpers terminal methods, i.e. `.find()`, `.reduce()`, etc.

author: flyovercoderky
body:
The aggregate Roth conversion path moves money between two different taxpayers, and says nothing about it.

## The defect

`simulate.ts` picks the destination once, as the first Roth account in Plan array order with **no owner predicate**, then draws from every convertible traditional account with **no owner filter**:

```ts
const rothTarget = balances.find((b) => b.account.type === 'roth')
for (const state of balances) {
  if (!isConvertibleToRoth(state.account) || remaining <= 0) continue
```

Nothing reconciles the two. Confirmed against the engine on the cleanest available discriminator — a married household whose only Roth belongs to person A and whose only convertible balance belongs to person B:

```
converted=50000  magi=50000  warnings=[]
```

$50,000 leaves B's traditional IRA, lands in A's Roth, the income is recognised, and **nothing warns**. The runtime journal even records `ownerPersonId` per source while crediting a single destination, so the evidence structure already knows the sources can span owners.

## Why it is not a conversion

- **IRC 408A(d)(3)(B)** states the requirement directly: a distribution from a plan *"maintained for the benefit of an individual which is contributed to a Roth IRA maintained for the benefit of such individual"*.
- **IRC 408(d)(3)(A)** fixes identity at both ends — the flush text requires payment *to* the individual for whose benefit the account is maintained, and clause (i) requires payment *into* an account *"for the benefit of such individual"*.
- **IRC 408A(e)(1)(B)(i)** is what drags §408(d)(3) into the conversion rules at all.

What the engine performs is a taxable distribution to B plus a Roth contribution by A — subject to the §408A(c) limits and AGI phase-out, and here largely an excess contribution attracting the §4973 excise the engine never charges.

**A trap in the chain, recorded in the record:** §408A(d)(3)(A) opens *"Notwithstanding sections 402(c), 403(b)(8), 408(d)(3), and 457(e)(16)"*, which reads as discarding the identity requirement. It does not — it displaces the rollover *exclusion* so the conversion is taxed. Treas. Reg. 1.408A-4 A-1(a) closes it by naming the one-rollover-per-year limit of §408(d)(3)(B) as the **only** carve-out a conversion gets, with the identity requirement not among the exceptions.

## Why `approximated` rather than fixed

Fixing it means deciding **which owner's dollars convert and where each lands** — and `SimulatorOwnedNonRothIraAnnualReplay.aggregateRothDestinationCredit` is not merely singular per year, it is **structurally ownerless**: its type carries `ownerPersonId: null` while `ownerReplays` beside it is a per-owner array. Crediting per owner makes it plural across `ownedNonRothIraRuntimeSourceSeries.ts`, `ownedNonRothIraContiguousReplay.ts`, `ownedNonRothIraAnnualAttemptSettlement.ts` and `annualPassTransaction.ts`.

That is the **same allocation-policy decision the Goal 4 promotion path is blocked on**. This defect and that blocker are one problem, not two — which is the most useful thing this PR establishes.

The enhancement plan's Problem section already described this behaviour (*"deposits the result into the first Roth account, without requiring matching owners"*). It has simply never been machine-checked. Now it is.

## Error direction

`bothDirections`, and my first reading of this was wrong. I argued it was tax-neutral in the conversion year on a joint return; that holds only where **both** spouses have convertible balances. In the discriminator above the authority permits **no conversion at all**, so the entire $50,000 inclusion is spurious and current-year tax is **overstated**. Afterwards it runs the other way — untaxed growth in A's Roth, B's unconsumed nondeductible basis, the uncharged §4973 excise — and overstated again via the §408A(d)(3)(F) clock A never earned. The neutral case is flagged in the rationale so a later reader does not rediscover it and conclude the record overstates the problem.

## The fixture, and its two controls

- **Owners match →** the same request converts the same amount, so the assertion is about *identity* rather than about a conversion happening.
- **No Roth at all →** the same block *does* warn, so the silence above is this path declining to speak rather than a path that never speaks.

One note on the fixture's own history, kept in the test rather than quietly fixed: its first draft asserted `year.warnings`, which does not exist on `YearResult`. It compared `undefined ?? []` against `[]` and passed while proving nothing. Only `tsc` caught it — the exact defect this registry exists to make impossible, reproduced by hand while writing a test for it.

## Evidence

- `npx vitest run --root packages/engine` — **3,916 tests pass**, 205 of 206 files. The one failure is the pre-existing `planJsonSchema.test.ts`, which cannot resolve `ajv` in this worktree; untouched by this branch.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/engine` — clean.
- `npx eslint packages/engine/src/rules` — clean.
- Conformance 35/35. The new `covers every approximated rule` guard from #190 fired on this record the moment it was added and before the fixture existed — its first encounter with a genuinely new record, and it worked.

All five quoted spans were verified by fetching raw GovInfo and eCFR markup, cross-checking every statutory span against law.cornell.edu word-for-word, and then asserting programmatically that each `quotedText` is a literal substring of its source.

author: yellowjackettour
body:
## Outcome

This PR ships the correctness-critical **core** of the requested analytics/portfolio system — a pure, fully-tested vault-aware PnL model — and is being submitted at this scope deliberately rather than bundled with unreviewed API/UI/indexer wiring on top of it. See "What's deferred" below; this is a foundation PR, not the full feature.

`lib/market/portfolio-pnl.ts` computes wallet PnL the way this system actually needs it:

- **Weighted-average cost basis per wallet per vault (generation), never per-NFT-ID FIFO/LIFO.** v-tokens are fungible within a generation — a wallet's position in, say, WormWood is one pooled cost basis, not N individually-tracked lots. Tested directly against what FIFO would say to prove the math diverges correctly (see "a partial sell realizes PnL against the weighted-average cost, not FIFO/LIFO").
- **Valued against redeemable NAV (pool ETH reserve / v-token total supply — the exact `ethReserve`/`totalSupply` pair `lib/market/vault.ts getVaultOnChainSnapshot` already reads), never last-trade price.** `unrealizedPnlWei` takes an explicit NAV-per-share argument and never looks at a trade price at all.
- **Realized vs. unrealized tracked and reported separately** — a decrease (sell/redeem) locks in realized PnL immediately against the running weighted-average cost; unrealized is computed on demand by marking the remaining position against a fresh NAV quote, without needing to replay history.
- **Vault mint/redeem fee drag broken out from raw price movement** (`feeDragWei`), so a wallet's realized PnL line isn't silently conflating "the vault fee cost me X" with "the market moved against me."
- **Trading-volume classification** (`isTradingVolumeEvent`) that matches the requirement directly: AMM `buy`/`sell` against a vault count as volume, `deposit`/`redeem`/`add_lp`/`remove_lp` (internal rebalancing) do not — so a volume chart built on top of this can't be inflated by vault mechanics, consistent with how `lib/market/activity.ts` already keeps vault deposit/redeem out of the collection "sale" feed.

## What's deferred (honest scope cut)

Per the size of the ask and to keep this PR reviewable, this ships the tested math engine only. **Not included in this PR:**

- The event-indexer wiring that turns `lib/market/vault-activity.ts`'s `Bought`/`Sold`/`Deposited`/`Redeemed` log stream into this module's `FlowEvent`s (straightforward — `buy`/`sell` map directly from `ethWei`; `deposit`/`redeem` need a NAV-per-share lookup at that historical block, which needs either an indexed NAV snapshot or a bounded historical `eth_call`).
- Durable storage/cron wiring (`scripts/refresh-market-data.ts` already has the exact pattern this would extend — a new `--pnl` step reading vault-activity + NAV snapshots and writing per-wallet cohort positions to KV/Postgres).
- API routes and UI (portfolio page, floor/volume charts, price alerts).

Given the "zero contract risk, pure data work" framing but the real size of items 1-4 in the ask, landing the tested cost-basis core first (the part most likely to have a subtle sign/rounding bug that everything else depends on) is the safer sequencing than shipping untested indexer→UI plumbing on top of unreviewed math.

## Scope

author: danielrochatka
body:
## Summary

### Defect corrected

When an entry-point load or callable-factory execution fails inside `discover_modules()`, the cleanup step was restoring `project_before` (only modules whose `__file__`/`__path__` is under the configured project module root) instead of `all_before` (the complete pre-attempt snapshot for the package prefix).

This meant that any **pre-existing installed, namespace-package, or other non-project-origin** `sys.modules` entries for the same top-level package name were permanently deleted after a failed EP attempt — even entries that were there before discovery started.

One-line change in `src/cauldron/modules/discovery.py`:

```python
# Before (wrong):
for key, mod in project_before.items():
    sys.modules[key] = mod

# After (correct):
for key, mod in all_before.items():
    sys.modules[key] = mod
```

### Exact restoration semantics

For each entry-point loading attempt:

1. `all_before`: snapshot of every `sys.modules` entry matching the top-level package prefix.
2. `project_before`: the project-origin subset of `all_before`; evicted before `ep.load()` so the EP loads from the installed package.
3. On success: retain the installed package state (neither snapshot is restored).
4. On failure (load or factory exception):
   - remove every current prefix entry from `sys.modules`;
   - restore `all_before` exactly, preserving object identity;
   - call `importlib.invalidate_caches()`.

After a failed attempt the package-prefix portion of `sys.modules` exactly matches its pre-attempt state.

## Tests added

- **`test_failed_ep_restores_preexisting_installed_package`**: pre-imports an installed package and its submodule; runs an EP whose `load()` raises `AttributeError` (missing attribute); asserts that the complete prefix mapping — keys and object identities — is unchanged.
- **`test_failed_factory_restores_preexisting_installed_package`**: same installed package pre-imported; EP returns a callable factory that imports an extra submodule then raises; asserts that the extra submodule is removed and the original package/helper identities are restored exactly.

## Commands run and outcomes

```
python3 tools/arch_check.py
# No architecture violations found.

python3 -m pytest tests/test_module_discovery.py tests/test_module_resolver.py \
  -q -k "not (TestEntryPointDiscovery or TestDuplicateSlugHandling)"
# 175 passed, 10 deselected

python3 -c "from cauldron.modules.discovery import discover_modules; r=discover_modules(); print(f'{len(r.modules)} modules, {len(r.errors)} errors')"
# 5 modules, 0 errors
```

(The 6 `TestFixtureModuleIntegration` failures in `test_module_registry.py`, the 1 `TestEntryPointDiscovery` failure, and the 1 `TestDuplicateSlugHandling` failure pre-exist on `main` and are unrelated to this change.)

author: florianbruckner
body:
### ⚡ Bolt Performance Optimization: Class and Suffix Matching Guards

#### 💡 What
This pull request optimizes the entities matching hot path inside `processDevices` (`src/data-processor.ts`):
1. **Local `hasOwn` Cache**: Caches `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` as a module-scoped constant `hasOwn` to completely bypass expensive dynamic prototype lookups.
2. **Device Class Matching Guard**: Guards the device class resolution block with `matchedClassesCount < requiredClasses.size || !hasAnchor`. Once all required classes and the anchor class are resolved, this bypasses attributes property lookup, device class checking, and Set queries entirely during subsequent iterations.
3. **Suffix Matching Fast-Continue**: Performs a fast `entitiesBySuffix[key] !== undefined` lookup first inside the suffix-matching loop and continues early, entirely avoiding the performance-heavy `String.prototype.endsWith` check on already matched suffix columns.

#### 🎯 Why
During frequent Home Assistant state updates, `processDevices` is invoked under high frequency. Each device is associated with a raw list of entities, which are iterated over to resolve the configuration columns (device class columns and suffix columns). Performing dynamic property checks, Set lookups, and suffix string comparisons on every entity in every device loop accumulates substantial rendering latency and garbage collection pressure. Adding fast-paths and early continues eliminates unnecessary checks.

#### 📊 Impact
- Bypasses redundant attributes lookups and `Set.has` operations.
- Avoids multiple redundant `endsWith` string function executions during nested device entity matching.
- Accelerates the overall execution of `processDevices` for configurations with multiple columns, contributing to smoother dashboard rendering.

#### 🔬 Measurement & Verification
- Validated formatting with `pnpm exec prettier --write src/data-processor.ts`.
- Ran and passed ESLint checks with `pnpm lint`.
- Ran and passed the complete Web Test Runner suite with `pnpm test`. All 64 tests passed seamlessly with zero regressions!

author: nathanneurotic
body:
Addresses zackcage6's repeated report: **error/notice message boxes show the previous frame as their background.**

## Cause

`guiMsgBox` and `guiRenderTextScreen` draw their background with `guiShow()`, which renders the current `screenHandler`. During a screen transition (the 26-frame cross-fade after `guiSwitchScreen`), `guiShow()` deliberately renders the **old, fading-out** screen for the first half. So a box raised right as a transition begins — exactly when errors tend to fire (pick a game → transition → launch fails) — sits on the previous screen for ~13 frames.

Verified the main screen otherwise repaints its own background every frame (`menuRenderMain` → theme background element), so `guiShow()` is not itself a stale-frame source outside a transition.

## Fix

`guiSnapTransition()` completes any in-flight transition to its destination before the box renders — the same state assignments `guiShow()` makes when a fade finishes naturally. One file, +29 lines. The input-freeze release timing shift it introduces is benign (documented inline; the box consumes its own edge-triggered dismiss).

## Deliberately out of scope

The other 'wrong background' shape — a box raised from a **settings flow** rendering the main screen instead of the dialog behind it — is **not** handled here. I prototyped it (record the active dialog, render it under the box) and adversarial review caught that it reintroduces the **#154 dangling-enum landmine**: the deferred error hook fires *after* the dialog's `guiShowXxx` setup returns and its **stack-local** enum arrays die, so rendering that dialog then dereferences freed stack (confirmed reachable via Network → Reconnect → sync eth re-init failure). A safe version requires making the affected dialog enum arrays `static` first — a separate change, only if the transition snap doesn't fully cover the report.

Separate from the #340 input work. HW test pending.

author: waelosamahelmi
body:
Found by auditing every studio's model pool against the live production catalog.

## Text-to-Video was listing models that cannot do text-to-video
The coarse `"video"` capability was folded into the `ttv` group because ~27 live models carry it — but several are unambiguously **image-to-video** (`wan-2.6-i2v`, `wan-2.7-i2v`, `wan-2.5-i2v`, …) or **video-to-video** (`wan-2.6-v2v`, `wan-2.6-flash-v2v`, `pixverse/extend`). They need a source image or clip, so picking one in T2V fails. `wan-2.6-v2v` was the **cheapest** entry in the pool, so any cost-sorted pick landed on it.

`inferCapability` now reads the unambiguous id markers (`-i2v` / `-v2v` / `-t2v`) first and only falls back to coarse `"video"` for models that genuinely accept text+image+video (`kling/*`, `bytedance/seedance-*`, `wan-animate-*`). Deliberately conservative — a model is only moved when its id leaves no doubt.

## Music was listing transformers, not composers
The Music studio's cheapest entry was `replace-section`, which edits an existing track. `cover-suno`, `extend-music`, `add-vocals`, `add-instrumental`, `upload-and-*`, `generate-mashup` and `boost-music-style` all require an existing track — they now classify into the utility/enhancement buckets **Audio Tools** lists, leaving Music to actual composers.

## Agent default is capability-aware
Picking purely on price resolved an audio step to `boost-music-style` — a utility. The default now respects what the step needs to produce.

The backfill script (`scripts/fix-model-categories.mjs`) persists the corrected capabilities; dry-run by default, idempotent.

## Tests
1128 unit / 100 integration / **174 e2e passed, 0 failed** across chromium, firefox, webkit and the new mobile project.

Numa carga de boletos, 5 PDFs cairam em "revisao manual" com *cliente X nao encontrado por nome nem pelo titulo Y*. **Tres desses clientes EXISTEM no cadastro** (RONILDA = 907, REGINALDO = 858, RUAN VITOR = 921).

O PostgREST corta a resposta em **1000 linhas** e a base tem **1325 clientes** — 25% do cadastro ficava invisivel para o matcher.
