Follow-up to the review of #1423, and the answer to "is this ready to promote?" — the one part of that change nobody can test before it ships.

## Why

Scheduled workflows run **only from the default branch**. So `aviation-data.yml`'s rewritten fail-closed logic cannot execute until it is on main — today's runs (17:17, 15:39) all used main's *old* code. The pre-merge signal was a grep of the workflow text:

```js
expect(aviation).toContain('if (wxOk)');
```

which cannot distinguish a working guard from a commented-out one, on the rule that decides whether the app's weather is published at all.

Extracted to `scripts/build-aviation-feeds.mjs` with the fetch injected — the same move #1423 made for `finalize-ims-manifests.mjs`. The job gains the checkout the heredoc never needed: read-only, with `persist-credentials: false`, since the data branches are pushed with an explicit x-access-token URL rather than the checkout's token.

## The first test found a live defect

```js
metars = await api('metar');              // assigns FIRST
if (!Array.isArray(metars)) throw ...;    // validates second
```

A 200 carrying a JSON object — an error envelope, a quota notice — leaves a non-array in `metars`. The catch sets `metarsOk = false` as intended, but the later `for (const m of metars)` throws an **uncaught TypeError** and kills the step, instead of printing *"publish skipped; preserving last-good branch."*

Fail-closed by crash, and not harmlessly: `sigmet.json` has already been written by then and is never published, because the publish step belongs to a job that just failed. So a malformed upstream response silently stops SIGMET updates too. Values are assigned only after validation now, and `collectStations` defends itself since it is exported.

## Coverage that was impossible before

Nine tests, including the two rules and *why they differ*:

| case | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| no SIGMETs over Israel | **published** — emptiness is real information; withholding would freeze an expired SIGMET on the map |
| empty station map | **withheld** — never real; would blank every field's METAR and TAF while reporting success |
| response lost `icaoId` | withheld — the likelier failure than an empty array, and `Array.isArray` alone waves it through |
| TAF fails, METAR fine | WX withheld whole; SIGMET unaffected |
| non-array body, total outage | nothing published, last-good untouched |

## Note on the tests I moved

The `workflow-hardening` assertions that grepped those strings out of the YAML now assert the wiring instead. Last time I moved a string out of a workflow I did not grep the suite first and e2e found it for me — so this time I did.

Full suite running; targeted specs 23 passing.

author: milyin
body:
Part of the `syntax → model` transition (umbrella #314). The endgame stage, as written into the umbrella after S35.

## What `produced` was

Every wrapper arm took `produced: &syn::Type` — "the Rust type the converter's function **yields**" — plus a `canonical` shape rebuilt from `t1`, and compared them token for token to discover what transparent wrappers stood between:

```rust
fn bridge_layers(spelling: &syn::Type, canonical: &syn::Type) -> Option<Vec<&'static WrapperOps>> {
    if spelling.to_token_stream().to_string() == canonical.to_token_stream().to_string() {
        return Some(Vec::new());
    }
    let (name, inner) = peel_transparent(spelling)?;
    …
}
```

That is `TypeRef::erased_wrappers()` — asked of the classification instead of re-derived from tokens, through a token-string comparison the ledger lists as a blind spot.

## Why it could not just take a reading

**One arm composes what it yields.** A `&[T]` parameter decodes to an owned `Vec<T>` the call site borrows, and #280 seals minting to the model, so `api::lang` has no way to produce that reading. The old code's comment said exactly this and concluded `produced` had to stay a spelling.

The conclusion doesn't follow — the parameter just needs to name the two cases the code already had:

```rust
pub(crate) enum Produced<'a> {
    Reading(&'a TypeRef),
    /// Composed by the adapter — no erased wrappers by construction.
    Composed(Box<syn::Type>),
}
```

`Composed` answers "no wrappers" structurally, which is what its token comparison against the canonical form was computing the long way round.

## What that removed

| | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `bridge_layers(spelling, canonical)` | peel `peel_transparent` until token-equal | `Produced::bridge_layers` over `erased_wrappers()` |
| `is_canonical_spelling(produced, canonical)` | `bridge_layers(..).is_some_and(is_empty)` | `Produced::is_canonical` |
| `read_as_canonical` / `build_from_canonical` | took `canonical` | don't |
| the five `let canonical: syn::Type = …` locals | rebuilt `&t1` / `Option<&t1>` / `Vec<t1>` / `Option<t1>` | gone |
| `output_wrapper_shape`'s two `if let syn::Type::Reference(r) = produced` | node match + `r.mutability.is_none()` | `Produced::borrow`, off `TypeKind::Ref` |
| the selector's optional-borrow guard | rebuild `Option<inner>`, compare token strings | `!ty.erased_wrappers().is_empty()` |

## Measurement

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| classification sites | 68 | **65** |
| escapes: types | 4 | **2** |
| escapes: items | 15 | 15 |

```
api/lang/jnigen/jni/selector.rs    [types]           2 -> 0
api/lang/jnigen/jni/trait_impl.rs  [classification]  4 -> 1
```

**Two type escapes left in the whole crate:**

* `cbindgen/trait_impl.rs` — `convert_with`'s reading, spelled for cbindgen's own selector chain, which still takes `&syn::Type`. The same move this PR makes on the jnigen side.
* `jnigen/jni/trait_impl.rs` — `self.types[key].rust_type`, the declare-phase read #291 documents as answerable only by the declaration: `reading()` legitimately returns `None` for a type nothing has interned yet.

## The claim

**Artifacts byte-identical.** That is the whole verification here: `erased_wrappers()` had to answer exactly what the token comparison answered, for every crossing in both examples, in both directions. A single disagreement — a fully-qualified `std::option::Option`, a `Box` the model erases but the comparison did not — would show up as a diff.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p prebindgen --all-features` — 638 lib, 22 doctests
- ledger regenerated, diff above
- clippy `--all-targets --all-features -D warnings` on stable **and** 1.85.0 (`large_enum_variant` on the new enum: the composed `syn::Type` is boxed)
- `cargo fmt --check` with the CI config
- `examples/regen-check.sh` — every generated artifact byte-identical

author: tsouza
body:
## Summary

- `internal/preflight/preflight.go` declares `minCHBase = 24.8` as cerberus's supported ClickHouse floor, but every CI substrate (`compatibility/{prometheus,loki,tempo}`, chDB-backed spec/property tests) runs ClickHouse 26.5 — so nothing automated ever exercised the 24.8-safe fallback SQL that `internal/chopt`'s version-gated feature registry protects.
- Verified the floor is real engineering, not fiction, before deciding the fix shape: reviewed `internal/chopt/registry.go` (every >24.8 feature — `ts_grid_*`, `condition_cache`, etc. — is `AutoSelect`-gated behind a documented `MinVersion` with a 24.8-safe fallback path) and locally ran a built cerberus binary against a genuine `clickhouse-server:24.8`, seeded via cerberus's own DDL/seed path. Startup resolved `server_ts_grid_capability=forbidden`, and a battery of `rate`/`increase`/`changes`/`resets`/`deriv`/`predict_linear`/`histogram_quantile`/`label_replace` queries all returned correct `200`s — confirming the fallback SQL genuinely works end to end.
- Given that evidence, the fix is to add automated coverage at the floor (Option A) rather than raise `minCHBase` to match what CI already runs (Option B) — the floor is honest, only untested.
- Adds `compatibility/prometheus-floor`: parametrises `compatibility/prometheus/docker-compose.yml`'s ClickHouse image via a new `CH_IMAGE` build arg (default unchanged, `26.5`) and adds a new `compatibility.yml` job that runs the exact same PromQL differential corpus against `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8`, gated by the same `compat-ratchet.mjs` against the same `compatibility/parity-baseline.json` `prometheus` roster — so a floor-only divergence is a real, tracked regression, not a second driftable baseline. Informational for now (not a branch-protection-required check), matching the existing `compatibility/promql-surface` / `schema-integration.yml` "soak on main first" precedent; promoting it to required needs a maintainer branch-protection edit out of this PR's scope.
- Also fixes `internal/preflight/preflight.go`'s stale comment, which incorrectly claimed the differential suite already ran 24.8.

Closes #1500

## Design fork: floor-pinned CI lane vs. raising `minCHBase` — the evidence

A reviewer's prior might be that `minCHBase` should simply move up to 25.8+
because `timeSeries*ToGrid` needs it — i.e. that 24.8 is just wrong, not
merely untested. That isn't what the registry says:

- `versions.yaml` carries **two** distinct version floors: `min_clickhouse:
  "24.8"` (the base preflight floor) and `min_native_rate: "25.9"` (a
  separately-tracked, higher floor for the native-rate feature family).
- `internal/chopt/registry.go` confirms these aren't independent numbers —
  they're exactly the floor split the registry already enforces per-feature.
  The *entire* `ts_grid_*` family (`Range`/`Resample`/`Changes`/`Resets`/
  `Deriv`/`PredictLinear`/`Recollapse`, i.e. `timeSeries*ToGrid`) is
  `MinVersion: 25.9`, `Stability: Experimental`, `RequiresExperimentalTSGrid:
  true` — floored at exactly `min_native_rate`, and gated behind an
  additional explicit opt-in on top of the version check, so it is never
  silently smuggled under the base floor regardless of server version. The
  only two `Stable`/`AutoSelect` features below that are
  `FeatureAggregationInOrder` (`MinVersion: 24.8`) and
  `FeatureConditionCache` (`MinVersion: 25.3`) — both comfortably covered by
  `minCHBase = 24.8`'s fallback path (aggregation-in-order's floor **is**
  24.8; condition-cache is `Stable`/`AutoSelect` but resolves OFF below its
  own 25.3 floor, exercising the same no-condition-cache fallback branch the
  24.8 lane already runs).
- In other words: 24.8 is coherent as the *base* floor precisely because the
  one feature family that would force it higher (`ts_grid_*`/native-rate) is
  already tracked under its own, higher, separately-enforced floor
  (`min_native_rate`) — not because nothing above 24.8 exists.
- This is confirmed empirically, not just by registry inspection: the local
  24.8 run described above genuinely goes green (all sampled functions
  return correct `200`s, `ts_grid` resolves `forbidden` and the fallback path
  answers instead) — if it hadn't, that would have been the answer to this
  fork, and `minCHBase` would need to move instead. It didn't, so it doesn't.

## Version-sync gate fix (CI feedback on this PR)

The first push broke the required `ch version-sync gate`
(`.github/scripts/clickhouse-version-sync.mjs`):
`compatibility/prometheus/docker-compose.yml: could not read the clickhouse
image tag`. Root cause: this PR's `image:
${CH_IMAGE:-clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.5}` interpolation (needed so the
new floor lane can override the tag) doesn't match the gate's old
literal-tag-only regex.

The fix teaches the gate about the floor lane as a first-class concept
instead of loosening the regex to tolerate interpolation (which would make
the gate pass while making it *less* true):

- `readComposeCHTag` now understands the `${VAR:-default}` form and returns
  the `:-` default — still the honest "what does this file pin" answer for
  the existing substrate-consistency checks.
- New check **(f)**: reads `compatibility.yml`'s `prometheus-floor` job's
  `CH_IMAGE` and asserts it equals `versions.yaml`'s `min_clickhouse`. This
  is what turns "one lane deliberately runs below `chdb_substrate`" into a
  tracked invariant instead of an unenforced escape hatch — if `minCHBase`
  (or the floor job's `CH_IMAGE`) ever drifts, check (f) catches it.
- Self-test extended (interpolated-default parse, floor-job-block
  extraction, and two new drift cases for check (f)); `--self-test` passes
  27/27, and the plain gate run against the live tree passes all checks
  (a)–(f), including `(f) prometheus-floor CH_IMAGE == min_clickhouse 24.8`.
- `docs/optimization-rules.md`, `.github/scripts/README.md`, and
  `docs/test-strategy.md` updated to state the invariant explicitly: every
  compatibility lane tracks `chdb_substrate` except `prometheus-floor`, which
  tracks `min_clickhouse`.

## Floor-lane flake fix: `-query-parallelism` (CI feedback on this PR, round 2)

Once the version-sync gate above was fixed, the new `compatibility/prometheus-floor`
job itself started failing reproducibly (2/2 independent CI runs, byte-identical
results): 20 of 739 cases — `histogram_quantile`, `resets`, `changes`, `clamp*` —
came back with `"unexpectedFailure": "Post \"http://localhost:29091/api/v1/query_range\":
context deadline exceeded"` and an empty `diff`, which the ratchet correctly read as
ARRIVED-FAILING against the shared 26.5-lane baseline.

This mattered directly for the design fork above: if the floor genuinely couldn't
answer these queries, `minCHBase` would need to move, not just gain a CI lane. So
before treating it as a harness bug, I ran the two hypotheses down:

- **Isolated latency.** Curled each failing query individually against a live
  24.8-pinned stack: all returned `200` in under 3s (`histogram_quantile` worst
  case ~2.1s, `resets`/`changes`/`clamp*` all <0.15s). Not a correctness gap.
- **Root cause.** `promql-compliance-tester`'s comparer
  (`upstream/promql/comparer/comparer.go`) wraps every comparison's ref+test
  `QueryRange` pair in one hardcoded `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)`
  with no flag to raise it, and the harness runs at the tester's default
  `-query-parallelism 20`. Below `min_native_rate` (25.9, #1500) every
  `ts_grid_*` feature resolves OFF, so the floor lane's fallback SQL does real
  per-row rate/quantile/reset aggregation instead of ClickHouse's native
  windowed functions — genuinely slower per query, and 20-way concurrency
  queues enough of those slower queries behind each other that some
  individually-fast queries miss the shared 10s deadline on pure contention.
- **Reproduced and fixed.** Firing the failing-query set at the same
  concurrency against a 2-vCPU-constrained container (matching a GH Actions
  standard run

body:
`71107` Queen's Bedchamber (m11_00) is reachable only **through the Erdtree Sanctuary**, i.e. past Morgott, so force-lighting it on region-open handed the player a warp to the far side of the capital's last fight.

Our own table already agreed with that reading and then contradicted itself: **71100 Elden Throne and 71101 Erdtree Sanctuary are both withheld** (9005810 asset-hidden, caught by the EMEVD oracle). We were withholding the grace AT the door and granting the one BEYOND it.

## Which set, and why not the other one

`_STATE_GATED_GRACE_FLAGS`, not `_BOSS_GATED_GRACE_FLAGS`. Like 76314 Capital Rampart, 71107 is **not** 9005810 asset-hidden -- the EMEVD oracle does not see it, so putting it in the derived set would be a hand entry that oracle actively disagrees with. It is a physically-present grace sealed by a boss-defeat state, which is precisely what the state-gated set is for.

## Effect

```python
'Leyndell': [71102, 71103, 71104, 71105, 71108, 71109]   # was [..., 71107, ...]
'Leyndell': [71102],  # East Capital Rampart -- landmark unchanged
```

Leyndell keeps its other six; the front door and the `REGION_GRACE_LANDMARKS` entry are untouched. `region_graces: 350 graces across 30 regions` (was 351).

## Verification

- Regen clean, `test_gf_data` green, and the three HTML pages regenerated for the `inputs_hash` ripple so `generators` should not trip.
- ⚠️ `test_gf_grace_gates` / `test_gf_grace_entrance` / `test_gf_grace_ground` need the AP tree (`BaseClasses`), which I cannot stand up in the sandbox -- those are CI's.

author: waelosamahelmi
body:
The studio was "complicated on phones". This measures the problem on a real phone viewport first, then fixes what it found.

## Measured, not guessed
Adds a `mobile` Playwright project (Pixel 5, 393×851, real touch) — **there was no mobile coverage at all before**. Its assertions are: no horizontal page scroll, every interactive control ≥44×44px, nothing hidden without a way to reach it.

**Before: 44 distinct offender types across 6 surfaces. After: 0 across all 8 sweeps.**

Worst offender: the announcement bar's dismiss button at **14×14px**.

## Reachability
The agent's side panel — balance, **Clear conversation**, plan summary, produced outputs — was unreachable on phones *and tablets*. The audit thought a `display:none` rule hid it; the truth was worse: a later equal-specificity rule kept it displayed, so it rendered but sat stacked underneath inside an `overflow:hidden` container. Present in the DOM, reachable by no gesture. Every other surface already had a way back; the agent now does too.

## Touch paths for drag-only interactions
Canvas layers, workflow steps and Director timeline clips all reorder by drag, which never fires on touch. Each now has a touch-capable path; mouse drag is untouched.

## Two blocking defects found while testing
- **Canvas was unusable from a cold start on any phone**: `.st-canvas__surface` computed to **0px tall** at 393px, and the empty-state card swallowed every tap.
- A CSS specificity bug meant small icon buttons stayed 32px on touch despite a rule intended to make them 44px.

## Also
Admin tables stack into label/value rows instead of trapping users in a nested sideways scroller; the 15-item admin nav gets a real affordance; and the studio's generation toasts were rendering **completely unstyled** because the component used classes that only load on the landing page — now on the app's own (previously unused) toast system.

## Tests

body:
## Problem

`frequentist/__init__.py` re-exports `t_test_continuous`, but the function is spelled `t_test_continous`. The `ImportError` fires on **any** import from the subpackage, so nothing in the package is usable:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 't_test_continuous'
from 'ab_testing.frequentist.continuous'
```

`t_test_summary` and `t_test_binary` are collateral damage — they import fine on their own, but `__init__.py` raises before they are reachable.

Confirmed on a clean clone and a real editable install: `pip install -e .` succeeds (exit 0, version resolves to 0.1.0), and then every import fails.

## Fix

One line — corrects the spelling at the definition rather than matching the misspelling in the re-export. Nothing outside `__init__.py` referenced the old name, so there is nothing else to update.

## Behaviour is unchanged

Deliberately scoped to the rename. Verified field-for-field against the pre-rename package:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| continuous, clean | identical |
| continuous, 25:75 split | identical |
| binary, clean 0/1 | identical |
| binary, bool metric column | identical |
| binary, NaN in metric | identical error |
| binary, non-binary values | identical error |
| binary, rare event | identical error |
| continuous, int assignment column | identical error |
| continuous, NaN in metric | identical error |

Every `TTestResult` field matches exactly, and every error path raises the same type with the same message.

Post-fix, on a clean venv:

```
from ab_testing.frequentist import TTestResult, t_test_summary, t_test_binary, t_test_continuous  -> OK
```

## Not included

Left alone deliberately, happy to follow up separately:

- `README.md` documents `from ab_testing import t_test_summary`, which still fails — the root `__init__.py` only sets `__version__`. The working import is `from ab_testing.frequentist import t_test_summary`, as the root docstring itself says.
- The README's "groups have equal sizes (50:50 split)" bullet isn't required by the maths — Welch handles unequal n, verified at 25:75.

author: edbertchan
body:
## Summary

On Aug 4 the Slack bot answered everything with "Invoker is down" for 15+ minutes. Invoker was not gone: a GUI instance held the database.

That GUI held the DB writer lock but never served the IPC socket. The bot could not reach it, and every owner it spawned died on the held lock.

Nothing recovered from this state. Relaunches failed forever, the launch throttle made the bot claim failure without attempting anything, and doomed spawns could unlink the live socket file.

This PR makes the state self-healing and self-diagnosing. A spawned owner that loses the lock now pings the holder over the socket first.

A healthy owner answers and the spawn exits cleanly. Silence means the lock-holder deadlock is reported with the holder PID.

Lock-holding owners run a sentinel that pings their own socket path and re-serves it if it vanishes.

The transport layer only unlinks a socket file after a refused connect proves it dead.

The Slack manager reports launch outcomes truthfully: throttled, failed, or deadlocked with the holder PID. An explicit `@Invoker restart` may SIGTERM a re-confirmed-unreachable holder; the automatic watchdog never kills anything.

## Review Claim

A process holding the Invoker DB writer lock is always reachable on the message bus or gets replaced: the spawn-side ping, the owner-side socket sentinel, the transport-side unlink guard, and truthful supervisor escalation close the lock-holder deadlock from every side.

## Review Lane

behavior

## Review Unit

routing

## Safety Invariant

The writer lock is never stolen: dead/recycled-PID reclaim is untouched, probes are read-only pings, and the sentinel re-serves the socket only inside the process that already holds the lock. Only an explicit human `@Invoker restart` may SIGTERM a holder, only after a fresh failed ping, never its own process, and stale-socket reclaim still requires a refused connect as proof of death.

## Slice Rationale

All five commits close one incident class from its different sides — app owner startup, owner self-check, supervisor messaging, transport socket handling — so they ship as one reviewable stack. Slice 1 defines the tri-state spawn exit, slice 2 enforces the invariant it diagnoses, slice 3 consumes it in the supervisor, slice 4 closes the socket-unlink entry path, slice 5 trims comments only.

## Non-goals

No change to the `cleanElectronEnv` / `INVOKER_HEADLESS_STANDALONE` env leak (in-flight separately), no change to Slack workflow-op semantics, no new headless commands, and no change to single-owner election on a healthy boot.

## Architecture

### Before

```mermaid
graph TD
    B["slack-manager watchdog"] -->|"spawn owner-serve"| S["spawned owner"]
    S -->|"writer lock held by live PID"| X["fatal exit, no diagnosis"]
    G["GUI owner (holds DB lock, socket lost)"] -.->|"unreachable over IPC"| B
    B -->|"throttled or failed"| M["'could not bring it back' (forever)"]
```

### After

```mermaid
graph TD
    B["slack-manager watchdog"] -->|"spawn owner-serve"| S["spawned owner"]
    S -->|"lock lost: probe owner-ping"| P{"holder answers?"}
    P -->|"yes"| OK["exit 0: owner already running"]
    P -->|"no"| SB["exit 1: owner-split-brain + holder PID"]
    G["lock-holding owner"] -->|"socket sentinel: self-ping, re-serve if lost"| G
    B -->|"throttled / failed / split-brain reported truthfully"| U["operator"]
    U -->|"explicit @Invoker restart"| K["SIGTERM re-confirmed-unreachable holder, respawn"]
```

## Visual Proof

This change has no window/UI behavior (main.ts edits are headless owner-serve wiring only); the observable surface is terminal output. Captures show the incident repro (writer lock held by a live, IPC-silent PID in an isolated `INVOKER_DB_DIR`) run against the real binary on origin/master and on this branch.

![origin/master build: generic writer-lock fatal with no diagnosis](https://pub-cf646cda2bd945d683792ee19b5f9d98.r2.dev/pr-images/20260804-37db96/master-build.png)

![this branch: distinct owner-split-brain error naming the live unreachable holder PID](https://pub-cf646cda2bd945d683792ee19b5f9d98.r2.dev/pr-images/20260804-37db96/branch-build.png)

## Test Plan

<details>
<summary>Test Plan</summary>

- [x] `cd packages/app && pnpm test` (1851 passed; the 2 failures are pre-existing on origin/master, verified in a clean worktree)
- [x] `cd packages/slack-manager && pnpm test` (46 passed; 1 pre-existing failure on origin/master)
- [x] `cd packages/transport && pnpm test` (50 passed)
- [x] `pnpm run check:types`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Incident repro against an isolated `INVOKER_DB_DIR`: hold `invoker.db.lock` with a live dummy PID and run `node scripts/electron.cjs packages/app/dist/main.js --headless owner-serve` — before: generic writer-lock fatal; after: `[owner-split-brain]` naming the holder PID

</details>

## Revert Plan

<details>
<summary>Revert Plan</summary>

- Safe to revert? Yes
- Revert command: `git revert 8ede903c4 1e34f2c47 7392494f9 7bf9eb86b 181c3a11a`
- Post-revert steps: restart the slack-manager daemon so it returns to the boolean launch() result
- Data migration? No

</details>

author: 0xb007ab1e
body:
## Found by reviewing the converge diff
Now that converge runs again (#93/#94), the first thing the diff showed was **my own bug from #92**:

```diff
-      - fablab
-      - shared_1
+      - fablab      - shared_1    healthcheck:
```

A converge would have written a **malformed `compose.yaml`**, `docker compose up` would have failed, and **staging's database would have gone down** — the exact outage #92 was meant to prevent.

## Cause
I validated the template with plain **jinja2**, where `trim_blocks` defaults to **False**. `ansible.builtin.template` renders with **`trim_blocks=True`**. Under that setting, the `{%- … %}` / `{%- endfor %}` markers I added as a "whitespace tidy" strip the newlines the loop body needs, collapsing the lines. Without the markers, `trim_blocks` alone produces exactly the right output.

## Fix + validation
Reverted to plain `{% for %}` / `{% endfor %}`, then validated **the way Ansible renders**:
- rendered with `trim_blocks=True` → `yaml.safe_load` **parses**; service networks `['fablab', 'shared_1']`; `shared_1` → `name: coolify, external: true`
- rendered output is **byte-identical** to the `compose.yaml` currently running on the VPS
- `make converge-check` against the real host: **no change reported** for *"mongodb : Render the compose file"* (drift 10 → 9 tasks)

## Lesson
Validate Ansible templates the way Ansible renders them, not with default jinja2. My local check passing is what let this through.

author: aeplay
body:
Specification only — no implementation, no behaviour change.

## Why

#1217 enabled every dormant test target. Three of the tests it surfaced are red
on the integration branch, all on the same guard at
`crates/jazz/src/tools/client.rs:1933`:

- `local_join_query_uses_current_permissions_for_joined_provenance_after_lens_transform`
- `table_rename_join_query_translates_join_target_on_old_branch`
- `table_rename_fk_array_lookup_finds_related_rows_on_old_branch`

Two need joins, one needs array subqueries. Core does lower `Query::joins`, but
only as a **root-row membership join** whose normalized result is a single
`RealRow` from the root table. These tests need a flattened cross-table result,
which neither `crate::query::Query` nor the relation facade can represent — the
facade explicitly normalizes to one output table.

Building this in the client instead would be the semantic duplication catalogued
in `dev/TS_SEMANTIC_DUPLICATION_AUDIT.md`, and would drift from core's
permission, provenance and ordering semantics — which is precisely what these
three tests assert.

## What this defines

`crates/jazz/SPEC/6_queries.md` and `crates/groove/SPEC/3_queries_operators.md`
now specify:

- **composite source-slot identity** for a result carrying columns from more
  than one source table;
- **per-source provenance and permissions after lens transforms** — a row must
  not become visible merely by being joined to a visible row;
- **stable cross-source ordering**;
- **identical one-shot and maintained semantics.** One-shot is the first-delta
  observation of the maintained program, not a separately assembled join, so
  the differential oracle stays meaningful. A maintained source delta emits only
  affected composite-row transitions and MUST NOT re-materialize or diff
  accumulated output state (`INV-INC-1`);
- **descriptor inputs required by `INV-QUERY-1A`** — ordered source-role/output
  schema, source table and read-view selections, projection mapping, join keys
  and null/inner semantics, per-source policy programs with canonical claim
  declarations, lens projections, ordering and window config, and the
  provenance/version fields needed at the terminal. Subject-specific claim
  values stay execution bindings, not baked constants, so node sharing remains
  sound.

## Feasibility: this is not a small change

Estimated **10–15 engineer-days plus soak and gate time**, touching the query
AST and lowering, terminal record descriptors, `CurrentRow` and the read APIs,
protocol and wire result members, maintained-view transition state, peer result
indexing and delivery, per-source provenance resolution, and core-owned array
result shaping.

So this is posted as a decision aid, not a plan of record. The three tests stay
red behind the guard until it is scheduled; `result_element_index` shares the
same blocker.

Landing the contract now means the eventual implementation has something to be
measured against, and that the reason those tests are red is written down rather
than remembered.

body: Unblocks the `check-skills` lane, red on `main` since 2026-07-25 (HIL-2820), which is blocking #24 and the #25 draft stacked on it. ## The failure `hiloop runs tree` no longer exists. The `runs` group is `list` / `show` / `tail` / `complete`. ## Verification Everything here was checked against the published **hiloop 0.16.0** binary, with `--help` run on every command documented. `runs tree`, `--lineage-path`, `--trace`, `--usage`, and `--subtree` were each confirmed *rejected by the parser*, not merely undocumented. `--columns` appears nowhere in the CLI's 1802-line help tree. `./scripts/check-skills.sh` with 0.16.0 on PATH: - on `origin/main`: reproduces exactly the two reported failures, exit 1 - on this branch: `OK: 12 skills — structure + CLI commands (24 top-level) all valid.`, exit 0 The check-existence layer really ran (24 top-level commands parsed), so this is not a skipped-layer false green. ## Scope: five occurrences, not two The CLI-existence layer only scans **fenced code blocks**, so it flagged 2 of 5 `runs tree` uses. The other three sit in inline prose and were equally stale: | file | how it read | caught by CI | |---|---|---| | `querying-observability-trees` §2 (×2) | code block | yes | | `autoresearch` §7 | code block | yes | | `annotating-runs` | prose | no | | `snapshotting-and-forking` | prose | no | | `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt` | index listings | no | ## The substitutions - **A lineage listing → `runs list --root-run-id `.** Verified: the flag sends `root_run_id` on `GET /v1/runs`. - **A `--columns ':'` projection → `query --sql` over the matching `ann_` view, scoped by `root_run_id`.** The views carry the fixed annotation context columns (`run_id`, `root_run_id`, `lineage_path`, …) and already return the current annotation per anchor, so the latest-value rollup `--columns` rendered is exactly one query. Every SQL column used here is documented in `references/events-sql.md` and present in the service's column list. ## Verdict on `querying-observability-trees`: rewrite, not delete Its premise is intact. The skill is about telemetry keyed by run lineage, and that model is fully live: `root_run_id` and `lineage_path` are real columns, they are the documented scoping mechanism, and `runs list --root-run-id` scopes a tree natively. What was withdrawn is one *rendering* verb, not the tree. Eight of nine sections needed no change, and §5 already taught the real mechanism (prefix predicates) with `runs tree` as mere convenience on top. Deleting would discard the still-accurate capture / query / tail / diff / annotations / data-views material that lives nowhere else. ## Additional drift removed Found while verifying the paragraphs above; all parser-rejected on 0.16.0: - `--lineage-path` on `query` and `runs tail` (§3, §5, §6, and the events-SQL reference). §5 is load-bearing for the tree framing that now replaces `runs tree`, so leaving it would have pointed readers at a broken command. The prefix-predicate SQL it becomes is the same idiom the reference doc already uses. - `runs show --trace` and `runs tree --usage` (same paragraph as the removed verb). - `annotations list --subtree`; the `--project` rollup is the honest replacement for reading a tree's annotations. ## Sequencing Based on `main` rather than piling onto #24: **zero file overlap** with #24/#25 (they touch `running-commands-in-a-sandbox`, `assembling-a-personal-devbox`, and a different `llms.txt` line), this is unrelated CLI-drift work that reviews on its own, and `main`'s own scheduled weekly run is red until it lands. #24 picks it up by merging `main`. ---

author: milanhorvatovic
body:
## What & why

One-skill change, two files, markdown only. git-toolkit's forge-portability work (#59–#61) standardized the fleet's forge vocabulary — `Codeberg / Forgejo` as the pair's name with `tea` identified as the wire-compatible Gitea CLI, `Bitbucket Cloud` as the surface actually covered — and this skill's `references/forge-portability.md` drifted from it in naming and, worse, in three facts its cells assert:

- **Bitbucket automation identity** said "app password / OAuth" — app passwords stopped working entirely in mid-2026; the cell now names scoped API tokens.
- **GitLab auto-merge** said MR "merge when pipeline succeeds" — GitLab renamed the feature to auto-merge and `glab`'s flag followed (`--auto-merge`); the cell says so.
- **Forgejo and Bitbucket auto-merge** both said "limited" — replaced with what is actually true: API-only on Forgejo (`merge_when_checks_succeed`; `tea` does not expose it), and on Bitbucket a branch-restriction merge check ("merge when builds pass") whose per-PR arming is UI-only.

The detection table and column headers align to the fleet naming, the Bitbucket lane is described as `curl` + scoped API token, and SKILL.md's reference-table row follows. Check behavior is untouched — this PR changes the reference's vocabulary and facts, not its degrade rules. The remaining "Gitea" mentions are deliberate: the CLI's identity and the shared `…/api/v1/version` probe naming.

All three fact corrections were verified against primary sources during the git-toolkit port; the same trail applies:

<details>
<summary>Fact-check trail</summary>

- App-password removal and scoped API tokens: https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/using-api-tokens/ and https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Bitbucket-articles/Deprecation-notice-Bitbucket-Cloud-app-password-brownout/ba-p/3237429
- `glab mr merge --auto-merge` (no `--when-pipeline-succeeds` remains): https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/mr/merge/
- Forgejo/Gitea merge option `merge_when_checks_succeed` (API-only; not in tea's flag surface): https://gitea.com/gitea/tea/src/tag/v0.15.1/docs/CLI.md and the live swaggers (https://gitea.com/swagger.v1.json, https://codeberg.org/swagger.v1.json)
- Bitbucket "merge when builds pass" as a branch-restriction kind with UI-only arming: https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/suggest-or-require-checks-before-a-merge/ and https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-branch-restrictions/

</details>

## Related issues

None — this is the cross-skill echo of the forge-portability sequence (#59, #60, #61).

## Checklist

- [x] PR title is a Conventional Commit scoped by skill (or repo area) — `fix(oss-repository-conventions)`
- [x] Bumped the touched skill's `metadata.version` for behavior-affecting changes — not by hand: release-please computes the patch bump from the `fix` title
- [x] Tests added/updated for any skill-shape change — no shape change; the structural suite carried it unchanged
- [x] `./venv/bin/pytest -q` passes locally — 620 passed, 28 subtests passed
- [x] Docs / SKILL.md updated where relevant — the forge-portability reference row now names GitLab, Codeberg/Forgejo, and Bitbucket Cloud

author: yassinsolim
body:
## Summary
- use the awaitable storage methods for extension and theme lifecycle changes
- serialize mutations with Dexie and keep related writes atomic
- hydrate storage inside the mutation queue before snapshotting durable state
- persist both the item and installed-item list before showing the reload modal
- await theme CSS apply/removal and the same writes during automatic updates
- surface async lifecycle failures through existing error notifications

## Root cause
The synchronous storage wrappers updated their in-memory cache while starting IndexedDB transactions without awaiting completion. Reloading immediately could therefore race the durable install or removal state.

There was also a startup race: a user could remove an extension while IndexedDB hydration was still in flight. Late hydration then replaced the cache with the old durable snapshot, causing the queued mutation to persist stale state and make the extension reappear after reload. Mutations now await hydration inside the serialized queue before cloning their previous/next states.

## Validation
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm biome check src/components/Card/Card.tsx src/logic/Storage.ts src/logic/Utils.ts`
- `pnpm build:local`
- targeted behavioral harnesses for serialized mutations, rollback after failed persistence, no-IndexedDB fallback, delayed-hydration uninstall, and durable removal through a fresh IndexedDB connection
- live Spotify 1.2.95.453 on macOS with Spicetify 2.44.0: removed Soundalike, accepted reload, confirmed Installed remained empty after reload, then reinstalled it and confirmed the delete affordance returned

The repository's existing TypeScript baseline still reports the same six unrelated errors; this branch adds no new TypeScript diagnostics.

Closes #1186

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

Fix the two defects in the template sync that made last week's sync unmergeable, and re-land the three template improvements that sync carried.

Every Monday a workflow copies files from the shared template repository into this one. Last week's run copied back 44 files that this repository had already deleted, and wrote merge-conflict markers into 80 more. [#3341](https://github.com/AlexanderMattTurner/agent-glovebox/pull/3341) cleaned up that branch by hand and closed unmerged, so `main` still carries both causes and next Monday repeats the whole thing.

The first cause is a path test that matched nothing. `EXCLUDE_PATHS` is documented to accept a directory and cover the files under it. `is_excluded` compared strings for equality, and the sync asks about one file at a time, so a directory entry never equalled the path of any file inside it. Three entries — `.claude/skills/update-pr`, `.claude/skills/conventional-commits`, `.claude/skills/markdown-block` — sat in the list and excluded nothing.

The second cause is why the same 44 files kept coming back. The sync copies in any template file this repository does not have, so it reads "absent" as "not delivered yet". It cannot read it as "deleted on purpose", and a deletion here therefore survives exactly one week. The sync now reads this repository's own history: a commit that deleted the path is this repository saying it does not want the file. Such a file is declined and listed in the sync PR under **Declined files**. A path with no deletion commit was never here, so it is a new template file and still arrives.

A third change closes the reason the first defect stayed hidden. An entry that names a path the template does not ship excludes nothing, and it said so nowhere. The run now warns per inert entry and lists them in the sync PR, so a misspelled or stale entry is visible instead of reading as though it works.

`.template-version` moves from `f3de29b1` to `8fa9f93`. That file supplies the merge base and nothing else. 61 of the 80 conflicts existed only because the pointer was stale: with no shared ancestor the sync cannot merge, so it writes both whole versions side by side. Moving the pointer gives those files an ancestor again.

The PR also adopts the three template fixes this repository lacked, all from the closed PR's review.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `.claude/hooks/session-setup.sh` | Reads `GH_REPO` only from a remote on the local proxy host. Any remote URL ending in `/git/owner/repo` used to set it, which pointed every later `gh` command at that repository. |
| `.github/scripts/gitleaks-scan.sh` | `set -euo pipefail`, with `${VAR:-}` on the three optional base-SHA variables. |
| `.github/scripts/fetch-security-report.sh` | Branches on the open-pull-request fetch's exit code. A failed fetch returned an empty list, and the report printed that as "no Socket.dev alerts found". |

## Review focus

Read `.github/scripts/template-sync.sh` first. The cross-file invariant is that `was_deleted_here` depends on the sync job checking out with `fetch-depth: 0`, which it does. A shallow checkout finds no deletion commit and falls back to copying in — the behaviour before this PR.

The part I am least sure of is a file this repository deleted long ago and now wants back. It reads as deleted-on-purpose and is declined. It appears in the sync PR body rather than vanishing silently, and copying the file in once adopts it for good.

## Decisions made

- **Move `.template-version` to `8fa9f93` rather than leave it.** Leaving it re-opens all 80 conflicts next Monday. Moving it means the template changes made before `8fa9f93` that this repository never took are not offered again; [#3341](https://github.com/AlexanderMattTurner/agent-glovebox/pull/3341) reviewed all 80 and adopted the three above. `git diff f3de29b1..8fa9f93` in the template repository recovers the rest if you want to re-review. The pointer makes no claim about what was delivered, so moving it cannot cause a file to be declined.
- **Read the deletion from this repository's git history, not from the template's tree at the recorded version.** The review caught the tree reading as a proxy: "available at that version" is equally true of every template file this repository never adopted, so every such file would have been declined forever. Under the alternative — keeping the tree test and enumerating the additions in this description — the reviewer of each sync PR has to sort real deletions from unadopted additions by hand, every week.
- **Do not add the 38 extra `EXCLUDE_PATHS` entries the closed PR proposed.** The declined-file behaviour keeps that whole set out on its own, and each entry would have to be maintained by hand. If the declined check ever regresses, the sync PR says so by listing nothing under Declined files.
- **Leave the no-ancestor behaviour alone.** Writing both versions as conflict markers is deliberate: it stops a template file with no shared ancestor from silently replacing a local file that has diverged.

## How it was tested

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

Head at the time of writing: the branch tip pushed with this body.

| Claim | Falsifying command |
| --- | --- |
| A directory exclusion now covers the files under it | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k directory_exclusion` — passes (observed) |
| A file deleted here is not re-added, and a genuinely new one still arrives | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k not_re_added` — passes (observed) |
| A first sync (no `.template-version`) still adds every file | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k first_sync_still_adds` — passes (observed) |
| Both behaviour tests are red on the unfixed script | Restored `git show HEAD:.github/scripts/template-sync.sh`, ran the two `-k` selections above — both failed on the assertion, not on setup (observed) |
| A template file present at the recorded version but never adopted here still arrives | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k not_re_added` — passes; restored the reviewed tree-based implementation and it failed with `assert False … never-adopted.txt.exists` (observed) |
| A directory exclusion does not swallow a sibling that shares its prefix | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k directory_exclusion` — `config/skipper.txt` arrives while `config/skip/b.txt` does not (observed) |
| The narrowed GH_REPO pattern is a strict subset of `_is_web_proxy_git` | Ran it over the real proxy URL plus `http://127.0.0.1:8080/git/o/r`, `https://attacker.example/git/evil/repo` and an `https` proxy URL — match, then three no-matches (observed) |
| An EXCLUDE_PATHS entry naming nothing in the template is reported | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -k names_nothing` — passes; red on the prior script with `KeyError: 'inert_excludes'` (observed) |
| The whole sync suite passes | `uv run pytest tests/test_template_sync.py -q` — 28 passed (observed) |
| The anchored `GH_REPO` pattern takes this session's remote and rejects a foreign host | Ran the pattern over the real proxy URL and three other URLs: match, no match for `https://attacker.example/git/evil/repo`, no match for `http://127.0.0.1.attacker.example/git/evil/repo`, no match for an SSH remote (observed) |
| The four edited shell files parse | `bash -n` on each (observed) |
| Local gates pass | `bash scripts/precheck.sh` — every gate over the changed set, pylint 10.00/10, pyright 0 errors (observed). The push-time hook then ran the whole pre-push set, all Passed (observed) |

Not verified here: whether next Monday's sync runs clean. That needs the cron fire, or a `workflow_dispatch` of `template-sync.yaml`.

Class check: two properties. The first is that a path-set membership test must answer for the value the caller passes, and the caller passes one file at a time. Both sites in this repository that hold such a list are `is_excluded` and the deleted-file scan, and the scan already matched with `case "$prev_file"

author: mirichard
body:
## Summary
Five tracked files on `main` contain unresolved merge-conflict remnants from Dependabot PR merges. The `<<<<<<<` and `>>>>>>>` marker prefixes were stripped, leaving bare branch names as literal text while the `=======` separators remained. The result is **invalid JSON** committed to the default branch.

## Root Cause Analysis
Dependabot merge conflicts were resolved with a marker-stripping edit (manual or scripted) that removed only the `<<<<<<< ` and `>>>>>>> ` prefixes rather than choosing a side. Both variants plus the `=======` separator were left in place. Evidence: residual branch names appear verbatim in the files, e.g. `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/multi-75e6bc5210`, `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/site/marked-16.2.1`, and `main`.

## Impact
`npm ci`, `npm install`, and `npm audit` fail outright in the root, `site/`, and `docs/site/` workspaces. This also **suppressed local vulnerability scanning** in those workspaces. Once the lockfiles parse, `npm audit` reveals previously unscannable vulnerabilities:
- `site/` — 40 total (1 critical, 16 high, 23 moderate)
- root — 6 total (2 high, 3 moderate, 1 low)
- `docs/site/` — 5 total (4 high, 1 moderate)

These are **not** fixed here; this PR only restores validity. Remediation follows in a separate security PR.

## Changes
Conflicts in `package.json` resolved by hand, taking Dependabot's proposed version where present and `main` otherwise:
- `site/package.json` — `marked` `^16.2.1`
- `integrations/jira-asana-sync/package.json` — `@vitest/coverage-v8` `^4.0.18`; `@types/node` `^25.1.0` (main's newer value, since Dependabot's PR only targeted `coverage-v8`)

Lockfiles regenerated with `npm install --package-lock-only` so they are valid and consistent with their manifests:
- `package-lock.json` (root) — resolves `glob ^13.0.0`, `js-yaml ^4.1.1` per the already-valid root `package.json`
- `site/package-lock.json`
- `docs/site/package-lock.json` — `vite` 7.3.6 (Dependabot's side); `astro` stays on 6.x, no major bump

Markdown conflict remnants:
- `docs/dashboard-mvp-demo.md` — two interleaved variants of the setup instructions produced duplicate `### Production build` headings and orphaned steps. Reconstructed into **Quick start** and **Manual setup**. The `cp .env.example .env.local` step was dropped because `dashboard-mvp/.env.example` does not exist.
- `docs/archive/README-20250805.md` — stray separators removed only. This archived snapshot has deeper pre-existing structural damage (duplicated sections, a mermaid block inside a table) that was intentionally **not** rewritten.

No dependency ranges were intentionally upgraded beyond resolving the conflicts. No major versions were bumped.

## Validation
- No `=======`, `<<<<<<<`, or `>>>>>>>` remnants remain in any tracked file (excluding `node_modules`)
- Every tracked `package.json` and `package-lock.json` parses as valid JSON
- `npm audit --package-lock-only` succeeds in root, `site/`, and `docs/site/` (previously errored)
- `npm ls --package-lock-only --depth=0` reports OK in all three

## Risk and Impact Analysis
Low. Restores files to a parseable state; no source or runtime code touched. The regenerated lockfiles are large diffs by nature but resolve to versions satisfying the existing, unchanged manifest ranges. Main risk is transitive-version drift in the three regenerated lockfiles, bounded by the declared semver ranges.

## Rollback Plan
`git revert` this PR's merge commit, or `git checkout main -- <path>` per file. Reverting restores the previous state exactly, including the invalid JSON. No data migration or external state is involved.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Security remediation of the newly visible alerts in `site/`, root, and `docs/site/`
- `scripts/start-dashboard-demo.sh` runs `cp .env.example .env.local` under `set -e`, but `dashboard-mvp/.env.example` does not exist, so the script fails. Either add the file or drop the line.
- `PM Tools Templates - Q3 2025 Delivery Cycle/.../template-selector/backend/package-lock.json` has 1,994 of 2,459 entries keyed to an out-of-tree path (`/private/tmp/pm-sparse/...`), so npm cannot apply available fixes.
- `workflow-orchestration/` has 6,392 `node_modules` files committed to git.
- Consider a CI check that rejects conflict markers and validates JSON, to prevent recurrence.

Co-Authored-By: Oz <oz-agent@warp.dev>

body:
Closes #72.

`powervault.info.*` and `powerflex.info.*` were missing from `fr`/`de`/`it`; `zfs.ashift*` and `nutanix.info.*` from `de`/`it`. They rendered as raw keys on screen.

The parity test was written **first**, so the gap list is measured rather than assumed: **38 keys**, not the ~34 the issue estimated (`fr` already had `nutanix.info.*`; `de` and `it` were each missing 15).

## The test

`tests/i18n/parity.spec.ts` discovers locales and namespaces from disk rather than hand-listing 32 file pairs, diffs every translation against the `en` reference recursively, and asserts **both** directions — a missing key renders as a raw key, an orphan key is dead weight from a typo or a removed feature. Failures name the locale, namespace and full key path. It also asserts each locale has the same set of namespace files.

Technical terms and product names left untranslated: RAID, ZFS, NVMe, IOPS, PowerVault, PowerFlex, Nutanix, ashift.

author: matslil
body:
## Summary

- advertise full-document semantic token support from `topal-lsp`
- derive highlighting from the shared lossless lexer
- distinguish variables, numbers, strings, comments, reserved literals, and operators
- delta-encode UTF-16 positions and lengths as required by LSP
- split multiline and incomplete string tokens into valid per-line tokens

## Why

Highlighting should remain consistent with interpreter/compiler tokenization and should still work while a user is typing malformed code. Reusing the recovery-friendly lexer avoids a separate editor grammar and immediately tests whether shared token spans are sufficient for protocol consumers.

## User and tool impact

Editors can request `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` and highlight the currently implemented Topal syntax, including comments, Boolean literals, exact numbers, callable symbols, Unicode identifiers, and multiline raw strings.

## Risk and review

Medium protocol range risk, especially around UTF-16 and multiline tokens. Tests cover an astral identifier, delta positions, incomplete tagged multiline strings, legend indices, and valid line splitting. This PR is independently mergeable to `main`.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` — 115 passed across 8 suites
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

author: alfhen
body:
## Summary

Adds a `TEST_FILE_DEMOTION_FACTOR = 0.8` multiplier to `search_code`'s lexical ranking (`packages/core/src/vectordb/sqlite/fts-search.ts`), applied when a result's file is a test file (`isTestFile`, reused from `@liendev/parser` — no second definition). Borrowed from zoekt's ranker, which does the same `factor *= 0.8` for a `_test.go` file.

Matches `applyStructuralBoost`'s existing shape exactly: a named constant with a doc comment on *why* 0.8, and an independent env escape hatch (`LIEN_TEST_FILE_RANKING=off`, separate from `LIEN_STRUCTURAL_RANKING` so either nudge is A/B-able on its own).

Both ranking call sites (`keywordSearch`'s within-corpus sort, and `OverlayBackend.mergeRankedHits`'s cross-corpus re-sort for worktree overlays) now go through one shared `computeRankingKey(ratio, dependentCount, filepath)` composer, so structural boost and test-file demotion can never diverge between the two sites — the exact "one decision implemented at N sites" failure mode this repo has shipped bugs from before (`applyStructuralBoost` itself was originally duplicated this way before #1071).

**Demotes, never excludes**, and **does not touch `applyStructuralBoost` or `BM25_WEIGHTS`** (both explicitly out of scope) — see constraints below, all satisfied.

## Why

Global-centrality measurements across 14 real corpora repeatedly surfaced test helpers/fixtures ranked above real source: `Assert.kt` test helpers at #1/#2 on Exposed (Kotlin), `lien-review-testbed/rust/*.rs` fixtures outranking real source on this repo, a test `NullTextWriter.cs` at #2 on serilog. zoekt's one-line `_test.go` demotion is a cheaper fix for this noise class than any graph work.

## Golden-diff verification (ranking-regression harness)

**First pass, and why it wasn't enough.** Regenerating the golden file against the plain ranking change produced a byte-identical result: all 8 fixture corpora were built as hub+handler+entry-point files, none containing anything `isTestFile()` matches, so `applyTestFileDemotion` was a no-op on every existing measurement. That's an honest "no delta," but on reflection it means this lever would have shipped with **zero regression coverage** — CI green, but nothing in it would notice the demotion silently stopping working. That's the exact shape of #1071 (`applyStructuralBoost` dead in six languages for weeks, undetected, because no test exercised it). Fixed below rather than shipped as a known gap.

**Fixture added:** `packages/cli/test/fixtures/ranking-corpora/go/internal/util/logger_test.go` — a genuine `_test.go` file (confirmed against the actual `isTestFile()` predicate, not assumed) placed alongside the hub `logger.go`, repeating `LogInfo` densely enough to out-bm25 `logger.go`'s own defining chunk on the corpus's existing `queries[0]` ("LogInfo") — the same query the harness already runs, so the demotion visibly reorders a real result set rather than sitting inert. Go resolves imports per-package, not per-file, so adding this file to the `internal/util` package gives it the exact same `dependentCount` (4) as `logger.go` — confirmed by a new assertion, not assumed — which isolates the demotion's effect from the structural-boost lever instead of conflating the two.

**Golden delta (non-zero, go corpus only):**
```diff
 === go ===
-files: 5
-filesWithDependents: 4
+files: 6
+filesWithDependents: 5
 maxDependentCount: 4
 medianBoostMultiplier: 1.10
 recall@1 (ON): 1.00
```
(recall@1/recall@5/MRR stay at 1.00 in both ON/OFF here because that toggle is `LIEN_STRUCTURAL_RANKING`, not the new lever — see the hard assertion below for the actual demotion proof, which is deliberately NOT routed through this golden diff.)

**New hard, non-golden assertion** (mirrors the harness's existing `dependentCount > 0` proof, assertion (a), applied to `applyTestFileDemotion`):
```
✓ test-file demotion resolves non-zero AND ties dependentCount with the hub file for logger_test.go (go)
✓ test-file demotion: LIEN_TEST_FILE_RANKING=off lets a genuine test file (logger_test.go) outrank
  the real source file it tests (logger.go) on their shared "LogInfo" query, and the default
  (demotion on) flips it back
```
Concretely: with `LIEN_TEST_FILE_RANKING=off`, `logger_test.go` ranks above `logger.go` for query `"LogInfo"`; with the default (on), `logger.go` ranks above `logger_test.go`. Both directions asserted, both green. This is deliberately kept OUT of the golden diff for the same reason assertion (a) is: whether the lever moves anything at all has one right answer, and a `UPDATE_RANKING_GOLDEN=1` regeneration must never be able to paper over it going dark.

All 12 ranking-regression tests pass (10 original + 2 new), including the pre-existing hard `dependentCount > 0` per-language assertions, unaffected by this change.

## Concrete before/after example (real corpus: JetBrains/Exposed)

Cloned `JetBrains/Exposed` (857 source files, all modules) and indexed it with this build. Query `"dialect"`:

**Before** (`LIEN_TEST_FILE_RANKING=off`, i.e. pure bm25 + structural boost only — the pre-this-PR behavior):
```
1. exposed-tests/.../tests/TestDB.kt              dependentCount=101  <- test-infra file
2. exposed-r2dbc-tests/.../tests/TestDB.kt        dependentCount=85   <- test-infra file
3. exposed-core/.../vendors/DatabaseDialect.kt    dependentCount=22   <- real production source
4. exposed-core/.../DatabaseApi.kt                dependentCount=6    <- real production source
5. exposed-r2dbc/.../R2dbcTypeMapping.kt          dependentCount=4
```
`TestDB.kt` — a test-database configuration helper, structurally massive at 101 dependents (test files reference it everywhere) — outranks `DatabaseDialect.kt`, the actual production class implementing "dialect."

**After** (default settings, this PR):
```
1. exposed-core/.../vendors/DatabaseDialect.kt    dependentCount=22   <- real production source, now #1
2. exposed-tests/.../tests/TestDB.kt              dependentCount=101
3. exposed-core/.../DatabaseApi.kt                dependentCount=6
4. exposed-r2dbc-tests/.../tests/TestDB.kt        dependentCount=85
5. exposed-r2dbc/.../R2dbcTypeMapping.kt          dependentCount=4
```
The demotion flips the order: real production source now ranks first.

**Findability check** — a query naming a test file directly still finds it at rank 1: query `"assertEqualCollections"` (a symbol defined only in Exposed's `Assert.kt` test helper) returns `Assert.kt` at ranks 1–5 exclusively, both with the demotion on and off. Demotion nudges ties, it doesn't hide the file.

**Honest caveat on the motivating examples**: this fix covers the `Assert.kt`-shape (Kotlin/C# paths that satisfy `isTestFile`'s existing conventions — confirmed both `Assert.kt`'s and serilog's `test/.../NullTextWriter.cs`'s paths match). It does **not** cover the `lien-review-testbed/rust/*.rs` case cited in the motivating examples — those fixture files (`cache.rs`, `analyzer.rs`, etc.) live under a `lien-review-testbed/` directory that doesn't match any `isTestFile` convention (no `test`/`tests`/`spec` path segment, no `_test.rs` suffix), so they aren't classified as test files and aren't demoted. Widening `isTestFile` to catch "testbed/fixture directory" as its own convention would be a second, broader definition change — out of scope here per the brief (reuse existing detection, don't invent a new one).

## Fix: overlay/base merge on raw ratio, not a value reconstructed from rounded score

**Major finding from review, fixed, not accepted as narrow.** `keywordSearch` emits `score = round4((1 - ratio) * 2)` — rounded to 4 decimals, not invertible. `OverlayBackend.mergeRankedHits` was reconstructing `ratio = 1 - hit.score / 2` to recompute the composed ranking key across the overlay/base boundary. Two hits — one from each corpus — whose raw ratios differ by less than the rounding granularity (~0.00005) round to the **identical** score, collapsing to an artificial tie. `Array.prototype.sort`'s stability then resolves that tie b

author: rickyrombo
body:
## What

Collapses `save_type` / `repost_type` `'album'` back into `'playlist'` — **670 saves and 528 reposts**.

Pairs with **OpenAudio/go-openaudio#428**, which stops the indexer writing `'album'`. **These ship together**: this backfill alone would be re-broken by the current indexer.

## Why

An album is a playlist with `is_album = true`. The indexer briefly derived a separate `'album'` type by reading `playlists.is_album` at index time — a side effect of an entity-id collision fix, not a deliberate convention. It first appears in prod `saves` *and* `reposts` on the same day, 2026-05-28, after seven years with zero.

`is_album` is mutable, but `save_type` is written once and is part of the primary key `(user_id, save_item_id, save_type, txhash)` — so the same chain history indexed at different times produced different rows. Nothing reads the distinction: every consumer is `track` / `!= track`, or ORs the two together (`get_account_playlists`, `reconcile_aggregates`). The notification triggers already derive album from `is_album` at read time.

## Two hazards, and how they're handled

**Duplicate notifications.** `on_save` / `on_repost` fire on `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE`, and the notification `group_id` embeds the type (`'save:<id>:type:<save_type>'`). A plain UPDATE would mint a *second* favourite notification per row under a new group_id. Those two triggers are disabled for the backfill; `trg_saves` / `trg_reposts` (the `pg_notify` → search indexer) stay enabled so ES still sees the change.

**Primary key.** The type is part of the PK. Verified against prod data that **no** `(user_id, item_id, txhash)` has both a `'playlist'` and an `'album'` row, so this is a straight UPDATE with no conflict handling.

Aggregate counts are unaffected either way — `handle_save`'s `delta` is transition-aware and evaluates to `0` when `is_delete` does not change.

## Verification

Applied against a fixture mirroring the real wiring (enums, 4-column PK, all four triggers):

- all `album` → `playlist`; `track` untouched
- **0** `on_save` / `on_repost` firings
- `pg_notify` fired exactly once per updated row
- a row that had *both* a `playlist` and an `album` version kept both (different `txhash`)
- all triggers re-enabled (`tgenabled = 'O'`) afterwards

⚠️ Not run against a real database. The repo's migration set can't be built from scratch locally (it assumes base tables created outside this repo), so the fixture covers the mechanism rather than the full schema.

## Notes

- Each table gets its own transaction with `lock_timeout` to keep the `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock from `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER` as short as possible. ~1.2k rows, so it should be milliseconds.
- Re-running is a no-op once no `'album'` rows remain.
- `'album'` is deliberately left in the `savetype` / `reposttype` enums — Postgres can't drop an enum value without rebuilding the type, and the indexer no longer writes it.

author: lhqing
body:
Closes #262 — the five carry-overs from the post-mapping report's three PRs, plus one the issue
missed and two review turned up.

Built by three subagents, one commit each, split by **file ownership** rather than by issue item:
items 1, 2 and 5 all live in `panels.py`, so an agent per item would have fought over one file.

## What changed

**The pinned column holds an identifier** (`e21248f`). The per-sample counting note left the sticky
`<th>` for a block under the table — one line per *distinct* note naming the samples that carry it, so
the attribution the old code argued for survives while the wrapping that crushed the column to ~115 px
does not. The `min-width` floor recorded in #220 was not re-tried; it was reverted on measurement for
good reason.

**The Evidence body is as wide as its panel** (`e21248f`). #262 framed the 768 px cap as a deliberate
reading measure grown conspicuous. That does not survive checking: the tab's only prose is the panel
lead, capped separately at 82ch — *narrower* than 768 px and **outside** the capped div. What the cap
actually narrowed was the verdict strip, the role × file grid, and score bars a reader compares by
length. Removed rather than widened; `max-w-5xl` was rejected as a cap 48 px from no cap.

**A hand-counted tree drifts** (`b170a10`). `_template.md` claimed "seventeen records" against 25.
Dropped the number rather than correcting it — the sentence's claim is about the *shape* records share,
so "every record in this tree" says it more strongly and cannot go stale. `0019` is a deliberate gap and
stays one. ADR 0025 gains one bullet naming `MODULES_WITHOUT_CROSS_CHECKS`, which ships **non-empty**
where its sibling ships empty, so a reader comparing them is not left to work out why.

**The cap, not the budget, was holding the page inside it** (`1e4b109`). `_ALERT_MAX_SAMPLES = 6`
truncates before the size budget notices — a mutation adding ~6 KB per firing sample was **not** caught.
The new guard renders a 96-well plate twice, once with the cap lifted, and measures the *untruncated*
page against the same budget, plus an anti-vacuity assertion that the cap genuinely binds. Measured at
~269 KB truncated / ~283 KB untruncated against a 500 KB budget, so it fires once an alert row costs
about 2.4 KB against the ~160 bytes one costs today.

## Found in passing, not on the issue

- **A pre-existing duplication**: `read_pipeline_stats` folded sample captions into `PipelineStats.notes`
  *and* the samples carried them, so the run-state block printed the same sentences unattributed.
- **`tests/test_docs.py`** carried the same stale count as `_template.md`, in a different file.

## From review (`25b16cf`)

The first fix above filtered the duplication out by **matching note strings back across a package
seam** — reword a caption in an adapter and the match silently stops, so the caption reappears where a
reader looks for failures. Fixed at the source instead: `read_pipeline_stats` no longer folds, `notes`
means one thing, and the consumer filters nothing. Verified the fold had no other reader first.

Review also caught `all N samples` being untested on a partial run, where N is the rows read and the
banner above says something else. It now says "shown" when the run is partial and drops it when complete.

## Verification

`pixi run check` green: **1254 passed, 4 skipped** (the four standing env gates). Every new guard was
watched failing on a real mutation and restored — the fold re-added, the cap slice deleted, N switched to
the contracted count, and ~6 KB padded per alert row. A guard that only passes today is the rule it
replaced.

Spec review: no findings. Standards review: no hard violations; the two substantive judgement calls are
fixed above, and two cosmetic ones were left with reasons.

author: rociocm
body:
An outfit can now carry **emotes as ordinary items**: they list among the wearables with no special treatment, count in the item count and the credits total, and are added by the add-all CTA. When a look includes one, its preview plays that emote instead of the default fashion pose.

## Emotes in outfits

- **`lib/outfit`** — `outfitPreviewUrns()` puts the playing emote at `urns[0]` and drops any others. The order is load-bearing: Babylon plays the **last** emote it finds among the urns, Unity's marketplace mode reads **`urns[0]`** and nothing else, so sending exactly one emote makes both renderers land on the same one (the first authored). `playingEmote()` names it.
- **Studio** — the picker gains a Wearables|Emotes toggle whose category also scopes the search (the placeholder used to hard-code "Search wearables…"), the row holding the playing emote is marked "Plays in preview", and publishing now requires at least one wearable. That last rule is client-only: the server has no catalog access to check categories.
- **Detail** — the ui2 playback bar renders through a new `OutfitPreview` `controls` slot, gated on the preview iframe actually existing. Mounting it earlier throws `Could not find an iframe with id=…` and takes the page down, because `WearablePreview` is itself lazy and suspends on a cold load.
- **No server change.** `items` already stored category-free refs and shop-server validates shape only — no migration, no schema edit.

## Discovery row: buyable from the creator

An outfit is admitted to the row only while **every** item is still buyable from its creator — priced, supply left, mint open (`isBuyableFromCreator`). The reason no longer matters: delisted, sold out and resale-only all drop the card, so a shopper never meets a look they cannot buy complete. Reasons stay on `/outfits/:id`, per item.

This needed no extra requests: `/v2` already reports `available` and the creator's mint price separately from the resale floor — the mapper just never read them.

## Pricing fix (pre-existing, same code path)

`/v2/catalog` quotes **MANA**, but the mapper read `price` as USD wei. A 15 MANA (3 credit) item rendered as **150 credits** on outfit cards, the outfit detail list and the favorites page — and prod's feed is currently 100% legacy/MANA-priced, so it affected every item.

Those rows now carry `manaWei` with no fixed credit price, and are priced at the live oracle rate through a shared `displayCredits()` — the same rule the browse grid already applies to any MANA-priced card. The rate folds into the resolution's `isLoading`/`isError`, so a missing rate reads as "still resolving", never as a zero price.

Batching was considered and ruled out: `/v3/catalog/unified` ignores `id`/`ids` (returns the whole feed) and repeated `contractAddress` returns only the first, and the 27 seeded looks span 102 unique items across 93 collections. An `id`-list filter on that endpoint is what would let the row move off `/v2`.

## Renderer

`OutfitPreview` is pinned to **Babylon**: no Unity mode can render a multi-item avatar today (`marketplace` reads one urn, `profile` reads none), so requesting Unity would drop most of the look the moment the flag turns on. Restore `unity` once the renderer supports it — the emote-at-`urns[0]` ordering is already what marketplace mode needs.

## Test harness

The outfits spec boots its own dev server alongside the shared one; both were writing `node_modules/.vite` and rewriting each other's optimized deps mid-run, 504ing the loser's browser. It now gets a private `VITE_CACHE_DIR` and pays the cold-start pre-bundle in `beforeAll` instead of inside the first test.

## Verified

`npm run lint`, `tsc -b`, **1646 unit tests**, **165 e2e tests (45 files)** — all green. New coverage: `outfitPreviewUrns` (asserting index 0, which is what Unity reads), `isBuyableFromCreator`, `displayCredits`, emote toggling in the studio selection, and four e2e cases plus a phone-width layout case.

Not covered by tests: the emote actually animating — the harness never runs the 3D renderer. Worth one manual check with a real emote in a draft.

body: ## Problem Spotted while verifying the v1.3.0 production deploy: `https://l.opn.onl/api-docs/openapi.json` reports `"version": "1.2.1"` while the running image is 1.3.0. The version lived as a string literal in `#[openapi(info(...))]`, so it only advanced when someone remembered to hand-edit it alongside `Cargo.toml`. Nobody did for 1.3.0. ## Fix utoipa 4 rejects `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` inside that attribute — it insists on a literal: ``` error: expected string literal --> src/openapi.rs:14:19 | 14 | version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), ``` So the document is built through a small `api_doc()` helper that stamps the crate version, and `swagger_routes()` serves that. Both the JSON spec and Swagger UI now follow `Cargo.toml` with no manual step. ## Test New case in `tests/audit_openapi.rs` drives the real router and asserts the served spec reports `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, so the next bump can't silently drift again. ``` cargo test --test audit_openapi → 2 passed cargo clippy --all-targets → 0 errors ``` ## Deploy note No release or image rebuild requested with this — production keeps reporting 1.2.1 in its API docs until the next release picks this up. author: copilot
body:
All 5 metadata scan workflows shared a single `group: metadata-scans` concurrency group. With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub Actions queues at most one pending run per group — so any scheduled trigger that arrived while another workflow was already queued was silently cancelled. In practice this meant technology and social media scans almost never ran, leaving `url_tech_results` empty and the published pages showing "No scan data yet."

## Changes

**Concurrency — all 5 workflows**
Each workflow now has its own concurrency group (`metadata-scans-technology`, `metadata-scans-social`, etc.), so they run independently and only self-protect against their own overlapping runs.

```yaml
# Before (shared — all workflows block each other)
concurrency:
  group: metadata-scans

# After (per-workflow — only blocks itself)
concurrency:
  group: metadata-scans-technology
```

**Schedule & runtime — `scan-technology.yml` and `scan-social-media.yml`**
- Schedule changed from `*/2 * * *` (every 2 h) to `*/8 * * *` (every 8 h) — fewer, longer runs rather than many cancelled short ones
- `timeout-minutes` raised from 25 → 65; `--max-runtime` raised from 15 → 55 min, giving ~6,600 URLs/run at 2 req/s (~88k URL corpus covered in ~5 days per scanner)
- `skip-recently-scanned-days` default changed from `7` → `30` to target monthly full-corpus coverage

**Runtime cap — `scan-overlays.yml`**
- `timeout-minutes` 120 → 65 and `--max-runtime` 110 → 55 to stay within the GITHUB_TOKEN expiry window (>60 min causes 403 errors on artifact uploads)

author: apecertooficial-arch
body:
## O problema

O catálogo montava o estoque filtrando só por `disponivel`:

```js
const availableUnits = units.filter((unit) => unit.disponivel);
```

Uma unidade de indicação nasce com `disponivel = true` e `aprovacao = 'pendente'`. Ou seja: **ela já entrava na contagem de disponíveis e no cálculo do "a partir de" antes de qualquer validação.** O botão Aprovar mudava um rótulo, não a visibilidade — a fila de aprovação sugeria um bloqueio que não existia.

## Impacto medido em produção (12 unidades pendentes hoje)

| Produto | Disponíveis (antes) | Disponíveis (depois) | "A partir de" antes | depois |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AP Moema | 26 | **21** | R$ 401.997 (unidade 404, pendente) | R$ 403.350 |
| Composite | 13 | **7** | R$ 431.280 | R$ 431.280 |
| Moema Studium | 2 | **1** | R$ 410.000 | R$ 410.000 |

Total do portfólio: 235 → 223 unidades disponíveis. Nenhuma unidade some do banco; elas apenas deixam de contar como estoque ofertável até serem aprovadas.

## O que mudou

- **`app/lib/estoque.ts`** (novo) — regra única: `ehOfertavel()` = `disponivel && aprovacao === 'aprovado'`, e `estaPendente()`. `aprovacao` é NOT NULL com default `'aprovado'`, então unidade de construtora continua contando normalmente; o coalesce cobre linhas antigas.
- **`app/api/catalog/route.ts`** — usa a regra no cálculo de disponíveis, preço mínimo e área mínima. O `select` das unidades passa a trazer `aprovacao` (sem isso a regra rodaria sem o campo). Devolve `pendingUnits` por produto, para o aprovador saber quantas aguardam validação.
- **`app/api/product/route.ts`** — mesma regra no `summary_price` / `summary_area` da ficha, para catálogo e ficha não divergirem.
- **`app/api/product/route.ts` (bypass de alçada)** — o insert de unidade pelo editor do produto não definia `aprovacao`, e o default da coluna é `'aprovado'`. Dava para cadastrar uma indicação **já aprovada** tendo apenas permissão de `produtos.editar`, pulando a alçada de admin/gestor/executivo exigida pelo `decideUnit`. Agora `de_terceiros` força `aprovacao: 'pendente'`.

## Testes

`tests/estoque-aprovacao.test.mjs` — 10 casos, 10 passando. Cobre a regra (aprovado / pendente / reprovado / indisponível / aprovacao ausente) e trava a regressão nos dois consumidores, incluindo o bypass do editor.

```
# tests 10
# pass 10
# fail 0
```

`tsc --noEmit`: 0 erros nos arquivos alterados. (O repo tem 57 erros de tipo pré-existentes em outros arquivos, não tocados aqui.)

## Não incluído neste PR

- O redesenho da tela de revisão da indicação e o comparativo de R$/m² contra a curva do prédio — depende do design system.
- A UI ainda não exibe `pendingUnits`; o campo já vem na resposta para quando a tela for ajustada.

## Checar depois do merge

O contador de "disponíveis" nos cards vai cair (é o efeito esperado). Se algum produto perder estoque que deveria estar no ar, é sinal de que aquela indicação está parada na fila esperando aprovação.
